words.en: If a problem or mystery is insoluble, it is impossible to solve or explain.

words.ex: Her story inspires me to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的故事激励我更加努力。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you to do something new or unusual, they make you want to do it.

words.ex: The car stopped in an instantaneous moment.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在瞬间停了下来。
words.en: Happening or done immediately.

words.ex: He answered the question instantly.
words.ex_cn: 他立即回答了问题。
words.en: If something happens instantly, it happens immediately.

words.ex: He tried to instigate a fight at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在聚会上挑起争斗。
words.en: If someone instigates an event or situation, they cause it to happen by their actions or behavior.

words.ex: The cat made an instinctive jump to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫本能地跳开以躲避狗。
words.en: An instinctive feeling, action, or idea is one that you have or do without thinking or reasoning.

words.tr:
n. 研究所；学院；协会；
v. 建立；制定；
words.ex: He works at a research institute.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家研究所工作。
words.en: An institute is an organization set up to do a particular type of work, especially research or teaching. It can also refer to the act of starting something such as a system or an official process.

words.ex: The hospital is a public institution.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一家公共机构。
words.en: An institution is a large important organization such as a university, church, or bank.

words.tr: v. 使制度化或习俗化；使送进专门机构
words.ex: The government wants to institutionalize the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望将这项新政策制度化。
words.en: To institutionalize something means to make it a fixed and accepted part of a system, organization, or society.

words.tr:
adj. 制度化的；（因长期生活在福利机构）缺乏自理能力的
v. 使制度化或习俗化；使送进专门机构；“institutionalize”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The practice was institutionalized in the 1980s.
words.ex_cn: 这种做法在20世纪80年代被制度化了。
words.en: If someone becomes institutionalized, they gradually become less able to think and act independently, because of having lived for a long time under the rules of an institution.

words.tr: adj. 教育性的；有启发的；有益的
words.ex: The movie is instructive for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对孩子们很有教育意义。
words.en: Providing useful or interesting information or knowledge.

words.tr: adj. 有帮助的；乐器的；仪器的；
words.ex: Her advice was instrumental in helping me pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对帮助我通过考试很有帮助。
words.en: If someone or something is instrumental in a process, plan, or system, they are one of the most important influences in causing it to happen.

words.ex: The student was insubordinate to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这名学生对老师不服从。
words.en: If someone is insubordinate, they deliberately do not obey someone of higher rank.

words.ex: His excuse was insubstantial and unconvincing.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口是无实质的，毫无说服力。
words.en: If something is insubstantial, it is not solid, large, or strong, and therefore often seems unsatisfactory or unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 海岛的；孤立的；思想褊狭的
words.ex: The insular village has no bridge to the mainland.
words.ex_cn: 这个海岛村庄没有桥通向大陆。
words.en: If you describe someone as insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.

words.tr: adj. 侮辱的； v. “insult”的现在分词；
words.ex: His insulting words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他侮辱的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's remarks or actions as insulting, you mean they are rude and offensive.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.tr: adj. 无法克服的；难以解决的；不可逾越的
words.ex: The problem seemed insurmountable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题似乎无法克服。
words.en: If you describe something as insurmountable, you mean that it is so great or severe that it cannot be dealt with.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.ex: Love is an intangible thing.
words.ex_cn: 爱是一种无形的东西。
words.en: Something that is intangible is not able to be touched or seen, but is still important or valuable.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.tr:
adj. 智力的；
n. 知识分子；
words.ex: He is an intellectual person who loves solving math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个热爱解决数学问题的智力型人。
words.en: An intellectual is someone who spends a lot of time studying and thinking about complicated ideas.

words.tr: adj. 可理解的；明白易懂的；清楚的
words.ex: His explanation was intelligible to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释人人都能听懂。
words.en: Capable of being understood; comprehensible.

words.ex: His intemperance in drinking led to health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他酗酒无度导致了健康问题。
words.en: Intemperance refers to a lack of moderation or restraint, especially in the indulgence of an appetite or desire.

words.tr: n. 激烈化；增强；增强明暗度
words.ex: The intensification of rain caused flooding.
words.ex_cn: 降雨的增强导致了洪水。
words.en: The act of becoming more intense or the process of making something more intense.

words.tr:
n. 意图；目的；
adj. 专注的；
words.ex: His intent was to help, not to hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他的意图是帮助，而不是伤害。
words.en: If you are intent on doing something, you are determined to get it done. If you have an intent to do something, you have a plan or purpose in mind.

words.ex: He gave an intentional wrong answer to confuse the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他故意答错答案来迷惑老师。
words.en: Something that is intentional is done on purpose, not by chance.

words.ex: The app has an interactive game for kids.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用有一个适合孩子的交互式游戏。
words.en: An interactive computer program or system is designed to involve the user in the exchange of information.

words.ex: These two words are interchangeable in this sentence.
words.ex_cn: 这两个词在这个句子中可以互换使用。
words.en: If one thing is interchangeable with another, the first can be used instead of the second because it has the same function or meaning.

words.ex: These two symbols can be used interchangeably in the equation.
words.ex_cn: 这两个符号在方程中可以可交换地使用。
words.en: In a way that allows two or more things to be used or exchanged in place of each other.

words.tr: adj. 相互连接的；互相联系的； v. “interconnect”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The cities are interconnected by highways.
words.ex_cn: 这些城市通过高速公路相互连接。
words.en: If things are interconnected, they are connected to each other in some way.

words.tr: adj. 互相依赖的；相倚的；
words.ex: The two countries are interdependent in trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上互相依赖。
words.en: If two or more things are interdependent, they depend on each other.

words.tr:
adj. 联锁的；相互扣住的
v. （使）连锁；（使）相互扣住；“interlock”的现在分词
words.ex: The puzzle pieces are interlocking.
words.ex_cn: 这些拼图碎片是相互扣合的。
words.en: Interlocking refers to the process or state of two or more things being connected or joined together in such a way that they move or operate together.

words.ex: The meeting felt interminable.
words.ex_cn: 这场会议感觉没完没了。
words.en: If you describe something as interminable, you are emphasizing that it continues for a very long time and indicating that you find it boring or annoying.

words.ex: The interplay between light and shadow creates beauty.
words.ex_cn: 光与影的相互作用创造了美。
words.en: The way in which two or more things have an effect on each other.

words.ex: The historian interpolated the text with his own opinions.
words.ex_cn: 这位历史学家在文本中插入了自己的观点。
words.en: To interpolate means to insert something between other things or parts, especially to insert words into a text.

words.ex: He interprets the poem as a love story.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首诗解释为一个爱情故事。
words.en: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

words.ex: The teacher gave a simple interpretation of the poem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这首诗做了一个简单的解释。
words.en: An interpretation of something is an explanation or understanding of it.

words.ex: The two ideas interrelate closely.
words.ex_cn: 这两个想法密切相关。
words.en: If two or more things interrelate, there is a connection between them and they have an effect on each other.

words.ex: The police did an interrogation at night.
words.ex_cn: 警察在晚上进行了审问。
words.en: The process of asking someone a lot of questions in order to get information, especially in a police or military context.

words.ex: The phone call caused an interruption in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 电话打断了会议。
words.en: An interruption is something that temporarily stops an activity or a situation.

words.ex: The two lines intersect at point A.
words.ex_cn: 两条线在点A相交。
words.en: If two or more lines or roads intersect, they meet or cross each other.

words.ex: They have an intimate friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着亲密的友谊。
words.en: having a close, friendly, or personal relationship with someone; private and personal

words.ex: He gave me an intimation that he would leave soon.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示我他很快就要离开了。
words.en: An intimation is an indirect suggestion or sign that something is likely to happen or be true.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: The problem is intractable and no one can solve it.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题很难处理，没人能解决。
words.en: If you describe a problem or a person as intractable, you mean that it is very difficult to deal with or to change.

words.tr: adj. 不妥协的；不让步的
words.ex: He is intransigent about his opinions.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的观点毫不让步。
words.en: If you describe someone as intransigent, you mean that they refuse to behave differently or to change their attitude to something.

words.ex: The intrepid explorer climbed the high mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的探险家爬上了高山。
words.en: If you describe someone as intrepid, you mean that they are brave, fearless, and willing to do things that might be dangerous.

words.ex: The intricacy of the clock made it very special.
words.ex_cn: 这座钟的复杂精细让它非常特别。
words.en: The quality of being intricate; complexity.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.tr: adj. 固有的；内在的；本身的；
words.ex: Honesty is an intrinsic part of her character.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是她性格中固有的部分。
words.en: belonging to a thing by its very nature

words.ex: He is introspective and often thinks about his feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他善于内省，经常思考自己的感受。
words.en: If you describe someone as introspective, you mean that they spend a lot of time examining their own thoughts, ideas, and feelings.

words.tr: n. 内向的人；不喜欢与人交往的人
words.ex: He is an introvert who likes reading alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是个喜欢独自读书的内向者。
words.en: An introvert is a person who tends to shrink from social contacts and to become preoccupied with their own thoughts.

words.tr:
adj. 打扰的；侵扰的
v. 闯入；打扰；强使；“intrude”的现在分词
words.ex: She felt uncomfortable with the constant intruding of her privacy.
words.ex_cn: 她对隐私不断被侵入感到不舒服。
words.en: If you say that someone is intruding into a particular place or situation, you mean that they are not wanted or welcome there.

words.ex: She spoke intrusively into their private conversation.
words.ex_cn: 她干扰地插入了他们的私人对话。
words.en: In a manner that involves intrusion or the act of intruding.

words.ex: I trusted my intuition and chose the right answer.
words.ex_cn: 我相信自己的直觉，选了正确的答案。
words.en: Intuition is the ability to understand or know something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.

words.ex: The app has an intuitive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用程序具有直观的设计。
words.en: An intuitive idea or feeling is based on an instinctive emotional response rather than on conscious thought.

words.ex: He inured himself to the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 他让自己适应了寒冷的天气。
words.en: If you are inured to something unpleasant, you have become used to it so that it no longer affects you.

words.ex: The army tried to invade the neighboring country.
words.ex_cn: 军队试图侵犯邻国。
words.en: To enter a country, town, or region by force in order to take control of it.

words.ex: The mistake will invalidate the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误会使结果无效。
words.en: To invalidate something such as a contract or an election means to make it officially not valid.

words.tr: adj. 永无变化的；始终如一的
words.ex: The speed of light is invariable.
words.ex_cn: 光速是不变的。
words.en: An invariable thing or quality never changes or is always the same.

words.ex: The telephone was a great invention.
words.ex_cn: 电话是一项伟大的发明。
words.en: An invention is a unique or novel device, method, composition or process. It may be an improvement upon a machine or product, or a new process for creating an object or a result. An invention that achieves a completely unique function or result may be a radical breakthrough. Such works are novel and not obvious to others skilled in the same field.

words.ex: The inventive child made a toy from cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个有创造力的孩子用纸板做了一个玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as inventive, you mean that they are good at inventing things or have clever and original ideas.

words.ex: The inverse order of the numbers is 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的倒序是5、4、3、2、1。
words.en: If there is an inverse relationship between two things, one of them becomes larger as the other becomes smaller.

words.ex: The police will investigate the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方将调查这起事故。
words.en: If someone, especially an official, investigates an event, situation, or claim, they try to find out what happened or what is the truth.

words.ex: The detective gave an investigative report.
words.ex_cn: 侦探提交了一份调查报告。
words.en: Involving or relating to the investigation of something, especially in a thorough and systematic way.

words.ex: The investor gave money to the new business.
words.ex_cn: 这位投资者为这家新企业提供了资金。
words.en: An investor is a person or organization that puts money into financial schemes, property, etc. with the expectation of achieving a profit.

words.tr: v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃
words.ex: The fresh air invigorates me every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早晨的新鲜空气让我精神焕发。
words.en: If something invigorates you, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.tr: adj. 未受（或不容）侵犯的；未受（或不容）亵渎的
words.ex: The sacred site remains inviolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个神圣的遗址仍然不受侵犯。
words.en: If something is inviolate, it has not been or cannot be disturbed, harmed, or profaned.

words.tr: adj. 非自愿的；不由自主的；
words.ex: His hand moved in an involuntary way.
words.ex_cn: 他的手不自觉地动了一下。
words.en: If you make an involuntary movement or exclamation, you make it suddenly and without intending to because you are unable to control yourself.

words.ex: The project involves simple math and writing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目包括简单的数学和写作。
words.en: If a situation or activity involves something, that thing is a necessary part or consequence of it.

words.ex: His involvement in the project helped it succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他参与这个项目帮助它取得了成功。
words.en: The act of taking part in something or the state of being connected with something.

words.tr: adj. 不会受伤害的；攻不破的；固若金汤的
words.ex: The fortress was said to be invulnerable.
words.ex_cn: 这座要塞据说无懈可击。
words.en: If someone or something is invulnerable, they cannot be harmed or damaged.

words.ex: He is irascible when he wakes up late.
words.ex_cn: 他起床晚时容易发怒。
words.en: If you describe someone as irascible, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.ex: The irate customer shouted at the clerk.
words.ex_cn: 这位愤怒的顾客对店员大喊大叫。
words.en: If someone is irate, they are very angry about something.

words.tr: adj. 彩虹色的；色彩斑斓的
words.ex: The soap bubble is iridescent in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 肥皂泡在阳光下呈现出彩虹色。
words.en: Showing luminous colors that seem to change when seen from different angles.

words.ex: It's ironic that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: If you say that it is ironic that something happens, you mean that it is odd or amusing because it involves a contrast or is the opposite of what you would expect.

words.ex: It's an irony that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: Irony is a subtle form of humor which involves saying things that you do not mean.

words.tr: v. 照射；用放射线处理；使明亮
words.ex: The sun irradiates the earth every day.
words.ex_cn: 太阳每天照射地球。
words.en: To expose to radiation; to illuminate or enlighten.

words.tr: adj. 不能根除的；根深蒂固的
words.ex: The pain of loss is irradicable.
words.ex_cn: 失去的痛苦是无法根除的。
words.en: If something is irradicable, it is impossible to remove or destroy.

words.ex: His refusal to listen is irrational.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝倾听是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings and behavior as irrational, you mean they are not based on logical reasons or clear thinking.

words.tr: adj. 不能调和的；无法化解的；不兼容的
words.ex: Their views are irreconcilable.
words.ex_cn: 他们的观点无法调和。
words.en: If two things such as opinions or proposals are irreconcilable, they are so different from each other that it is not possible to believe or have both of them.

words.tr: adj. 不能赎回的；不能兑现的；不可救药的
words.ex: The bond is irredeemable and will never be paid back.
words.ex_cn: 这种债券是不能赎回的，永远不会被偿还。
words.en: If you describe something as irredeemable, you mean that it is so bad or undesirable that there is no way to improve it or make it acceptable.

words.tr: adj. 无可辩驳的；不能否认的
words.ex: The evidence is irrefutable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If you describe something such as evidence or a fact as irrefutable, you mean that it cannot be denied or disproved.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不相关的；
words.ex: His opinion is irrelevant to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见与这个决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as irrelevant, you mean that it is not important to or not connected with the present situation or discussion.

words.tr: adj. 不能修复的；不可弥补的；无可挽救的
words.ex: The damage was irreparable.
words.ex_cn: 损坏是无法修复的。
words.en: If something is irreparable, it cannot be repaired or corrected.

words.ex: Her irrepressible laugh filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 她抑制不住的笑声充满了房间。
words.en: If someone is irrepressible, they are full of energy and enthusiasm and cannot be controlled or stopped.

words.tr: adj. 无可指责的；无过失的
words.ex: Her behavior has always been irreproachable.
words.ex_cn: 她的行为一直无可指责。
words.en: If you say that someone's character or behaviour is irreproachable, you mean that they behave so well that they cannot be criticized.

words.tr: adj. 有极大诱惑力的；不可抵抗的；
words.ex: The chocolate cake looked irresistible.
words.ex_cn: 那块巧克力蛋糕看起来极具诱惑力。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as irresistible, you mean that they are so good or attractive that you cannot stop yourself from liking them or wanting them.

words.tr: adj. 无决断的；犹豫不决的
words.ex: He was irresolute about which job to accept.
words.ex_cn: 他对于接受哪份工作犹豫不决。
words.en: If someone is irresolute, they are uncertain about what to do or are unable to make decisions.

words.tr: adj. 不负责任的；无责任感的；
words.ex: He is irresponsible because he never pays his bills.
words.ex_cn: 他从不付账单，所以是不负责任的。
words.en: If you describe someone as irresponsible, you are criticizing them because they do things without properly considering their possible consequences.

words.tr: adj. 不敬的；不逊的；无礼的
words.ex: He made an irreverent joke about the king.
words.ex_cn: 他对国王开了一个不敬的玩笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as irreverent, you mean that they do not show respect for people or things that are generally respected.

words.ex: The damage to the environment is irreversible.
words.ex_cn: 对环境的破坏是不可逆转的。
words.en: If a change is irreversible, it cannot be changed back to how it was before.

words.tr: adj. 无法改变的；不能取消的
words.ex: The decision was irrevocable.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是不可撤销的。
words.en: If a decision, action, or process is irrevocable, it cannot be changed or reversed.

words.ex: Farmers irrigate their fields with water from the river.
words.ex_cn: 农民用河里的水灌溉他们的田地。
words.en: To supply land or crops with water by means of channels or pipes.

words.ex: He is irritable when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候容易烦躁。
words.en: If someone is irritable, they are easily annoyed.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.tr: adj. 惹人生气的； v. “irritate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The loud noise is irritating.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音很惹人生气。
words.en: If you describe something as irritating, you mean that it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

words.ex: He iterate the importance of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他反复说诚实的重要性。
words.en: To say or do something again or several times.

words.tr:
adj. 巡回的；流动的
n. 四处奔波的人；流浪者
words.ex: The itinerant worker moves from town to town for jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这位流动工人为了工作从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: Someone who is itinerant travels from place to place, usually because they have no permanent home or job, or because they are involved in a particular activity that requires this.

words.tr: adj. 精疲力竭的；腻烦的；无兴致的
words.ex: She felt jaded after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 工作了一整天后，她感到精疲力竭。
words.en: If you are jaded, you feel bored, tired, and not enthusiastic, especially because you have had too much of something.

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.tr:
n. 说笑；玩笑
v. 开玩笑
words.ex: He likes to jest with his friends during lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在午餐时和朋友开玩笑。
words.en: A jest is a remark that is intended to be amusing or funny, especially one that is made in a light-hearted or teasing manner.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；爱开玩笑的；滑稽的
words.ex: He is jocular during breaks, making everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他在休息时很幽默，让大家笑个不停。
words.en: If you say that someone has a jocular manner, you mean that they are cheerful and often make jokes or try to make people laugh.

words.tr:
n. 震动；震击
v. （使）颠簸摇晃；使震惊；“jolt”的现在分词
words.ex: The jolting motion of the bus made it difficult to sleep.
words.ex_cn: 公共汽车的颠簸让人难以入睡。
words.en: Causing a sudden shock or surprise; moving abruptly and forcefully.

words.tr: adj. 新闻业的；新闻工作（者）的
words.ex: He has a journalistic style of writing.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种新闻业的写作风格。
words.en: relating to the work of a journalist or to journalism

words.tr: adj. 欢腾的；欢欣鼓舞的
words.ex: The children were jubilant after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们赢了比赛后非常高兴。
words.en: If you are jubilant, you feel extremely happy because of a success.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.ex: At this juncture, we need to make a decision.
words.ex_cn: 在这一关键时刻，我们需要做出决定。
words.en: A particular point in events or time, especially one that is critical or decisive.

words.tr: adj. 可辩解的；可证明为正当的；有理的
words.ex: His action was justifiable because he protected his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为是合理的，因为他保护了他的朋友。
words.en: If something is justifiable, there is a good reason for it.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.tr:
adj. 青少年的；幼稚的；
n. 少年；
words.ex: The book is written for juvenile readers.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是为青少年读者撰写的。
words.en: A juvenile is a child or young person who is not yet old enough to be considered an adult.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；热心的；敏锐的；
words.ex: He is keen to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望学习英语。
words.en: If you are keen on doing something, you very much want to do it. If you are keen that something should happen, you very much want it to happen.

words.ex: He drank water to help his kidney work better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝水以帮助肾脏更好地工作。
words.en: One of the two organs in your lower back that separate waste products from your blood and make urine.

words.tr: n. 不适当的结合（尤婚配）
words.ex: The marriage was criticized as a misalliance.
words.ex_cn: 这桩婚姻被批评为不适当的结合。
words.en: A misalliance is a marriage or union that is considered unsuitable because the people involved are not well matched.

words.tr: n. 厌恶世人者；遁世者
words.ex: He is a misanthrope who avoids people.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个避世的人，不喜欢与人交往。
words.en: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes and avoids other people.

words.ex: He had a misapprehension about the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则有一个误解。
words.en: A misapprehension is a failure to understand something correctly, often leading to a mistaken belief or idea.

words.tr: adj. 调皮的；恶作剧的；有害的
words.ex: The mischievous boy laughed and hid his sister's shoes.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽皮的男孩笑着藏起了他姐姐的鞋子。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as mischievous, you mean that they enjoy playing tricks on people or doing things to annoy or embarrass them.

words.ex: He misconstrued her smile as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的微笑，以为是生气。
words.en: If you misconstrue something that has been said or something that happens, you interpret it wrongly.

words.tr: v. 指错方向；误导；使用不当
words.ex: The instructions were misdirected and led us to the wrong location.
words.ex_cn: 这些指示误导了我们，导致我们去了错误的地方。
words.en: To direct someone or something incorrectly or towards the wrong place or purpose.

words.ex: He felt miserable after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

words.ex: He felt deep misery after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的痛苦。
words.en: Misery is a state of great unhappiness and emotional distress.

words.tr: n. 误称…之名；不当之名
words.ex: Calling a tomato a vegetable is a misnomer.
words.ex_cn: 把番茄称为蔬菜是一种错误的称呼。
words.en: A misnomer is a name that is wrongly or unsuitably applied to someone or something.

words.ex: The play explores the theme of misogyny in modern society.
words.ex_cn: 这部剧探讨了现代社会中的厌女症主题。
words.en: Misogyny is the hatred of, contempt for, or prejudice against women or girls.

words.tr: n. 螨；小虫；极小量；小家伙
words.ex: A mite is very small and lives on animals.
words.ex_cn: 螨虫非常小，生活在动物身上。
words.en: A mite is a very small creature which is related to spiders. There are many different kinds of mites, some of which can cause diseases in plants, animals, and humans.

words.tr:
adj. 缓和的；减轻的
n. 缓和物
words.ex: The drug acts as a mitigant to the pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物作为缓解疼痛的因素。
words.en: A mitigant is something that serves to mitigate or alleviate.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.tr: adv. 适度地；不过分地；有节制地；
words.ex: He eats moderately to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他适度饮食以保持健康。
words.en: In a manner that is neither too much nor too little; to a moderate extent.

words.ex: The city plans to modernize its old subway system.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市计划现代化其老旧的地铁系统。
words.en: To modernize something means to change it so that it is more modern, for example by using more recent technology or methods.

words.tr: adj. 不多的；适度的；谦虚的；
words.ex: He made a modest profit last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年的利润不多。
words.en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

words.tr: adv. 谦虚地；谨慎地；适度地
words.ex: She modestly accepted the award.
words.ex_cn: 她谦虚地接受了奖项。
words.en: In a way that is not excessive or extreme; with modesty.

words.ex: The modifier controls the volume of the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 这个调节器控制扬声器的音量。
words.en: A modifier is a word or phrase that provides additional information about another word or phrase, often to make its meaning more specific.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He modulates his voice to sound calm.
words.ex_cn: 他调节自己的声音以显得平静。
words.en: To modulate means to change or adjust something, such as your voice or a piece of equipment, to achieve a desired effect or to make it suitable for a particular situation.

words.ex: She moistened the dry bread with water.
words.ex_cn: 她用水把干面包弄湿了。
words.en: To make something slightly wet.

words.tr: adj. 分子的；分子构成的；
words.ex: Water is a molecular compound.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种分子化合物。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of molecules.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.ex: The molten lava flowed down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 熔化的岩浆从山上流下。
words.en: Molten is used to describe substances that have been heated to a very high temperature and have turned into a liquid.

words.ex: He paused momentarily to catch his breath.
words.ex_cn: 他停了一下，喘口气。
words.en: For a very short time; immediately.

words.ex: The momentous decision changed his life.
words.ex_cn: 这个重要的决定改变了他的一生。
words.en: If you refer to a decision, event, or change as momentous, you mean that it is very important, often because of the effects that it will have in the future.

words.ex: The monetary policy affects prices.
words.ex_cn: 货币政策影响价格。
words.en: Monetary means relating to money, especially the total amount of money in a country.

words.tr: adj. 单色的； 单频的（光、辐射等）
words.ex: The painting is monochromatic, using only shades of blue.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是单色的，只使用了不同深浅的蓝色。
words.en: Consisting of one color or wavelength.

words.ex: The monolith stands alone in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 那座巨石独自矗立在沙漠中。
words.en: A monolith is a large, single upright block of stone, especially one shaped into or serving as a pillar or monument.

words.ex: The big company tries to monopolize the market.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司试图垄断市场。
words.en: If a company or person monopolizes something, they have complete control over it, so that other people cannot share it.

words.tr: n. 单调；枯燥；千篇一律
words.ex: He felt bored because of the monotony of his daily work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为日常工作的单调而感到无聊。
words.en: If you refer to the monotony of something, you are criticizing it because it is boring and has no variety.

words.ex: The project was a monumental task.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目是一项巨大的任务。
words.en: If you describe something as monumental, you are emphasizing that it is very large and impressive, or that it is of great importance or significance.

words.ex: His moralistic tone made the lecture boring.
words.ex_cn: 他那说教的语调让讲座变得无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone as moralistic, you are critical of them for making harsh judgments of other people's behavior based on their own beliefs about what is right and wrong.

words.ex: The government declared a moratorium on new construction.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布暂停新的建筑项目。
words.en: A moratorium is a temporary prohibition of an activity.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.tr:
adj. 尖刻的；刻薄的；尖锐讥讽的
n. 媒染剂
words.ex: His mordant wit made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的幽默让大家笑了。
words.en: A mordant remark is one that is critical and sarcastic. In chemistry, a mordant is a substance used to set dyes on fabrics or tissue sections by forming a coordination complex with the dye which then attaches to the fabric or tissue.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.ex: The mortality rate in the region increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年该地区的死亡率上升了。
words.en: Mortality refers to the state of being subject to death or the number of deaths in a particular population or period.

words.ex: He was mortified when he forgot his lines on stage.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记舞台上的台词时，他感到非常羞愧。
words.en: To mortify someone means to cause them to feel very embarrassed or ashamed. To mortify a part of your body means to discipline it by denying it things that it wants or needs.

words.ex: The motif of love appears in many poems.
words.ex_cn: 爱的主题出现在许多诗歌中。
words.en: A motif is a design or pattern that is used in a piece of art or music, or a theme that is repeated in a work of literature.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.tr:
adj. 杂色的；混杂的
n. 杂色；混杂
words.ex: The motley crowd cheered at the parade.
words.ex_cn: 这群杂乱的人群在游行中欢呼。
words.en: If you describe a group of things or people as motley, you mean that they are very different from each other and do not seem to belong together.

words.ex: He sang a mournful song at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他在葬礼上唱了一首悲伤的歌。
words.en: If you are mournful, you are very sad.

words.tr: n. 运动；动作；活动；乐章；
words.ex: The movement of the sun changes the shadow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的运动改变了影子。
words.en: The act or process of moving or being moved; a change of position or place.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使糊涂；胡乱应付
n. 混乱；糊涂
words.ex: He muddled the instructions and got confused.
words.ex_cn: 他把说明搞混了，感到困惑。
words.en: If you muddle things or people, you get them mixed up, so that you do not know which is which.

words.ex: A tree is a multicellular organism.
words.ex_cn: 树是一种多细胞生物。
words.en: Consisting of many cells.

words.ex: He is a multifaceted person who can sing, paint, and code.
words.ex_cn: 他是个多方面的人，会唱歌、绘画和编程。
words.en: Having many facets or aspects.

words.ex: The store offers multiple flavors of ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供多种口味的冰淇淋。
words.en: If something is multiple, it consists of or involves many things of the same kind.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.ex: His daily routine is mundane and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活平凡而无聊。
words.en: Something that is mundane is very ordinary and not at all interesting or unusual.

words.tr: n. 宽宏大量；慷慨给与
words.ex: Her munificence in donating to charity is well known.
words.ex_cn: 她对慈善机构的慷慨捐赠是众所周知的。
words.en: Munificence is the quality of being extremely generous.

words.tr: adj. 慷慨的；优厚的； 大方的
words.ex: He gave a munificent donation to the school.
words.ex_cn: 他向学校捐赠了一笔慷慨的款项。
words.en: If you describe someone as munificent, you mean that they are very generous, often in the form of giving money or gifts.

words.ex: The artist painted a colorful mural on the school wall.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家在学校墙上画了一幅色彩斑斓的壁画。
words.en: A mural is a large painting, typically executed directly on a wall.

words.ex: The murderous storm killed many people.
words.ex_cn: 这场致命的风暴夺去了许多人的生命。
words.en: If you describe an action or a way of behaving as murderous, you mean that it is very violent and intended to kill someone.

words.ex: The river water looked murky after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，河水看起来污浊。
words.en: If you describe something as murky, you mean that the details of it are not clear or that it is difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 可变的；易变的；性情不定的
words.ex: Her mood is as mutable as the weather.
words.ex_cn: 她的情绪就像天气一样多变。
words.en: Capable of or subject to change or alteration.

words.tr:
adj. 无数的；
n. 无数；
words.ex: There are myriad stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.tr:
adj. 神秘的；神秘主义的
n. 神秘主义者
words.ex: He saw a mystic light in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里看到一道神秘的光。
words.en: A mystic is a person who seeks by contemplation and self-surrender to obtain unity with or absorption into the Deity or the absolute, or who believes in the spiritual apprehension of truths that are beyond the intellect.

words.ex: The book delves into the mysticism of ancient religions.
words.ex_cn: 这本书深入探讨了古代宗教的神秘主义。
words.en: Mysticism is the belief that there is hidden meaning in life or that each human being can unite with God or the universe.

words.ex: The story is about a mythic hero who saves the world.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事讲述了一位神话般的英雄拯救世界。
words.en: Something that is mythic is based on or relates to myths or mythology.

words.ex: The baby eats navete with bread.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝吃萝卜配面包。
words.en: The quality or state of being naive; lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment.

words.tr:
n. 麻醉药；镇定剂；致幻毒品
adj. 麻醉的；催眠的
words.ex: He took a narcotic for his pain.
words.ex_cn: 他服了一种麻醉药来缓解疼痛。
words.en: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, relieves pain, and induces sleep. It can also refer to something that has a soothing or numbing effect.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.tr:
adj. 狭窄的；窄小的；
v. 使窄小；
words.ex: The road is narrow and hard to drive on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路很窄，开车很难。
words.en: If something narrows, or if you narrow it, it becomes less wide.

words.tr: adj. 整洁时髦的；设计精妙的
words.ex: He wears a natty suit to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天穿一件时髦的西装去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as natty, you mean that their clothes are smart and fashionable.

words.tr: adj. 自然主义的；写实主义的；
words.ex: The painting has a naturalistic style, showing trees and animals as they really look.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画具有自然主义风格，真实地描绘了树木和动物。
words.en: Naturalistic describes something that is made or done in a way that is very similar to nature.

words.tr: v. 导航；应付（复杂情况）；
words.ex: He uses a map to navigate the city.
words.ex_cn: 他用地图来导航这座城市。
words.en: To navigate is to plan and direct the route or course of a ship, aircraft, or other form of transport, especially by using instruments or maps.

words.tr: adj. 云雾状的；朦胧的；模糊的
words.ex: The nebulous cloud floated slowly across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 那团云雾状的云缓缓飘过天空。
words.en: If you describe something as nebulous, you mean that it is vague and not clearly defined or not easy to describe.

words.ex: He tries to negate the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图否认事实。
words.en: If someone negates something, they say that it does not exist or is not true.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；粗心的；不在意的
words.ex: He was negligent in doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做作业时很疏忽。
words.en: If you say that someone is negligent, you mean that they do not take enough care over something that they are responsible for.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.tr: adv. 可忽略不计地；微不足道地；极小地
words.ex: The difference in temperature is negligibly small.
words.ex_cn: 温度差异小得可以忽略不计。
words.en: In a manner or to a degree that is so small or unimportant as to be not worth considering.

words.tr: adj. 可协商的；可转让的；可通行的
words.ex: The price is negotiable.
words.ex_cn: 价格可以商量。
words.en: If you describe something as negotiable, you mean that it can be changed or agreed upon through discussion.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.ex: People in the Neolithic age used stone tools.
words.ex_cn: 新石器时代的人们使用石器。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the later part of the Stone Age, when ground or polished stone weapons and implements prevailed.

words.ex: The neutron has no electric charge.
words.ex_cn: 中子不带电荷。
words.en: A neutron is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of every atom except that of simple hydrogen. It has no electric charge and a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.

words.ex: The accident was newsworthy because many people were hurt.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故很有新闻价值，因为很多人受伤了。
words.en: If something is newsworthy, it is interesting enough to be reported as news.

words.tr:
v. 轻咬；啃；一点点地吃
n. 一小口；轻咬；少量
words.ex: The dog nibble the biscuit slowly.
words.ex_cn: 狗慢慢地轻咬着饼干。
words.en: To nibble means to take small bites of something, especially food.

words.ex: Owls are nocturnal animals.
words.ex_cn: 猫头鹰是夜间活动的动物。
words.en: Nocturnal means happening in the night or active at night.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；令人不愉快的
words.ex: The noisome smell made everyone leave the room.
words.ex_cn: 那股难闻的气味让所有人都离开了房间。
words.en: If you describe something as noisome, you mean that it is extremely unpleasant, especially because it has a very strong or bad smell.

words.ex: The nomadic family moves with their sheep every season.
words.ex_cn: 这个游牧家庭每季都随着羊群迁移。
words.en: A nomadic way of life is one in which people move from place to place instead of living in one place all the time.

words.tr: adv. 有名无实地；名义上地
words.ex: He is nominally the boss, but others make the decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他名义上是老板，但实际决策由别人做出。
words.en: If something is nominally true, it is true according to the name or title, but it may not really be true in fact.

words.tr: n. 漠不关心；无动于衷
words.ex: He showed nonchalance when the glass fell.
words.ex_cn: 当玻璃杯掉下来时，他表现得若无其事。
words.en: The state of being nonchalant; a casual lack of concern or indifference.

words.tr: adj. 若无其事的；不在乎的；冷淡的
words.ex: He was nonchalant about the test result.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试结果表现得漫不经心。
words.en: If you describe someone as nonchalant, you mean that they appear not to worry or care about things and that they seem very calm.

words.tr: adv. 漠不关心地；满不在乎地
words.ex: She tossed her hair nonchalantly and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 她冷淡地甩了甩头发，然后走开了。
words.en: If you behave nonchalantly, you are calm and relaxed, and you do not seem to care about anything or be worried about anything.

words.tr: adj. 态度暧昧的；不表态的；含糊的
words.ex: He gave a noncommittal answer when asked about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到计划时，他给出了一个模棱两可的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or attitude as noncommittal, you mean that they do not express their opinion or intentions clearly.

words.tr:
adj. 不信奉国教的；不墨守成规的；不随大流的
n. 不墨守成规者；（不信奉英国国教的）新教徒
words.ex: He is a nonconformist who does not attend church.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名不信奉国教的人，不去教堂。
words.en: A nonconformist is someone who does not conform to prevailing ideas or practices in their behavior or views.

words.tr: n. 无足轻重的人；不存在
words.ex: He felt like a nonentity in the big meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在大型会议上觉得自己毫无存在感。
words.en: A nonentity is someone who is not important or significant at all.

words.tr: adj. 不燃烧的；不易燃的
words.ex: The bottle is nonflammable.
words.ex_cn: 这个瓶子是不易燃的。
words.en: Not easily set on fire; not flammable.

words.tr:
adj. 不知所措的；陷于窘境的
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措；“nonplus”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He was nonplussed by the unexpected question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个意外的问题感到不知所措。
words.en: If you are nonplussed, you are so surprised and confused that you do not know what to say or do.

words.ex: The nonporous surface does not absorb water.
words.ex_cn: 这个无孔隙的表面不吸水。
words.en: Not allowing liquid or air to pass through; impermeable.

words.ex: The material is nonradioactive and safe for handling.
words.ex_cn: 这种材料是非放射性的，可以安全处理。
words.en: Not emitting or relating to the emission of ionizing radiation or particles.

words.tr: adj. 无意义的；荒谬的；胡说八道的
words.ex: His nonsensical story made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他那荒谬的故事让大家笑了。
words.en: If you say that something is nonsensical, you mean that it is silly or foolish.

words.ex: The teacher gave a nonthreatening smile to calm the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个无威胁的微笑来安抚学生。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as nonthreatening, you mean that it does not make you feel frightened or in danger.

words.tr: adj. 不能生长发育的；不可行的
words.ex: The embryo was deemed nonviable after the first trimester.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎在第一孕期后被认为不能存活。
words.en: If something is nonviable, it is not capable of succeeding or continuing, especially because it is not practical or it is too expensive.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.ex: The teacher asked students to annotate the text with notes.
words.ex_cn: 老师让学生们在文本上做注释。
words.en: To add notes or comments to a text or diagram, providing explanation or criticism.

words.tr:
n. V字形刻痕；等级；切口
v. 赢得；刻凹痕
words.ex: He made a notch on the stick to count days.
words.ex_cn: 他在木棍上刻了一个刻痕来计数天数。
words.en: A notch is a small cut or indentation in a surface. It can also refer to a level or degree in a scale or a narrow pass between mountains.

words.tr: n. 恶名；坏名声；声名狼藉
words.ex: The criminal gained notoriety for his bold robberies.
words.ex_cn: 这名罪犯因大胆的抢劫而声名狼藉。
words.en: Notoriety is the state of being famous or well known for something bad.

words.tr: adj. 声名狼藉的；臭名昭著的；
words.ex: He is a notorious thief who stole from many stores.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个声名狼藉的小偷，偷过许多商店。
words.en: Someone or something that is notorious is well known for something bad.

words.tr: adv. 臭名昭著地；众所周知地；
words.ex: He notoriously breaks the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他臭名昭著地违反规则。
words.en: used to emphasize that a particular quality, fact, etc. is very well known, especially when it is bad

words.ex: The toy store sells many novelty items for children.
words.ex_cn: 玩具店出售许多为儿童设计的新奇物品。
words.en: The quality of being new, original, or unusual; something new, original, or unusual.

words.ex: He is a novice at playing the guitar.
words.ex_cn: 他是个吉他新手。
words.en: A novice is someone who has just started learning or doing something and does not have much experience.

words.ex: He noticed the nuance in her voice.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了她声音中的细微差别。
words.en: A very slight difference in meaning, sound, color, or someone's feelings that is not usually very obvious.

words.ex: The nubile girl is just starting high school.
words.ex_cn: 这个年轻的女孩刚上高中。
words.en: A nubile person is someone, especially a young woman, who is sexually mature and therefore considered ready for marriage.

words.ex: The signature is null without a date.
words.ex_cn: 没有日期的签名是无效的。
words.en: Having no legal or binding force; completely void or invalid.

words.ex: There are numerous books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: If people or things are numerous, they exist or are present in large numbers.

words.tr:
n. 教养；养育；培育；
v. 培养；
words.ex: Her parents gave her good nurture.
words.ex_cn: 她的父母给了她良好的教养。
words.en: To nurture someone or something is to care for and encourage their growth or development.

words.ex: Vegetables are rich in nutrient.
words.ex_cn: 蔬菜富含营养物。
words.en: A nutrient is a substance that is essential for life and growth, such as the vitamins and minerals in food.

words.ex: This food has good nutritional value.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物有很好的营养价值。
words.en: Relating to the process of providing or obtaining the food necessary for health and growth.

words.ex: Eating fruits and vegetables is nutritious.
words.ex_cn: 吃水果和蔬菜是有营养的。
words.en: Nutritious food contains substances which help your body to be healthy.

words.tr: adj. 顽固的；执拗的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: He is obdurate and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他固执己见，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obdurate, you mean that they are determined not to change their mind or attitude in spite of efforts to persuade them.

words.ex: He is obese because he eats too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他因为吃太多垃圾食品而肥胖。
words.en: If someone is obese, they are extremely fat.

words.tr: v. （故意地）混淆；使混乱；使困惑
words.ex: He tries to obfuscate the truth with complicated words.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用复杂的词语混淆真相。
words.en: To obfuscate something means to deliberately make it unclear or difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 有义务的；有责任的； v. “obligate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: I am obligated to help my friend.
words.ex_cn: 我有义务帮助我的朋友。
words.en: If you feel obligated to do something, you feel that it is your duty to do it.

words.tr: adj. 强制性的；义务的；必须的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is obligatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制性的。
words.en: If something is obligatory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.ex: The law obliges parents to send their children to school.
words.ex_cn: 法律责成父母送孩子上学。
words.en: If you describe someone as obliging, you mean that they are willing and eager to be helpful.

words.ex: The architect had to consider the obliqueness of the roof when designing the building.
words.ex_cn: 建筑师在设计建筑物时必须考虑屋顶的斜度。
words.en: The quality or state of being oblique; deviation from a straight line or course; indirectness.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.tr: adj. 没注意到的；未觉察的；忘却的；
words.ex: He was oblivious to the noise around him.
words.ex_cn: 他对周围的噪音毫无察觉。
words.en: If you are oblivious to something or oblivious of it, you are not aware of it.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

words.ex: The artist lived in obscurity for most of his life.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家一生大部分时间都默默无闻。
words.en: The state of being unknown, inconspicuous, or unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 奉承的；逢迎的；谄媚的
words.ex: He was obsequious to his boss to get a promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他为了得到晋升，对老板阿谀奉承。
words.en: If you describe someone as obsequious, you are criticizing them because they are too eager to help or agree with someone more important than them.

words.ex: His obsequiousness made others feel uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他的谄媚让其他人感到不舒服。
words.en: Excessive eagerness to please or to obey all the wishes of someone in authority.

words.tr: adj. 观察力敏锐的；谨慎遵守的；
words.ex: She is observant and notices small details.
words.ex_cn: 她观察力敏锐，能注意到细小的细节。
words.en: Someone who is observant pays close attention to things and notices more about them than most people do.

words.tr: adj. 着迷的；（受…）困扰的； v. “obsess”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is obsessed with video games.
words.ex_cn: 他着迷于电子游戏。
words.en: If someone is obsessed with a person or thing, they keep thinking about them and find it difficult to think about anything else.

words.ex: The technology is becoming obsolescent as newer models are introduced.
words.ex_cn: 随着新模型的推出，这项技术正在变得过时。
words.en: Becoming obsolete or going out of use.

words.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
words.ex_cn: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstacle is something which makes it difficult for you to go forward or to achieve something.

words.ex: His obstinacy in refusing treatment led to his condition worsening.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝治疗的固执态度导致他的病情恶化。
words.en: The quality or state of being obstinate; stubbornness.

words.ex: His obstinateness made it hard to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他的固执使他很难改变主意。
words.en: The quality or state of being obstinate; stubbornness.

words.ex: The fallen tree obstructs the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树挡住了道路。
words.en: If something obstructs a road or path, it blocks it, stopping people or vehicles from getting past.

words.tr: adj. 能获得的；可得到的
words.ex: The prize is obtainable if you win the game.
words.ex_cn: 如果你赢了比赛，这个奖品就能得到。
words.en: If something is obtainable, it is possible to get it.

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.ex: It is obvious that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is obvious, it is easy to see or understand.

words.ex: He makes occasional visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他偶尔去看望祖父母。
words.en: Occasional means happening or done sometimes, but not regularly or often.

words.ex: The occupation of the city by foreign troops lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 外国军队对这座城市的占领持续了多年。
words.en: An occupation is a job or profession, or a way of spending your time.

words.tr: adj. 可憎的；讨厌的；令人作呕的
words.ex: The smell of the garbage was odious.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾的气味令人讨厌。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as odious, you think that they are extremely unpleasant, horrible, or disgusting.

words.tr: adj. 无臭的；没有气味的
words.ex: The water is odorless and clean.
words.ex_cn: 水没有气味，很干净。
words.en: Having no odor or smell.

words.tr:
adj. 即时的；未经准备的；唐突无礼的
adv. 即时地；未经思索地；随便地
words.ex: He gave an offhand answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个即时的回答。
words.en: If you say something offhand, you say it without checking the details or facts of it beforehand.

words.tr: adj. 爱发号施令的；多管闲事的
words.ex: The officious clerk refused to help unless I filled out another form.
words.ex_cn: 那位爱多管闲事的职员拒绝帮忙，除非我再填一份表格。
words.en: If you describe someone as officious, you are critical of them because they are eager to tell people what to do when you think they should not.

words.tr:
adj. 走调的
adv. 走调
words.ex: Her singing was off-key and distracting.
words.ex_cn: 她的歌声走音且令人分心。
words.en: Not in tune; discordant.

words.ex: The dogs had three offspring last spring.
words.ex_cn: 这些狗去年春天生了三只幼崽。
words.en: Someone's offspring are their children.

words.tr:
adj. 舞台后面的；后台的；台下的
adv. 舞台后面地；后台地；幕后地
words.ex: The actor waited offstage before his turn.
words.ex_cn: 演员在幕后等待上场。
words.en: Offstage refers to the area of a theater that is not visible to the audience, often used by performers and crew when not on stage.

words.tr: n. 寡头政治集团成员
words.ex: The oligarch owns many big companies.
words.ex_cn: 这位寡头拥有许多大公司。
words.en: An oligarch is a very rich business leader with a great deal of political influence, especially in Russia.

words.ex: The dark clouds looked ominous before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨来临前，乌云显得不祥。
words.en: If you describe something as ominous, you mean that it worries you because it makes you think that something unpleasant is going to happen.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；无所不能的
words.ex: The god is omnipotent.
words.ex_cn: 这个神是无所不能的。
words.en: Having unlimited power, able to do anything.

words.ex: The onerous workload made her tired every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量让她每天都很累。
words.en: If you describe a task as onerous, you dislike having to do it because you find it difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: The project is ongoing.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目正在进行中。
words.en: An ongoing situation has been happening for quite a long time and seems likely to continue for some time in the future.

words.ex: The glass has opacity so we cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这玻璃不透明，所以我们看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: Opacity refers to the quality of being difficult to see through or understand, often due to a lack of transparency or clarity.

words.ex: The sea looks opalescent at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 夕阳下，大海呈现出虹彩光泽。
words.en: An opalescent object or color appears to change in different lights, showing soft, shimmering colors like those of an opal.

words.tr: adj. 可操作的；可以动手术的；切实可行的
words.ex: The machine is operable after the repair.
words.ex_cn: 维修后，这台机器可以运行了。
words.en: Capable of being operated or dealt with in a particular way.

words.tr:
adj. 起作用的；运作中的
n. 技工；密探；特工
words.ex: The operative plan is to start tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 实施的计划是明天开始。
words.en: An operative system or plan is one that is in use or being used. An operative is someone who works for a government agency or a private company, often doing secret or confidential work.

words.tr: adj. 固执己见的；顽固的
words.ex: He is opinionated and never changes his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很有主见，从不改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as opinionated, you mean that they have very strong opinions and refuse to accept that they may be wrong.

words.ex: He defeated his opponent in the chess game.
words.ex_cn: 他在国际象棋比赛中击败了对手。
words.en: An opponent is someone who is competing against you in a contest, game, or argument, or someone who is opposed to an idea or plan.

words.ex: We arrived at the opportune moment, just as the meeting was starting.
words.ex_cn: 我们到达得很及时，正好会议刚开始。
words.en: If something happens at an opportune time or is opportune, it happens at the time that is most convenient for someone or most likely to lead to success.

words.tr: adj. 反对的；敌对的； v. 反对；反抗；“oppose”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was opposed to the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这个新规定。
words.en: If you are opposed to something, you disagree with it or disapprove of it.

words.tr:
n. 反面；对立面；
adj. 对面的；
prep. 与…相对；
words.ex: The opposite of black is white.
words.ex_cn: 黑色的反面是白色。
words.en: If one thing is opposite another, it is on the other side of a space from it.

words.tr: adj. 压迫的；沉重的；难以忍受的；闷热的
words.ex: The oppressive heat made it hard to breathe.
words.ex_cn: 令人窒息的炎热让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a society, its laws, or customs as oppressive, you think they treat people in an unfair and cruel way and prevent them from having opportunities and freedom.

words.tr: adj. 侮辱的；辱骂的；鄙俗的
words.ex: He shouted opprobrious words at the driver.
words.ex_cn: 他向司机喊出辱骂的话。
words.en: Expressing scorn or criticism; conveying disgrace or shame.

words.ex: He uses optical lenses to see small objects.
words.ex_cn: 他使用光学镜片来看小物体。
words.en: Relating to sight, especially in relation to the physical action of light.

words.ex: This is the optimal time to plant flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这是种植花卉的最佳时间。
words.en: Most favorable or desirable; best.

words.tr: n. 乐观；乐观主义；乐观精神；
words.ex: His optimism helps him stay happy even when things are hard.
words.ex_cn: 他的乐观让他即使在困难时也能保持快乐。
words.en: Optimism is a feeling of hopefulness and confidence about the future or the success of something.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.ex: He is optimistic about the future.
words.ex_cn: 他对未来持乐观态度。
words.en: Someone who is optimistic is hopeful about the future or the success of something in particular.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.ex: The palace had opulent carpets and golden chandeliers.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿里有华丽的地毯和金色的吊灯。
words.en: Having or displaying great wealth or richness.

words.ex: The satellite moves in an orbital path around Earth.
words.ex_cn: 卫星在围绕地球的轨道上运行。
words.en: Relating to an orbit or orbits.

words.tr: v. 改编为管弦乐；策划；精心安排
words.ex: He orchestrated the folk song for a symphony orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他将这首民歌改编为管弦乐。
words.en: To orchestrate something means to organize or arrange it in a very detailed and carefully planned way, especially in order to achieve a particular effect or result.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.tr: adj. 普通的；平常的；一般的；
words.ex: He wore an ordinary shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件普通的衬衫去学校。
words.en: Something that is ordinary is not special or different in any way.

words.tr: n. 生物体；有机体；有机组织；
words.ex: A bacterium is a simple organism.
words.ex_cn: 细菌是一种简单的生物体。
words.en: An organism is a living thing that has an organized structure, can react to stimuli, reproduce, grow, adapt, and maintain homeostasis.

words.tr:
adj. 原来的；有创造性的；原版的；新颖的；
n. 原件；原稿；
words.ex: This is the original book I bought last year.
words.ex_cn: 这是我去年买的那本原版书。
words.en: An original piece of writing or music was written recently and has not been published or performed before.

words.ex: The garden has ornamental flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有装饰性的花卉。
words.en: Something that is ornamental is intended to be attractive and is not necessary or useful.

words.ex: The old rules have ossified over time.
words.ex_cn: 这些旧规则随着时间的推移变得僵化了。
words.en: To ossify means to change or develop into bone, or to become fixed and unable to change or develop.

words.ex: He wore gold chains as a show of ostentation.
words.ex_cn: 他戴金链子是为了炫耀。
words.en: Ostentation is the act of showing off your wealth, possessions, or abilities in a way that is meant to impress others.

words.tr: adj. 炫耀的；浮华的；卖弄的
words.ex: He wore an ostentatious gold watch to show off his wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一块华丽的金表来炫耀他的财富。
words.en: If you describe something as ostentatious, you disapprove of it because it is expensive and is intended to impress people.

words.ex: They ostracize him for being different.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他与众不同而排斥他。
words.en: To ostracize someone means to exclude them from a society or group.

words.ex: The team will oust the coach after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 球队在输球后将撤换教练。
words.en: If someone is ousted from a position of power, job, or place, they are forced to leave it.

words.ex: He had an outburst when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时大发雷霆。
words.en: An outburst is a sudden release of strong emotion, often in a way that is unexpected or uncontrolled.

words.ex: This phone is outdated and doesn't work well.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机过时了，用起来不好。
words.en: If you describe something as outdated, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.tr: adj. 外向的；即将离职的；往外去的；
words.ex: He is an outgoing boy who loves talking to new people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的男孩，喜欢和新朋友聊天。
words.en: Someone who is outgoing is very friendly and likes meeting and talking to people.

words.ex: The child outgrew his shoes in one year.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子一年内就长高了，鞋子都穿不下了。
words.en: If you outgrow a particular way of behaving or thinking, you change and become more mature, so that you no longer behave or think in that way.

words.tr: n. 长出物；副产物；自然发展（或结果）
words.ex: The new park is an outgrowth of the community's love for nature.
words.ex_cn: 这个新公园是社区热爱自然的产物。
words.en: An outgrowth is something that develops naturally from something else, often as a result of it.

words.ex: He will outlast his rivals in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他将在比赛中胜过他的对手。
words.en: To continue to exist or be effective for a longer time than someone or something else.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；纲要；
v. 描画轮廓；概述；
words.ex: The artist drew the outline of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家画出了山的轮廓。
words.en: An outline is a line that shows or forms the outer edge of something, or a general description or plan showing the essential features of something but not the detail.

words.tr: adj. 边远的；偏远的；远离市镇的
words.ex: The outlying village has no bus service.
words.ex_cn: 这个偏远的村庄没有公交车服务。
words.en: Situated far from a center or main area.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；老式的； v. “outmode”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This phone is outmoded and needs to be replaced.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，需要更换。
words.en: If you describe something as outmoded, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.tr: adj. 直言无讳的；坦率的；
words.ex: He is an outspoken teacher who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位直言不讳的老师，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is outspoken expresses their opinions frankly and honestly, even if they are likely to shock or offend people.

words.ex: The new car outstrips the old one in speed.
words.ex_cn: 这辆新车在速度上超过了旧车。
words.en: To outstrip means to go faster or to do better than someone or something else.

words.ex: The benefits outweigh the risks.
words.ex_cn: 好处超过了风险。
words.en: If one thing outweighs another, the first thing is of greater importance, benefit, or significance than the second thing.

words.ex: The table has an oval shape.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是椭圆形的。
words.en: An oval is a shape that is like a circle but is longer in one direction than the other.

words.ex: The teacher overawed the students with her strict rules.
words.ex_cn: 老师用严格的规则震慑了学生。
words.en: If you are overawed by someone or something, you are so impressed or frightened by them that you feel nervous and unable to think or behave normally.

words.ex: The heavy bag overbalanced the chair.
words.ex_cn: 沉重的包使椅子失去了平衡。
words.en: To cause to lose balance or to be more than equal in weight, force, or importance.

words.ex: He overbear his little brother every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天压制他的弟弟。
words.en: To overbear means to dominate or overwhelm someone or something, often through the use of authority or physical strength.

words.tr: adj. 夸张的； v. “overblow”的过去分词；
words.ex: The news report was overblown and not true.
words.ex_cn: 这条新闻报道太过夸张，不真实。
words.en: If you describe something as overblown, you mean that it is given more importance or is more elaborate than necessary.

words.ex: The sky is overcast today.
words.ex_cn: 今天天空多云。
words.en: If the sky or the day is overcast, it is covered with cloud; dull and not sunny.

words.tr: adj. 过分自信的；自负的
words.ex: He is overconfident about passing the test.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己通过考试过于自信。
words.en: If someone is overconfident, they are too confident in their abilities or opinions and so they sometimes make mistakes or cause problems because they do not think enough about what they are doing.

words.ex: The bus was overcrowd with passengers.
words.ex_cn: 这辆公交车挤满了乘客。
words.en: To fill a space with more people or things than is comfortable or safe.

words.tr: v. 透支；过度往后拉；过分描述
words.ex: He overdraws his bank account every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都透支银行账户。
words.en: To overdraw means to withdraw more money from a bank account than the account holds, resulting in a negative balance. It can also mean to exaggerate or embellish in description or representation.

words.ex: The book is overdue at the library.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在图书馆逾期了。
words.en: If you say that a change or an event is overdue, you mean that you think it should have happened before now.

words.tr: v. 过分强调；过分着重
words.ex: He overemphasizes grades too much.
words.ex_cn: 他过于强调成绩。
words.en: To give too much emphasis to something; to stress something more than is necessary or appropriate.

words.ex: He overestimated his ability to finish the task in one day.
words.ex_cn: 他过高估计了自己一天内完成任务的能力。
words.en: If you overestimate something, you think it is greater in amount or more important than it really is.

words.ex: The balloon is overinflated and will burst.
words.ex_cn: 气球充气过足，会爆掉。
words.en: If something is overinflated, it is excessively expanded or exaggerated, often beyond a reasonable or desirable level.

words.tr:
v. 交叠；使部分重叠；
n. 重叠部分；
words.ex: The two colors overlap on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 两种颜色在墙上交叠。
words.en: If one thing overlaps another, or if you overlap them, a part of the first thing occupies the same area as a part of the other thing. You can also say that two things overlap.

words.ex: The truck suffered an overload and broke down.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车因超载而抛锚了。
words.en: To load or burden someone or something excessively.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.tr: v. 制服；压倒；令人折服；使难以忍受
words.ex: The police officer overpowered the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察制服了小偷。
words.en: If you overpower someone, you defeat them because you are stronger than they are.

words.tr:
adj. 压倒性的；强烈的；使人无法忍受的
v. 制服；压倒；令人折服；使难以忍受；“overpower”的现在分词
words.ex: The smell of flowers was overpowering.
words.ex_cn: 花的气味非常强烈。
words.en: An overpowering feeling or smell is so strong that you cannot resist it.

words.ex: Don't overrate his skills; he is not that good.
words.ex_cn: 不要高估他的能力；他没那么好。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is overrated, you mean that people consider them to be better or more important than they really are.

words.ex: The boss can override the rules if needed.
words.ex_cn: 如果需要，老板可以凌驾于规则之上。
words.en: If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.

words.ex: The judge will overrule the objection.
words.ex_cn: 法官将驳回这个异议。
words.en: If someone in authority overrules a decision or order, they officially decide that it is wrong and change it.

words.ex: His talent overshadowed his brother's achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华使他兄弟的成就黯然失色。
words.en: If an unpleasant event or feeling overshadows something, it makes it less happy or enjoyable.

words.ex: He overstates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸大自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you say that someone is overstating something, you mean they are describing it in a way that makes it seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

words.tr: v. 课税过重；负担过度；使工作过度
words.ex: The high taxes overtax the poor families.
words.ex_cn: 高额税收压垮了贫困家庭。
words.en: To impose too much tax on someone or something, or to make excessive demands on someone's strength or resources.

words.tr: adj. 累过头的，过度疲劳的
words.ex: He is overtired from working all night.
words.ex_cn: 他因为通宵工作而极度疲劳。
words.en: Exhausted from too much work or lack of sleep.

words.tr:
v. 推翻；颠覆；打倒
n. 推翻；颠覆；打倒
words.ex: The court will overturn the old law.
words.ex_cn: 法院将推翻这项旧法律。
words.en: If a decision, result, etc. is overturned, it is officially changed so that it becomes the opposite of what it was before.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.tr: adj. 过分劳累的；过度兴奋的；过分紧张的
words.ex: He felt overwrought after working 16 hours straight.
words.ex_cn: 他连续工作了16个小时，感到精疲力尽。
words.en: If someone is overwrought, they are very upset and are not thinking or behaving calmly or sensibly.

words.tr:
n. 和平主义者；反战主义者
adj. 非战主义的
words.ex: He is a pacifist and refuses to fight in wars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名和平主义者，拒绝参与战争。
words.en: A pacifist is someone who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable and that disputes should be settled by peaceful means.

words.tr:
v. 包装；收拾行李；
n. 包裹；小包；
words.ex: She packs the gift in colorful paper.
words.ex_cn: 她用彩纸包装礼物。
words.en: A pack is a container of a particular kind, especially one made of strong paper or plastic and containing a number of the same items. As a verb, pack means to put something into a container, especially in a neat and efficient way.

words.tr: adj. 充满...的；挤满人的；拥挤的； v. 包装；“pack”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The bus was packed with people.
words.ex_cn: 公交车上挤满了人。
words.en: Filled with a large number of people or things.

words.ex: The choir sang a paean of praise for the retiring principal.
words.ex_cn: 合唱团为即将退休的校长唱了一首赞歌。
words.en: A paean is a song of praise, joy, or triumph.

words.ex: He painstakingly checked every answer before submitting the test.
words.ex_cn: 他在提交试卷前极其仔细地检查了每一个答案。
words.en: With great care and thoroughness.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.ex: Paleolithic people used stone tools.
words.ex_cn: 旧石器时代的人使用石器。
words.en: The Paleolithic period is the earliest part of the Stone Age, preceding the Mesolithic and Neolithic periods.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: He gave a paltry amount of money to charity.
words.ex_cn: 他捐给慈善机构的钱微不足道。
words.en: If you describe an amount of money as paltry, you mean that it is very small.

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.ex: The pancreas makes insulin to control blood sugar.
words.ex_cn: 胰腺分泌胰岛素来控制血糖。
words.en: The pancreas is a large gland behind the stomach which secretes digestive enzymes into the duodenum. Embedded in the pancreas are the islets of Langerhans, which secrete into the blood the hormones insulin and glucagon.

words.tr:
n. 哑剧；（英）圣诞童话剧
v. 打手势；演哑剧
words.ex: The children laughed at the clown's pantomime.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们笑了，因为小丑的哑剧表演。
words.en: Pantomime is a type of entertainment where performers express a story or represent characters through gestures and body movements without using speech.

words.ex: The parable of the Good Samaritan teaches compassion and kindness.
words.ex_cn: 好撒玛利亚人的寓言教导了同情和善良。
words.en: A simple story used to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson, as told by Jesus in the Gospels.

words.ex: This experiment is a paradigm of scientific method.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验是科学方法的范例。
words.en: A paradigm is a model or pattern that is considered to be a typical example of something.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

words.ex: It is paradoxical that he sleeps all day but stays awake at night.
words.ex_cn: 他白天睡觉却晚上醒着，这很矛盾。
words.en: If something is paradoxical, it involves two facts or qualities which seem to contradict each other.

words.tr: adj. （男性）家长制的；族长制的；父权制的
words.ex: He lives in a patriarchal family where the father makes all the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他生活在一个父亲做所有决定的父权家庭中。
words.en: Relating to, characteristic of, or denoting a system of society or government controlled by men.

words.ex: The company received patronage from a local businessman.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司收到了一位本地商人的赞助。
words.en: The support, encouragement, privilege, or financial aid that an organization or individual bestows to another.

words.tr: v. 惠顾；资助；屈尊俯就
words.ex: He often patronizes the local bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他经常光顾这家本地面包店。
words.en: If someone patronizes you, they speak or behave towards you in a way which seems friendly, but which shows that they think they are superior to you in some way.

words.tr:
adj. 自以为高人一等的；屈尊俯就的
v. 惠顾；资助；屈尊俯就；“patronize”的现在分词
words.ex: He gave a patronizing smile when she asked a simple question.
words.ex_cn: 当她问了一个简单的问题时，他露出了居高临下的微笑。
words.en: If someone is patronizing, they speak or behave towards you in a way that seems friendly, but which shows that they think they are superior to you.

words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.ex: This town has a peculiar custom of dancing at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有一个独特的午夜跳舞习俗。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peculiar, you think that they are strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way.

words.ex: He lost his pecuniary support after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后失去了经济支持。
words.en: Pecuniary means relating to money, especially in terms of financial gain or loss.

words.tr: adj. 教育学的；教学法的
words.ex: The teacher used pedagogic methods to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师使用了教学法来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Pedagogic relates to the methods and theory of teaching.

words.tr: n. 迂腐之人；书呆子；学究
words.ex: He is a pedant who corrects every small mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑剔的书呆子，会纠正每一个小错误。
words.en: A pedant is a person who is excessively concerned with minor details and rules or with displaying academic learning.

words.tr: n. 迂腐；拘泥于形式；卖弄学问
words.ex: He corrects every small mistake, showing too much pedantry.
words.ex_cn: 他纠正每一个小错误，表现出太多的死抠细节。
words.en: Pedantry is behavior that is too concerned with formal rules and small details, especially in teaching or learning.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.tr: adj. 无可匹敌的；盖世无双的
words.ex: Her singing is peerless.
words.ex_cn: 她的歌唱无人能及。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peerless, you mean that they are better than any other person or thing of the same type.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；坏脾气的；乖戾的
words.ex: She had a peevish tone when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 她说话时带着一种易怒的语气。
words.en: If you describe someone as peevish, you mean that they are easily irritated by unimportant things.

words.tr:
adj. 贬损的；轻蔑的
n. 贬损语
words.ex: He used a pejorative word to describe his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个贬义词来描述他的邻居。
words.en: A pejorative word or expression is one that expresses criticism or disapproval.

words.ex: The penal system aims to punish criminals.
words.ex_cn: 刑罚制度旨在惩罚罪犯。
words.en: Relating to, used for, or prescribing the punishment of offenders under the legal system.

words.tr: v. 对…予以惩罚；使处于不利地位
words.ex: The teacher will penalize students who cheat.
words.ex_cn: 老师会惩罚作弊的学生。
words.en: To penalize someone means to punish them or make them suffer in some way because they have done something wrong.

words.ex: He has a penchant for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: A penchant is a strong liking or taste for something.

words.tr:
adj. 待定的；即将发生的
prep. 在等待…期间；直到…为止
words.ex: The decision is pending.
words.ex_cn: 决定尚未做出。
words.en: If something is pending, it has not yet happened or been decided, and is often waiting for something else to happen first.

words.tr:
adj. 敏锐的；尖锐的；穿透的；有洞察力的
v. 渗透；看穿；洞察；“penetrate”的现在分词
words.ex: His penetrating eyes saw the truth immediately.
words.ex_cn: 他敏锐的目光立刻看出了真相。
words.en: Able to make a way through or into something; showing an ability to understand things clearly and deeply.

words.tr:
adj. 忏悔的；悔过的
n. 忏悔者；悔罪者
words.ex: He sat in the church, a penitent man seeking forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在教堂里，一个忏悔的人寻求宽恕。
words.en: Feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong; repentant.

words.ex: The phone is expensive.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机很贵。
words.en: Costing a lot of money; having a high price.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.tr: adj. 极端或过分热情的
words.ex: His perfervid speech inspired the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他那热情洋溢的演讲激励了群众。
words.en: Having or showing intense and fervent feeling or enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背信弃义的
words.ex: The perfidious traitor betrayed his comrades.
words.ex_cn: 那个背信弃义的叛徒背叛了他的同伙。
words.en: If you describe someone as perfidious, you mean that they have betrayed someone or cannot be trusted.

words.ex: She bought a new perfume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一瓶新香水。
words.en: A perfume is a pleasant-smelling liquid which people put on their skin to make themselves smell nice.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
