words.en: If someone or something tantalizes you, they make you feel hopeful and excited about getting what you want, usually before disappointing you by not letting you have it.

words.tr: adj. 同等的；相等的；相当于
words.ex: Lying is tantamount to cheating.
words.ex_cn: 撒谎等于欺骗。
words.en: If you say that one thing is tantamount to a second, more serious thing, you are emphasizing how bad, unacceptable, or unfortunate the first thing is by comparing it to the second.

words.tr:
adj. 尖端细的；渐渐减少的
v. 逐渐变细；逐渐减少；“taper”的现在分词
words.ex: The path grew narrower as it tapering into the woods.
words.ex_cn: 小路逐渐变窄，延伸到树林中。
words.en: Becoming gradually narrower or thinner towards one end.

words.tr: adj. 迟的；缓慢的；迟缓的
words.ex: He is tardy for school every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上学都迟到。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tardy, you think that they are later than they should be or later than expected.

words.tr:
v. （使）失去光泽；使晦暗；玷污
n. 晦暗；污渍
words.ex: The silver spoon will tarnish if not cleaned.
words.ex_cn: 如果银勺不清洗，就会变暗。
words.en: If you say that something tarnishes someone's reputation or image, you mean that it causes people to have a worse opinion of them than they would otherwise have had.

words.tr: adj. 无味的；格调低的；粗俗的
words.ex: The soup is tasteless and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe something such as a remark, joke, or gesture as tasteless, you mean that it is offensive, usually because it involves sex or death and is inappropriate in the circumstances.

words.ex: He taunted his brother for losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他奚落弟弟比赛输了。
words.en: If someone taunts you, they say unkind or insulting things to you, especially about your weaknesses or failures.

words.tr: adj. 拉紧的；绷紧的；紧张的
words.ex: The sail was taut in the strong wind.
words.ex_cn: 帆在强风中绷得紧紧的。
words.en: If something such as a rope or wire is taut, it is stretched very tight. If muscles or parts of the body are taut, they are stretched tight, often because of physical effort or anxiety.

words.tr: adj. 俗丽而不值钱的；花里胡哨的
words.ex: She wore a tawdry dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿着一件俗丽的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as tawdry, you mean that it is showy and bright but of very poor quality.

words.tr:
adj. 繁重的；费力的；伤脑筋的
v. 对...征税；使负重荷；“tax”的现在分词
words.ex: The math test was taxing for the students.
words.ex_cn: 这次数学考试让学生们感到很吃力。
words.en: If you describe a task as taxing, you mean that it requires a lot of mental or physical effort.

words.ex: He learned a new technique to paint better.
words.ex_cn: 他学了一种新的绘画技术。
words.en: A technique is a particular method of doing an activity, usually a method that involves practical skills.

words.ex: The long meeting was tedious.
words.ex_cn: 这场漫长的会议很沉闷。
words.en: If you describe something such as a job, task, or situation as tedious, you mean it is boring and rather frustrating.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.ex: Our team won the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 我们的团队赢得了足球比赛。
words.en: A team is a group of people who play a particular sport or game together against other similar groups of people.

words.ex: He is a temperate person who never shouts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个温和的人，从不大喊大叫。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as temperate, you mean that it is calm and reasonable, not extreme or emotional.

words.ex: The temporal change of seasons affects our daily life.
words.ex_cn: 季节的时间变化影响我们的日常生活。
words.en: Relating to time as opposed to eternity; relating to worldly life as opposed to spiritual life.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.ex: He resisted the temptation to eat cake.
words.ex_cn: 他抵制了吃蛋糕的诱惑。
words.en: If you feel you want to do something or have something, even though you know you really should avoid it, you can refer to this feeling as temptation.

words.tr: adj. 吸引人的；诱人的； v. “tempt”的现在分词；
words.ex: The smell of fresh bread is very tempting.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜面包的香味非常诱人。
words.en: If something is tempting, it makes you feel that you want to have it or do it.

words.tr: adj. 说得过去的；站得住脚的；可防守的
words.ex: His excuse was a little weak, but still tenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口有点牵强，但还是说得过去的。
words.en: If an idea, argument, or plan is tenable, it is reasonable and could be successfully defended against criticism.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.ex: His tenacity helped him finish the marathon despite the pain.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚韧让他即使疼痛也完成了马拉松。
words.en: The quality or fact of being able to grip something firmly; the quality or fact of being very determined and not giving up easily.

words.tr: adj. 倾向性的；有偏见的；有争议的
words.ex: The media's tendentious reporting often misrepresents the truth.
words.ex_cn: 媒体的带有倾向性的报道常常歪曲事实。
words.en: If something is tendentious, it expresses a particular opinion or point of view very strongly, especially one that many people disagree with.

words.ex: Honesty is the main tenet of his life.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是他生活的宗旨。
words.en: A tenet is a principle or belief, especially one that is part of a larger system of beliefs.

words.tr: n. 紧张；紧张局势；紧张关系；
words.ex: There was tension between the two friends after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 两人争吵后，彼此之间出现了紧张。
words.en: Tension is a feeling of worry and anxiety which makes it difficult for you to relax. It can also refer to the state of being stretched tight or the degree of tightness of a stretched string, wire, etc.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.ex: He tentatively agreed to join the team.
words.ex_cn: 他试验性地同意加入团队。
words.en: If you do something tentatively, you do it without being confident or sure of what you are doing.

words.ex: Their agreement was tenuous and easily broken.
words.ex_cn: 他们的协议很脆弱，容易破裂。
words.en: If you describe something such as a connection, a reason, or someone's position as tenuous, you mean that it is very uncertain or weak.

words.tr: adj. 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
words.ex: He drank the tepid water slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他慢慢地喝着温吞的水。
words.en: Slightly warm; lukewarm. Also, showing little enthusiasm.

words.ex: The termite ate the wooden table.
words.ex_cn: 白蚁吃掉了木桌子。
words.en: A termite is a small, pale soft-bodied insect that lives in large colonies with several different castes, typically within a mound of cemented earth. Termites feed on wood and can cause extensive damage to buildings and other wooden structures.

words.ex: The terrestrial animals live on land.
words.ex_cn: 陆地动物生活在陆地上。
words.en: Of, on, or relating to the earth.

words.tr: adj. 令人害怕的；令人恐惧的； v. “terrify”的现在分词；
words.ex: The dark forest looked terrifying at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个黑暗的森林在晚上看起来令人害怕。
words.en: If you describe something as terrifying, you mean that it makes you feel extremely frightened.

words.ex: The two countries argued over territorial rights.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家就领土权利发生了争执。
words.en: Relating to the ownership of an area of land or sea.

words.tr: v. 恐吓；恫吓；实施恐怖统治
words.ex: The bully tries to terrorize the new student.
words.ex_cn: 这个霸凌者试图恐吓新学生。
words.en: To terrorize someone means to make them very frightened by using violence or threats.

words.ex: Her terse reply left no room for further discussion.
words.ex_cn: 她简洁的回答没有留下进一步讨论的余地。
words.en: A terse statement or comment is brief and to the point, often seeming rude or unfriendly because of its brevity.

words.ex: The texture of the bread is soft and fluffy.
words.ex_cn: 这种面包的质地柔软蓬松。
words.en: The feel, appearance, or consistency of a surface or a substance.

words.tr: adj. 有纹理的；质地粗糙的
words.ex: The wall has a textured surface.
words.ex_cn: 这面墙有纹理的表面。
words.en: Having a rough or uneven surface that can be felt by touch.

words.tr:
n. 茅草；茅草屋顶；盖住头顶的蓬乱头发
v. 用茅草覆盖屋顶
words.ex: The cottage has a thatch roof.
words.ex_cn: 小屋有一个茅草屋顶。
words.en: Thatch is a roof covering made of dry vegetation such as straw, water reed, sedge, rushes, or heather, layered so as to shed water away from the inner roof.

words.ex: The theatrical lighting made the stage look magical.
words.ex_cn: 剧场的灯光让舞台显得神奇。
words.en: Theatrical means relating to the theatre or to the performance of plays. It can also describe behaviour that is exaggerated and intended to attract attention.

words.ex: The movie has a thematic focus on friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的主题聚焦于友谊。
words.en: Relating to or constituting a theme or themes.

words.ex: He is learning theoretical physics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习理论物理。
words.en: A theoretical study or explanation is based on or uses the ideas and abstract principles of a subject, rather than the practical aspects or uses of it.

words.ex: The therapeutic massage helped her relax.
words.ex_cn: 这种治疗性的按摩帮助她放松了。
words.en: If something is therapeutic, it helps you to relax or to feel better about things, especially if you have been feeling worried or upset.

words.ex: He is receiving therapy for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受治疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Therapy is the treatment of someone with mental or physical illness without the use of drugs or operations.

words.ex: His thesis is that exercise improves memory.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是锻炼能改善记忆力。
words.en: A thesis is a long piece of writing based on your own ideas and research that you do as part of a university degree, especially a higher degree such as a PhD.

words.ex: The political issue is thorny and hard to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这个政治问题很棘手，难以解决。
words.en: A thorny problem or subject is difficult to deal with because it is complex and involves many different aspects.

words.ex: He gave a thoughtful answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个深思的答案。
words.en: If you are thoughtful, you are quiet and serious because you are thinking about something.

words.tr:
adj. 千倍的
adv. 成千倍
words.ex: Her happiness increased thousandfold after she found her lost dog.
words.ex_cn: 在找到她丢失的狗后，她的快乐增加了千倍。
words.en: To a thousand times as much or as many; multiplied by a thousand.

words.ex: The spider spun a threadlike web.
words.ex_cn: 蜘蛛织了一根细如线的网。
words.en: Resembling or characteristic of a thread in being long, thin, and flexible.

words.ex: The storm is a threat to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对村庄构成了威胁。
words.en: A threat is a statement of an intention to inflict pain, injury, damage, or other hostile action on someone in retribution for something done or not done.

words.ex: He threatened to call the police.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁要叫警察。
words.en: If someone threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

words.ex: She is thrifty and saves money every week.
words.ex_cn: 她很节约，每周都存钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is thrifty, you are praising them for saving money and not spending it on unnecessary things.

words.tr: v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；
words.ex: Plants thrive in sunny places.
words.ex_cn: 植物在阳光充足的地方茁壮成长。
words.en: To thrive means to grow or develop well or vigorously.

words.tr:
v. 阻挠；妨碍；挫败
n. 横坐板
words.ex: The rain thwarted our picnic plans.
words.ex_cn: 雨水破坏了我们的野餐计划。
words.en: If you thwart someone or thwart their plans, you prevent them from doing or getting what they want.

words.ex: Her room is always tidy.
words.ex_cn: 她的房间总是很整洁。
words.en: If you describe something as tidy, you mean that it is neat and arranged in an orderly way.

words.ex: He ties his shoelaces before running.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑步前系鞋带。
words.en: To fasten or secure with or as if with a cord, rope, or strap.

words.ex: Doing homework by hand is time-consuming.
words.ex_cn: 手写作业很耗时。
words.en: If you describe an activity as time-consuming, you mean that it takes a lot of time to do.

words.ex: The timeliness of the report was crucial to the success of the project.
words.ex_cn: 报告的及时性对项目的成功至关重要。
words.en: The quality or fact of being done or occurring at a favorable or useful time; opportune.

words.ex: He is timorous when speaking in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前说话时很胆怯。
words.en: If you describe someone as timorous, you mean that they are nervous and lack courage or confidence.

words.ex: The tined rake easily gathered the leaves.
words.ex_cn: 有齿的耙子轻松地收集了树叶。
words.en: Having prongs or points, as a fork.

words.ex: She tinted the glass blue.
words.ex_cn: 她把玻璃染成了蓝色。
words.en: A tint is a small amount of a particular color, especially when it is used to make the main color lighter or darker.

words.ex: The doctor examined the tissue under a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 医生在显微镜下检查了组织。
words.en: Tissue is a group of cells that have a similar structure and that work together to perform a specific function.

words.ex: The company made a titanic effort to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司做出了巨大的努力来按时完成项目。
words.en: If you describe something as titanic, you mean that it is very big or important, and usually that it involves very powerful forces.

words.tr: adj. 名义上的；有名无实的
words.ex: He is the titular head of the company.
words.ex_cn: 他是该公司的名义上的负责人。
words.en: Holding or constituting a purely formal position or title without any real authority.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；谄媚
n. 谄媚者；马屁精
words.ex: He was always the first to toady to the boss.
words.ex_cn: 他总是第一个拍老板马屁的人。
words.en: A toady is someone who flatters or ingratiates themselves with someone else in order to gain advantage.

words.tr:
adj. 有趾的；斜着钉进去的
v. 以趾踏触；用脚尖走；“toe”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The shoes were designed with extra padding around the toed area.
words.ex_cn: 这双鞋在脚趾区域设计了额外的衬垫。
words.en: Having toes or a toe; shaped like a toe.

words.ex: The map shows topographical details of the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图显示了山脉的地形细节。
words.en: Relating to the arrangement of the physical features of an area.

words.tr: v. 倾倒；摇摇欲坠；将…推翻；使…跌倒
words.ex: The strong wind toppled the old tree.
words.ex_cn: 大风把那棵老树吹倒了。
words.en: If someone or something topples, or if someone or something topples them, they become unsteady or unstable and fall over.

words.tr: adj. 迟缓的；呆钝的；不活泼的；蛰伏的
words.ex: The cat was torpid in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 猫在阳光下懒洋洋的。
words.en: If you are torpid, you are mentally or physically inactive, especially because you are feeling lazy or sleepy.

words.ex: The cold weather put the animal into torpor.
words.ex_cn: 寒冷的天气让动物陷入麻木状态。
words.en: a state of physical or mental inactivity; lethargy.

words.ex: The tortuous road wound through the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这条弯曲的道路蜿蜒穿过山脉。
words.en: If you describe something as tortuous, you mean that it is very long, complicated, and difficult to understand.

words.tr:
adj. 极权主义的
n. 极权主义者
words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A totalitarian political system is one in which there is only one political party which controls everything and does not allow any opposition parties.

words.tr:
n. 触摸；触觉；触感；
v. 触摸；接触；触动；
words.ex: The touch of her hand was gentle.
words.ex_cn: 她手的触摸很温柔。
words.en: If you touch something, you feel it with your hand, or come into physical contact with it.

words.tr: v. 触摸；接触；触动；“touch”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He touched the warm cup with his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手摸了摸温热的杯子。
words.en: If you are touched by something, it affects you emotionally, often making you feel grateful or sympathetic.

words.tr: v. 触摸；接触；“touch”的现在分词；
words.ex: The child is touching the soft blanket.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在触摸柔软的毯子。
words.en: If something is touching, it causes feelings of sadness or sympathy.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难以处理的；敏感的
words.ex: He is touchy about his weight.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己体重很敏感。
words.en: If you describe someone as touchy, you mean that they are easily upset, offended, or irritated.

words.tr: v. 兜售；招徕；吹捧；倒卖（高价票）
words.ex: He touts the new phone as the best on the market.
words.ex_cn: 他吹捧这款新手机是市场上最好的。
words.en: If someone touts something, they try to sell it or convince people that it is good, especially in an aggressive or exaggerated way.

words.tr: adj. 高耸的；杰出的；激烈的； v. “tower”的现在分词；
words.ex: The towering building stood above all others in the city.
words.ex_cn: 那座高耸的建筑矗立在城市中所有其他建筑之上。
words.en: Very tall or high; outstanding or extreme.

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

words.ex: The poison in the snake is a natural toxin.
words.ex_cn: 蛇的毒液是一种天然毒素。
words.en: A toxin is a poisonous substance, especially one produced by bacteria, which causes disease.

words.tr:
n. 痕迹；轨迹；微量；
v. 追踪；追溯；仔细查找；
words.ex: There was no trace of blood on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 地板上没有血迹。
words.en: If you trace something such as a pattern or a shape, you draw it carefully over a piece of thin paper. You can also trace someone or something that is missing or has disappeared, by following their movements or actions.

words.tr: adj. 可追踪的；可追溯的；
words.ex: The package is traceable using the tracking number.
words.ex_cn: 使用跟踪号码可以追踪这个包裹。
words.en: If something is traceable, it can be tracked or followed back to its source or origin.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

words.ex: The company has a famous trademark on its logo.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在其标志上有一个著名的标记。
words.en: A trademark is a recognizable sign, design, or expression which identifies products or services of a particular source from those of others.

words.tr: adj. 悲剧的；悲惨的；不幸的；
words.ex: The accident was a tragic event.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故是一场悲剧。
words.en: A tragic event or situation is extremely sad, usually because it involves death or suffering.

words.ex: Honesty is a good trait.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种好的特性。
words.en: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

words.ex: The cows trample the grass in the field.
words.ex_cn: 牛在田野里践踏草地。
words.en: If someone tramples something or tramples on it, they step heavily and carelessly on it and damage it.

words.tr: adj. 安静的；平静的；宁静的；
words.ex: The lake was tranquil in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨的湖面很安静。
words.en: If a place or situation is tranquil, it is calm, peaceful, and quiet, with no disturbance or agitation.

words.ex: She transcended her fears to speak on stage.
words.ex_cn: 她超越了自己的恐惧，在舞台上发言。
words.en: If something transcends normal limits or boundaries, it goes beyond them, because it is more significant than them.

words.tr: adj. 超越的；杰出的；卓越的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was transcendent.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是超凡的。
words.en: If you describe something as transcendent, you mean that it is extremely good or impressive, often in a way that goes beyond the ordinary.

words.ex: The transcontinental railway was a monumental engineering achievement.
words.ex_cn: 横贯大陆的铁路是一项伟大的工程成就。
words.en: Extending or going across a continent.

words.ex: The lab technician transcribes the DNA sequence into RNA.
words.ex_cn: 实验室技术员将DNA序列转录成RNA。
words.en: To transcribe something means to write it down or to copy it from one form of recording to another.

words.ex: He did the transcription of the meeting notes by hand.
words.ex_cn: 他手抄了会议记录。
words.en: The process of transcribing something, or a written or printed representation of this.

words.ex: Her skills are transferable to other jobs.
words.ex_cn: 她的技能可以转移到其他工作上。
words.en: If something is transferable, it can be moved or passed from one person, place, or situation to another.

words.ex: The new teacher transformed the class into a lively group.
words.ex_cn: 这位新老师把班级变成了一个充满活力的团体。
words.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and usually improve their appearance, form, or structure.

words.ex: The transformation of the old factory into a park made the city nicer.
words.ex_cn: 把旧工厂改造成公园让城市变得更美了。
words.en: A transformation is a complete change in the appearance, form, or nature of something or someone.

words.ex: He was punished for transgressing the law.
words.ex_cn: 他因违法而受到惩罚。
words.en: To transgress means to go beyond the limits of what is morally, socially, or legally acceptable.

words.ex: The joy was transient, like a brief smile.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是短暂的，像一个短暂的微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as transient, you mean that it lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: The transit of goods takes three days.
words.ex_cn: 货物的运输需要三天。
words.en: The act or process of passing through or across; the conveyance of people or goods from one place to another.

words.ex: This is a transitional phase between childhood and adulthood.
words.ex_cn: 这是从童年到成年的过渡阶段。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a process or period of transition.

words.ex: The transitoriness of joy is hard to accept.
words.ex_cn: 快乐的短暂性很难接受。
words.en: The quality or state of being transient or temporary.

words.ex: The joy was transitory, and soon he felt sad again.
words.ex_cn: 这种快乐是暂时的，不久他又感到悲伤了。
words.en: Something that is transitory lasts only for a short time.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.ex: The wizard can transmute lead into gold.
words.ex_cn: 巫师可以把铅变成金子。
words.en: To change something completely, especially into something different and better.

words.ex: The accident left him with a serious trauma on his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿受了严重的伤。
words.en: A trauma is a very distressing or disturbing experience.

words.ex: The treacherous road made driving very scary.
words.ex_cn: 这条危险的道路让驾驶非常可怕。
words.en: If you describe someone as treacherous, you mean that they are likely to betray you and cannot be trusted. If you say that something is treacherous, you mean that it is very dangerous and unpredictable.

words.tr:
v. 踩；踏；践踏
n. 脚步声；胎面
words.ex: He tread carefully on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you tread on something, you put your foot on it when you are walking. The tread of a tyre is the pattern of lines on its surface that prevent it from slipping.

words.ex: He wrote a treatise on ancient Chinese philosophy.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部关于中国古代哲学的专著。
words.en: A treatise is a formal and systematic written discourse on some subject, generally longer and more detailed than an essay.

words.tr: adj. 尖锐的；有力的；精辟的
words.ex: His trenchant criticism left no room for doubt.
words.ex_cn: 他尖锐的批评让人没有怀疑的余地。
words.en: If you say that someone's speech or writing is trenchant, you mean that it is very clear and effective, often in criticizing something.

words.ex: The trend shows more people are using electric cars.
words.ex_cn: 这个趋势表明越来越多的人在使用电动汽车。
words.en: A trend is a general development or change in a situation or in the way that people are behaving.

words.tr: n. 开创者；引领者；潮人
words.ex: She is a trendsetter in the fashion industry.
words.ex_cn: 她是时尚界的潮流引领者。
words.en: A trendsetter is someone who starts a new fashion or style that becomes popular.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.tr:
v. 非法侵入；侵扰；冒犯
n. 非法进入；冒犯
words.ex: He trespasses on private land.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自进入私人土地。
words.en: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without their permission.

words.ex: The tribal people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 部落的人住在森林里。
words.en: Tribal relates to a tribe or tribes.

words.ex: The tribulations of war left many families devastated.
words.ex_cn: 战争的苦难使许多家庭陷入了绝望。
words.en: A tribulation is a cause of great trouble or suffering.

words.ex: The small river flows into the main river as a tributary.
words.ex_cn: 这条小河作为支流汇入主河。
words.en: A tributary is a stream or river that flows into a larger stream or main stem (or parent) river or a lake. A tributary does not flow directly into a sea or ocean.

words.tr:
v. 滴流；慢慢移动
n. 细流；徐徐地流
words.ex: Water trickles down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 水从山上缓缓流下。
words.en: If a liquid trickles somewhere, it flows slowly in a thin stream.

words.ex: This puzzle is tricky for kids.
words.ex_cn: 这个谜题对孩子来说很棘手。
words.en: If you describe a task or problem as tricky, you mean that it is difficult to deal with and requires careful thinking or skill.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.ex: He watched the Harry Potter trilogy last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他上周末看了《哈利·波特》三部曲。
words.en: A trilogy is a series of three books, plays, or films that have the same subject or the same characters.

words.ex: His speech was full of trite phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了陈腐的表达。
words.en: If you say that something such as an idea, remark, or story is trite, you mean that it is dull and boring because it has been said or told too many times.

words.ex: The team celebrated their triumph after winning the match.
words.ex_cn: 球队在赢得比赛后庆祝了他们的胜利。
words.en: A triumph is a great success or achievement, often one that has been gained with a lot of skill or effort.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.tr: n. 停战（协定）；休战（协定）
words.ex: The two sides agreed to a truce.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意停火。
words.en: A truce is an agreement between enemies or opponents to stop fighting or arguing for a certain time.

words.ex: The truculence of the opponent's team was evident in their aggressive play.
words.ex_cn: 对手球队的好战性在他们激烈的比赛中显而易见。
words.en: The quality of being eager or quick to argue, fight, or start a conflict; aggressiveness.

words.tr: adj. 好战凶猛的；寻衅的；言词刻毒的
words.ex: He gave a truculent reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了好斗的答复。
words.en: If you say that someone is truculent, you mean that they are bad-tempered and aggressive.

words.ex: The software allows you to truncate long filenames.
words.ex_cn: 该软件允许你截断过长的文件名。
words.en: To shorten something by cutting off the top or the end.

words.ex: He is a trustworthy friend who always keeps his promises.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个值得信赖的朋友，总是信守承诺。
words.en: If you describe someone as trustworthy, you mean they are reliable, honest, and truthful.

words.tr: adj. 狂暴的；骚动的；动荡的；汹涌的
words.ex: The turbulent sea made the boat shake.
words.ex_cn: 汹涌的海让船摇晃。
words.en: A turbulent situation, time, or relationship is one in which there is a lot of change, confusion, and often conflict.

words.tr: n. 混乱；动荡；骚乱；恐慌
words.ex: The storm caused turmoil in the town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给小镇带来了混乱。
words.en: A state of great disturbance, confusion, or uncertainty.

words.tr:
n. 扭打；斗争
v. 扭打；打斗
words.ex: They had a tussle over the last piece of cake.
words.ex_cn: 他们为了最后一块蛋糕扭打起来。
words.en: A tussle is a rough physical struggle or fight.

words.tr: v. 作为…的典型；代表；象征
words.ex: He typifies a true leader.
words.ex_cn: 他代表了一位真正的领导者。
words.en: If something or someone typifies a situation or type of behavior, they have all the usual characteristics of it and are a typical example of it.

words.tr: adj. 排字上的；印刷上的
words.ex: The typo was a typographical error.
words.ex_cn: 这个拼写错误是一个排版错误。
words.en: Relating to the arrangement, appearance, or style of printed matter.

words.tr: adj. 暴虐的；压制的；残暴的
words.ex: The tyrannical king punished people for small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 这个暴虐的国王因为小错误惩罚人民。
words.en: Using power in a cruel and unfair way over people in a country or group.

words.ex: The tyrant ruled the country with fear.
words.ex_cn: 暴君用恐惧统治国家。
words.en: A tyrant is a ruler who has complete power in a country and uses it in a cruel and unfair way.

words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.ex: His ulterior motive was to get money.
words.ex_cn: 他别有用心，目的是弄到钱。
words.en: If you say that someone has an ulterior motive for doing something, you believe that they have a hidden reason for doing it.

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.ex: He worked hard, and ultimately succeeded.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作，最终成功了。
words.en: You use ultimately to indicate that something is the final result of a series of events or the most important part of a situation.

words.ex: He gave an ultimatum: leave now or stay forever.
words.ex_cn: 他发出最后通牒：现在走，或者永远留下。
words.en: An ultimatum is a final demand or statement of terms, the rejection of which will result in retaliation or a breakdown in relations.

words.ex: The doctor used ultrasonic waves to check the baby.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用超声波来检查婴儿。
words.en: Ultrasonic refers to sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper limit of human hearing.

words.ex: We sat under the umbrage of the big tree.
words.ex_cn: 我们坐在大树的树荫下。
words.en: A feeling of pique or resentment at some often fancied slight or insult.

words.tr: adj. 没有装饰的；不加渲染的；朴素的
words.ex: The room was unadorned, with no pictures or decorations.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间很朴素，没有图片或装饰。
words.en: If something is unadorned, it is plain and not decorated with anything.

words.tr: adj. 无美感的；缺乏美感的
words.ex: The building's design was criticized for being unaesthetic.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的设计因缺乏美感而受到批评。
words.en: If you describe something as unaesthetic, you think that it is not attractive or beautiful.

words.tr: adj. 不可更改的；无法改变的
words.ex: The laws of physics are unalterable.
words.ex_cn: 物理定律是不可改变的。
words.en: If something is unalterable, it cannot be changed.

words.ex: The rain was unavoidable during the storm.
words.ex_cn: 暴风雨期间，下雨是不可避免的。
words.en: If something is unavoidable, it cannot be avoided or prevented.

words.tr: adj. 不恰当的；不得体的；无吸引力的
words.ex: It is unbecoming to shout at teachers.
words.ex_cn: 对老师大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or remarks as unbecoming, you mean that they are shocking and unsuitable for that person.

words.ex: The judge gave an unbiased decision.
words.ex_cn: 法官作出了无偏见的判决。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unbiased, you mean they are fair and not likely to support one particular person or group involved in something.

words.tr: adj. 不能架桥的；不可逾越的；无法弥合的
words.ex: The gap between them was unbridgeable.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的鸿沟是无法跨越的。
words.en: If a gap or difference is unbridgeable, it is so large or so great that it cannot be bridged or made any smaller.

words.tr: adj. 无辔头的；不受控制的；放纵的
words.ex: The unbridled horse ran across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹无辔头的马在田野上奔跑。
words.en: If you describe behaviour or feelings as unbridled, you mean that they are not controlled or limited in any way.

words.tr: adj. 未破的；不间断的；未驯服的（马）
words.ex: The unbroken chain of events led to the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这一连串未被打断的事件导致了事故。
words.en: If something is unbroken, it is continuous or complete and has not been interrupted or damaged.

words.tr: adj. 神秘的；不可思议的；
words.ex: The uncanny silence in the forest made him nervous.
words.ex_cn: 森林里那神秘的寂静让他感到紧张。
words.en: If you describe something as uncanny, you mean that it is strange and difficult to explain.

words.ex: His uncharitable remark hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他那刻薄的话伤了她的心。
words.en: If you describe someone's remarks, thoughts, or behaviour as uncharitable, you mean they are unkind or unfair.

words.tr: adj. 图上没标明的；无人涉足的；未知的
words.ex: The explorers sailed into uncharted waters.
words.ex_cn: 探险家们驶入了未被探索的水域。
words.en: If you describe a situation, experience, or activity as uncharted, you mean that it is new and unfamiliar, and therefore difficult to predict or understand.

words.tr: adj. 不承担义务的；未表态的；未指定用途的
words.ex: She remained uncommitted to any political party.
words.ex_cn: 她没有加入任何政党。
words.en: If someone is uncommitted, they have not yet pledged or decided to support a particular person, group, or cause.

words.tr: adj. 不爱说话的；寡言少语的
words.ex: She was uncommunicative during the interview, providing only brief answers.
words.ex_cn: 她在面试中沉默寡言，只给出了简短的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncommunicative, you are critical of them because they do not talk to other people very much and are unwilling to express opinions or give information.

words.tr: adj. 不让步的；不妥协的；强硬的
words.ex: He is uncompromising about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他在诚实方面毫不妥协。
words.en: If you describe someone as uncompromising, you mean that they are determined not to change their opinions or aims in any way.

words.tr: adj. 未经证实的；未确证的
words.ex: The report is still unconfirmed by the authorities.
words.ex_cn: 这份报告尚未得到官方证实。
words.en: Not confirmed or verified.

words.tr: adj. 无意识的；无知觉的；
words.ex: He was unconscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他失去了意识。
words.en: If someone is unconscious, they are not awake, usually because they have had a severe injury or illness.

words.ex: The proposal was so uncontroversial that it passed unanimously.
words.ex_cn: 这个提议如此不会引起争论，以至于全票通过。
words.en: If something is uncontroversial, it is not likely to cause disagreement or argument.

words.ex: He remained unconvinced by the explanation.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个解释仍不信服。
words.en: If you are unconvinced, you are not sure that something is true or right.

words.tr: adj. 假情假义的；油腔滑调的
words.ex: His unctuous manner made me uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他油腔滑调的态度让我感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as unctuous, you are critical of them because they seem to be full of praise, kindness, or interest, but in a way that is not sincere.

words.tr: adj. 破译不出的；不可识别的
words.ex: The message was undecipherable due to the poor handwriting.
words.ex_cn: 由于字迹潦草，信息难以辨认。
words.en: If something is undecipherable, it cannot be understood or interpreted because it is written in a code or language that is not known or because it is too difficult to understand.

words.tr: adj. 要求不高的；不苛求的；不费力的
words.ex: She found the job surprisingly undemanding.
words.ex_cn: 她发现这份工作出乎意料地要求不高。
words.en: If you describe something as undemanding, you mean that it is not difficult or challenging, and is therefore easy to do or deal with.

words.tr: adj. 无法证明的，难以证明的；无法表明的
words.ex: The theory is undemonstrable with current scientific methods.
words.ex_cn: 这个理论用当前的科学方法无法证明。
words.en: Not able to be demonstrated or proven.

words.ex: The new policy undercut the company's profits.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策削弱了公司的利润。
words.en: To undercut means to sell something at a lower price than a competitor, or to weaken something or someone.

words.ex: The country has an underdeveloped economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经济不发达。
words.en: An underdeveloped country or region is one that is less developed economically and socially than most others, with many of its people living in poverty.

words.ex: He underestimated the difficulty of the test.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了考试的难度。
words.en: If you underestimate something, you do not realize how large, great, or serious it is.

words.tr: v. 低估；对…估计不足；“underestimate”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 被低估了的；
words.ex: They underestimated the difficulty of the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们低估了考试的难度。
words.en: To underestimate someone or something means to fail to understand how strong, skillful, intelligent, or important they really are.

words.tr:
adj. 地下的；
n. 地铁；地下；
adv. 在地下；
words.ex: The underground tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接了两座建筑。
words.en: Something that is underground is below the surface of the ground. It can also refer to secret activities or organizations.

words.tr: adj. 暗中的；卑劣的；人手不足的
words.ex: He was accused of using underhanded tactics to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控在选举中使用卑劣手段获胜。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as underhanded, you are criticizing them because they are secret and dishonest.

words.tr: v. 构成…的基础（或起因）
words.ex: Poor diet underlies many health problems.
words.ex_cn: 不良饮食是许多健康问题的根源。
words.en: If something underlies a situation or activity, it is the cause or basis of it.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；表演不充分
words.ex: He underplays his talent to avoid jealousy.
words.ex_cn: 他故意低估自己的才华，以避免引起嫉妒。
words.en: To represent something as being less important or significant than it really is.

words.ex: He underrates his own talent.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了自己的才华。
words.en: To underrate something or someone means to fail to recognize their true value or importance.

words.ex: Women are underrepresented in science jobs.
words.ex_cn: 女性在科学工作中人数不足。
words.en: If a group of people or things is underrepresented in a larger group, there are fewer of them in the larger group than there should be.

words.ex: The teacher underscored the importance of homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了作业的重要性。
words.en: To emphasize the importance of something or to draw a line underneath a word or phrase.

words.tr: v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说
words.ex: He understated the cost of the repair.
words.ex_cn: 他轻描淡写了维修的费用。
words.en: If you understate something, you describe it in a way that suggests it is less important or serious than it really is.

words.tr:
adj. 不夸张的；朴素的；简朴的
v. 轻描淡写；打折扣地说；少说；“understate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She wore an understated dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条低调的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as understated, you mean that it is simple and not exaggerated, often in a way that is elegant or effective.

words.ex: He will undertake a new project next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月将从事一个新项目。
words.en: To undertake a task or job means to start doing it and accept responsibility for it.

words.ex: The machine is underutilized because few people know how to use it.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器使用不足，因为很少有人知道如何操作它。
words.en: If something is underutilized, it is not being used as much as it could be.

words.tr:
adv. 在水下；
adj. 水下的；
words.ex: The divers swam underwater to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员在水下游泳以探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: Located, occurring, or used beneath the surface of the water.

words.ex: The charity helps those who are truly undeserving of their plight.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善机构帮助那些真正不配遭受困境的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as undeserving, you mean that they do not deserve to be treated in a particular way, especially with kindness or special attention.

words.tr: adj. 不合意的；不想要的；
words.ex: The weather is undesirable for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 这种天气不适合野餐。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as undesirable, you think they will have harmful effects or cause problems.

words.tr: adj. 无差别的；未分化的
words.ex: The cells look undifferentiated under the microscope.
words.ex_cn: 在显微镜下，这些细胞看起来没有分化。
words.en: Not having developed or specialized in form or function.

words.ex: The graph is undirected, so edges have no arrows.
words.ex_cn: 这个图是无向的，因此边没有箭头。
words.en: Not directed or guided; lacking direction or purpose.

words.ex: The explorer found an undiscovered island.
words.ex_cn: 探险家发现了一个未被发现的岛屿。
words.en: If something is undiscovered, it has not been discovered or found out.

words.ex: The image was clear and undistorted.
words.ex_cn: 图像清晰且未被扭曲。
words.en: If something is undistorted, it is not altered or misrepresented; it remains true to its original form or character.

words.ex: The cat slept undisturbed on the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 猫在沙发上安静地睡觉，没有被打扰。
words.en: If something is undisturbed, it is not touched, moved, or used by anyone.

words.ex: They unearthed an old coin in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他们在花园里挖出了一枚旧硬币。
words.en: To unearth something means to find it by digging in the ground or to discover something that was hidden or unknown.

words.ex: The use of plastic bags is unecological because they harm the environment.
words.ex_cn: 使用塑料袋对生态有害，因为它们会破坏环境。
words.en: Not ecological; harmful to the environment.

words.tr: adj. 未刊行的；未编辑的；未经审查的
words.ex: The raw footage remained unedited.
words.ex_cn: 原始素材仍未经过编辑。
words.en: If something is unedited, it has not been changed or corrected before being published or broadcast.

words.tr: adj. 不受妨碍的；没有负担的
words.ex: She felt unencumbered by the responsibilities of her former job.
words.ex_cn: 她感觉摆脱了以前工作中的责任负担。
words.en: If you are unencumbered by something, you are not burdened or hindered by it, allowing you to move or act freely.

words.tr: adj. 未受启蒙的；不知情的；不文明的；落后的
words.ex: He was unenlightened about the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as unenlightened, you mean they have not been given the necessary information or education about something, and so they do not understand it properly.

words.tr: adj. 毫不含糊的；清楚明白的
words.ex: His answer was unequivocal.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答是明确无误的。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude as unequivocal, you mean that it is completely clear and very firm.

words.ex: She unerringly picked the correct answer.
words.ex_cn: 她毫无差错地选择了正确答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's judgement or ability as unerring, you mean that they are always correct and never make mistakes.

words.tr: adj. 不平坦的；不均匀的；
words.ex: The road is uneven and hard to drive on.
words.ex_cn: 这条路不平坦，很难开车。
words.en: Something that is uneven is not regular, consistent, or equal.

words.tr: adj. 无重大事件的；太平无事的
words.ex: The trip was uneventful.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行很平静，没什么事发生。
words.en: If you describe a period of time as uneventful, you mean that nothing interesting, exciting, or important happened during it.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的
words.ex: Her performance was unexceptionable.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现无可挑剔。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unexceptionable, you mean that they are unlikely to be criticized or objected to, because they are very good, standard, or normal.

words.tr: adj. 无穷尽的；经久不衰的；永远可靠的
words.ex: Her unfailing smile made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 她永不消失的微笑让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone's good qualities or behaviour as unfailing, you mean that they never change.

words.ex: He showed unfeigned joy when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 当他赢得奖品时，他表现出真诚的喜悦。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or actions as unfeigned, you mean that they are genuine and not pretended.

words.tr: adj. 未施肥的；未受精的
words.ex: The unfertilized soil cannot grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 未施肥的土壤无法种植庄稼。
words.en: Not having been fertilized; not having had fertilizer applied.

words.tr: adj. 无拘束的；无牵挂的
words.ex: She felt an overwhelming sense of unfettered freedom.
words.ex_cn: 她感到一种无拘无束的自由感。
words.en: If you describe something as unfettered, you mean that it is not controlled or limited by anyone or anything.

words.ex: His fear is unfounded.
words.ex_cn: 他的恐惧是没有根据的。
words.en: If you describe a rumour, belief, or feeling as unfounded, you mean that it is wrong because it is not based on facts or evidence.

words.ex: The ungainly boy tripped over his own feet.
words.ex_cn: 这个笨拙的男孩被自己的脚绊倒了。
words.en: If you describe a person, animal, or vehicle as ungainly, you mean that they look awkward or clumsy, often because they are big.

words.tr: adj. 不领情的；忘恩负义的
words.ex: He was ungrateful for the gift.
words.ex_cn: 他对这份礼物毫不感激。
words.en: If you describe someone as ungrateful, you are criticizing them for not showing thanks or for being unkind to someone who has helped them or done them a favour.

words.ex: He was an unheralded artist who painted quietly for years.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位被埋没的艺术家，多年来默默作画。
words.en: If something is unheralded, it happens without any warning or without being announced in advance.

words.tr: adj. 线性的；一维的；一度空间的
words.ex: The line is unidimensional.
words.ex_cn: 这条线是一维的。
words.en: Involving or having only one dimension.

words.tr:
adj. 一致的；统一的；
n. 制服；
words.ex: The students wear a uniform shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们穿一致的衬衫去学校。
words.en: A uniform is a special set of clothes which some people, for example soldiers or the police, wear to work in and which some children wear at school. It is also used to describe something that is the same in all parts and does not vary.

words.tr: v. （使）统一；（使）联合；（使）成一体；
words.ex: The two teams decided to unify their efforts.
words.ex_cn: 这两个团队决定统一他们的努力。
words.en: To unify means to make or become united, uniform, or whole.

words.tr: adj. 没有激情的；不感情用事的；平静的
words.ex: Her unimpassioned response indicated a lack of interest.
words.ex_cn: 她不动感情的回应表明了缺乏兴趣。
words.en: Not showing or feeling strong emotion; calm and rational.

words.tr: adj. 无懈可击的；无可指责的；可靠的
words.ex: His unimpeachable honesty earned everyone's trust.
words.ex_cn: 他无可挑剔的诚实赢得了每个人的信任。
words.en: If you describe someone as unimpeachable, you mean that they are completely honest and reliable.

words.tr: adj. 印象平平的；无深刻印象的；不以为然的
words.ex: She remained unimpressed by his extravagant displays of wealth.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的奢华炫富行为无动于衷。
words.en: If you are unimpressed by something or someone, you do not think they are very good, interesting, or important.

words.tr: adj. 外行的；不谙此道的；
words.ex: The uninitiated found the technical terms hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 外行觉得这些术语很难理解。
words.en: If you describe someone as uninitiated, you mean that they have no special knowledge or experience of a particular subject or activity.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏创造力的；单调乏味的
words.ex: The movie was uninspired and lacked originality.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影缺乏灵感，毫无新意。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as uninspired, you mean they have no exciting qualities or features.

words.tr: adj. 难以理解的；难懂的
words.ex: The handwriting was unintelligible.
words.ex_cn: 字迹无法辨认。
words.en: If speech or writing is unintelligible, it is impossible to understand.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: This rule is universal for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则对所有学生都是普遍适用的。
words.en: Something that is universal affects or relates to every part of the world or the universe.

words.tr: n. 普遍性；一般性；通用
words.ex: The universality of human rights is a concept that transcends national boundaries.
words.ex_cn: 人权的普遍性是一个超越国界的概念。
words.en: The quality or state of being universal; the fact of existing or being found everywhere.

words.tr: adj. 不能证明为正当的；无可辩解的；没有道理的
words.ex: The price increase was deemed unjustifiable by the consumers.
words.ex_cn: 消费者认为价格上涨是不合理的。
words.en: If you describe something as unjustifiable, you mean that it cannot be justified because it is wrong or unacceptable.

words.ex: The storm unleashed heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 风暴释放出大雨。
words.en: If you say that someone or something unleashes a powerful force, feeling, activity, or group, you mean that they suddenly start it or send it to move somewhere.

words.ex: It is unlikely to rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天不大可能下雨。
words.en: If you say that something is unlikely to happen or unlikely to be true, you mean that you think it will not happen or that it is not true, although it is not certain.

words.tr: adj. 不矫揉造作的；不咬文嚼字的
words.ex: His writing is unliterary and plain.
words.ex_cn: 他的写作缺乏文学性，很朴素。
words.en: Not literary in character or style.

words.ex: Her skills are unmatched in the team.
words.ex_cn: 她的技能在团队中无人能及。
words.en: If you describe something as unmatched, you are emphasizing that it is better or greater than all other things of the same kind.

words.tr: adj. 没有减轻的；十足的；绝对的
words.ex: The criticism was unmitigated and harsh.
words.ex_cn: 批评是全然的严厉。
words.en: If you describe something as unmitigated, you are emphasizing that it is completely bad or good, without any qualification.

words.tr: adj. 无动于衷的；坚定的；不动心的
words.ex: She remained unmoved by his pleas.
words.ex_cn: 对他的恳求，她无动于衷。
words.en: If you are unmoved by something, you are not emotionally affected by it.

words.ex: The mistake was unnoteworthy and did not affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误微不足道，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as unnoteworthy, you mean that it is not particularly interesting, significant, or deserving of attention.

words.tr: adj. 无阻碍的；没有阻挡的
words.ex: The view is unobstructed from the top of the hill.
words.ex_cn: 从山顶上看，视野没有遮挡。
words.en: Not blocked or hindered; free from obstacles.

words.ex: The door handle was unobtrusive and blended with the wall.
words.ex_cn: 门把手不显眼，与墙壁融为一体。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as unobtrusive, you mean that they are not easily noticed or do not draw attention to themselves.

words.ex: He unpacks his bags after arriving home.
words.ex_cn: 他到家后打开行李。
words.en: To unpack means to open and remove the contents of a container, such as a suitcase or a box, or to explain or analyze something in detail.

words.tr: adj. 味道不好的；让人不快的；难以接受的；
words.ex: The soup was unpalatable and too salty.
words.ex_cn: 这汤味道不好，太咸了。
words.en: If you describe an idea as unpalatable, you mean that you find it unpleasant and difficult to accept.

words.ex: Her talent is unparalleled.
words.ex_cn: 她的才华是无比的。
words.en: Having no parallel or equal; unmatched.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.ex: The weather is unpredictable today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气不可预测。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as unpredictable, you mean that you cannot tell what they are going to do or how they are going to behave.

words.tr: adj. 非预谋的；非事先策划的
words.ex: The response was completely unpremeditated.
words.ex_cn: 这个回答完全是即兴的。
words.en: Not planned or thought out in advance; spontaneous.

words.tr: adj. 谦逊的；不夸耀的；不矫饰的
words.ex: The house had an unpretentious charm that made it feel welcoming.
words.ex_cn: 这座房子有一种不炫耀的魅力，让人感到宾至如归。
words.en: If you describe a place, person, or thing as unpretentious, you approve of them because they are simple in appearance or character, rather than sophisticated or luxurious.

words.tr: adj. 没有希望的；无前途的；不乐观的
words.ex: The weather looks unpromising for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气看起来不适合野餐。
words.en: If you describe something as unpromising, you think that it is unlikely to be successful or produce anything good in the future.

words.tr: adj. 未经证明的；未经检验的
words.ex: The theory is unproven but interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这个理论尚未被证明，但很有趣。
words.en: If you describe something as unproven, you mean that it has not been tested or has not been proved to be true or effective.

words.tr: adj. 不合格的；没资格的；完全的；绝对的
words.ex: He is unqualified for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他没有资格胜任这份工作。
words.en: If you are unqualified for something, you do not have the qualifications that are needed for it. It can also mean complete or total, without any doubt or limitation.

words.tr: adj. 无疑问的；确凿的；无可非议的
words.ex: His honesty is unquestionable.
words.ex_cn: 他的诚实是无可置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something as unquestionable, you are emphasizing that it is so obviously true or real that nobody can doubt it.

words.tr: adj. 不加疑问的；无条件的；绝对的
words.ex: He gave unquestioning support to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他毫无保留地支持他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's belief or attitude as unquestioning, you are emphasizing that they accept something without any doubt or disagreement.

words.ex: It is unreasonable to expect help without asking.
words.ex_cn: 不请求帮助就指望别人帮忙是不合理的。
words.en: If you say that someone is being unreasonable, you mean that they are behaving in a way that is not fair or sensible.

words.tr: adj. 未被认可到的；不被人注意的；不受重视的
words.ex: His talent remained unrecognized for years.
words.ex_cn: 他的才华多年未被认可。
words.en: not identified or acknowledged

words.ex: The market was unregulated, leading to many fraudulent activities.
words.ex_cn: 市场未受管制，导致了许多欺诈活动。
words.en: If something is unregulated, it is not controlled by rules or laws.

words.tr: adj. 不可靠的；不能信赖的；
words.ex: This clock is unreliable; it often stops.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟不可靠；它经常停。
words.en: If you describe a person, machine, or method as unreliable, you mean that you cannot trust them.

words.ex: The rain was unremitting all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都没有停过。
words.en: If you describe someone's effort or activity as unremitting, you mean that it is continued without stopping or becoming less intense.

words.tr: adj. 不典型的；非代表性的
words.ex: The sample is unrepresentative of the whole population.
words.ex_cn: 这个样本不能代表整个群体。
words.en: If you describe something as unrepresentative, you mean that it is not typical or representative of a particular group or thing.

words.tr: adj. 未被预订的；无保留的；不隐瞒的
words.ex: He gave an unreserved apology.
words.ex_cn: 他毫无保留地道歉了。
words.en: If you describe someone's feelings or behaviour as unreserved, you mean that they have expressed their feelings or done something in a very open and full way.

words.tr: adj. 不受限制的；无限制的；完整清晰的
words.ex: The kids have unrestricted access to the playground.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们可以自由进入游乐场。
words.en: If something is unrestricted, it is not limited or controlled by anyone or anything.

words.tr: adj. 没有受伤的；未受损害的；
words.ex: He walked away from the crash unscathed.
words.ex_cn: 他从车祸中安然无恙地走开了。
words.en: If someone is unscathed after a dangerous experience, they have not been injured or harmed by it.

words.ex: She bought an unscented lotion to avoid skin irritation.
words.ex_cn: 她买了一瓶无香味的乳液，以避免皮肤刺激。
words.en: Not having a scent or fragrance.

words.ex: He made an unscrupulous deal to save money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了省钱做了不道德的交易。
words.en: If you describe someone as unscrupulous, you are critical of them because they are prepared to act in a dishonest or immoral way in order to get what they want.

words.tr: adj. 不体面的；不相配的；不适宜的
words.ex: It is unseemly to shout in a library.
words.ex_cn: 在图书馆大喊大叫是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that someone's behaviour is unseemly, you disapprove of it because it is not appropriate in a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 不需要特殊技能的；
words.ex: He took an unskilled job at the warehouse.
words.ex_cn: 他在仓库找了一份不需要特殊技能的工作。
words.en: If someone is unskilled, they have no particular training or skill for a job.

words.tr: adj. 不可靠的；不稳固的；无根据的；不佳的
words.ex: The building's structure was found to be unsound.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的结构被发现是不牢靠的。
words.en: If something or someone is unsound, they are not in a good condition or are not based on good reasons.

words.ex: The beach is unspoiled and clean.
words.ex_cn: 这片海滩未被破坏，很干净。
words.en: If you describe a place as unspoiled, you think it is beautiful because it has not been changed or built on for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 没有污点的；清白的
words.ex: Her record is unspotted.
words.ex_cn: 她的记录没有任何污点。
words.en: If something is unspotted, it is free from spots or stains, and is often used to describe something that is pure or untarnished.

words.ex: The table is unstable and might fall.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子不稳，可能会倒。
words.en: Something that is unstable is not firm and therefore not safe, or is likely to change suddenly and become worse.

words.tr: adj. 大量地给予的；不吝啬的
words.ex: She was unstinting in her praise for the volunteers.
words.ex_cn: 她对志愿者们给予了慷慨的赞扬。
words.en: If you describe someone's support or effort as unstinting, you mean that they give it generously and completely, without holding back.

words.tr: adj. 未经证实的；未被证明的；
words.ex: The news reported an unsubstantiated claim about the president.
words.ex_cn: 新闻报道了一条未经证实的关于总统的言论。
words.en: If you describe something as unsubstantiated, you mean that it is not supported by any evidence or facts.

words.tr: adj. 不确定的；不肯定的；无把握的；
words.ex: I am unsure about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 我对这个答案不确定。
words.en: If you are unsure about something, you are not certain about it.

words.ex: Her singing voice is unsurpassed.
words.ex_cn: 她的歌声无可匹敌。
words.en: If you describe something as unsurpassed, you mean that it is better than anything else of the same kind.

words.tr: adj. 毫不怀疑的；无危险意识的；无戒备心的
words.ex: The unsuspecting man gave his wallet to the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个毫无戒心的人把钱包给了陌生人。
words.en: If you describe someone as unsuspecting, you mean that they are not aware of something that is happening or going to happen, especially something that will cause them harm.

words.tr: adj. 未被污染的；未被玷污的
words.ex: The water from the spring is untainted.
words.ex_cn: 泉水没有被污染。
words.en: If something is untainted, it is not spoiled or made less pure by something else.

words.ex: He is untalented in singing.
words.ex_cn: 他在唱歌方面没有天赋。
words.en: If you describe someone as untalented, you mean that they do not have any natural ability for a particular activity or skill.

words.tr: adj. 未被驯服的；难控驭的；原始的
words.ex: The untamed wild horse ran fast across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 那匹未经驯服的野马在平原上快速奔跑。
words.en: If you describe something as untamed, you mean that it has not been changed or controlled by people.

words.tr: adj. 塞子未开的；未使用的；
words.ex: The untapped bottle of soda still has its cap on.
words.ex_cn: 那瓶未开盖的苏打水还封着盖子。
words.en: If something is untapped, it has not yet been used or exploited.

words.tr: adj. 未失去光泽的；未受玷污的
words.ex: Her reputation remains untarnished.
words.ex_cn: 她的声誉依然完好无损。
words.en: If something is untarnished, it has not lost its good qualities or been spoiled in any way.

words.tr: adj.  未被尝过的；未体验过的
words.ex: The cake is untasted by anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这块蛋糕还没人尝过。
words.en: Not having been tasted or tried.

words.tr: adj. 难以捍卫的；站不住脚的；不堪一击的
words.ex: His excuse was untenable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口站不住脚。
words.en: If an argument, theory, or position is untenable, it cannot be defended or supported against criticism.

words.tr: adj. 不合时宜的；过早发生的
words.ex: His untimely death shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他突如其来的去世让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: If you describe an event as untimely, you mean that it happened earlier than it should, or sooner than you expected.

words.ex: There are untold stories behind this war.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争背后有着数不清的故事。
words.en: If you refer to an amount as untold, you are emphasizing that it is very large, usually so large that it cannot be measured or counted.

words.ex: The box remained untouched on the table.
words.ex_cn: 盒子原封不动地留在桌子上。
words.en: If something is untouched, it has not been changed or affected by something.

words.tr: adj. 未经治疗的；未处理的
words.ex: The water is untreated and unsafe to drink.
words.ex_cn: 这水未经处理，不能喝。
words.en: If something is untreated, it has not been dealt with in any way.

words.tr: adj. 不能信赖的；不可靠的；
words.ex: He is untrustworthy because he always lies.
words.ex_cn: 他总是撒谎，所以不可信赖。
words.en: If you describe someone as untrustworthy, you think they are not reliable and cannot be trusted.

words.tr: adj. 未受到教导的；未经正式训练的
words.ex: He is an untutored artist who paints beautifully.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位没有受过指导的艺术家，画得非常美。
words.en: If someone is untutored, they have not been formally taught or trained in a particular subject or skill.

words.tr: adj. 不合理的；没有根据的；无端的
words.ex: The teacher gave an unwarranted warning.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个没有理由的警告。
words.en: If you describe something as unwarranted, you are critical of it because there is no need or reason for it.

words.tr: adj. 笨重的；难处理的；臃肿的；庞大的
words.ex: The box was unwieldy and hard to carry.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子又大又笨重，很难搬。
words.en: An unwieldy object is difficult to move or handle because of its size, shape, or weight.

words.tr: adj. 不知情的；不经意的
words.ex: He was the unwitting victim of a prank.
words.ex_cn: 他是不知情的恶作剧受害者。
words.en: If someone is unwitting, they do not know or realize something.

words.ex: He made an unwonted silence during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议上出乎意料地保持了沉默。
words.en: Not usual or common; unusual.

words.tr: adj. 非世俗的；不慕金钱的；不谙世故的
words.ex: He has an unworldly smile, like he doesn't understand money.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种超凡脱俗的微笑，好像不懂金钱。
words.en: If you describe someone as unworldly, you mean that they are not interested in material possessions or in gaining power or status, and they are often unaware of or indifferent to practical matters.

words.tr: adj. 不屈的；不屈服的；坚硬的
words.ex: He is unyielding in his decision.
words.ex_cn: 他在决定上毫不退让。
words.en: If you describe someone as unyielding, you mean that they are very determined and not likely to change their mind.

words.ex: The judge will uphold the law.
words.ex_cn: 法官将维护法律。
words.en: If you uphold something such as a law, a principle, or a decision, you support and maintain it.

words.ex: They eat at an upscale restaurant every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他们每周末都在一家高档餐厅吃饭。
words.en: If you describe something as upscale, you mean it is of high quality or intended for people who are wealthy.

words.tr:
v. 使相形见绌；抢…的风头
adv. 在（或向）舞台后部
words.ex: She tried to upstage her co-star by wearing a more extravagant gown.
words.ex_cn: 她试图通过穿一件更华丽的礼服来抢走她搭档的风头。
words.en: If someone upstages you, they draw attention away from you by being more attractive or interesting.

words.tr: n. 自命不凡的新上任者；狂妄自大的新手
words.ex: The upstart claimed he could run the company better than the founder.
words.ex_cn: 这个自命不凡的新上任者声称他比创始人更能管理公司。
words.en: An upstart is someone who has suddenly risen to a higher social or economic class and behaves in a way that is considered arrogant or presumptuous.

words.tr: adj. 温文儒雅的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: He is an urbane man who speaks politely.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个举止文雅、说话有礼貌的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as urbane, you mean that they are polite, confident, and comfortable in social situations.

words.ex: The city plans to urbanize the village next year.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市计划明年将这个村庄城市化。
words.en: To make an area more urban by building houses, industries, and other facilities.

words.ex: The doctor sensed the urgency and acted quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生感受到了紧急情况，迅速采取了行动。
words.en: The quality or condition of being urgent; pressing importance.

words.ex: This tool is usable for beginners.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具初学者可以用。
words.en: If something is usable, it is in a good enough state or condition to be used.

words.tr: adj. 实用的；功利主义的；
words.ex: The chair is utilitarian and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子实用又舒适。
words.en: Utilitarian means relating to or adhering to the belief that the value of a thing or an action is determined by its utility.

words.tr: n. 效用；实用；公用事业；
words.ex: The utility of this tool is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具的效用非常高。
words.en: Utility refers to the state of being useful, profitable, or beneficial.

words.ex: We can utilize solar energy to power the house.
words.ex_cn: 我们可以利用太阳能来为房子供电。
words.en: To utilize something means to use it in a practical or effective way.

words.tr: adj. 乌托邦的；空想完美主义的；
words.ex: His plan for a perfect society is utopian.
words.ex_cn: 他关于完美社会的计划是乌托邦式的。
words.en: If you describe a plan or idea as utopian, you are criticizing it because it is unrealistic and shows a belief that things can be improved much more than is possible.

words.tr: v. 游移不定；踌躇；犹豫
words.ex: He vacillates between choosing tea or coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他在选择茶还是咖啡之间犹豫不决。
words.en: To vacillate means to waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.

words.ex: The vagueness of his answer made me confused.
words.ex_cn: 他回答的模糊让我感到困惑。
words.en: The quality or state of being unclear, indefinite, or indistinct.

words.tr: adj. 非常自负的；自命不凡的
words.ex: He was so vainglorious that he believed his own press clippings.
words.ex_cn: 他非常自负，以至于相信了自己的新闻剪报。
words.en: If you describe someone as vainglorious, you are critical of them because they are very proud of their own status, abilities, or achievements.

words.tr: n. 极度自负；极度的虚荣心
words.ex: He shouted about his wins out of vainglory.
words.ex_cn: 他因虚荣而大肆宣扬自己的胜利。
words.en: Excessive pride in oneself or one's achievements; overly vain.

words.ex: The valiant soldier fought bravely to protect his team.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的士兵英勇战斗以保护他的队友。
words.en: Someone who is valiant is very brave and determined, especially in a difficult situation.

words.ex: The system will validate your password.
words.ex_cn: 系统将验证你的密码。
words.en: To validate something such as a claim or statement means to prove or confirm that it is true or correct.

words.ex: The courageous soldier made a valorous charge.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的士兵进行了英勇的冲锋。
words.en: If you describe someone as valorous, you mean that they are very brave, especially in battle.

words.ex: The water valve is broken and needs repair.
words.ex_cn: 这个水阀坏了，需要修理。
words.en: A valve is a device attached to a pipe or a tube which controls the flow of air or liquid through it.

words.ex: He bought a new mirror because of his vanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为虚荣心买了一面新镜子。
words.en: The quality of being vain; excessive pride in or admiration of one's own appearance or achievements.

words.ex: The variability of weather makes it hard to plan outdoor events.
words.ex_cn: 天气的可变性使得计划户外活动很困难。
words.en: The quality or state of being subject to change or variation.

words.tr: n. （同一事物）不同种类；多样性；（动植物的）品种；变化；
words.ex: The store sells a variety of apples.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种各样的苹果。
words.en: If something has variety, it consists of things which are different from each other.

words.tr:
adj. 拱形的；有拱顶的
v. 跳跃；“vault”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The church has a vaulted ceiling.
words.ex_cn: 这座教堂有一个拱形天花板。
words.en: Having an arched roof or ceiling.

words.tr:
v. 改变方向；转向
n. 转向
words.ex: The car veers to the left when the driver turns too fast.
words.ex_cn: 当司机转得太快时，汽车会向左偏转。
words.en: If something veers in a certain direction, it suddenly changes direction and moves in that direction.

words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

words.tr: n. 车辆；交通工具；媒介；
words.ex: The vehicle stopped at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在红灯前停了下来。
words.en: A vehicle is a machine such as a car, bus, or truck which has an engine and is used to carry people or goods from place to place.

words.ex: She wore a white veil on her wedding day.
words.ex_cn: 她在婚礼那天戴了一条白色的面纱。
words.en: A veil is a piece of thin soft cloth that women sometimes wear over their heads and which can also cover their face.

words.tr: adj. 贪赃枉法的；腐败的
words.ex: The official was venal and took bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员贪腐，接受了贿赂。
words.en: If you describe someone as venal, you disapprove of them because they are prepared to do almost anything in return for money, even things which are dishonest or immoral.

words.ex: The venerable teacher has taught for over 40 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位值得尊敬的老师已经教书40多年了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as venerable, you mean that they are old and respected.

words.ex: People venerate the ancient sage for his wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 人们因他的智慧而崇敬这位古代圣人。
words.en: To regard with respect or reverence.

words.ex: He made a venial mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告中犯了一个可以原谅的错误。
words.en: If you describe a wrong action as venial, you mean that it is not very serious or grave, and therefore easy to forgive.

words.tr: adj. 分泌毒液的；有毒的；恶毒的
words.ex: The snake is venomous.
words.ex_cn: 这条蛇是有毒的。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as venomous, you mean that they show great bitterness and anger toward someone.

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: He was known for his venturesome spirit and willingness to take risks.
words.ex_cn: 他以冒险精神和愿意承担风险而闻名。
words.en: If you describe someone as venturesome, you mean that they are willing to take risks, especially in order to try out new things.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；说实话的；准确的
words.ex: He is a veracious person who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个诚实的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is veracious is truthful and honest.

words.ex: The veracity of his story was questioned by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事的真实性受到了警方的质疑。
words.en: Veracity refers to the quality of being true or accurate.

words.ex: He gave a verbose answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对简单的问题给出了冗长的回答。
words.en: Using or containing more words than are necessary; long-winded.

words.ex: The verbosity of the report made it difficult to understand.
words.ex_cn: 报告的冗长使得它难以理解。
words.en: Verbosity is the quality of using more words than needed; wordiness.

words.ex: The verdant hills looked beautiful in spring.
words.ex_cn: 青翠的山丘在春天看起来很美。
words.en: Green with grass or other rich vegetation.

words.tr: adj. 可核实的；能证实的
words.ex: The result must be verifiable by anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果必须能被任何人验证。
words.en: Capable of being verified or confirmed by evidence or testimony.

words.ex: The verification of the password took only a few seconds.
words.ex_cn: 密码的验证只花了几秒钟。
words.en: Verification is the process of establishing the truth, accuracy, or validity of something.

words.tr: v. 证实；“verify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The scientist verified the results with a second test.
words.ex_cn: 科学家用第二次实验证实了结果。
words.en: Confirmed as true or accurate by evidence or testimony.

words.ex: Please verify your email address.
words.ex_cn: 请核实你的电子邮件地址。
words.en: To verify something means to check or prove that it is true, accurate, or justified.

words.ex: He writes a verse every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上写一首诗。
words.en: A verse is one of the parts into which a poem, a song, or a chapter of the Bible or the Koran is divided.

words.ex: Fish and birds are vertebrates.
words.ex_cn: 鱼和鸟是脊椎动物。
words.en: A vertebrate is an animal that has a spine or backbone.

words.ex: The fishing vessel sailed out at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 那艘渔船在黎明时出海。
words.en: A vessel is a large boat or a container for holding liquids.

words.ex: The old house has a vestige of its original design.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子还保留着它原始设计的痕迹。
words.en: A vestige is a small part or amount of something that remains after the rest has disappeared or been destroyed.

words.tr: adj. 残留的；残余的；退化的
words.ex: The human tailbone is a vestigial structure.
words.ex_cn: 人类的尾骨是一个退化的结构。
words.en: Vestigial is used to describe something that is a remnant of a once more developed or functional structure or characteristic, now reduced in size or function.

words.ex: The loud noise vexes my little brother.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让我的小弟弟很烦。
words.en: If someone or something vexes you, they make you feel annoyed, puzzled, and frustrated.

words.ex: The loud noise caused him vexation.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让他感到烦恼。
words.en: The state of being annoyed, frustrated, or worried.

words.ex: This plan is viable and can be done with little money.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划是可行的，而且用很少的钱就能完成。
words.en: If something is viable, it is capable of doing what it is intended to do.

words.ex: The children are vibrant and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们充满活力。
words.en: If you describe something as vibrant, you mean that it is bright, lively, and full of energy.

words.ex: He gave a vicious smile before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前露出一个恶毒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as vicious, you mean that they are violent and cruel, or that they are intended to cause someone great harm or suffering.

words.ex: Life is full of vicissitude.
words.ex_cn: 生活充满起伏。
words.en: A change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome or unpleasant.

words.ex: The guard showed vigilance during the night shift.
words.ex_cn: 守卫在夜班期间保持警惕。
words.en: Vigilance is the action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties.

words.ex: The guard is vigilant at night.
words.ex_cn: 这名守卫在夜里非常警惕。
words.en: Someone who is vigilant gives careful attention to a particular problem or situation and concentrates on noticing any danger or trouble that there might be.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: He did not agree with the policy, but he did not want to vilify those who supported it.
words.ex_cn: 他不同意这项政策，但不想诋毁那些支持它的人。
words.en: To vilify someone means to say or write very unpleasant things about them in order to hurt their reputation.

words.ex: He proved his innocence to vindicate his name.
words.ex_cn: 他证明了自己的清白以洗清自己的名声。
words.en: To clear someone of blame or suspicion.

words.tr: adj. 想复仇的；报复性的；怀恨的
words.ex: He was vindictive and refused to forgive her.
words.ex_cn: 他心怀报复，拒绝原谅她。
words.en: If you say that someone is vindictive, you are critical of them because they deliberately try to upset or cause trouble for someone who they think has done them harm.

words.ex: He violated the school rule by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: If someone violates an agreement, law, or promise, they break it.

words.ex: The viral infection made him feverish for three days.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒引起的感染让他发烧了三天。
words.en: Relating to or caused by a virus; becoming very popular by circulating quickly from person to person, especially on the internet.

words.ex: Honesty is a great virtue.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种伟大的美德。
words.en: A virtue is a good quality or way of behaving.

words.tr:
n. 艺术名家；音乐演奏名家
adj. 技艺精湛的；功力深厚的
words.ex: He is a virtuoso on the violin.
words.ex_cn: 他是小提琴方面的天才。
words.en: A virtuoso is someone who is extremely skilled at doing something, especially playing a musical instrument.

words.tr: adj. 品行端正的；品德高的；
words.ex: He is a virtuous man who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品行端正的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Having or showing high moral standards.

words.ex: The virulence of the virus shocked the doctors.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒的毒性让医生们感到震惊。
words.en: The severity or harmfulness of a disease or poison; the degree of pathogenicity of a microorganism as indicated by the severity of disease produced and its ability to invade the tissues of the host.

words.ex: Honey is a viscous liquid.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜是一种黏稠的液体。
words.en: A viscous liquid is thick and sticky and does not flow easily.

words.ex: The stars are visible at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚可以看到星星。
words.en: If something is visible, it can be seen.

words.tr:
adj. 幻想的；有远见的
n. 空想家；有远见的人
words.ex: He had a visionary idea about flying cars.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个关于飞行汽车的幻想想法。
words.en: A visionary is someone who has strong ideas about how things might be different in the future, especially in a way that leads to changes in society or technology.

words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.ex: The child shows great vitality while playing.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩耍时充满活力。
words.en: Vitality refers to the state of being strong and active; energy.

words.tr: v. 使变质；损害；使失效
words.ex: The poison vitiated the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒物使水源变质。
words.en: To vitiate something means to impair or reduce the quality, value, or effectiveness of it.

words.tr: adj. 刻薄的；尖刻的；恶意的
words.ex: His vitriolic words hurt everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他刻薄的话伤害了房间里所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as vitriolic, you disapprove of it because it is full of bitterness and hate, and so causes a lot of distress and pain.

words.ex: The painter used vivid colors to show the forest.
words.ex_cn: 画家用鲜艳的颜色来描绘森林。
words.en: If you describe memories and descriptions as vivid, you mean that they are very clear and detailed.

words.ex: Blue jeans are in vogue this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年牛仔裤很时髦。
words.en: If something is in vogue, it is very popular and fashionable.

words.ex: The alcohol is volatile and evaporates quickly.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是易挥发的，会迅速蒸发。
words.en: A volatile situation or person is one that is likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially by getting worse.

words.ex: The volcanic eruption destroyed the village.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷发摧毁了村庄。
words.en: Volcanic is used to describe things that are connected with volcanoes or caused by volcanoes.

words.tr: adj. 健谈的；滔滔不绝的
words.ex: He is a voluble speaker who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个健谈的人，整天说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as voluble, you mean that they talk a lot with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 宽松的；容积大的；部头大的；卷数多的
words.ex: She wore a voluminous dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条宽松的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is voluminous is very large or contains a lot of things.

words.ex: He did voluntary work at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院做志愿工作。
words.en: If something is voluntary, you do it because you choose to, and not because you have to.

words.tr: adj. 激起性欲的；满足感官的；撩人的
words.ex: The painting showed a voluptuous woman with flowing curves.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位身材性感、曲线优美的女人。
words.en: If you describe a woman as voluptuous, you mean that she has large breasts and hips and is considered sexually attractive.

words.tr: n. 窥淫癖者；好刺探他人隐私者
words.ex: He was arrested for being a voyeur, spying on people in their private moments.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窥他人隐私时刻而被捕，是一个窥淫狂者。
words.en: A voyeur is someone who gets sexual pleasure from secretly watching other people, especially when they are naked or having sex.

words.tr: adj. 庸俗的；粗俗的；粗野的；下流的
words.ex: He used a vulgar word in class.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上说了一个粗俗的词。
words.en: If you describe something as vulgar, you mean that it is in bad taste or of poor quality.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: The walrus swims in the cold sea.
words.ex_cn: 海象在寒冷的海里游泳。
words.en: A walrus is a large marine mammal with flippers, a thick layer of blubber, and long tusks, found in the Arctic Ocean and subarctic seas.

words.ex: She had a strong wanderlust and traveled to many countries.
words.ex_cn: 她有强烈的旅游热，去过许多国家。
words.en: A strong desire to travel.

words.tr:
v. 衰落；减弱；缺；亏
n. 衰退；减弱；缺；亏
words.ex: The moon begins to wane after the full moon.
words.ex_cn: 满月之后，月亮开始变暗。
words.en: If something wanes, it becomes gradually weaker or less, often so that it eventually disappears.

words.tr:
v. 使翘棱；使扭曲变形
n. 弯曲；歪曲
words.ex: The heat will warp the metal.
words.ex_cn: 热量会使金属变形。
words.en: To warp is to bend or twist something out of its natural shape, often as a result of heat or moisture. It can also refer to the state of being bent or twisted.

words.ex: The evidence warrants a new investigation.
words.ex_cn: 证据使新的调查成为必要。
words.en: If something warrants a particular action, it makes the action seem necessary or appropriate for the circumstances.

words.tr: adj. 可保证的；可承认的；正当的
words.ex: His claim is warrantable with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的说法有明确的证据支持。
words.en: If something is warrantable, it is able to be justified or authorized.

words.tr: adj. 保证的； v. “warrant”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The repair was warranted by the store.
words.ex_cn: 这次维修由商店保证。
words.en: If something is warranted, there is a good reason for it and it can be accepted.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.ex: The wavy line looks like a snake.
words.ex_cn: 波浪形的线看起来像一条蛇。
words.en: Something that is wavy has a series of curves or waves in it.

words.ex: The leaves have a waxy surface.
words.ex_cn: 这些叶子表面似蜡的。
