words.ex: He caught a big carp in the river.
words.ex_cn: 他在河里钓到了一条大鲤鱼。
words.en: To complain or find fault continually, typically about trivial matters.

words.ex: The carpenter made a wooden table.
words.ex_cn: 木匠做了一张木桌子。
words.en: A carpenter is a person whose job is making and repairing wooden objects and structures.

words.tr:
n. 腐肉；死肉
adj. 腐肉的；吃腐肉的
words.ex: The vulture eats carrion on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 秃鹫在地面上吃腐肉。
words.en: The dead and rotting flesh of an animal.

words.ex: My brother watches cartoon every evening.
words.ex_cn: 我弟弟每天晚上看卡通片。
words.en: A cartoon is a humorous drawing or series of drawings in a newspaper or magazine, or a film made using animation techniques.

words.tr: adj. 随意的；非正式的；偶然的；
words.ex: He wore casual clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了随意的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behavior as casual, you mean they are not very concerned about what they are doing or what is happening around them, or they are not taking it seriously.

words.ex: He looked at the catalog to find the book.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看目录来找那本书。
words.en: A catalog is a list of things, such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

words.tr: n. 发泄情绪；情感宣泄
words.ex: The novel provided a catharsis for her emotions.
words.ex_cn: 这部小说为她的情感提供了一个宣泄的出口。
words.en: Catharsis refers to the process of releasing, and thereby providing relief from, strong or repressed emotions.

words.tr:
n. 天主教徒；
adj. 天主教的；
words.ex: He is a catholic who goes to church every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名每周日都去教堂的天主教徒。
words.en: If you describe a collection of things or people as catholic, you are emphasizing that it is varied and includes many different types of things or people.

words.tr: n. 政党会议；核心小组会议；特别利益集团
words.ex: The caucus decided on a new strategy for the upcoming election.
words.ex_cn: 党团会议决定了一项新的选举策略。
words.en: A caucus is a meeting of the members of a political party to select candidates or decide policy.

words.ex: The fish swims with its caudal fin.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼用它的尾鳍游泳。
words.en: Relating to the tail or the posterior part of the body.

words.ex: He used caulk to seal the gaps around the window.
words.ex_cn: 他用填料密封了窗户周围的缝隙。
words.en: To fill or seal (a gap or seam) to make it watertight.

words.ex: The doctor cauterized the wound to stop the bleeding.
words.ex_cn: 医生烧灼伤口以止血。
words.en: To burn the skin or wound with a hot instrument or caustic substance to stop bleeding or prevent infection.

words.ex: The cavalry charged quickly across the field.
words.ex_cn: 骑兵迅速冲过田野。
words.en: The cavalry refers to the part of an army that originally fought on horseback, now typically used in modern armies to refer to units that are mobile and intended for rapid deployment.

words.ex: The children cavort in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里嬉戏。
words.en: If people cavort, they leap about in a noisy and excited way because they are very happy.

words.tr: v. 割让（领土）；放弃（权力）
words.ex: He will cede his land to the government.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地让给政府。
words.en: To give up control or possession of something, especially land or territory, often as a result of war or negotiation.

words.tr: adj. 著名的； v. 庆祝；“celebrate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a celebrated painter in China.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位在中国著名的画家。
words.en: A celebrated person or thing is famous and much admired.

words.ex: The celebrity smiled at the fans outside the theater.
words.ex_cn: 这位名人向剧院外的粉丝微笑。
words.en: A celebrity is a famous person, especially in entertainment or sports.

words.ex: The project was completed with remarkable celerity.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目以惊人的速度完成了。
words.en: Celerity is the quality of being swift or rapid.

words.ex: He plays the cello every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上拉大提琴。
words.en: A cello is a large stringed instrument of the violin family, tuned an octave below the viola.

words.ex: They used cement to build the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他们用水泥建造了这堵墙。
words.en: Cement is a powdery substance which is mixed with water and used for sticking things together or for making very hard surfaces.

words.ex: The centrifugal force pushes the water outward.
words.ex_cn: 离心力把水向外推。
words.en: Moving or tending to move away from a center.

words.ex: The centripetal force keeps the ball moving in a circle.
words.ex_cn: 向心力使球保持圆周运动。
words.en: Moving or tending to move toward a center.

words.ex: The baby is in a cephalic position before birth.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿在出生前是头位。
words.en: Relating to the head or the head end of the body.

words.ex: The wedding ceremony was beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼仪式很美丽。
words.en: A ceremony is a formal event held on special occasions such as weddings, graduations, or official functions, often involving traditional or religious rituals.

words.ex: He received a certification for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证明。
words.en: Certification is the act of certifying or the state of being certified, often involving the issuance of a certificate or official document attesting to a status or level of achievement.

words.ex: The cession of land was agreed upon by both countries.
words.ex_cn: 两国同意转让土地。
words.en: The act of ceding or giving up something, especially land or rights, to another party.

words.tr:
adj. 嘲弄的；玩笑的
v. 开玩笑；戏弄；“chaff”的现在分词
words.ex: He is chaffing his friend about his new haircut.
words.ex_cn: 他正在拿朋友的新发型开玩笑。
words.en: To tease someone in a friendly way.

words.tr: n. 变色龙；见风使舵的人
words.ex: The chameleon changes color to hide.
words.ex_cn: 变色龙改变颜色来隐藏自己。
words.en: A chameleon is a type of lizard that can change the color of its skin in order to blend in with its surroundings.

words.ex: The chandelier hangs above the dining table.
words.ex_cn: 吊灯悬挂在餐桌上方。
words.en: A chandelier is a decorative ceiling-mounted light fixture with branches for several light bulbs or candles.

words.tr:
n. 圣歌；赞美诗；喊叫
v. 吟唱；诵扬；反复叫喊
words.ex: The monks sang a traditional chant during the morning prayer.
words.ex_cn: 修道士们在晨祷时唱了一首传统圣歌。
words.en: A chant is a word or group of words that is repeated over and over again. It can also refer to a simple song, especially one that is sung in a religious service.

words.ex: The room was in chaos after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对之后，房间一片混乱。
words.en: A state of complete disorder and confusion.

words.ex: The char cleaned the office every morning.
words.ex_cn: 女清洁工每天早上打扫办公室。
words.en: To char is to burn something so that it becomes black or to work temporarily in a job.

words.tr: n. 特性描述；人物性格塑造；
words.ex: The characterization of the hero shows his bravery.
words.ex_cn: 对英雄的特性描述展现了他勇敢的品质。
words.en: The act of describing or representing the qualities or peculiarities of a person or thing.

words.tr:
n. 明显的伪装；装模作样
(~s：看手势猜字谜游戏)
words.ex: His apology was a charade to hide his true feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他的道歉是一种明显的伪装，为了隐藏他真实的情感。
words.en: A charade is a situation in which people pretend that something is true when it clearly is not, or a game in which one team acts out a word or phrase for the other team to guess.

words.ex: His charisma made everyone want to follow him.
words.ex_cn: 他的超凡魅力让所有人都想追随他。
words.en: Charisma is a compelling attractiveness or charm that can inspire devotion in others.

words.ex: The charity helps poor children get food and education.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善团体帮助贫困儿童获得食物和教育。
words.en: An organization that helps people in need, or the act of giving money, food, or help to those who need it.

words.ex: Her smile has a special charm.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑有一种特别的魅力。
words.en: If you say that someone has charm, you mean that they behave in a friendly and pleasant way that makes people like them. A charm is also a small ornament that is fixed to a bracelet or necklace.

words.tr:
v. 追逐；
n. 追逐；
words.ex: The dog chases the cat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗每天早上追逐猫。
words.en: To chase someone or something means to quickly follow them or it in order to catch them.

words.tr: adj. 贞洁的；忠贞的；朴素的
words.ex: She remained chaste despite the pressure.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有压力，她依然保持贞洁。
words.en: If you describe someone as chaste, you mean that they do not have sex with anyone, or they only have sex with their husband or wife.

words.ex: The coach chastened the team for their poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 教练因球队表现不佳而惩罚了他们。
words.en: If you are chastened by something, it makes you regret that you have behaved badly or stupidly.

words.ex: The teacher chastised the boy for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为男孩在课堂上说话而责备了他。
words.en: To chastise someone means to punish or criticize them severely.

words.tr: adj. 沙文主义的；盲目爱国的；大男人主义的
words.ex: His chauvinistic remarks about the superiority of his own country were met with disapproval.
words.ex_cn: 他关于自己国家优越性的沙文主义言论遭到了反对。
words.en: If you describe someone as chauvinistic, you believe that they think their own country or sex is better than any other.

words.tr: adj. 分成方格的； v. “checker”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The table has a checkered cloth.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子上有块方格布。
words.en: Something that is checkered has a pattern of squares, usually of two different colors, or has had a lot of different experiences or events, often both good and bad.

words.tr: adj. 厚脸皮的；鲁莽放肆的；大胆无礼的
words.ex: He gave a cheeky smile when he got caught.
words.ex_cn: 他被抓到时露出了调皮的微笑。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as cheeky, you mean that they are slightly rude or disrespectful but in a charming or amusing way.

words.tr: adj. 天使般可爱的；天使般纯真的
words.ex: The cherubic boy smiled at everyone.
words.ex_cn: 那个天使般的孩子对每个人微笑。
words.en: Having the innocence or plump prettiness of a cherub.

words.ex: She wore a chic dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条别致的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as chic, you mean that they are stylish and fashionable.

words.ex: He resorted to chicanery to win the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他依靠狡辩赢得了争论。
words.en: The use of trickery to achieve a political, financial, or legal purpose.

words.ex: My mother chides me for coming home late.
words.ex_cn: 我妈妈因为我回家晚而责备我。
words.en: If you chide someone, you speak to them angrily because they have done something wrong.

words.tr: n. 喀迈拉；妄想；嵌合体
words.ex: The myth says the chimera has a lion's head, a goat's body, and a snake's tail.
words.ex_cn: 这个神话说喀迈拉有狮子的头、山羊的身体和蛇的尾巴。
words.en: In Greek mythology, a chimera is a creature that is composed of parts of different animals. In modern usage, it refers to an illusion or fabrication of the mind; especially an unrealizable dream.

words.ex: The chipmunk scurried across the path, gathering nuts.
words.ex_cn: 花栗鼠匆匆穿过小径，收集坚果。
words.en: A chipmunk is a small, striped rodent of the squirrel family, found in North America and Asia.

words.tr:
adj. 兴高采烈的；活泼的；活跃的
n. 切东西的人或工具 
v. （使）高兴起来；吱吱叫；喋喋而言
words.ex: She is chipper after drinking coffee.
words.ex_cn: 她喝完咖啡后心情很好。
words.en: If you describe someone as chipper, you mean that they are cheerful and lively.

words.ex: The bird made a soft chirp in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在早晨发出轻柔的唧唧声。
words.en: If a bird or an insect chirps, it makes short high-pitched sounds.

words.tr:
n. 凿子
v. 雕；凿；欺骗
words.ex: He used a chisel to carve the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他用凿子雕刻石头。
words.en: A chisel is a tool with a long metal blade which has a sharp edge for cutting wood, stone, or metal.

words.ex: He made a choice to study hard.
words.ex_cn: 他选择努力学习。
words.en: If you have a choice, you can choose between two or more things.

words.ex: The smoke made him choke.
words.ex_cn: 烟让他窒息。
words.en: If you choke, or if something chokes you, you cannot breathe properly because there is not enough air or because something is blocking your throat.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；暴躁的；脾气不好的
words.ex: He is a choleric man who shouts when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个易怒的人，一生气就大喊大叫。
words.en: A choleric person is someone who gets angry very easily.

words.tr: adj. 挑剔的；过分讲究的
words.ex: She is choosy about what she eats.
words.ex_cn: 她对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you describe someone as choosy, you mean they are very careful in choosing what they do or buy, and will only accept exactly what they want.

words.tr:
v. 高兴得咯咯笑；哈哈大笑
n. 哈哈大笑；开心地笑
words.ex: He chortled when he saw the funny cat.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那只搞笑的猫时咯咯笑了。
words.en: To laugh in a breathy, gleeful way; chuckle.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.tr: v. 扔；抛；丢掷；放弃；离职
words.ex: He chucked the old book into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把那本旧书扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: To throw something carelessly or casually; to give up or stop doing something.

words.tr:
v. 轻声笑；咯咯笑；暗自笑
n. 暗自发笑；咯咯声
words.ex: He chuckled when he saw the funny dog.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那只搞笑的狗时笑了起来。
words.en: To laugh quietly or inwardly.

words.ex: He was considered a churl by his neighbors for his miserly ways.
words.ex_cn: 由于他的吝啬，邻居们都认为他是个吝啬鬼。
words.en: A churl is a rude, ill-bred person; a boor. It can also refer to a miserly person.

words.tr:
n. 纤毛虫
adj. 有纤毛的；具缘毛的
words.ex: The ciliate protozoa are characterized by the presence of cilia.
words.ex_cn: 纤毛原生动物的特点是具有纤毛。
words.en: Having cilia; relating to or characteristic of ciliates.

words.ex: The children played near the cinder pile after the fire.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在火堆后的煤渣堆旁玩耍。
words.en: A cinder is a small piece of partly burnt coal or wood that has stopped giving off flames but still has combustible matter in it.

words.tr: adj. 圆圈的；环形的；循环的；
words.ex: The table has a circular top.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子有一个圆形的桌面。
words.en: Something that is circular is shaped like a circle.

words.ex: He gave a citation from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他引用了这本书中的一段话。
words.en: A citation is a reference to a published or unpublished source (not always the original source). More precisely, a citation is an abbreviated alphanumeric expression embedded in the body of an intellectual work that denotes an entry in the bibliographic references section of the work for the purpose of acknowledging the relevance of the works of others to the topic of discussion at the spot where the citation appears.

words.ex: The civilian population stayed safe during the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 平民在冲突期间保持安全。
words.en: A civilian is a person who is not a member of the military or of a police or firefighting force.

words.ex: He claims to have clairvoyance and can see the future.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己有预知能力，能看到未来。
words.en: The supposed faculty of perceiving things or events in the future or beyond normal sensory contact.

words.tr:
n. 透视者；千里眼的人；有洞察力的人
adj.  透视的；有洞察力的
words.ex: The clairvoyant claimed to foresee the future events.
words.ex_cn: 这位能预知未来的人声称可以预见未来的事件。
words.en: A clairvoyant is someone who claims to have the ability to perceive events in the future or beyond normal sensory contact.

words.tr: adj. 冷湿的；黏糊糊的；冷而黏的
words.ex: His hands were clammy from fear.
words.ex_cn: 他的手因为害怕而变得潮湿冰冷。
words.en: Something that is clammy is unpleasantly damp, soft, sticky, and usually cool.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；暗中行事的
words.ex: He made a clandestine meeting with his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他与朋友进行了一次秘密会面。
words.en: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit.

words.ex: The clarity of her explanation helped everyone understand.
words.ex_cn: 她解释的清晰帮助了每个人理解。
words.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear, in particular the quality of being easy to understand or see.

words.ex: The two teams clashed during the match.
words.ex_cn: 这两支队伍在比赛中发生了冲突。
words.en: A clash is a loud, harsh noise, like the clash of cymbals. It can also refer to a conflict or disagreement.

words.tr:
n. 钩；扣；紧握；紧抱
v. 抱紧；握紧；扣紧
words.ex: The necklace has a gold clasp.
words.ex_cn: 这条项链有一个金色的钩。
words.en: A clasp is a small device that fastens something, or the act of holding someone or something tightly.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；裂口
adj. 劈开的
v. 劈开；砍开；坚守；信守；忠于；“cleave”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The rock has a small cleft where water collects.
words.ex_cn: 这块岩石上有一个小裂缝，水会积在那里。
words.en: A cleft is a narrow opening or fissure, especially in a rock or the ground.

words.ex: The clement teacher gave students extra time.
words.ex_cn: 这位仁慈的老师给了学生更多时间。
words.en: Mild or merciful in disposition or character; lenient; compassionate.

words.tr:
v. 握紧；捏紧；咬牙切齿
n. 抓紧；咬紧；抓紧用具
words.ex: He clenched his fist when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个消息时握紧了拳头。
words.en: To close or hold something very tightly, especially in a determined or angry way.

words.ex: He used a cliche to describe the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个陈词滥调来形容日落。
words.en: A cliché is an idea or phrase that has been used so much that it is no longer interesting or effective.

words.tr:
v. 钉牢；用臂互抱；达成（协议等）；最终解决
n. 钉牢；扭抱
words.ex: He clinched the board to the wall with nails.
words.ex_cn: 他用钉子把木板钉在墙上。
words.en: To settle something conclusively; to secure or fasten something by flattening the ends of nails, screws, etc.

words.ex: The child clings to his mother's leg.
words.ex_cn: 孩子紧贴着妈妈的腿。
words.en: If you cling to someone or something, you hold onto them tightly.

words.tr:
n. 凝块；泥团；密集的一群
v. 凝结成块
words.ex: The blood began to clot after the cut.
words.ex_cn: 伤口流血后开始凝固。
words.en: A clot is a sticky lump that forms when blood dries up or becomes thick. If blood clots, it becomes thick and forms a lump.

words.ex: The cloudburst flooded the street suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 暴雨突然淹没了街道。
words.en: A cloudburst is a sudden, very heavy rainfall.

words.tr: v. （使）吃腻（甜食）；（使）过饱；因过量而厌烦
words.ex: The rich dessert soon cloyed my appetite.
words.ex_cn: 丰富的甜点很快就让我感到腻了。
words.en: If something cloys, it becomes unpleasant because it is too sweet, rich, or sentimental.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: The blood will coagulate if it is left outside the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液如果留在体外，就会凝结。
words.en: If a liquid coagulates, it becomes thick and almost solid.

words.ex: The wound showed coagulation after a few minutes.
words.ex_cn: 几分钟后，伤口出现了凝固。
words.en: Coagulation is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel, forming a clot.

words.ex: The soap coarsens her skin.
words.ex_cn: 肥皂让她的皮肤变粗糙了。
words.en: To make or become coarse.

words.ex: The coda of the symphony brought the concert to a powerful conclusion.
words.ex_cn: 交响乐的终曲为音乐会带来了强有力的结束。
words.en: The concluding passage of a piece or movement, typically forming an addition to the basic structure.

words.ex: She coddles her little brother too much.
words.ex_cn: 她太宠着她的弟弟了。
words.en: To treat someone in an indulgent or overprotective way.

words.tr:
adj. 同年代的
n. 同时代的人
words.ex: The two ancient temples are coeval.
words.ex_cn: 这两座古代神庙是同时期的。
words.en: Having the same age or date of origin; contemporary.

words.ex: The king kept gold in his coffer.
words.ex_cn: 国王把黄金存放在他的金库中。
words.en: A coffer is a large strong chest used for storing valuable objects such as money or gold.

words.tr: v. 深思熟虑；慎重考虑
words.ex: He cogitates before he answers the question.
words.ex_cn: 他在回答问题之前会深思。
words.en: To think deeply about something; to ponder or meditate.

words.ex: The team's cohesion helped them win the match.
words.ex_cn: 团队的凝聚力帮助他们赢得了比赛。
words.en: Cohesion refers to the action or fact of forming a united whole, especially in the context of a group of people or the parts of a substance.

words.tr: n. 拼贴画；拼贴艺术；杂烩
words.ex: He made a collage from old magazine pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他用旧杂志的图片做了一幅拼贴画。
words.en: A collage is a picture that has been made by sticking pieces of colored paper, cloth, or photographs onto a surface.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: He collates the papers before the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议前整理了这些文件。
words.en: To collate information or data means to collect it together and examine it carefully in order to compare it or find something out.

words.ex: The car crash was a serious collision.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次严重的碰撞。
words.en: A collision occurs when two or more objects come into contact with each other, often resulting in damage or a change in direction.

words.ex: They had a quiet colloquy after class.
words.ex_cn: 他们课后进行了一次安静的交谈。
words.en: A colloquy is a formal conversation or dialogue.

words.ex: They collude to cheat in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他们串通在考试中作弊。
words.en: If one person colludes with another, they co-operate with them secretly or illegally.

words.ex: The colt runs fast across the field.
words.ex_cn: 小马在田野上快速奔跑。
words.en: A colt is a young male horse, especially one that is less than four years old.

words.ex: He fell into a coma after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故后陷入了昏迷。
words.en: A coma is a state of deep unconsciousness that lasts for a prolonged or indefinite period, caused especially by severe injury or illness.

words.tr: adj. 昏迷不醒的；不省人事的；困乏的
words.ex: The man became comatose after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，这个人陷入了昏迷。
words.en: If someone is comatose, they are in a coma and are not conscious.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.ex: She was a talented comedienne known for her witty performances.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位以机智表演著称的有才华的喜剧女演员。
words.en: A female comedian or comic actor.

words.ex: She is a comely girl with a sweet smile.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个面容姣好、带着甜美微笑的姑娘。
words.en: Pleasant to look at; attractive.

words.ex: The mushroom is comestible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这种蘑菇可食用且安全。
words.en: Something that is comestible is suitable or safe for eating.

words.tr: n. 应得的惩罚；因果报应
words.ex: He lied too much, and now he got his comeuppance.
words.ex_cn: 他撒了太多谎，现在遭到报应了。
words.en: A punishment or retribution that someone deserves.

words.ex: He wrote, 'I love apples, bananas, and oranges.'
words.ex_cn: 他写道：'我喜欢苹果、香蕉和橙子。'
words.en: A comma is a punctuation mark (,) used to indicate a pause or to separate items in a list.

words.ex: They plant trees to commemorate the fallen soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 他们种树以纪念阵亡的士兵。
words.en: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially created object.

words.ex: The class will commence at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程将在上午9点开始。
words.en: To begin something; to start.

words.tr: n. 开始；毕业典礼；学位授予典礼
words.ex: The commencement of the class was at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程的开始时间是上午9点。
words.en: The commencement of something is its beginning.

words.tr: v. 承诺；犯（罪、错）；（公开地）表达意见；
words.ex: He commit to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺帮助他的朋友。
words.en: To commit means to carry out or perpetrate a mistake, crime, or immoral act; or to pledge or bind oneself to a certain course of action.

words.ex: This is a commonplace event in big cities.
words.ex_cn: 这在大城市里是件普通的事。
words.en: Something that is commonplace is ordinary and not very interesting.

words.ex: He used common sense to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他用常识解决了这个问题。
words.en: Common sense is the natural ability to make good judgments and to behave in a practical and sensible way.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.ex: The company will compensate you for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 公司会因延误而补偿你。
words.en: If you compensate for a lack of something or for something you have done wrong, you do something to show that you are sorry or that you are trying to make things better.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.tr: n. 彬彬有礼；殷勤；奉承
words.ex: Her complaisance in the face of adversity was admirable.
words.ex_cn: 她在逆境中的顺从态度令人钦佩。
words.en: Willingness to please others by being polite and not causing any disagreement.

words.tr: adj. 殷勤的；顺从的；讨好的
words.ex: He was overly complaisant to his boss, always agreeing with everything he said.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板过于顺从，总是同意他说的每一件事。
words.en: Willing to please others; obliging; agreeable.

words.ex: He was accused of complicity in the theft.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控参与了这起盗窃案。
words.en: Complicity is involvement with other people in an illegal activity or wrongdoing.

words.ex: He compresses the file to save space.
words.ex_cn: 他压缩文件以节省空间。
words.en: To compress something means to press it or squeeze it so that it takes up less space.

words.tr: n. 强迫；强制；难以抗拒的冲动
words.ex: He felt a compulsion to check the door again.
words.ex_cn: 他感到一种必须再次检查门的强迫感。
words.en: A compulsion is a very strong desire to do something, which you find difficult to control.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是必须的。
words.en: If something is compulsory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.tr: n. 良心的责备；后悔；悔恨
words.ex: He felt no compunction about lying to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他撒谎骗朋友时毫无愧疚。
words.en: A feeling of guilt or moral scruple that prevents or follows the doing of something bad.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；欺骗
v. 欺骗；诈骗
words.ex: He fell for a con and lost all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他上了一个骗局的当，失去了所有钱。
words.en: If someone cons you, they persuade you to do something or believe something by telling you things that are not true.

words.ex: She concatenates two strings to make one word.
words.ex_cn: 她把两个字符串连接成一个单词。
words.en: To link things together in a chain or series.

words.ex: The spoon has a concave surface.
words.ex_cn: 勺子有一个凹的表面。
words.en: A concave surface is curved inward, like the inside of a bowl.

words.ex: His conceit makes him ignore others' advice.
words.ex_cn: 他的自负让他忽视别人的建议。
words.en: An excessively favorable opinion of one's own abilities or worth; vanity.

words.ex: He bought a concession ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了电影的减价票。
words.en: A concession is a point or principle that is granted or acknowledged in the course of an argument or negotiation, often as a compromise or to facilitate agreement.

words.tr: v. 安抚；讨好；使息怒；调和
words.ex: He tried to conciliate his angry neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他试图安抚他生气的邻居。
words.en: If you conciliate someone, you try to end a disagreement with them by doing or saying things that will make them less angry or more friendly.

words.ex: The concinnity of the poem pleased the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的和谐之美让老师很满意。
words.en: The quality of being harmonious or well-arranged in parts or details.

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: The two countries reached a concord on trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在贸易上达成了一致。
words.en: Concord is a state of agreement or harmony between people or groups.

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: He condescended to explain the simple math to his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他屈尊向弟弟解释了简单的数学。
words.en: If someone condescends to do something, they agree to do it in a way which shows that they think they are superior to the people they are doing it for.

words.ex: The punishment was condign for the crime committed.
words.ex_cn: 这个惩罚对于所犯的罪行来说是应得的。
words.en: Deserved; appropriate; fitting.

words.ex: She wrote a letter to condole with him on his loss.
words.ex_cn: 她写了一封信，对他的损失表示慰问。
words.en: To express sympathy or sorrow for someone who has experienced a misfortune or loss.

words.ex: A quiet room is conducive to studying.
words.ex_cn: 安静的房间有助于学习。
words.en: If one thing is conducive to another thing, it makes the other thing likely to happen.

words.ex: The confederacy fought against the union in the civil war.
words.ex_cn: 南方联盟在内战中与联邦作战。
words.en: A confederacy is a union of states or groups of people who have joined together for a common purpose or by a common agreement.

words.ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on him.
words.ex_cn: 大学授予他一个荣誉学位。
words.en: To confer something such as a degree or an honor on someone means to give it to them in a formal way. To confer with someone means to discuss something with them in order to make a decision.

words.ex: He confesses that he made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承认自己犯了一个错误。
words.en: If you confess to doing something, you admit that you did it.

words.ex: He is my confidant and I tell him everything.
words.ex_cn: 他是我的知己，我什么都告诉他。
words.en: A confidant is someone you can share your secrets with or discuss personal matters with, knowing that they will keep your information private.

words.ex: The document is confidential and cannot be shared.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件是机密的，不能分享。
words.en: If you talk to someone in a confidential way, you talk to them quietly because what you are saying is secret or private.

words.ex: The police confiscate illegal drugs.
words.ex_cn: 警察没收非法毒品。
words.en: If you confiscate something from someone, you take it away from them, usually as a punishment.

words.ex: The blood began to congeal on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 血液开始在地面上凝结。
words.en: If a liquid congeals, it becomes very thick and sticky and almost solid.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: He tries to conjoin the two pieces with glue.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用胶水把两块粘在一起。
words.en: If two or more things conjoin, they are joined or combined together.

words.ex: He listened to his conscience and told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他听从了良心，说出了真相。
words.en: Your conscience is the part of your mind that tells you whether what you are doing is right or wrong.

words.tr:
v. 征募；征召
n. 应征士兵
words.ex: He was conscripted into the army last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被征召入伍。
words.en: To conscript someone means to make them join the armed forces of a country, especially in a time of war.

words.tr: v. 奉为神圣；贡献；奉献
words.ex: They consecrate the church with prayer and song.
words.ex_cn: 他们用祈祷和歌声将教堂奉为神圣。
words.en: To consecrate something means to officially declare it to be holy and to be used for religious purposes.

words.ex: The team reached a consensus on the project plan.
words.ex_cn: 团队就项目计划达成了共识。
words.en: A consensus is general agreement among a group of people.

words.ex: He asked for her consent before starting the project.
words.ex_cn: 他在开始这个项目之前征求了她的同意。
words.en: Consent is permission for something to happen or agreement to do something.

words.ex: The decision was consequential for the future of the company.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来意义重大。
words.en: Something that is consequential is important or significant, often because it has effects on other things.

words.tr:
v. 安慰；慰问
n. 控制台；操纵台
words.ex: She whispered kind words to console her crying friend.
words.ex_cn: 她轻声说些安慰的话来安抚哭泣的朋友。
words.en: If you console someone who is unhappy about something, you try to make them feel more cheerful.

words.ex: The company will consolidate two departments next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将合并两个部门。
words.en: To consolidate something means to make it stronger, more secure, or more solid.

words.ex: The two notes sound consonance together.
words.ex_cn: 这两个音一起听起来很和谐。
words.en: Consonance refers to agreement or harmony between things or people, or the repetition of consonant sounds in poetry or music.

words.ex: The letter 'b' is a consonant.
words.ex_cn: 字母 'b' 是一个辅音。
words.en: A consonant is a speech sound that is articulated with complete or partial closure of the vocal tract.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.tr: n. 星座；一群杰出人物；一系列（相关的想法、事物）
words.ex: He saw the Orion constellation in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 他在夜空中看到了猎户座。
words.en: A constellation is a group of stars which form a pattern and have a name.

words.tr:
v. 建造；构造；
n. 概念；
words.ex: They construct houses with bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他们用砖块建造房屋。
words.en: To construct something means to build or create it, usually something large such as a building, road, or machine.

words.ex: The consul helped the tourist with a lost passport.
words.ex_cn: 领事帮助这位游客处理了遗失的护照。
words.en: A consul is an official appointed by a government to live in a foreign city and protect and promote the government's citizens and interests there.

words.ex: The box contains five apples.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子包含五个苹果。
words.en: If something such as a box, bag, room, or place contains things, those things are inside it.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.tr:
adj. 满足的
v. 使满足；“content”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt contented after a simple meal with his family.
words.ex_cn: 他和家人吃了一顿简单的饭后感到满足。
words.en: If you are contented, you are satisfied with your life or the situation you are in.

words.ex: He won the spelling contest.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了拼写比赛。
words.en: A contest is a competition or a struggle for victory between individuals or groups.

words.tr: adj. 相接的；相邻的；接壤的
words.ex: The two countries are contiguous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家是相邻的。
words.en: Being in contact; touching or next to each other.

words.ex: He contorts his face to make the kids laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他扭曲面部表情来逗孩子们笑。
words.en: If someone's face or body contorts or is contorted, it moves into an unnatural and unattractive shape or position.

words.ex: He controverts the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: To argue about (a subject) in a formal manner; to dispute or contradict.

words.tr: adj. 拒不服从的；藐视法庭的
words.ex: He was contumacious and refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他桀骜不驯，拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If someone is contumacious, they are stubbornly or willfully disobedient to authority.

words.tr: n. 拒不服从；藐视法庭
words.ex: His contumacy led to a contempt of court charge.
words.ex_cn: 他的拒不服从导致了他被指控藐视法庭。
words.en: Contumacy is the refusal to obey or comply with authority, often characterized by stubborn resistance or disobedience.

words.ex: He bore the contumely with dignity.
words.ex_cn: 他以尊严承受了侮辱。
words.en: Insolent or insulting language or treatment.

words.ex: No example sentences
words.ex_cn: 没有例句
words.en: A conundrum is a confusing and difficult problem or question.

words.ex: He is staying in a convalescent home to get better.
words.ex_cn: 他住在康复院里休养康复。
words.en: A convalescent person is someone who is recovering from an illness or medical treatment.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The convergent series gets closer to a final number.
words.ex_cn: 这个会聚级数逐渐接近一个最终数值。
words.en: Convergent refers to the process or state of coming together or moving toward union or uniformity, especially in the context of ideas, cultures, or scientific phenomena.

words.tr:
v. 定罪；宣判有罪
n. 罪犯；囚犯
words.ex: The court convicted him of theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院判定他犯有盗窃罪。
words.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

words.ex: The president convoked an emergency meeting.
words.ex_cn: 总统召集了一次紧急会议。
words.en: To call together for a meeting or assembly.

words.tr:
n. 护送；护航；护卫
v. 护航；护送
words.ex: The army sent a convoy to protect the trucks.
words.ex_cn: 军队派出护送队保护卡车。
words.en: A convoy is a group of vehicles or ships traveling together, typically accompanied by armed troops, warships, or other vehicles for protection.

words.ex: The nation was convulsed by political scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家因政治丑闻而剧烈震动。
words.en: If someone convulses or if they are convulsed by or with something, their body moves suddenly and violently, often in an uncontrolled way.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

words.ex: The coronation ceremony was a grand event.
words.ex_cn: 加冕典礼是一个盛大的活动。
words.en: A coronation is a ceremony in which a king or queen is officially crowned.

words.tr: adj. 物质的；有形的；实体的；身体的
words.ex: He believes that the soul is not corporeal.
words.ex_cn: 他相信灵魂不是物质的。
words.en: Relating to a person's body, especially as opposed to their spirit.

words.ex: The correspondent reported the news from the city.
words.ex_cn: 记者从城市报道了新闻。
words.en: A correspondent is someone who reports news from a particular place or on a particular subject for a newspaper, magazine, or television or radio station.

words.ex: The iron fence will corrode in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 铁栅栏在雨中会生锈。
words.en: If metal or stone corrodes, or if something corrodes it, it is gradually destroyed by a chemical reaction.

words.ex: The box is made from corrugated cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是由瓦楞纸板制成的。
words.en: To corrugate something means to shape it into parallel ridges and grooves.

words.tr:
adj. 缩成皱纹的；使起波状的
v. （使）起皱褶；“corrugate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The box is made of corrugated cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是由波纹纸板制成的。
words.en: Something that is corrugated has parallel rows of folds that look like a series of waves when viewed from the edge.

words.tr:
v. 使腐败；
adj. 腐败的；
words.ex: The official was corrupt by taking bribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员因收受贿赂而腐败。
words.en: If someone is corrupt, they do things that are dishonest or illegal in order to gain money or power.

words.ex: The stars coruscate in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中闪烁。
words.en: If something coruscates, it flashes, sparkles, or glitters brightly.

words.tr: n. 世界大同主义；四海一家
words.ex: He loves cosmopolitanism because he enjoys meeting people from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱世界主义，因为他喜欢结识来自许多国家的人。
words.en: The ideology that all human ethnic groups belong to a single community based on a shared morality.

words.ex: He loves to watch the cosmos at night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在夜晚观看宇宙。
words.en: The cosmos refers to the universe seen as a well-ordered whole, or to any system or structure that is complex and orderly.

words.tr:
v. 宠爱；娇养；纵容
n. 宠儿
words.ex: She cosseted her baby with soft blankets and gentle songs.
words.ex_cn: 她用柔软的毯子和轻柔的歌声呵护她的婴儿。
words.en: To cosset someone means to treat them with great care and attention, often in a way that is excessive or indulgent.

words.ex: He wore a funny costume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对穿了一套滑稽的服装。
words.en: A costume is a set of clothes in a style typical of a particular country or historical period, or a set of clothes worn by an actor for a particular role.

words.ex: The small room was cosy with a warm blanket and a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间铺着温暖的毯子，喝着热茶，非常舒适。
words.en: A place or situation that is cosy is comfortable and warm.

words.ex: The little cabin is cozy and warm.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋舒适又温暖。
words.en: A place that is cozy is comfortable and warm.

words.tr: adj. 有共同边界的； 毗连的
words.ex: The two regions are coterminous.
words.ex_cn: 这两个区域是边界相连的。
words.en: Having the same boundaries or limits; sharing a common border.

words.tr: adj. 像乡下的；乡土气息的；土里土气的
words.ex: He wears countrified clothes to the city party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着乡土风格的衣服去城市派对。
words.en: Having characteristics typical of the countryside; rustic or rural in nature.

words.ex: His sudden win in the race was a real coup.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中突然获胜，真是了不起的成就。
words.en: A coup is a sudden, violent, and illegal seizure of power from a government.

words.tr:
n. 协约；契约
v. 订立契约
words.ex: They made a covenant to always help each other.
words.ex_cn: 他们立下契约，永远互相帮助。
words.en: A covenant is a formal agreement or promise between two or more people, often involving legal obligations.

words.tr:
adj. 秘密的；隐蔽的
n. （动物可藏身的）小树丛
words.ex: He made a covert plan to leave without telling anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他秘密制定了一个不告诉任何人就离开的计划。
words.en: Covert activities or situations are secret or hidden.

words.ex: The farmer milks the cow every morning.
words.ex_cn: 农夫每天早上给母牛挤奶。
words.en: A cow is a large female animal that is kept on farms for its milk.

words.tr:
n. 懦夫；胆小鬼；胆怯者
adj. 胆小的；怯懦的
words.ex: He was a coward and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他是个懦夫，逃跑了。
words.en: A coward is someone who is easily frightened and avoids dangerous or difficult situations.

words.ex: The dog cowers when the thunder sounds.
words.ex_cn: 当雷声响起时，狗会蜷缩起来。
words.en: To crouch down in fear.

words.tr: adj. 腼腆的；怕羞的；忸怩的
words.ex: She gave a coy smile when asked about her new boyfriend.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及她的新男友时，她露出了腼腆的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as coy, you mean they are pretending to be shy about something in order to attract attention or to deceive people.

words.ex: He cozens his friend into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他哄骗朋友借给他钱。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.ex: He caught a crab at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在海滩上抓到一只蟹。
words.en: A crab is a sea creature with a flat round body covered by a shell, and five pairs of legs with large claws on the front pair. Crabs usually move sideways.

words.ex: His crabbed handwriting made it hard to read the note.
words.ex_cn: 他难辨认的笔迹让这张便条很难阅读。
words.en: If you describe someone's writing or behavior as crabbed, you mean that it is small and difficult to read or understand, often because it is written in a very small space.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；噼啪声；
v. 破裂；
words.ex: There is a small crack in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: If something hard cracks, or if you crack it, it becomes slightly damaged, with lines appearing on its surface.

words.tr:
adj. 古怪的；离奇的；不切实际的
n. 怪人；狂徒
words.ex: He is a crackpot who believes the Earth is flat.
words.ex_cn: 他是个疯子，相信地球是平的。
words.en: If you describe someone as a crackpot, you mean that their ideas or behaviour are strange or crazy.

words.ex: The crafty fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone as crafty, you mean they are clever at achieving their aims by indirect or deceitful methods.

words.tr:
n. 抽筋；痉挛；夹钳
v. 束缚；使痉挛；用夹钳夹紧
words.ex: He got a cramp in his leg while running.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑步时腿抽筋了。
words.en: A cramp is a sudden, involuntary muscle contraction or over-shortening; while generally temporary and non-damaging, they can cause mild-to-severe pain, and a paralysis-like immobility of the affected muscle.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；暴躁的；有毛病的
words.ex: He is cranky when he doesn't sleep well.
words.ex_cn: 他睡眠不好时会脾气暴躁。
words.en: If you describe someone as cranky, you mean they are bad-tempered and irritable.

words.ex: His crass joke made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他愚蠢的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as crass, you mean they are so stupid and insensitive that they offend you.

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.ex: The witness gave credence to the story by crying.
words.ex_cn: 证人通过哭泣使这个故事显得可信。
words.en: Credence is a belief in or acceptance of something as true.

words.ex: His credo is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A credo is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way a person lives or works.

words.ex: The cat creeps slowly toward the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹑手蹑脚地向鸟靠近。
words.en: To move slowly and quietly, especially in a way that does not attract attention.

words.tr: adj. 拂晓的；黄昏的；朦胧的
words.ex: The rabbit is crepuscular, so it comes out at dawn and dusk.
words.ex_cn: 这只兔子是晨昏活动的，所以它在黎明和黄昏时出来。
words.en: Relating to or resembling twilight; dim or indistinct.

words.tr: n. 声音渐增；高潮；顶峰
words.ex: The music reached a loud crescendo at the end.
words.ex_cn: 音乐在结尾处达到响亮的高潮。
words.en: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness or intensity in music, or any situation where there is a gradual increase in intensity.

words.tr:
n. 饲料槽；有栏小卧床
v. 抄袭
words.ex: The horse eats hay from the crib.
words.ex_cn: 马从饲料槽里吃干草。
words.en: A crib is a bed with high sides for a baby or very young child. It can also mean to copy someone else's work and present it as your own.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.ex: The crudity of his speech surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他言语的粗俗让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being crude in manner or expression; lack of sophistication or refinement.

words.ex: A crumb fell on the table after he ate the bread.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完面包后，掉了一小块碎屑在桌子上。
words.en: A crumb is a very small piece of bread, cake, or biscuit.

words.ex: The old wall began to crumble after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 旧墙在雨后开始坍塌。
words.en: If something crumbles, or if you crumble it, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: He joined a crusade for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了一场为清洁用水而发起的运动。
words.en: A crusade is a long and determined attempt to achieve something that you strongly believe in, especially to bring about social or political change.

words.ex: The child played with a wooden cube.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩了一个木制立方体。
words.en: A cube is a solid object with six square faces which are all the same size.

words.ex: She cuddles her baby every night.
words.ex_cn: 她每天晚上都拥抱她的宝宝。
words.en: To hold someone or something close in your arms as a way of showing love or affection.

words.ex: The teacher gave a cue to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了开始游戏的提示。
words.en: A cue is a signal for someone to do something, or a piece of information that helps someone to understand something.

words.tr: v. 挑出（老弱动物）杀死；
words.ex: Farmers cull weak sheep to keep the herd healthy.
words.ex_cn: 农民挑出虚弱的羊杀死，以保持羊群健康。
words.en: To cull animals means to kill the weaker animals in a group in order to reduce their numbers or to prevent them from spreading disease.

words.ex: The concert was the culmination of his music career.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会是他音乐生涯的顶点。
words.en: The culmination of something is the highest or final point of it, often after a long period of development.

words.ex: The police caught the culprit who stole the bike.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了偷自行车的罪犯。
words.en: A culprit is someone who has done something wrong or illegal.

words.ex: Some people follow that cult blindly.
words.ex_cn: 有些人盲目追随那个狂热崇拜。
words.en: A cult is a group of people who have extreme admiration for a particular person, idea, or thing, often following unusual or extreme practices or beliefs.

words.ex: Farmers cultivate rice in the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植水稻。
words.en: To cultivate land means to prepare it and grow crops on it. To cultivate a particular quality, skill, or attitude means to try hard to develop it and make it stronger.

words.tr: adj. 栽培的；耕作的； v. 栽培；“cultivate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The cultivated vegetables taste better than wild ones.
words.ex_cn: 栽培的蔬菜比野生的更好吃。
words.en: If you describe someone as cultivated, you mean they are well educated and have good manners.

words.ex: The heavy snow cumbered our progress.
words.ex_cn: 大雪阻碍了我们的前进。
words.en: To hinder or obstruct the movement or progress of someone or something.

words.tr:
adj. 狡猾的；奸诈的；巧妙的
n. 奸诈；狡猾
words.ex: The cunning fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is cunning is clever and good at deceiving others in order to get what they want.

words.ex: His cupidity led him to make risky investments.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪导致他进行了高风险的投资。
words.en: Intense desire for wealth or possessions; greed.

words.ex: The curator arranged the paintings in the museum.
words.ex_cn: 馆长在博物馆里布置了这些画作。
words.en: A curator is someone who is in charge of the objects or works of art in a museum or art gallery.

words.ex: The milk curdled when it was left out too long.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶放置太久后凝固了。
words.en: If a liquid curdles, or if you curdle it, it develops lumps and becomes thicker, often as a result of a chemical change.

words.ex: The city has a curfew at 10 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市晚上10点实行宵禁。
words.en: A curfew is an order given by the authorities that people must stay indoors between certain hours, typically at night.

words.ex: She placed the cutlery neatly on the table.
words.ex_cn: 她把餐具整齐地放在桌子上。
words.en: Cutlery refers to the tools used for eating or serving food, such as knives, forks, and spoons.

words.ex: The cyclone destroyed many houses near the coast.
words.ex_cn: 气旋摧毁了沿海的许多房屋。
words.en: A cyclone is a violent tropical storm in which the air goes round and round.

words.tr: n. 愤世嫉俗者；悲观者；怀疑者
words.ex: He is a cynic who never believes in good intentions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个不相信任何善意的愤世嫉俗者。
words.en: A cynic is someone who believes that people are motivated purely by self-interest rather than acting for honorable or unselfish reasons.

words.tr: n. 注意的焦点； 引人注目的事物；北极星
words.ex: The new museum became the cynosure of all eyes in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这座新博物馆成为全城瞩目的焦点。
words.en: A cynosure is someone or something that is the center of attention or admiration.

words.ex: He likes to dabble in various hobbies.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢涉猎各种爱好。
words.en: If you dabble in something, you take part in it but not very seriously.

words.tr: adj. 愚笨的；癫狂的；痴傻的
words.ex: He wore a daft hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶傻气的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as daft, you mean that they are silly, foolish, or crazy.

words.ex: She wore a dainty necklace with tiny pearls.
words.ex_cn: 她戴了一条小巧精致的珍珠项链。
words.en: If you describe something as dainty, you mean that it is small, delicate, and pretty.

words.tr: n. （短暂的）情事；调情；短暂参与
words.ex: He had a short dalliance with a singer.
words.ex_cn: 他与一位歌手有过一段短暂的恋情。
words.en: Dalliance refers to a casual involvement with something, especially a romantic or sexual relationship, without serious intentions.

words.tr: v. 浪费时间；拖延；玩弄；调情
words.ex: He dallys with his homework instead of finishing it.
words.ex_cn: 他浪费时间在作业上，而不是完成它。
words.en: To dally means to act or move slowly, or to spend time idly or in trifling.

words.tr:
adj. 该死的；可恶的；糟透的
v. 咒骂（某人下地狱）
words.ex: It's a damn good idea.
words.ex_cn: 这是个该死的好主意。
words.en: If you say that someone is damned if they do something, you mean that they will be in a very difficult situation if they do it.

words.ex: The ground is damp after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后地面是潮湿的。
words.en: Something that is damp is slightly wet, often in a way that is unpleasant.

words.ex: The keys dangle from his belt.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙挂在他的腰带上。
words.en: If something dangles from somewhere or if you dangle it somewhere, it hangs or swings loosely.

words.ex: The basement was dank and cold.
words.ex_cn: 地下室又潮又冷。
words.en: Unpleasantly damp and cold.

words.tr: adj. 衣冠楚楚的；干净利落的；短小精悍的
words.ex: He was a dapper man, always impeccably dressed.
words.ex_cn: 他是个衣冠楚楚的人，总是穿着无可挑剔。
words.en: If you describe a man as dapper, you mean that he is small and neat in appearance and moves quickly and energetically.

words.tr:
adj. 蛮勇的；鲁莽大胆的
n. 鲁莽大胆的人
words.ex: He is a daredevil rider who jumps over cars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个蛮勇的骑手，会跳过汽车。
words.en: A daredevil is someone who enjoys doing dangerous things and taking risks.

words.ex: Add a dash of salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 给汤里加一点盐。
words.en: If you dash somewhere, you run or go there quickly and suddenly. A dash is a straight, horizontal line used in writing, for example to separate two main clauses whose meanings are closely connected.

words.ex: She daubed the wall with paint.
words.ex_cn: 她在墙上随意涂抹颜料。
words.en: To daub means to spread a substance such as paint, mud, or oil over a surface in a rough or careless way.

words.ex: He dawdled away the afternoon at the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里混掉了整个下午。
words.en: If you dawdle, you spend more time than is necessary going somewhere or doing something.

words.tr:
v. 使发昏；使迷乱
n. 恍惚； 晕眩
words.ex: The loud noise dazed him for a moment.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他一时发昏。
words.en: If someone is in a daze, they are feeling confused and unable to think clearly, often because they have had a shock or surprise.

words.tr: v. 缓和；减弱（感觉）；降低（声音）
words.ex: The noise deadened after the door closed.
words.ex_cn: 门关上后，噪音减弱了。
words.en: If something deadens a feeling or a sound, it makes it less strong or loud.

words.ex: The two teams are in a deadlock over the budget.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队在预算上陷入了僵局。
words.en: A deadlock is a situation in which no progress can be made or no agreement is reached, especially because of a disagreement between two or more parties.

words.ex: He was debarred from entering the building.
words.ex_cn: 他被禁止进入那栋楼。
words.en: To officially prevent someone from doing something or from entering a place.

words.tr: v. 卸货；（使）下船（或飞机，车等）
words.ex: The passengers began to debark as soon as the ship docked.
words.ex_cn: 船一靠岸，乘客们就开始下船。
words.en: To leave a ship or airplane; to disembark.

words.ex: His debility was due to a long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱是由于长期患病。
words.en: Debility is a state of physical weakness, especially as a result of illness.

words.tr: adj. 潇洒的；风度翩翩的；温文尔雅的
words.ex: He had a debonair manner that put everyone at ease.
words.ex_cn: 他温文尔雅的举止让每个人都感到轻松自在。
words.en: A debonair man is charming, confident, and stylish, especially in his behavior and appearance.

words.tr: v. 听取（执行任务的）情况汇报
words.ex: The officer was debriefed after returning from the mission.
words.ex_cn: 这名军官在任务返回后接受了盘问。
words.en: To question someone in order to obtain information, especially after a mission or task.

words.ex: The storm left debris on the road.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在道路上留下了碎片。
words.en: The remains of something that has been destroyed or broken up.

words.ex: The scientist debunked the myth that sugar makes children hyper.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家揭穿了糖会使孩子多动的谬论。
words.en: If you debunk a widely held belief, you show that it is false. If you debunk something that is widely admired, you show that it is not as good as people think it is.

words.tr: v. 离营；匆忙秘密地离开
words.ex: The soldiers decamp at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在黎明时撤离。
words.en: To leave a place suddenly or secretly.

words.tr: v. 倾注（移入其他容器）
words.ex: He carefully decanted the wine into the decanter.
words.ex_cn: 他小心地把酒倒入醒酒器中。
words.en: To pour a liquid from one container into another, especially without disturbing the sediment.

words.ex: His deceit made his friends lose trust in him.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗让朋友们失去了对他的信任。
words.en: Deceit is behaviour that is intended to make someone believe something that is not true.

words.ex: He showed decency by helping the old man.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助那位老人，表现出了礼貌和善良。
words.en: Decency is behaviour that is considered to be polite, moral, and acceptable.

words.ex: The company wants to decentralize its operations.
words.ex_cn: 公司希望将运营去中心化。
words.en: To decentralize means to distribute the administrative functions or powers of (a central authority) over a less concentrated area.

words.ex: His deception fooled everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗骗过了派对上的所有人。
words.en: Deception is the act of deceiving someone or the state of being deceived.

words.tr: v. 慷慨陈词；高声朗诵
words.ex: He likes to declaim poetry in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在全班面前朗诵诗歌。
words.en: To declaim means to speak or recite something in a dramatic or impassioned way, often in public.

words.ex: The decomposition of the apple took weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果的分解花了几个星期。
words.en: Decomposition is the process by which organic substances are broken down into simpler organic or inorganic matter such as carbon dioxide, water, simple sugars and mineral salts.

words.tr:
n. 诱饵；（诱捕鸟兽的）动物
v. 引诱
words.ex: The hunter used a decoy to attract ducks.
words.ex_cn: 猎人用假鸭子来吸引鸭子。
words.en: A decoy is a person, thing, or action that is used to trick someone into doing something or going somewhere, especially by making them think they are going to get something they want.

words.tr:
n. 法令；判决
v. 判决；颁布；裁定
words.ex: The king issued a decree to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An official order issued by a legal authority.

words.ex: His dedication to teaching helped many students succeed.
words.ex_cn: 他对教学的奉献帮助了许多学生取得成功。
words.en: The act of dedicating or the state of being dedicated; commitment.

words.ex: He can deduce the answer from the clues.
words.ex_cn: 他能从线索中推断出答案。
words.en: If you deduce something or deduce that something is true, you reach that conclusion because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: He deducts tax from his salary every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每月从工资中扣除税款。
words.en: If you deduct an amount from a total, you subtract it from the total.

words.ex: He uses deductive reasoning to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他使用演绎推理来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Deductive reasoning is a logical process in which a conclusion is based on the concordance of multiple premises that are generally assumed to be true.

words.ex: He is tired, and indeed he fell asleep quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很累，的确很快就睡着了。
words.en: You use indeed to confirm or agree with something that has just been said.

words.tr: v. 损伤…的外观；在…上乱涂乱画
words.ex: They deface the wall with graffiti.
words.ex_cn: 他们用涂鸦破坏了墙壁。
words.en: To deface something means to spoil its appearance by writing or drawing on it, or by damaging it in some other way.

words.tr: v. 诽谤；中伤；损毁名誉
words.ex: He tried to defame his rival with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用虚假的故事诋毁他的竞争对手。
words.en: To defame someone means to damage their reputation by saying or writing bad things about them that are not true.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.tr:
v. 弄脏；亵渎；玷污
n. 小道；狭谷
words.ex: They defile the river with trash.
words.ex_cn: 他们用垃圾污染了这条河。
words.en: To defile something means to make it dirty or impure. As a noun, it refers to a narrow pass or gorge between mountains.

words.ex: The mirror deflects the light to the wall.
words.ex_cn: 镜子把光线反射到墙上。
words.en: If you deflect something such as criticism or attention, you act in a way that prevents it from being directed towards you or affecting you.

words.ex: He tried to defraud the bank with a fake check.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一张假支票诈骗银行。
words.en: If someone defrauds you, they take something away from you or stop you from getting what is rightfully yours by deceiving you.

words.ex: The company agreed to defray the travel expenses.
words.ex_cn: 公司同意支付差旅费。
words.en: If you defray someone's costs or expenses, you give them money which represents the amount that they have spent, for example while they have been doing something for you or acting on your behalf.

words.ex: The police helped to defuse the situation.
words.ex_cn: 警察帮助减少了危险。
words.en: To remove the fuse from (an explosive device) in order to prevent it from exploding; to reduce the danger or tension in (a situation).

words.tr:
adj. 沮丧的；低落的；垂头丧气的
v. 使…情绪低落；使沮丧；“deject”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He felt dejected after failing the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格后感到沮丧。
words.en: If you are dejected, you feel miserable or unhappy, especially because you have just been disappointed by something.

words.ex: He felt delectation while eating the sweet cake.
words.ex_cn: 他吃甜蛋糕时感到愉悦。
words.en: Delectation is a feeling of great pleasure and enjoyment.

words.ex: The manager will delegate the task to her assistant.
words.ex_cn: 经理将把这个任务委派给她的助手。
words.en: A delegate is a person who is chosen or elected to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of people, especially at a conference or a meeting. As a verb, to delegate means to give a task or responsibility to another person, especially someone who is less senior than you.

words.tr: adj. 精致的；微妙的；易碎的；脆弱的；
words.ex: She wore a delicate lace dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一条精致的蕾丝连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: Something that is delicate is small and beautifully shaped. It can also be easily broken or damaged.

words.tr:
adj. 失职的；违法的；拖欠债务的
n. 违犯者；少年罪犯；违法者
words.ex: The delinquent worker ignored his duties.
words.ex_cn: 这位失职的员工忽视了他的职责。
words.en: A delinquent is someone, especially a young person, who commits a crime or breaks the law.

words.tr: n. 精神错乱；谵妄；极度兴奋
words.ex: The patient was in a state of delirium after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术后，病人处于精神错乱的状态。
words.en: A state of wild excitement or mental confusion, often accompanied by hallucinations.

words.ex: He has a delusion that he is a famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种错觉，认为自己是一位著名歌手。
words.en: A delusion is a belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by what is generally accepted as reality or rational argument, typically a symptom of mental disorder.

words.ex: He stayed in a deluxe room at the hotel.
words.ex_cn: 他住在酒店的豪华房间里。
words.en: If you describe something as deluxe, you mean that it is very luxurious and expensive.

words.ex: He delves into the history of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他探究古代文明的历史。
words.en: If you delve into something, you try to discover new information about it by searching or investigating carefully.

words.tr: n. 煽动者；蛊惑民心的政客
words.ex: The politician is a demagogue who uses angry words to win votes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客是一个煽动者，用愤怒的言辞赢得选票。
words.en: A demagogue is a political leader who seeks support by appealing to popular desires and prejudices rather than by using rational argument.

words.ex: The treaty will demarcate the new borders between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 条约将划定两国之间的新边界。
words.en: To set the boundaries or limits of something.

words.ex: His calm demeanour surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他冷静的举止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Demeanour refers to the way in which a person behaves towards others; their outward behaviour or bearing.

words.tr: adj. 发狂的；精神错乱状态的
words.ex: The demented man laughed loudly in the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个精神失常的男人在街上大声笑。
words.en: Someone who is demented behaves in a wild and uncontrolled way because they are mentally ill.

words.tr: n. 摧毁；拆毁；拆除；大败；
words.ex: The demolition of the old building started last week.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧楼的拆除上周开始了。
words.en: The act of demolishing something, especially a building.

words.tr:
adj. 明白表示的；证实的；公然表示情绪的
n. 指示词
words.ex: He is demonstrative with his love for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他对家人表达爱意时很外露。
words.en: If you are demonstrative, you show your feelings or behave in a way that shows your love for someone.

words.tr: v. 使士气低落；使失去斗志
words.ex: The bad news demoralized the team.
words.ex_cn: 这个坏消息使团队士气低落。
words.en: If something demoralizes someone, it makes them lose so much confidence in what they are doing that they want to give up.

words.ex: The manager decided to demote him for poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 经理因他表现不佳决定降职他。
words.en: If someone is demoted, they are given a lower rank or a less important position than they had before.

words.tr: adj. 娴静的；端庄的；假装矜持的
words.ex: She is a demure girl who never speaks loudly.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个文静的女孩，从不大声说话。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially a young woman, as demure, you mean they are quiet, shy, and behave so that they do not attract attention to themselves.

words.ex: The lion returned to its den at night.
words.ex_cn: 狮子晚上回到了它的兽穴。
words.en: A den is the home of certain types of wild animals such as lions or foxes, or a place where someone feels safe and private.

words.ex: He wears dentures to eat food.
words.ex_cn: 他戴假牙来吃东西。
words.en: Dentures are artificial teeth worn by people who have lost their own teeth.

words.ex: The storm denuded the trees of their leaves.
words.ex_cn: 风暴把树上的叶子都刮掉了。
words.en: To strip something of its covering, possessions, or assets; to make bare.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: The politician was quick to denunciate the corruption in the government.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家迅速谴责了政府中的腐败现象。
words.en: To denunciate means to publicly declare to be wrong or evil.

words.ex: The prisoners suffered from sleep deprivation.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯们因睡眠剥夺而受苦。
words.en: Deprivation is the lack or denial of something considered to be a necessity.

words.ex: He will depute his assistant to attend the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他将委派他的助手去参加会议。
words.en: To appoint or assign someone to perform a task or duty on one's behalf.

words.tr: v. 担任代表；充当代理人
words.ex: He had to deputize for the manager while she was on leave.
words.ex_cn: 经理休假期间，他不得不代理她的职务。
words.en: To appoint someone as a deputy; to delegate authority to someone to act on one's behalf.

words.ex: The deputy signed the document for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 代理人替经理签署了文件。
words.en: A deputy is a person who is appointed to act as a substitute for another, especially in a position of authority.

words.ex: The government's policy aimed to deracinate the rebel group.
words.ex_cn: 政府的政策旨在根除叛乱组织。
words.en: To deracinate someone or something means to remove them from their natural environment or culture, especially in a way that causes them to lose their identity or characteristics.

words.tr: n. 荒废；弃置；玩忽职守
words.ex: The dereliction of duty by the officer led to a serious breach of security.
words.ex_cn: 这名官员的玩忽职守导致了一次严重的安全漏洞。
words.en: The act of abandoning or neglecting something, especially a duty or responsibility.

words.ex: The derivation of this word is from Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这个词的起源是拉丁语。
words.en: Derivation refers to the process by which a word is formed from another word or from a root, especially by the addition of an affix.

words.ex: He never derogates his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他从不贬低他的同事。
words.en: To derogate means to take away from something, especially in a way that is unfair or undeserved. It can also mean to detract from the value or importance of something.

words.ex: The camel walks across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 骆驼穿越沙漠。
words.en: A desert is a large area of land that has very little water and very few plants growing on it. Many deserts are covered by sand. If you desert someone or something, you leave them and no longer help or support them.

words.tr: n. 背弃者；逃兵；擅离职守者
words.ex: He was branded as a deserter after abandoning his post.
words.ex_cn: 他因擅离职守而被视为逃兵。
words.en: A deserter is a person who leaves their job, duty, post, or obligation without permission, especially a soldier who leaves the army without permission.

words.ex: The sun will desiccate the leaves in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天阳光会把叶子晒干。
words.en: To remove the moisture from something, typically in order to preserve it.

words.tr: n. 所愿望之物；迫切需要之物
words.ex: A clean environment is the desideratum for a healthy society.
words.ex_cn: 清洁的环境是健康社会的迫切需要之物。
words.en: Something that is needed or wanted.

words.ex: He must desist from cheating on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他必须停止在考试中作弊。
words.en: If you desist from doing something, you stop doing it.

words.ex: The desert looks desolate and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠看起来荒凉而空旷。
words.en: If you describe a place as desolate, you mean that it is empty and looks sad because there are no people there or because it has been damaged.

words.ex: He despises lying.
words.ex_cn: 他鄙视撒谎。
words.en: If you despise something or someone, you dislike them and have a very low opinion of them.

words.tr: v. 抢劫；掠夺；蹂躏；破坏
words.ex: The invaders despoiled the village.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者抢劫了村庄。
words.en: To despoil something means to steal from it or damage it, especially in a violent or destructive way.

words.ex: The despotic king ruled with fear.
words.ex_cn: 这位专制的国王用恐惧统治。
words.en: If you say that someone is despotic, you are emphasizing that they use their power over other people in a very unfair or cruel way.

words.tr: n. 专制统治；独裁制；暴政
words.ex: The king ruled with despotism.
words.ex_cn: 国王以专制统治。
words.en: Despotism is a form of government in which a single entity rules with absolute power. The ruling entity may be an individual, as in an autocracy, or a group, as in an oligarchy.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.ex: The charity aims to alleviate destitution among the elderly.
words.ex_cn: 该慈善机构旨在减轻老年人的贫困。
words.en: Destitution is the state of having no money or possessions.

words.tr: adj. 可破坏的；易被摧毁的
words.ex: The building was made of destructible materials.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑是用易损坏的材料建造的。
words.en: Capable of being destroyed.

words.ex: The old law fell into desuetude.
words.ex_cn: 这项旧法律逐渐被废弃了。
words.en: The state of being no longer used or practiced.

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.tr: n. 洗涤剂；洗衣粉；去垢剂；
words.ex: She uses detergent to wash the clothes.
words.ex_cn: 她用洗涤剂洗衣服。
words.en: A detergent is a substance that is used for cleaning things, especially clothes and dishes.

words.ex: The bomb will detonate at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹将在午夜爆炸。
words.en: To detonate something means to cause it to explode.

words.ex: The detonation of the bomb caused widespread destruction.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹的爆炸造成了大范围的破坏。
words.en: A detonation is a large or powerful explosion.

words.ex: His comment was pure detraction.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论完全是诽谤。
words.en: Detraction refers to the act of taking away from the value or reputation of something or someone, often through criticism or slander.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: He devised a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他设计了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: To devise something means to plan or invent a new way of doing something.

words.tr: n. 爱好者；热衷者；信徒
words.ex: He is a music devotee and listens to songs every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是音乐爱好者，每天都听歌曲。
words.en: A devotee is a person who is very interested in and enthusiastic about someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 虔诚的；献身的；宗教仪式的
words.ex: She spent her mornings in devotional prayer.
words.ex_cn: 她早上用来进行虔诚的祷告。
words.en: Devotional activities or writings are related to religious worship or prayer.

words.ex: The surgeon's dexterity saved the patient's life.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生的灵巧救了病人的命。
words.en: Skill and grace in physical movement, especially in the use of the hands; adroitness.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.ex: The teacher drew a diagram to explain the water cycle.
words.ex_cn: 老师画了一个图表来解释水循环。
words.en: A diagram is a simple drawing which consists mainly of lines and is used, for example, to explain how a machine works.

words.ex: The diaphanous curtain let in the morning light.
words.ex_cn: 那层薄纱窗帘让晨光透了进来。
words.en: A diaphanous substance or fabric is very thin and almost transparent.

words.ex: He gave a loud diatribe against the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他对新法律发表了一通激烈的抨击。
words.en: A diatribe is an angry speech or piece of writing that strongly criticizes something or someone.

words.tr:
v. 讨价还价；争执（小问题）
n. 小生意
words.ex: He dickered with the seller over the price.
words.ex_cn: 他和卖家就价格讨价还价。
words.en: To dicker means to argue or haggle, especially over the terms of a transaction or agreement.

words.ex: The dictator ruled the country for many years.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者统治这个国家很多年。
words.en: A dictator is a ruler who has complete power in a country, especially when this power has been obtained by force and is used unfairly or cruelly.

words.tr: n. 宣言；声明；格言；警句
words.ex: The judge's dictum was clear and final.
words.ex_cn: 法官的宣言清晰而最终。
words.en: A dictum is a formal pronouncement from an authoritative source; it can also be a short statement that expresses a general truth or principle.

words.ex: Can you differentiate between the two colors?
words.ex_cn: 你能区分这两种颜色吗？
words.en: To differentiate means to recognize or express the difference between things or people.

words.tr:
v. 弥漫；
adj. 分散的；
words.ex: Smoke began to diffuse through the room.
words.ex_cn: 烟开始弥漫在整个房间里。
words.en: If something such as knowledge or information is diffused, or if it diffuses, it is made known over a wide area or to a lot of people.

words.ex: Good digestion helps your body absorb nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 良好的消化有助于身体吸收营养。
words.en: The process by which food is broken down in the stomach and intestines so that the body can absorb it and use it for energy and nutrients.

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.ex: He digresses when he talks about his vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他谈论假期时会跑题。
words.en: If you digress, you move away from the subject you are talking or writing about and talk or write about something different for a while.

words.ex: He made a digression to tell a funny story.
words.ex_cn: 他岔开话题讲了个有趣的故事。
words.en: A digression is a temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.

words.ex: The old house dilapidated after years of no care.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子因多年无人照料而荒废了。
words.en: To cause or allow (a building or structure) to fall into a state of disrepair or ruin, as by misuse or neglect.

words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.ex: He shows diligence in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天认真完成作业。
words.en: Conscientiousness in paying proper attention to a task; giving the degree of care required in a given situation.

words.tr: v. 闲混；磨蹭；三心二意地浪费时间
words.ex: He dillydallys instead of doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他拖延而不做作业。
words.en: To waste time, especially by being slow, or by not being able to make a decision.

words.tr:
adj. 暗淡的；昏暗的；模糊的
v. （使）变暗淡；（使）变模糊；（使）减弱
words.ex: The room is dim because the lights are off.
words.ex_cn: 房间很暗，因为灯关了。
words.en: If a light or a place is dim, it is not bright or is not lit very strongly.

words.ex: He has a dimple when he smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他笑的时候有一个酒窝。
words.en: A dimple is a small natural indentation in the flesh on a part of the human body, especially one formed in the cheeks when someone smiles.

words.tr: adj. 又黑又脏的；昏暗的；肮脏的
words.ex: The room was dingy and small.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间又脏又小。
words.en: If you describe a place or thing as dingy, you mean that it is rather dull and depressing to look at, and perhaps also dirty.

words.ex: The car's fender showed a dint from the collision.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的挡泥板因碰撞而出现了一个凹痕。
words.en: If you achieve something by dint of a particular quality or action, you achieve it by means of that quality or action.

words.ex: The weather was dire, with heavy rain and strong winds.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常可怕，下着大雨，刮着大风。
words.en: If you describe a situation as dire, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or serious.

words.ex: The new policy has disaffected many of the employees.
words.ex_cn: 新政策使许多员工感到不满。
words.en: If something disaffects someone, it makes them lose their affection or loyalty towards a person or organization.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a big disaster.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了一场大灾难。
words.en: A disaster is an unexpected event causing great damage, destruction, or distress.

words.ex: He disavow any connection to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 他否认与这起犯罪有任何关联。
words.en: If you disavow something, you say that you are not responsible for it or you do not agree with it.

words.ex: The bank will disburse the loan next week.
words.ex_cn: 银行将在下周发放贷款。
words.en: To disburse means to pay out money from a fund or account.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.tr: v. 否认；放弃；拒绝承认
words.ex: He disclaims any responsibility for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他否认对这个错误负有任何责任。
words.en: If you disclaim knowledge of something or disclaim responsibility for something, you say that you did not know about it or are not responsible for it.

words.ex: He refused to disclose the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝透露这个秘密。
words.en: To disclose information means to make it known to the public.

words.tr:
adj. 打乱的；混乱的； 扰乱的
v. 使混乱； 扰乱；“discombobulate”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She felt discombobulated after losing her keys.
words.ex_cn: 她丢了钥匙后感到非常困惑。
words.en: If you are discombobulated, you are confused and cannot think clearly, often because you have been surprised or upset by something.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.tr: adj. 自由决定的；酌情行事的；便宜行事的
words.ex: He spent his discretionary money on a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的可自由支配的钱花在了一部新手机上。
words.en: If something is discretionary, it is available for use as someone chooses, rather than according to a set plan or rule.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.tr:
adj. 脱离肉体的；无实体的；不具形体的
v. 使脱离肉体；“disembody”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The voice sounded disembodied, echoing through the empty room.
words.ex_cn: 那声音听起来空洞无物，在空荡的房间里回响。
words.en: If you describe a voice or a form as disembodied, you mean that it is not connected to a physical body.

words.tr: v. 使不抱幻想；使不再着迷；使醒悟
words.ex: The truth disenchant him about his hero.
words.ex_cn: 真相让他对他的偶像不再抱有幻想。
words.en: If you are disenchanted with something, you are disappointed with it and no longer believe that it is good or worthwhile.

words.tr: v. 解开；分离；使解脱；脱离战斗
words.ex: He tried to disengage from the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从争论中抽身。
words.en: To disengage means to separate or detach oneself from something or someone, or to release from a connection or obligation.

words.tr: v. 解开；解脱；解决（纠纷等）
words.ex: He tried to disentangle the tangled wires.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把缠在一起的电线解开。
words.en: To free something or someone from being tangled or twisted, or to separate things that are twisted together.

words.tr: v. 损毁…的外形；使变丑
words.ex: The accident disfigured his face.
words.ex_cn: 那次事故使他的脸变形了。
words.en: To disfigure someone or something means to spoil their appearance.

words.ex: The new law disfranchised many citizens.
words.ex_cn: 新法律剥夺了许多公民的选举权。
words.en: To deprive someone of a privilege, right, or power, especially the right to vote.

words.ex: The long wait disgruntles the customers.
words.ex_cn: 漫长的等待让顾客感到不满。
words.en: If you are disgruntled, you are angry or dissatisfied because something has not happened the way you wanted.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.
