words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.ex: The doctor used a germicide to clean the wound.
words.ex_cn: 医生用杀菌剂清洁了伤口。
words.en: A germicide is a substance that kills germs, especially pathogenic microorganisms.

words.tr: n. 老人统治；老人政治；老人政府
words.ex: The village was ruled by a gerontocracy, with all major decisions made by the eldest members.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄由一群老人统治，所有重大决策都由最年长的成员做出。
words.en: A gerontocracy is a society, organization, or group that is governed by old people.

words.ex: The artist gestated the idea for years before finally creating the masterpiece.
words.ex_cn: 这位艺术家孕育这个想法多年后，最终创作出了杰作。
words.en: To carry a developing embryo or fetus within the womb; to develop an idea or plan in the mind.

words.ex: He gesticulates when he talks about his travels.
words.ex_cn: 当他谈论旅行时，他会用手势示意。
words.en: If you gesticulate, you make movements with your arms and hands, usually while you are describing something that is difficult to express in words.

words.ex: He made a gesture of welcome with his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他用手做了一个欢迎的姿态。
words.en: A gesture is a movement that you make with a part of your body, especially your hands, to express emotion or information.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯地笑
n. 咯咯笑；趣事
words.ex: The children giggle when they see the clown.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小丑时咯咯笑。
words.en: To laugh in a silly, often high-pitched way, especially in a nervous or embarrassed manner.

words.ex: He tried to gild the old box with gold paint.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用金漆把旧盒子镀金。
words.en: To cover something with a thin layer of gold or to make something seem more attractive or valuable than it really is.

words.ex: The ad used a cheap gimmick to attract customers.
words.ex_cn: 这个广告用了一个廉价的噱头来吸引顾客。
words.en: A gimmick is a trick or device intended to attract attention, publicity, or trade.

words.tr:
adv. 小心地；谨慎地
adj. 小心的；谨慎的
words.ex: He walked gingerly on the icy path.
words.ex_cn: 他小心翼翼地走在结冰的小路上。
words.en: If you do something gingerly, you do it in a careful manner, usually because you expect it to be dangerous, unpleasant, or painful.

words.ex: Can you tell me the gist of the story?
words.ex_cn: 你能告诉我这个故事的要点吗？
words.en: The main or essential part of a matter.

words.ex: The gladiator fought in the ancient arena.
words.ex_cn: 角斗士在古代竞技场中战斗。
words.en: In ancient Rome, a gladiator was a man trained to fight with weapons against other men or wild animals in an arena.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.ex: The glare of the sun made it hard to see.
words.ex_cn: 阳光的刺眼使我看不清。
words.en: If you glare at someone, you look at them with an angry expression on your face. Glare is also a very bright light that is uncomfortable to look at.

words.tr:
v. 闪烁；隐约闪现
n. 亮光；闪光
words.ex: The sun gleams on the water.
words.ex_cn: 阳光照在水面上，闪闪发亮。
words.en: A gleam is a small, bright light, especially one that shines for a short time.

words.ex: The old woman gleaned wheat from the field after the harvest.
words.ex_cn: 这位老妇人在收割后从田里拾落穗。
words.en: To gather information or material bit by bit.

words.ex: The children shouted with glee when they saw the ice cream truck.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到冰淇淋车时高兴地大喊。
words.en: Glee is a feeling of great happiness, usually because something good has happened.

words.tr: adj. 油腔滑调的；口齿伶俐的；圆滑的
words.ex: He gave a glib answer to the difficult question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个难题给出了一个轻率的回答。
words.en: If you describe what someone says as glib, you disapprove of it because it implies that something is simple or easy, or that there are no problems involved, when this is not the case.

words.ex: The bird glide smoothly over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在湖面上滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and continuously along, as if without effort or resistance.

words.tr:
n. 微弱的闪光；微弱的迹象；一丝
v. 发出微弱的闪光
words.ex: I saw a glimmer of light in the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 我在黑暗的房间里看到一丝光亮。
words.en: A glimmer is a faint, wavering light or a slight indication or trace of something.

words.ex: I caught a glimpse of the cat before it ran away.
words.ex_cn: 我在它跑掉之前瞥了一眼那只猫。
words.en: A glimpse is a brief, quick look at something or someone.

words.tr:
v. 闪光；闪耀
n. 闪光；闪耀
words.ex: The dew glistens on the grass in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨露珠在草地上闪闪发亮。
words.en: If something glistens, it shines, usually because it is wet or oily.

words.tr:
n. 闪耀；闪烁；小发光物
v. 闪耀；闪亮；流露（感情）
words.ex: The glitter of the stars lit up the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星的闪耀照亮了夜空。
words.en: If something glitters, light comes from or is reflected off different parts of it.

words.tr: adj. 黑暗的；幽暗的；忧郁的；沮丧的
words.ex: The room was gloomy with no windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间没有窗户，很黑暗。
words.en: If a place is gloomy, it is almost dark so that you cannot see very well. If people are gloomy, they are unhappy and have no hope.

words.ex: The movie glorifies violence as heroism.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影美化了暴力，将其视为英雄主义。
words.en: To glorify someone or something means to praise them or make them seem more important or better than they really are.

words.ex: The glow of the fire warmed the room.
words.ex_cn: 火的炽热温暖了房间。
words.en: If something glows, it produces a dull, steady light.

words.ex: He glowered at the boy who broke his vase.
words.ex_cn: 他怒视着打碎他花瓶的那个男孩。
words.en: If you glower at someone or something, you look at them in an angry way.

words.tr: adj. 光辉的； v. “glow”的现在分词；
words.ex: The glowing sun rose over the hills.
words.ex_cn: 光辉的太阳从山上升起。
words.en: If you describe something as glowing, you mean that it is very positive and enthusiastic.

words.ex: The mouse is gnawing on the wood.
words.ex_cn: 老鼠正在啃木头。
words.en: To gnaw means to bite or chew something persistently, especially something hard, or to cause persistent worry or discomfort.

words.tr:
adj. 令人痛苦的；折磨人的
n. 咬；苛责；不断的苦痛
v. 啃；咬；啮；折磨；侵蚀；“gnaw”的现在分词
words.ex: He felt a gnawing hunger after skipping lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐没吃，感到一阵阵饥饿。
words.en: If you describe a feeling as gnawing, you mean that it causes you to feel anxious or uncomfortable over a long period of time.

words.tr:
n. （赶牲畜的）尖头棒；激励；刺激
v. 刺激；驱使
words.ex: The farmer used a goad to guide the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一根尖头棒赶牛。
words.en: If you goad someone, you deliberately make them feel angry or irritated, often causing them to react by doing something.

words.tr:
v. 狼吞虎咽；吞并；火鸡咯咯叫
n. 火鸡叫声
words.ex: The dog will gobble up its food quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗会很快把食物狼吞虎咽地吃掉。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, often making a noise.

words.ex: He drank water from a glass goblet.
words.ex_cn: 他用玻璃高脚杯喝水。
words.en: A goblet is a type of cup with a stem and a base, often used for drinking wine.

words.tr:
n. 谷歌（网络搜索引擎）；
vt. 用搜索引擎搜索（尤指用谷歌搜索引擎）；
words.ex: I use Google to find information online.
words.ex_cn: 我使用谷歌在网上查找信息。
words.en: To use the Google search engine to find information on the internet.

words.tr:
v. 偷懒；称病；欺诈
n. 假金砖；懒汉；赝品
words.ex: He is goldbricking instead of working.
words.ex_cn: 他正在偷懒而不工作。
words.en: To avoid work or responsibility, especially by pretending to be busy or by shirking duties.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；傻瓜；蠢人
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；混；打发时间
words.ex: He made a goof when he forgot his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他忘记带作业，犯了一个愚蠢的错误。
words.en: If you call someone a goof, you mean they are silly or stupid. As a verb, to goof means to make a mistake or do something badly.

words.ex: The hikers walked through a deep gorge.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者走过一个深峡谷。
words.en: A gorge is a deep, narrow valley with steep sides, often carved by a river. It can also refer to the act of eating greedily.

words.ex: He was a gourmand who loved trying exotic dishes from around the world.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢尝试世界各地异国菜肴的美食家。
words.en: A gourmand is someone who enjoys eating and often eats too much.

words.ex: He eats gourmet food at a fancy restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家高档餐厅吃精致美食。
words.en: A gourmet is someone who knows a lot about food and cooking, and who enjoys eating high-quality food.

words.ex: Good governance helps the city run smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 良好的治理有助于城市顺利运行。
words.en: The way that a country, company, etc. is controlled by the people who run it.

words.tr: adj. 纤细而优美的；纤弱的
words.ex: She had a gracile figure that turned heads wherever she went.
words.ex_cn: 她纤细优美的身姿走到哪里都引人注目。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as gracile, you mean that they are slender or graceful.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；仁慈的
words.ex: She was gracious and thanked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 她很友善，感谢了每一个人。
words.en: If you describe someone, especially someone you think is superior to you, as gracious, you mean that they are very well-mannered and pleasant.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.ex: The medicine comes in small granules.
words.ex_cn: 这种药是小颗粒状的。
words.en: A granule is a small compact particle of a substance.

words.tr:
adj. 一味攫取的；贪婪的；贪心的
v. 抓紧； 领会；“grasp”的现在分词
words.ex: He was a grasping businessman who always looked for more profit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪婪的商人，总是寻求更多的利润。
words.en: If you describe someone as grasping, you are criticizing them for wanting to get and keep as much money as possible, and for being unwilling to spend it.

words.tr:
v. 磨碎；磨擦；（使）烦躁；发出磨擦声
n. 炉栅；炉箅
words.ex: The food was grated into small pieces.
words.ex_cn: 食物被擦成了小块。
words.en: To grate means to reduce food to small shreds by rubbing it on a grater. It can also mean to make a harsh, scraping sound or to cause irritation or annoyance.

words.ex: He waits for the gratification of winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他等待赢得比赛的满足感。
words.en: Gratification is the pleasure or satisfaction you feel when you get something you wanted or worked for.

words.tr: n. 小费；赏钱；退职金；退伍金
words.ex: She left a small gratuity on the table for the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 她在桌上给服务员留下了一点小费。
words.en: A gratuity is a sum of money given to someone, typically to a service worker, in addition to the payment due for the service provided.

words.ex: The children played on the gravel path.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在砾石小路上玩耍。
words.en: Gravel consists of very small stones. It is often used to make paths and roads.

words.tr: v. 受引力（重力）作用；移向；被吸引
words.ex: The moon gravitates around the earth.
words.ex_cn: 月球受地球引力作用而围绕它运转。
words.en: If you gravitate towards a particular place, thing, or activity, you are attracted by it and go to it or get involved in it.

words.tr: n. 新手；涉世不深的人；无经验易受骗的人
words.ex: He was a greenhorn when he first started the job.
words.ex_cn: 他刚接手这份工作时还是个生手。
words.en: A greenhorn is someone who is new to a particular activity or job and therefore lacks experience.

words.ex: His gregariousness makes him popular at parties.
words.ex_cn: 他的外向性格让他在派对上很受欢迎。
words.en: The quality of being fond of company; sociability.

words.ex: He filed a grievance about the unfair treatment.
words.ex_cn: 他因不公平的对待提出了不满。
words.en: A grievance is a feeling of resentment over something believed to be wrong or unfair.

words.tr: adj. 痛苦的；严重的；剧烈的
words.ex: The injury caused him grievous pain.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤给他带来了巨大的痛苦。
words.en: If you describe something such as a loss or injury as grievous, you mean that it is extremely serious or worrying in its effects.

words.tr:
n. 烤架；铁格子
v. 烧烤；拷问
words.ex: He cooked the burgers on the grill.
words.ex_cn: 他用烤架烤了汉堡。
words.en: To cook food on a metal frame over a fire, or a metal frame used for cooking food in this way.

words.ex: He grimaced when he tasted the bitter medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他喝下苦涩的药时皱起了脸。
words.en: A grimace is an ugly, twisted expression on a person's face, usually because they are experiencing pain or strong feelings.

words.ex: He wore a big grin after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后露出了灿烂的咧嘴笑容。
words.en: If you grin, you smile broadly, usually showing your teeth.

words.tr:
v. 抱怨；发牢骚；绞痛
n. 抱怨；肠绞痛
words.ex: He always gripes about the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他总是抱怨天气。
words.en: If you gripe, you complain about something in a persistent, irritating way.

words.ex: The crime scene was grisly and made everyone feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 犯罪现场很可怕，让所有人都感到恶心。
words.en: Grisly is used to describe something that is extremely unpleasant and horrifying, often because it involves death or violence.

words.ex: The children played in the grit near the road.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在路边的沙砾中玩耍。
words.en: Grit is very small pieces of stone. It is often used to make surfaces less slippery. Grit is also a quality of character that enables someone to continue with determination in the face of difficulties.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；叹息
n. 呻吟声；叹息声
words.ex: He groaned when he saw the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他看到那个沉重的箱子时呻吟了一声。
words.en: If you groan, you make a long, low sound because you are in pain, or because you are upset or unhappy about something.

words.ex: The mother grooms her puppy every morning.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈每天早上给她的小狗梳理毛发。
words.en: A groom is a man who is getting married. Also, to groom means to clean and brush an animal, or to prepare someone for a particular job or position.

words.ex: The nail fits into the groove.
words.ex_cn: 钉子卡在槽里。
words.en: A groove is a long, narrow space or cut in a surface, often made to guide the movement of something or to hold something in place. It can also refer to a settled routine or way of doing things that is hard to change.

words.ex: The gross income of the company is $5 million.
words.ex_cn: 公司的总收入是500万美元。
words.en: If you describe something as gross, you mean it is very obvious, unacceptable, or unpleasant.

words.tr:
adj. 怪诞的；丑陋奇异的；奇形怪状的
n. 奇形怪状的东西；奇异风格
words.ex: The painting showed a grotesque face with twisted eyes.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画上有一个扭曲眼睛的怪诞面孔。
words.en: If you say that something is grotesque, you mean that it is extremely unattractive, exaggerated, and often shocking or disturbing.

words.tr:
n. 爱发牢骚的人；不满；牢骚
v. 闹脾气；发牢骚
words.ex: He is a grouch who complains every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是个每天早上都抱怨的脾气暴躁的人。
words.en: A grouch is a person who is often in a bad mood and complains a lot.

words.ex: The children played in a small grove behind the house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房子后面的小树林里玩耍。
words.en: A grove is a small group of trees.

words.ex: The dog grovelled on the ground to beg for food.
words.ex_cn: 狗趴在地上乞求食物。
words.en: If you grovel, you behave in a very submissive way in order to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done or to try to get someone to forgive you or do something for you.

words.tr:
v. 咆哮；低声吼叫；发出隆隆声
n. 咆哮；怒吼声；轰鸣声
words.ex: The dog growl at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 狗向陌生人咆哮。
words.en: To make a deep, guttural sound of anger or hostility, often by an animal.

words.ex: The movie showed a gruesome accident.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一起令人毛骨悚然的事故。
words.en: Something that is gruesome is extremely unpleasant and shocking, especially because it involves death or injury.

words.tr: adj. 粗鲁的；生硬的；粗哑的
words.ex: The old man gave a gruff answer.
words.ex_cn: 老人粗声粗气地回答了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as gruff, you mean that they seem rather unfriendly or bad-tempered.

words.tr: adj. 性情乖戾的；脾气暴躁的
words.ex: He is grumpy when he wakes up early.
words.ex_cn: 他早起时会脾气不好。
words.en: If you say that someone is grumpy, you mean that they are bad-tempered and miserable.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.tr:
v. 哄笑；大笑
n. 哄笑；大笑
words.ex: The audience broke into a guffaw when the comedian slipped on stage.
words.ex_cn: 喜剧演员在舞台上滑倒时，观众哄堂大笑。
words.en: A guffaw is a very loud laugh.

words.tr: adj. 不奸猾的；厚道的；坦率的
words.ex: He is a guileless boy who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个纯真无邪的男孩，总是说真话。
words.en: If you describe someone as guileless, you mean that they behave openly and truthfully and do not try to deceive people.

words.ex: He spoke in the guise of a friend.
words.ex_cn: 他以朋友的伪装说话。
words.en: An external form, appearance, or manner of presentation, typically concealing the true nature of something.

words.tr: n. 冲沟；沟壑；激流峡谷
words.ex: The rainwater flowed down the gulch.
words.ex_cn: 雨水沿着峡谷流下。
words.en: A gulch is a narrow and steep-sided ravine marking the course of a fast stream.

words.tr:
v. 大口吞咽；喘气；抑制
n. 一大口；吞咽
words.ex: He gulped down his water quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速地吞下了水。
words.en: If you gulp something, you eat or drink it very quickly by swallowing large quantities of it at once.

words.ex: The tree produces a sticky gum.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树分泌出一种粘稠的树胶。
words.en: Gum refers to the firm area of flesh in the mouth to which the teeth are attached, or a type of sweet, flavored, synthetic rubber which is chewed for pleasure.

words.tr: n. 精明强干；机智；老练；胆量
words.ex: He had enough gumption to start his own business.
words.ex_cn: 他有足够的胆识去创办自己的公司。
words.en: If someone has gumption, they are able to think what it would be sensible to do in a particular situation, and they do it.

words.ex: The discovery of a gusher revolutionized the local economy.
words.ex_cn: 一口喷油井的发现彻底改变了当地经济。
words.en: A gusher is a well from which oil or water flows out strongly and suddenly without being pumped.

words.ex: The art of wine tasting involves the science of gustation.
words.ex_cn: 品酒的艺术涉及味觉的科学。
words.en: Gustation is the act or faculty of tasting, the sense by which the qualities and flavor of a substance are distinguished by the taste buds.

words.ex: The gustatory sense helps us taste food.
words.ex_cn: 味觉帮助我们品尝食物。
words.en: Relating to the sense of taste.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏勇气的；怯懦的
words.ex: He was gutless and refused to speak up.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，不敢站出来说话。
words.en: If you describe someone as gutless, you think they have a weak character and lack courage or determination.

words.tr:
n. 排水沟；阴沟；贫民区
v. 忽明忽暗；摇曳不定
words.ex: The rain water flows down the gutter.
words.ex_cn: 雨水沿着排水沟流下。
words.en: A gutter is a channel at the edge of a road or roof that collects and directs rainwater away.

words.ex: He guttled his food like a starving man.
words.ex_cn: 他像一个饿极了的人一样狼吞虎咽地吃着食物。
words.en: To consume food greedily or in large quantities.

words.tr: v. 狂吃暴饮；大吃大喝；大量消耗
words.ex: He guzzles soda every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都大口喝苏打水。
words.en: If you guzzle something, you drink it quickly and greedily.

words.tr: v. 旋转；螺旋形地运转；剧烈起伏
words.ex: The dancer gyrated to the rhythm of the music.
words.ex_cn: 舞者随着音乐的节奏旋转。
words.en: If something or someone gyrates, they move around in a circle, especially very quickly.

words.tr: adj. 适合居住的；可居住的；
words.ex: The planet is habitable because it has water and air.
words.ex_cn: 这颗行星有水和空气，适合居住。
words.en: A place that is habitable is suitable or good enough for people to live in.

words.tr: n. 栖息地；居留地；产地；
words.ex: The panda's habitat is in the mountains of China.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫的栖息地在中国的山区。
words.en: The natural environment in which a species or group of species lives.

words.tr: adj. 憔悴的；形容枯槁的
words.ex: He looked haggard after working all night.
words.ex_cn: 他熬了一整夜后看起来憔悴不堪。
words.en: Someone who is haggard looks exhausted and unwell, often because they have been through a very difficult or stressful experience.

words.ex: He remembers those halcyon days of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他怀念那些童年的宁静时光。
words.en: A halcyon time is a time in the past that was peaceful or happy.

words.tr: adj. 神圣化的； 受崇敬的
words.ex: The hallowed ground is where the heroes rest.
words.ex_cn: 那片神圣的土地是英雄们安息的地方。
words.en: Something that is hallowed is respected and admired, usually because it is old, important, or has a good reputation.

words.ex: He had a hallucination after taking the medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他服药后出现了幻觉。
words.en: A hallucination is a perception in the absence of external stimulus that has qualities of real perception. Hallucinations are vivid, substantial, and are perceived to be located in external objective space.

words.tr:
n. 锤子；
v. 锤打；
words.ex: He hit the nail with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 他用锤子敲钉子。
words.en: A hammer is a tool that consists of a heavy piece of metal at the end of a handle, used for hitting things.

words.tr: adj. 羞愧的；卑躬屈膝的
words.ex: He looked hangdog after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 输掉比赛后，他一副垂头丧气的样子。
words.en: If someone has a hangdog expression, they look sad, ashamed, or guilty.

words.ex: She hankers after a simpler life.
words.ex_cn: 她向往一种更简单的生活。
words.en: If you hanker after something, you have a strong desire for it.

words.tr:
n. 渴望；期望
v. 渴望；追求；“hanker”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a hankering for adventure.
words.ex_cn: 他对冒险有着强烈的渴望。
words.en: A hankering is a strong feeling of wanting something.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.tr:
n. 高谈阔论；长篇大论；大声斥责的讲话
v. 作长篇大论；高谈阔论；猛烈的批评或训斥
words.ex: The politician gave a long harangue about taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客就税收问题发表了一番长篇高谈阔论。
words.en: A harangue is a lengthy and aggressive speech, especially one delivered in public.

words.ex: The dark clouds are a harbinger of storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预兆。
words.en: A harbinger is something that shows that something is going to happen soon, especially something bad.

words.tr: adj. 通过经历而变得顽强的；坚毅的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: The hard-bitten soldier never gave up, even in the face of overwhelming odds.
words.ex_cn: 面对压倒性的劣势，这位顽强的士兵也从未放弃。
words.en: If you describe someone as hard-bitten, you mean that they have been through a lot of difficult or unpleasant experiences and are tough as a result.

words.ex: His hardihood in the face of danger was admired by all.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前表现出的刚毅受到所有人的钦佩。
words.en: Boldness or daring, especially in challenging situations.

words.tr: adj. 能吃苦耐劳的；耐寒的；
words.ex: He is a hardy farmer who works in the field all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个能吃苦耐劳的农民，整天在田里干活。
words.en: Someone who is hardy is strong and able to cope with difficult conditions.

words.tr:
v. 利用；
n. 马具；
words.ex: We must harness the power of the sun.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须利用太阳的能量。
words.en: A harness is a set of straps which fit under a person's arms and fasten round their body in order to keep a piece of equipment in place or to prevent the person moving from a place.

words.tr: adj. 锋利的；骤变的；灵敏的；尖刻的；
words.ex: The knife is sharp enough to cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀足够锋利，可以切纸。
words.en: Having a thin edge or a fine point that is capable of cutting or piercing; keen.

words.ex: The harpsichord was used extensively in Baroque music.
words.ex_cn: 羽管键琴在巴洛克音乐中被广泛使用。
words.en: A harpsichord is a musical instrument played by means of a keyboard. It produces sound by plucking a string when a key is pressed.

words.ex: The farmer used a harrow to break up the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用耙来松土。
words.en: A harrow is a piece of farm equipment that is used to break up and smooth out the surface of the soil.

words.tr:
adj. 悲痛的；令人伤心的
v. 耙地；折磨；使愁苦；“harrow”的现在分词
words.ex: The harrowing story of the survivors left a deep impression on everyone.
words.ex_cn: 幸存者的悲惨故事给每个人留下了深刻的印象。
words.en: Causing feelings of deep distress or anguish.

words.tr: v. 不断骚扰；打扰；侵扰；
words.ex: The neighbors harry the old man with loud music every night.
words.ex_cn: 邻居们每晚用吵闹的音乐不断骚扰那位老人。
words.en: To harry someone means to repeatedly attack them or to cause them problems.

words.ex: The teacher punished the student harshly.
words.ex_cn: 老师严厉地惩罚了那个学生。
words.en: In a severe or cruel manner; with severity or cruelty.

words.tr:
n. 肉丁；杂乱；#号
v. 切碎；弄糟；推敲
words.ex: He added hash to his breakfast plate.
words.ex_cn: 他把肉丁加到了早餐盘里。
words.en: Hash can refer to a dish of cooked meat cut into small pieces and recooked, usually with potatoes. In computing, a hash is a function that converts an input of letters and numbers into an encrypted output of a fixed length.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.tr: adj. 匆忙的；草率的；急躁的
words.ex: He made a hasty decision and regretted it.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个仓促的决定，后来后悔了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as hasty, you mean that they are acting too quickly, without thinking carefully, often with unwanted results.

words.ex: He spoke with hauteur when he met the new teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他见到新老师时说话一副高傲的样子。
words.en: Hauteur is the quality of being haughty; arrogance.

words.tr: n. 大破坏；大毁坏；大混乱；
words.ex: The storm caused havoc in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给这个小镇带来了大破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as havoc, you mean that it causes a great deal of disorder, confusion, or destruction.

words.ex: A hawk flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 一只鹰飞过田野。
words.en: A hawk is a bird of prey with a strong beak and sharp claws, known for its keen vision and swift flight. As a verb, to hawk means to sell goods aggressively, often in public places.

words.tr: adj. 朦胧的；模糊的；不清楚的
words.ex: The sky looks hazy this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上天空看起来雾蒙蒙的。
words.en: If it is hazy, it is not clear because there is a lot of mist, smoke, or dust in the air.

words.tr:
adv. 头向前地；倒栽葱地；急速地；鲁莽地
adj. 头向前的；倒栽葱的；急速的；急骤的
words.ex: He jumped headlong into the pool.
words.ex_cn: 他头向前地跳进了泳池。
words.en: If you move headlong in a particular direction, you move there very quickly and without thinking carefully about what you are doing.

words.tr: n. 前进；进展；间隔时间
words.ex: He made headway in solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解决这道数学题上取得了进展。
words.en: If you make headway, you progress towards achieving something.

words.ex: The heady smell of fresh flowers made her smile.
words.ex_cn: 新鲜花朵的兴奋香气让她露出了微笑。
words.en: If you describe something as heady, you mean that it has a strong or exhilarating effect, especially in making you feel excited, enthusiastic, or slightly drunk.

words.ex: The wound will heal in a few days.
words.ex_cn: 伤口几天后就会愈合。
words.en: To make or become healthy or whole again; to cure or recover from an injury or illness.

words.ex: He will hearken to his teacher's advice.
words.ex_cn: 他会听从老师的建议。
words.en: To listen attentively or give heed to something or someone.

words.tr: n. 传闻；谣传；道听途说
words.ex: He believed the hearsay without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就相信了这些流言。
words.en: Information received from other people that one cannot adequately substantiate; rumor.

words.tr: adj. 使人悲痛的；令人心碎的
words.ex: The story of the orphan's struggle was heartrending.
words.ex_cn: 这个孤儿奋斗的故事令人心碎。
words.en: Causing great sadness or distress.

words.tr:
v. 举起；投掷；起伏；喘息；呕吐
n. 举；投；掷；起伏
words.ex: He heave the box onto the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把箱子举到了桌子上。
words.en: To lift or haul something heavy with great effort; to throw something forcefully; to rise and fall rhythmically or with effort.

words.ex: The crowd began to heckle the speaker during the debate.
words.ex_cn: 在辩论期间，观众开始嘲笑那位演讲者。
words.en: To heckle someone means to interrupt them while they are speaking, especially in a public situation, by shouting out questions or comments, often in order to challenge or embarrass them.

words.ex: Her mornings are hectic with work and kids.
words.ex_cn: 她的早晨因为工作和孩子而紧张忙碌。
words.en: If you describe a situation as hectic, you mean that it is very busy and involves a lot of rushed activity.

words.ex: He tried to hector the little boy into giving up his toy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图威吓那个小男孩，让他交出玩具。
words.en: If you say that someone is hectoring you, you do not like the way they are trying to make you do something by bothering you and talking to you aggressively.

words.tr:
n. 树篱；防范措施
v. 用树篱围住；限制；避免
words.ex: He planted a hedge around his garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园周围种了一排树篱。
words.en: A hedge is a row of bushes or small trees which have been planted along the edge of a garden, field, or road to separate it from another area or to protect it. As a verb, to hedge means to avoid committing oneself or to limit or qualify something by conditions or exceptions.

words.ex: The deer is herbivorous.
words.ex_cn: 这只鹿是食草的。
words.en: Herbivorous animals are those that feed on plants.

words.ex: He was accused of heresy for rejecting the church's teachings.
words.ex_cn: 他因拒绝教会的教义而被指控为异端。
words.en: Heresy is a belief or opinion that is contrary to the orthodox religious doctrine, especially in Christianity.

words.tr: adj. 密封的；不透气的；与外界隔绝的
words.ex: The container was hermetic to ensure the contents stayed fresh.
words.ex_cn: 这个容器是密封的，以确保内容物保持新鲜。
words.en: If something is hermetic, it is so tightly sealed that no air can get in or out.

words.tr: v. 砍；劈；削成…形状；开辟；坚持；遵守
words.ex: He hews wood every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上砍柴。
words.en: To cut or shape something with a tool such as an axe, or to make something by cutting.

words.tr: adj. 顽固守旧的；死板保守的
words.ex: He is hidebound and refuses to change his old ways.
words.ex_cn: 他思想僵化，拒绝改变他的老办法。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as hidebound, you are criticizing them for having old-fashioned attitudes or ideas and being unwilling or unlikely to change.

words.ex: He hie to the store after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后急忙去商店。
words.en: To go quickly; hasten.

words.ex: The ancient Egyptians used hieroglyphic to write messages.
words.ex_cn: 古埃及人用象形文字书写信息。
words.en: Hieroglyphic refers to a system of writing that uses pictures or symbols to represent words or sounds, especially the ancient Egyptian writing system.

words.tr: n. 有文化修养的人；有高雅趣味的人；
words.ex: He is a highbrow who loves classical music and old novels.
words.ex_cn: 他是个有文化修养的人，喜欢古典音乐和古典小说。
words.en: A highbrow person or thing is interested in or concerned with intellectual or cultural matters, often to the exclusion of more practical or popular interests.

words.tr:
n. 远足；
v. 远足；
words.ex: We went on a long hike in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 我们去山里进行了一次长途远足。
words.en: A hike is a long walk in the country, especially one that you go on for pleasure. It can also refer to an increase in the cost or amount of something.

words.ex: The movie was hilarious and made us laugh a lot.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影非常搞笑，让我们笑得很开心。
words.en: If you describe something as hilarious, you mean that it is extremely funny and it makes you laugh a lot.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.ex: The door opens on a metal hinge.
words.ex_cn: 这扇门装在一个金属枢纽上。
words.en: A hinge is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is used to join two things together so that one of them can swing or move freely.

words.ex: He spoke in a hoarse voice after shouting all day.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一整天后，声音变得沙哑。
words.en: If your voice is hoarse or if you are hoarse, your voice sounds rough and unclear, for example because your throat is sore.

words.tr: adj. 灰白的；须发斑白的
words.ex: The old man had a hoary beard.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人有一头灰白的胡须。
words.en: If you describe something as hoary, you mean that it is old and often repeated and therefore not interesting or original.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.tr: v. 跛行；蹒跚；捆绑（马等的）两腿
words.ex: The old man hobbled along the street.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人一瘸一拐地走在街上。
words.en: If you hobble, you walk in an awkward way, usually because your feet or legs hurt.

words.tr:
n. 锄头
v. 锄（地）；锄（草）
words.ex: He uses a hoe to dig in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他用锄头在花园里翻土。
words.en: A hoe is a gardening tool consisting of a long handle with a flat metal blade at the end, used for breaking up soil and removing weeds.

words.ex: The workers used a hoist to lift the heavy beams.
words.ex_cn: 工人们用吊升机械吊起沉重的梁。
words.en: To hoist something means to lift or pull it up to a higher position, usually using some kind of equipment such as a crane or pulley.

words.ex: The film is an homage to old Hollywood movies.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是对老好莱坞电影的致敬。
words.en: Homage is respect shown towards someone or something you admire, or to a person in authority.

words.tr: adj. 像家般舒适的；朴素的；
words.ex: The small cabin had a homely feel with soft blankets and a warm fire.
words.ex_cn: 这座小木屋有柔软的毛毯和温暖的火炉，感觉像家一样舒适。
words.en: If you describe something as homely, you mean that it is simple and plain, often in a way that is comforting. If you describe a person as homely, you mean that they are not very attractive.

words.tr:
n. 电话；
v. 打电话；
words.ex: I lost my phone yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我昨天丢了电话。
words.en: A phone is a piece of equipment that you use to talk to someone who is in another place.

words.tr:
n. 带来厄运的人；不祥之物
v. 使倒霉
words.ex: He believed that the hoodoo would bring bad luck to his family.
words.ex_cn: 他认为那个不祥的人会给他的家庭带来厄运。
words.en: Hoodoo refers to a set of spiritual practices, traditions, and beliefs that are a blend of African, Native American, and European folklore, primarily found in the Southern United States. It involves the use of magical rituals and spells to influence events or to protect against evil.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.tr:
n. 箍；环；圈
v. 加箍于；围绕
words.ex: The barrel is held together by a wooden hoop.
words.ex_cn: 这个桶由一个木制的箍固定在一起。
words.en: A hoop is a large ring made of wood, metal, or plastic, used in games or as a decoration.

words.ex: The line is horizontal on the graph.
words.ex_cn: 这条线在图上是水平的。
words.en: Parallel to the plane of the horizon; at right angles to the vertical.

words.ex: The cow has two long horns.
words.ex_cn: 这头牛有两只长角。
words.en: A horn is a pointed projection on the head of various animals, consisting of a core of bone surrounded by a sheath of keratin, or a device for making a loud warning noise.

words.ex: The accident looked horrendous.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故看起来很可怕。
words.en: If you describe something as horrendous, you are emphasizing that it is very unpleasant or shocking.

words.ex: His words were hortative, urging everyone to try harder.
words.ex_cn: 他的话具有激励性，鼓励大家更加努力。
words.en: If you describe something as hortative, you mean that it is intended to encourage or incite someone to do something.

words.ex: He works in horticulture at a local garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在当地的一个花园从事园艺工作。
words.en: Horticulture is the study and practice of growing and cultivating plants, especially flowers, fruits, and vegetables.

words.ex: The wolf is a howler at night.
words.ex_cn: 狼是夜晚嚎叫的动物。
words.en: A howler is a person or thing that howls, or a very stupid or embarrassing mistake.

words.ex: His hubris made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, often leading to downfall or failure.

words.ex: The hue of the sky changed at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空的色调发生了变化。
words.en: A hue is a particular shade of a color.

words.tr: adj. 生气的；不高兴的；发怒的
words.ex: She gave a huffish reply when asked about her plans.
words.ex_cn: 当被问及她的计划时，她不高兴地回答了。
words.en: If you describe someone as huffish, you mean that they are easily annoyed or offended, and often behave in a sulky or bad-tempered way.

words.tr: adj. 怒冲冲的；易生气的
words.ex: She got huffy when I didn't agree with her.
words.ex_cn: 当我不同意她的意见时，她变得怒冲冲的。
words.en: If someone is huffy, they are easily annoyed and often become angry or offended over small things.

words.ex: The hull of the boat was damaged by the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 船的船体被岩石损坏了。
words.en: The main body of a ship or other vessel, including the bottom, sides, and deck but not the masts, superstructure, rigging, engines, and other fittings.

words.ex: The air feels humid after it rains.
words.ex_cn: 雨后空气感觉湿润。
words.en: You use humid to describe an atmosphere or climate that is very damp, and usually very hot.

words.ex: His humor makes everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他的幽默让大家都笑了。
words.en: The quality of being amusing or comic, especially as expressed in literature or speech.

words.ex: The protesters hunkered down in the square overnight.
words.ex_cn: 抗议者们在广场上蹲了一整夜。
words.en: To squat or crouch down low, often to protect oneself or to stay hidden.

words.tr:
n. 跨栏；障碍；难关
v. 越过障碍；克服
words.ex: He jumped over the hurdle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速跳过了跨栏。
words.en: A hurdle is a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve something.

words.tr: v. 猛冲；猛投；猛烈碰撞
words.ex: The car hurtled down the hill.
words.ex_cn: 汽车飞速冲下山坡。
words.en: If someone or something hurtles somewhere, they move there very quickly, often in a uncontrolled way.

words.ex: Her husband cooks dinner every night.
words.ex_cn: 她的丈夫每天晚上做晚饭。
words.en: A married man considered in relation to his spouse.

words.ex: He learned husbandry from his father on the farm.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里学会了畜牧业。
words.en: Husbandry is the careful management of resources, especially in agriculture or farming, to ensure their efficient use and conservation.

words.tr:
v. 使安静；使肃静
n. 安静
words.ex: Please hush, the baby is sleeping.
words.ex_cn: 请安静，宝宝在睡觉。
words.en: If you hush someone or if they hush, they stop speaking or making a noise.

words.ex: The choir sang a beautiful hymn on Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 星期天，唱诗班唱了一首优美的赞美诗。
words.en: A hymn is a religious song or poem of praise to God or a god.

words.tr: n. 天花乱坠的广告宣传；炒作；
words.ex: The new phone got a lot of hype before its release.
words.ex_cn: 这款新手机在发布前受到了大量天花乱坠的广告宣传。
words.en: If someone or something is hyped, they are praised or advertised a lot in newspapers, on television, etc., especially in a way that is intended to make them seem very exciting or important.

words.tr: n. 活动过度；极度活跃
words.ex: The child shows hyperactivity during class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在课堂上表现出多动。
words.en: Hyperactivity is a state of being unusually or abnormally active.

words.ex: He is a hypocrite because he says he loves peace but fights often.
words.ex_cn: 他是个伪君子，因为他声称热爱和平，却经常打架。
words.en: A hypocrite is someone who pretends to have certain beliefs or opinions that they do not really have, especially in order to deceive people.

words.ex: An icicle hangs from the roof.
words.ex_cn: 一个冰锥挂在屋顶上。
words.en: An icicle is a pointed piece of ice that is formed when dripping water freezes, typically hanging from a surface.

words.ex: He is an icon of pop music.
words.ex_cn: 他是流行音乐的偶像。
words.en: An icon is a small picture or symbol on a computer screen that represents a program or a file.

words.tr: n. 攻击传统观念的人；
words.ex: He is an iconoclast who challenges old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他是个挑战传统观念的人。
words.en: An iconoclast is someone who criticizes or attacks cherished beliefs or institutions.

words.ex: He used an idiom to explain his idea.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个成语来解释他的想法。
words.en: An idiom is a group of words in a fixed order that have a particular meaning that is different from the meanings of each word on its own.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.tr: v. 奉为偶像；盲目崇拜
words.ex: Many fans idolatrize the famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 许多粉丝崇拜那位著名歌手。
words.en: To idolatrize means to worship or admire someone or something excessively and blindly, often to the point of obsession.

words.tr: v. 偶像化；过分崇拜；奉为神圣
words.ex: He idolizes his older brother.
words.ex_cn: 他崇拜他的哥哥。
words.en: If you idolize someone, you admire them very much.

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.tr: adj. 无知的；缺乏知识的
words.ex: He was ignorant of the basic rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对基本规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as ignorant, you mean that they do not know things they should know. If someone is ignorant of a fact, they do not know it.

words.ex: He drinks a glass of milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝一杯牛奶。
words.en: Milk is a white liquid produced by cows, goats, and some other animals, which people drink and use in cooking.

words.tr: adj. 非自由主义的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The government's illiberal policies restricted free speech.
words.ex_cn: 政府的非自由主义政策限制了言论自由。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as illiberal, you are critical of them because they do not allow or approve of much freedom or choice of action.

words.ex: The lamp illuminate the dark room.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯照亮了黑暗的房间。
words.en: To illuminate something means to shine light on it and to make it brighter and more visible.

words.ex: The Illuminati are often depicted as a secretive and powerful group.
words.ex_cn: 光照派常被描绘成一个神秘且强大的团体。
words.en: The Illuminati refers to a secret society founded in Bavaria in 1776, which aimed to oppose superstition, prejudice, religious influence over public life, abuses of state power, and to support women's education and gender equality.

words.ex: The mirage in the desert is an illusive image.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠中的海市蜃楼是一个虚幻的景象。
words.en: If something is illusive, it is based on an illusion and is not real or true.

words.tr: v. 举例说明；给书籍、杂志等加插图；
words.ex: The teacher illustrated the point with a simple story.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的故事来举例说明这个观点。
words.en: To illustrate something means to explain or demonstrate it clearly, often by giving examples or by using pictures or diagrams.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.tr:
n. 笨蛋；蠢货；低能者
adj. 低能的；愚笨的
words.ex: He called the man an imbecile for making such a silly mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为那个人犯了这么愚蠢的错误而称他为傻子。
words.en: If you call someone an imbecile, you are showing that you think they are stupid or have done something stupid.

words.ex: He imbibes coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喝咖啡。
words.en: To imbibe means to drink, especially alcohol, or to absorb or take in something, such as knowledge or ideas.

words.ex: The legal imbroglio complicated the company's expansion plans.
words.ex_cn: 法律上的纠葛使公司的扩张计划变得复杂。
words.en: An imbroglio is a very confusing or complicated situation.

words.tr: adj. 内在的；无所不在的
words.ex: The immanent laws of nature govern all living things.
words.ex_cn: 自然界的内在法则支配着所有生物。
words.en: Existing or operating within; inherent.

words.ex: This custom has existed from time immemorial.
words.ex_cn: 这个习俗从远古时代就存在了。
words.en: Something that is immemorial has existed or been happening for such a long time that it cannot be remembered.

words.tr: n. 广大；巨大；浩瀚无垠
words.ex: The immensity of the ocean surprised him.
words.ex_cn: 海洋的浩瀚让他感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality or state of being immense; vastness or hugeness.

words.ex: He immersed the cloth in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把布浸在水里。
words.en: To immerse something or someone means to put them into a liquid so that they are completely covered by it. It can also mean to involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest.

words.tr: v. 牺牲；宰杀作祭品；献祭
words.ex: He decided to immolate himself in protest.
words.ex_cn: 他决定自焚以示抗议。
words.en: To kill or offer as a sacrifice, especially by burning.

words.ex: Legends say that some heroes are immortal.
words.ex_cn: 传说有些英雄是不死的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as immortal, you mean that they are so famous or popular that they will be remembered for a very long time.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: Vaccines help build immunity against diseases.
words.ex_cn: 疫苗有助于增强对疾病的免疫力。
words.en: Immunity is the state of being immune from or insusceptible to a particular disease or the legal status of being exempt from certain obligations or penalties.

words.ex: The doctor will immunize the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To immunize someone or something means to protect them against a disease by giving them a vaccine.

words.tr: v. 监禁；禁闭；把...嵌在墙上
words.ex: He was immured in the old tower for years.
words.ex_cn: 他被囚禁在那座旧塔里多年。
words.en: To confine someone within or as if within walls; imprison.

words.tr:
n. 影响力；冲击（力）；
v. 对…产生影响；
words.ex: The new law had a big impact on education.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律对教育产生了重大影响。
words.en: The effect or influence of one person, thing, or action, on another.

words.ex: The knight was impaled on the spear.
words.ex_cn: 骑士被长矛刺穿了。
words.en: To impale someone or something means to pierce them with a sharp object such as a spear or spike.

words.tr: adj. 无法触及的；摸不着的；难解的
words.ex: The concept of infinity is often considered impalpable.
words.ex_cn: 无限的概念常常被认为是难以理解的。
words.en: Impalpable means something that cannot be perceived by touch or is very difficult to understand or define.

words.tr: n. 绝境；僵局；死路；死胡同
words.ex: The talks reached an impasse and no one could move forward.
words.ex_cn: 谈判陷入了僵局，没有人能继续前进。
words.en: An impasse is a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible, especially because of disagreement; a deadlock.

words.ex: The president may be impeached for lying.
words.ex_cn: 总统可能因撒谎而被弹劾。
words.en: If a government official is impeached, they are formally charged with a serious crime in a special government court.

words.ex: The danger impels him to act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 危险驱使他迅速行动。
words.en: If something impels you to do something, it makes you feel very strongly that you must do it.

words.ex: A storm is about to impend.
words.ex_cn: 一场暴风雨即将来临。
words.en: If an event impends, usually an event that is unpleasant or unwanted, it is going to happen soon.

words.tr: adj. 不知悔悟的；无悔意的
words.ex: The impenitent criminal continued to commit crimes despite repeated warnings.
words.ex_cn: 尽管一再警告，那个不知悔改的罪犯仍然继续犯罪。
words.en: If you describe someone as impenitent, you mean that they are not ashamed of their bad behavior or attitudes, and they do not wish to change them.

words.ex: Smoking can imperil your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会危及你的健康。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk of being harmed, damaged, or destroyed.

words.tr: n. 不能透过的性质；不渗透性
words.ex: The impermeability of the fabric ensures that water cannot pass through.
words.ex_cn: 这种织物的不渗透性确保了水不能通过。
words.en: The quality or state of being impermeable; the inability of a substance to allow fluids or gases to pass through it.

words.ex: His impertinence made the teacher angry.
words.ex_cn: 他的无礼让老师生气了。
words.en: Impertinence refers to a lack of respect or rudeness, especially towards someone who is older or in a position of authority.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.ex: The new law impinges on people's privacy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律侵犯了人们的隐私。
words.en: To impinge means to have an effect or influence, especially a negative one, on someone or something.

words.ex: The dentist placed a dental implant to replace the missing tooth.
words.ex_cn: 牙医植入了一个牙科植入物来替代缺失的牙齿。
words.en: To implant something means to put it firmly into something else, especially into a person's body.

words.tr: v. 使牵连其中；涉及；暗示；指明起因
words.ex: The evidence may implicate him in the crime.
words.ex_cn: 证据可能使他牵连进这起犯罪中。
words.en: To show or suggest that someone is involved in something illegal or morally wrong.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.ex: The old building will implode if the explosives go off.
words.ex_cn: 如果炸药引爆，这座旧楼会坍塌。
words.en: If something implodes, it collapses into itself in a sudden and violent way.

words.ex: She implored him to stay.
words.ex_cn: 她恳求他留下。
words.en: If you implore someone to do something, you ask them to do it in a forceful, emotional way.

words.tr: v. 不断请求；胡搅蛮缠
words.ex: He importunes his boss for a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他不断向老板请求加薪。
words.en: To importune someone means to ask them for something repeatedly and in a way that is annoying or troublesome.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.ex: The war impoverished many families.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使许多家庭变得贫困。
words.en: To make someone poor or to reduce the quality, strength, or richness of something.

words.ex: He muttered imprecations under his breath.
words.ex_cn: 他低声念着咒语。
words.en: An imprecation is a curse or a swear word.

words.tr: adj. 坚不可摧的；不可战胜的
words.ex: The castle was impregnable during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争期间固若金汤。
words.en: An impregnable building or place is so strong and secure that it cannot be entered or captured by force.

words.tr:
v. 盖印；印刻；使铭记
n. 盖印；痕迹
words.ex: He used a stamp to imprint his name on the box.
words.ex_cn: 他用印章在盒子上盖印了他的名字。
words.en: To imprint something means to mark or stamp it with a design or a symbol. It can also mean to fix something firmly in someone's mind.

words.ex: He felt impuissance after the failure.
words.ex_cn: 失败后，他感到无能为力。
words.en: The state or condition of being powerless or lacking strength.

words.ex: The imputation of blame was unjust.
words.ex_cn: 归咎于责备是不公平的。
words.en: The act of imputing something, especially a fault or crime, to someone.

words.ex: His inadvertence caused the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了错误。
words.en: The fact of not paying attention or making a mistake because you are not paying attention.

words.ex: He inadvertently dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他非故意地打翻了玻璃杯。
words.en: If you do something inadvertently, you do it without realizing it, or by accident.

words.ex: The chair is inanimate.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是没有生命的。
words.en: Something that is inanimate is not alive, such as a rock or a chair. It can also describe something that lacks energy or spirit.

words.ex: The difference is inappreciable.
words.ex_cn: 这个差异微不足道。
words.en: An inappreciable amount or effect is so small that it cannot be seen or felt.

words.ex: The man was incarcerated for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: If people are incarcerated, they are kept in a prison or other place.

words.ex: There is uncertainty about the weather tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天的天气还不确定。
words.en: Uncertainty is a situation in which something is not known, or something that is not known or certain.

words.ex: The book is 10 inches long.
words.ex_cn: 这本书长10英寸。
words.en: An inch is a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot.

words.tr: adj. 初始的；早期的；未形成的
words.ex: His idea was still inchoate.
words.ex_cn: 他的想法还很不成熟。
words.en: If something is inchoate, it is just beginning to form or is not fully developed or clear.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.ex: The doctor made a small incision to remove the tumor.
words.ex_cn: 医生做了一个小切口来切除肿瘤。
words.en: An incision is a cut that is made in someone's body during surgery.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: The weather was inclement, so we stayed home.
words.ex_cn: 天气恶劣，所以我们待在家里。
words.en: (of weather) unpleasantly cold or wet.

words.tr: adj. 无思虑的；考虑不周的
words.ex: His incogitant remarks hurt her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 他无心的话语伤了她的感情。
words.en: Lacking thought or consideration; thoughtless.

words.tr: adj. 不调和的；不一致的
words.ex: The design of the building was incongruent with its surroundings.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的设计与其周围环境不协调。
words.en: If one thing is incongruent with another, they do not fit together well or are not in harmony.

words.tr: n. 反复无常；不忠；不专一
words.ex: His inconstancy made her sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的不忠让她伤心。
words.en: The quality of being inconstant; lack of stability or uniformity.

words.tr: n. 屡教不改；难望矫正
words.ex: His incorrigibility made the teacher give up on him.
words.ex_cn: 他的不可救药让老师放弃了他。
words.en: The quality or state of being incorrigible, which means not able to be corrected or reformed.

words.ex: The temperature increases by one increment every hour.
words.ex_cn: 温度每小时增加一个单位。
words.en: An increment is an amount by which something increases or is increased.

words.tr: v. 使负罪；指控…有罪；牵连
words.ex: He did not want to incriminate his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让他的朋友涉罪。
words.en: If something incriminates someone, it suggests that they are guilty of a crime or wrongdoing.

words.ex: The incubation of eggs takes about 21 days.
words.ex_cn: 鸡蛋的孵化需要大约21天。
words.en: The process of keeping eggs at the right temperature so that they develop and hatch, or the period of time that a disease takes to develop before symptoms appear.

words.tr: n. 梦淫妖；沉重的精神负担
words.ex: He felt like an incubus pressing on his chest at night.
words.ex_cn: 他感觉晚上有个梦魇压在胸口。
words.en: An incubus is a male demon believed to have sexual intercourse with sleeping women. In a broader sense, it can also refer to a cause of distress or anxiety.

words.tr: v. 反复灌输；谆谆劝导
words.ex: Parents try to inculcate good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To inculcate is to teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions.

words.ex: He tried to inculpate his friend for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把错误归咎于他的朋友。
words.en: To inculpate someone means to accuse them of a crime or to make them seem guilty of it.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: The memory of her smile is indelible.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑的记忆是无法磨灭的。
words.en: If you say that something leaves an indelible impression, you mean that it is very unlikely to be forgotten.

words.ex: The insurance company agreed to indemnify the victims for their losses.
words.ex_cn: 保险公司同意赔偿受害者的损失。
words.en: To indemnify someone means to compensate them for harm or loss they have suffered.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.ex: He suffered an indignity at the hands of the guards.
words.ex_cn: 他受到了守卫的羞辱。
words.en: An indignity is a situation or event that causes you to feel ashamed or embarrassed because it involves something that is unfair or insulting.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.tr: v. 使正式就任；给予职位
words.ex: They inducted the new mayor with a ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过一场仪式使新市长正式就任。
words.en: To induct someone into a position or organization means to formally install them in that position or officially introduce them into that organization.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.tr:
v. 使醉；使陶醉
n. 酒鬼
words.ex: He was inebriated after a few drinks at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上喝了点酒后便醉了。
words.en: To make someone drunk or to exhilarate or stupefy as if with alcohol.

words.tr: adj. 不可言喻的；无法形容的；避讳的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was ineffable.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是无法言喻的。
words.en: If you describe something as ineffable, you mean that it is so impressive or extreme that it cannot be described in words.

words.tr: n. 非弹性； 无弹力
words.ex: The inelasticity of demand means people buy the same amount even if prices rise.
words.ex_cn: 需求的非弹性意味着即使价格上涨，人们购买的数量也不会改变。
words.en: The lack of elasticity or responsiveness in the face of changes in price or income.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
words.ex: The outcome was ineluctable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不可避免的。
words.en: Something that is ineluctable cannot be avoided or escaped from.

words.tr: adj. 不适当的；不明智的
words.ex: It would be inexpedient to disclose the details now.
words.ex_cn: 现在透露细节是不明智的。
words.en: If you say that something is inexpedient, you mean that it is not practical or convenient to do in a particular situation, because it is likely to lead to problems or difficulties.

words.tr: adj. 不能抵偿的；不能平息的
words.ex: His crimes were deemed inexpiable by society.
words.ex_cn: 他的罪行被社会视为不可赎回的。
words.en: If a crime or sin is inexpiable, it is so bad that it cannot be forgiven or atoned for.

words.ex: The infantry marched through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 步兵穿过森林行进。
words.en: Infantry refers to soldiers who fight on foot, especially in contrast to cavalry or artillery.

words.tr: v. 使冲昏头脑；弄糊涂；使着迷
words.ex: He is infatuated with his new classmate.
words.ex_cn: 他迷上了他的新同学。
words.en: To inspire with a foolish or extravagant love or admiration.

words.ex: His infelicitous remark made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他那不恰当的言论让所有人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe something as infelicitous, you mean that it is inappropriate or unsuitable in some way.

words.tr: n. 不恰当的言行；不幸
words.ex: The infelicity of his words made her sad.
words.ex_cn: 他话语的不妥让她感到难过。
words.en: The state or quality of being infelicitous; inappropriateness or unhappiness.

words.tr: adj. 地狱的；恶魔似的；可憎的
words.ex: The heat in the room was infernal.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的热量像地狱一样。
words.en: If you describe something as infernal, you are emphasizing that it is extremely annoying or unpleasant.

words.ex: His rude words inflamed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了人群。
words.en: To inflame a situation or feeling means to make it much more intense or serious.

words.tr: n. 发炎；炎症；燃烧；激动
words.ex: The redness and swelling show inflammation.
words.ex_cn: 发红和肿胀表明有炎症。
words.en: Inflammation is a condition in which a part of your body becomes red, swollen, and painful as a reaction to infection or injury.

words.ex: There was a large influx of tourists during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天期间涌入了大量游客。
words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 了解情况的； v. 通知；告知；“inform”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is an informed voter who reads the news daily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个了解情况的选民，每天阅读新闻。
words.en: If someone is informed, they know a lot about a particular subject or situation.

words.tr: n. 告密者；告发者；线人
words.ex: The informer told the police about the crime.
words.ex_cn: 举报人向警方透露了这起犯罪。
words.en: An informer is someone who gives information to the police or other authorities about criminal activities.

words.ex: He got a fine for a small infraction.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个小违规行为被罚款。
words.en: An infraction is a violation or infringement of a law, agreement, or set of rules.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.ex: The ingestion of too much sugar can cause health problems.
words.ex_cn: 摄食过多的糖会导致健康问题。
words.en: The process of taking food, drink, or another substance into the body by swallowing or absorbing it.

words.ex: He tries to ingratiate himself with his boss by bringing coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上送咖啡给老板，试图讨好他。
words.en: If someone tries to ingratiate themselves with you, they do things to try and make you like them.

words.ex: The security guard checked the ID of everyone attempting ingress.
words.ex_cn: 保安检查了每一个试图进入的人的身份证。
words.en: Ingress refers to the act of entering or the means by which one enters.

words.ex: He inhale the fresh air in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他早上吸入新鲜空气。
words.en: To inhale means to breathe in air, smoke, or gas.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.ex: The judge condemned the iniquity of the corrupt system.
words.ex_cn: 法官谴责了腐败制度的邪恶。
words.en: Iniquity refers to gross immorality or injustice.

words.ex: She had only the faintest inkling of what he was planning.
words.ex_cn: 她对他正在策划的事情只有一点模糊的概念。
words.en: An inkling is a slight knowledge or suspicion of something.

words.tr: n. （医院或监狱中的）同宿者；监犯
words.ex: The inmate shared his cell with two others.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯和另外两个人共用一间牢房。
words.en: A person who is confined in a prison, hospital, or other institution.

words.tr:
n. 影射；暗指
v. 旁敲侧击地表达；含沙射影
words.ex: He made an innuendo about her being late.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她迟到了。
words.en: An indirect or subtle, usually derogatory implication in expression; an insinuation.

words.tr: v. 预防注射；接种疫苗
words.ex: The doctor will inoculate the child against measles.
words.ex_cn: 医生会给这个孩子接种麻疹疫苗。
words.en: To inoculate someone against a disease means to inject a weak form of the disease into their body as a way of protecting them against it.

words.ex: The army made an inroad into the enemy's territory.
words.ex_cn: 军队对敌方领土发动了一次袭击。
words.en: An inroad is an advance or penetration often at the expense of someone or something, or a hostile incursion or invasion.

words.tr: adj. 疯狂的；精神失常的；精神错乱的
words.ex: He thinks it's insane to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 他认为无证驾驶是疯狂的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insane, you mean that they are very foolish or crazy.

words.tr: n. 精神错乱；精神失常；疯狂
words.ex: He was sent to a hospital because of insanity.
words.ex_cn: 他因精神错乱被送进了医院。
words.en: Insanity is the state of being seriously mentally ill; madness.

words.ex: He inscribes his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在石头上。
words.en: To write, mark, or engrave (words, symbols, etc.) on a surface, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；难以理解的；神秘莫测的
words.ex: His expression was inscrutable.
words.ex_cn: 他的表情难以捉摸。
words.en: If someone or something is inscrutable, it is impossible to understand or know what they are thinking or feeling.

words.ex: He wore the school insignia on his jacket.
words.ex_cn: 他把学校的徽章戴在夹克上。
words.en: An insignia is a badge or a sign that shows someone's rank, membership, or achievements.

words.ex: Her insolence made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 她的傲慢让每个人都感到不适。
words.en: Insolence is rude and disrespectful behavior.

words.ex: The company went bankrupt due to insolvency.
words.ex_cn: 由于资不抵债，这家公司破产了。
words.en: The state of being unable to pay one's debts.

words.tr: n. 漫不经心； 漠不关心；无忧无虑
words.ex: He showed insouciance when the teacher scolded him.
words.ex_cn: 老师批评他时，他表现得毫不在意。
words.en: A feeling of not worrying about anything because you do not think anything bad will happen.

words.tr: adj. 漫不经心的；漠不关心的；无忧无虑的
words.ex: She wore an insouciant smile as she walked down the street.
words.ex_cn: 她走在街上，脸上挂着一副无忧无虑的微笑。
words.en: If you say that someone is insouciant, you mean that they are calm and seem not to worry or care about anything.

words.ex: The painting gave me inspiration.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画给了我灵感。
words.en: Inspiration is a feeling of enthusiasm you get from someone or something, which gives you new and creative ideas.

words.tr: v. 鼓舞；激励；“inspire”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 有灵感的；
words.ex: Her speech inspired the students to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 她的演讲鼓舞了学生们更加努力学习。
words.en: If someone or something inspires you, they give you new ideas and a strong feeling of enthusiasm.

words.ex: The chef inspissated the sauce to make it thicker.
words.ex_cn: 厨师将酱汁浓缩以使其更浓稠。
words.en: To thicken or condense a liquid by evaporation or by adding a thickening agent.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.ex: The king will instate a new prime minister next week.
words.ex_cn: 国王下周将任命一位新的首相。
words.en: To instate someone in a position or job means to formally establish them in that position or job.

words.tr: v. 逐步渗透；逐渐灌输
words.ex: Parents try to instill good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To instill something in someone means to gradually but firmly establish an idea or attitude in their mind.

words.ex: The water supply is insufficient for the whole village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对整个村庄来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is insufficient, it is not enough for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The language barrier was insuperable for him.
words.ex_cn: 语言障碍对他来说是难以克服的。
words.en: If you describe a problem or obstacle as insuperable, you mean that it is impossible to overcome.

words.ex: The insurrection failed because people did not support it.
words.ex_cn: 这次起义失败了，因为人们不支持它。
words.en: An insurrection is a violent uprising against an authority or government.

words.tr: n. 不可触知性；无形；不能把握
words.ex: The intangibility of emotions makes them difficult to measure.
words.ex_cn: 情感的无形性使得它们难以测量。
words.en: The quality of being intangible; not having physical presence or not being able to be touched.

words.ex: Honesty is an integral part of a good relationship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是良好关系中不可或缺的一部分。
words.en: Something that is integral is very important or necessary. If something is an integral part of a whole, it is an essential part of that whole.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: The storm will intensify tonight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴今晚会加强。
words.en: To make or become more intense or intensive.

words.ex: He inter his dog in the backyard.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的狗关在后院里。
words.en: To place a dead body in the ground or in a tomb.

words.ex: He will intercede for his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他会为他的朋友出面说情。
words.en: If you intercede with someone, you try to persuade them to forgive someone or end their disagreement with them.

words.ex: The police intercepted the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察拦截了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If you intercept someone or something that is going from one place to another, you stop them before they get there.

words.tr: adj. 各学科间的；跨学科的；
words.ex: The project is interdisciplinary, combining biology and chemistry.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目是跨学科的，结合了生物学和化学。
words.en: Involving two or more academic, scientific, or artistic disciplines.

words.ex: The radio signal suffered from interference.
words.ex_cn: 收音机信号受到了干扰。
words.en: Interference refers to the action of interfering or the process of being interfered with, especially in a context where it is unwelcome or inappropriate.

words.tr: n. 感叹词；插入之语词
words.ex: He shouted 'Wow!' as an interjection.
words.ex_cn: 他喊了一声‘哇！’作为感叹词。
words.en: An interjection is a word or phrase that expresses a strong feeling or emotion, such as surprise, pleasure, or anger, and is often used in speech to interrupt or emphasize a statement.

words.ex: The threads of the tapestry are intricately interlace.
words.ex_cn: 挂毯的线错综复杂地交织在一起。
words.en: If things interlace or are interlaced, they are joined together by being crossed over each other.

words.ex: His speech was interlarded with technical jargon.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲中夹杂着专业术语。
words.en: To insert or mix something among other things, especially in a way that is noticeable or unwelcome.

words.tr:
v. （使）连锁；（使）相互扣住
n. 互锁设备
words.ex: The puzzle pieces interlock tightly.
words.ex_cn: 拼图块紧密地互锁在一起。
words.en: To interlock means to fit together firmly or closely, or to cause things to fit together in this way.

words.tr: n. 闯入者；干涉他人事务者
words.ex: The interloper walked into the meeting without permission.
words.ex_cn: 那个闯入者未经允许走进了会议。
words.en: An interloper is someone who becomes involved in a situation or place where they are not wanted or are considered not to belong.

words.tr: n. 间歇；插曲；幕间节目
words.ex: He took an interlude to drink water.
words.ex_cn: 他休息了一下喝水。
words.en: An interlude is a short period of time that comes in the middle of something, or a short piece of music, talk, or entertainment that comes between the main parts of a performance or event.

words.ex: The colors intermingle in the painting.
words.ex_cn: 画中的颜色混合在一起。
words.en: If things intermingle, they mix together or are mixed together.

words.tr: n. 间歇；暂停；中间休息
words.ex: There is a ten-minute intermission during the play.
words.ex_cn: 这场戏中间有十分钟的中场休息。
words.en: An intermission is a short break between parts of a play, film, concert, or other performance.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.tr: v. 置于…之间；插入；插嘴；介入
words.ex: The mediator tried to interpose before the situation escalated.
words.ex_cn: 调解人试图在局势升级之前进行干预。
words.en: If you interpose something between two people or things, you place it between them. If you interpose, you interrupt with a comment or question.

words.ex: The police will interrogate the suspect tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 警察明天会审问嫌疑人。
words.en: To interrogate someone means to ask them a lot of questions for a long time in order to get information, sometimes using threats.

words.tr:
adj. 疑问的；质问的
n. 疑问句；疑问词；疑问结构
words.ex: He asked an interrogative sentence to check her understanding.
words.ex_cn: 他问了一个疑问句来检查她的理解。
words.en: An interrogative word or sentence is used to ask a question.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.ex: She intersperses flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里分散地种着花。
words.en: To place something at intervals among other things.

words.ex: The scientist examined the interstices between the rocks.
words.ex_cn: 科学家检查了岩石之间的裂缝。
words.en: An interstice is a small or narrow space or gap between things.

words.ex: The two stories intertwine in the final chapter.
words.ex_cn: 这两个故事在最后一章交织在一起。
words.en: If two or more things are intertwined, they are closely connected with each other in many ways.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: The artist interweaves colors to make a beautiful pattern.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家将颜色交织在一起，创造出美丽的图案。
words.en: To interweave means to weave or blend together two or more things so that they cannot be separated easily.

words.tr:
adj. 未留遗嘱的
n. 无遗嘱的死亡者
words.ex: The estate was distributed according to the laws of intestate succession.
words.ex_cn: 遗产根据无遗嘱继承法进行了分配。
words.en: If someone dies intestate, they die without having made a will.

words.tr: v.  使中毒；使醉；使 ...陶醉
words.ex: The dirty water can intoxicate animals.
words.ex_cn: 脏水会使动物中毒。
words.en: To intoxicate someone means to make them lose control of their actions or behavior because they have drunk alcohol or taken drugs. It can also mean to make someone feel very excited and happy.

words.ex: He does not want to intrude on their conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他不想插话他们的谈话。
words.en: To intrude means to enter somewhere or become involved in a situation where you are not wanted or are not supposed to be.

words.tr: v. 淹没；泛滥；使不胜负荷；使应接不暇
words.ex: The rain inundated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 大雨淹没了这个小镇。
words.en: To inundate means to flood or overwhelm something with a large amount of water or things.

words.ex: His speech was full of invective against his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了对对手的辱骂。
words.en: Invective is rude and unpleasant things that people shout at someone they hate or are angry with.

words.tr: v. 猛烈抨击；痛骂；激烈反对
words.ex: He often inveighs against the corruption in the government.
words.ex_cn: 他经常猛烈抨击政府中的腐败现象。
words.en: If you inveigh against something, you criticize it strongly.

words.ex: He tried to inveigle her into lending him money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图哄骗她借钱给他。
words.en: If you inveigle someone into doing something, you cleverly persuade them to do it when they do not really want to.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.tr: adj. 招致不满的；不公平的；难以决定的
words.ex: He made an invidious comparison between his two students.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的两个学生做了令人不快的比较。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as invidious, you mean that it is likely to make you unpopular because it is unpleasant or difficult to do.

words.tr:
n. 发票；发货单；
v. 开发票；记清单；
words.ex: He paid the bill after receiving the invoice.
words.ex_cn: 他收到发票后付了款。
words.en: An invoice is a document that lists goods or services that have been provided and says how much money you owe for them.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: He didn't care about an iota of the details.
words.ex_cn: 他对这些细节的极小量都不在意。
words.en: An iota is an extremely small amount of something.

words.ex: His voice trembled with ire.
words.ex_cn: 他的声音因愤怒而颤抖。
words.en: Anger or wrath.

words.ex: The butterfly's wings displayed a stunning iridescence in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶的翅膀在阳光下展现出令人惊叹的彩虹色。
words.en: The phenomenon whereby certain surfaces display a play of colors that change with the angle of view or illumination.

words.tr: v. 使恼怒；使厌烦；使烦恼
words.ex: The loud noise irks her every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上，巨大的噪音都让她感到烦躁。
words.en: To irritate, annoy, or exasperate someone.

words.tr: adj. 使人厌烦的；令人生气的
words.ex: The irksome noise from the construction site kept me awake all night.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的恼人噪音让我整晚都没睡着。
words.en: If something is irksome, it annoys you.

words.tr: adj. 不能补救的；不能挽回的
words.ex: The damage to the painting was irremediable.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的损坏是无法挽回的。
words.en: If something is irremediable, it is impossible to correct or improve.

words.ex: The irritation on his arm hurt when he touched it.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上的疼痛处一碰就疼。
words.en: Irritation is the feeling of annoyance, especially when something keeps happening that you do not like.

words.ex: We planned our itinerary before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们在旅行前规划了路线。
words.en: An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.

words.tr:
v. 刺；戳；捅；用拳猛击
n. 刺；戳；捅；猛击
words.ex: He gave a quick jab to his opponent.
words.ex_cn: 他给了对手一记快速的刺拳。
words.en: To poke or thrust sharply; to make a quick, sharp punch.

words.tr:
v. 急促、含混不清地讲话；吱吱喳喳地叫；喋喋不休
n. 急促不清的话；吱吱喳喳的叫声；闲聊
words.ex: He was jabbering on about his latest project.
words.ex_cn: 他正在激动地谈论他最新的项目。
words.en: To talk rapidly, indistinctly, or nonsensically; chatter.

words.tr: adj. 锯齿状的； v. “jag”的过去式；
words.ex: The jagged edge of the rock cut his hand.
words.ex_cn: 岩石的锯齿状边缘割伤了他的手。
words.en: Something that is jagged has a rough, uneven shape or edge with lots of sharp points.

words.tr: n. 门窗的侧柱；边框；旁柱
words.ex: The carpenter measured the jamb to ensure the door fit perfectly.
words.ex_cn: 木匠测量了门侧壁，以确保门能完美贴合。
words.en: A jamb is the vertical side of a doorway or window frame.

words.tr: n. 欢乐的集会；喧闹的集会；庆祝会
words.ex: The kids joined a big jamboree last summer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们去年夏天参加了一个盛大的集会。
words.en: A jamboree is a large, festive gathering or celebration, often involving music, dancing, and other forms of entertainment.

words.ex: He told a silly jape to make his friends laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个愚蠢的玩笑来逗朋友们笑。
words.en: A jape is a practical joke or a witty remark.

words.ex: She stored jam in a glass jar.
words.ex_cn: 她把果酱存放在一个玻璃罐里。
words.en: A jar is a glass or clay container with a wide opening at the top and a lid, used especially for storing food.

words.ex: He used too much jargon in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中用了太多行话。
words.en: Special words or expressions that are used by a particular profession or group and are difficult for others to understand.

words.tr:
adj. 刺耳的；不和谐的；冲突的
v. （使）震动；令人不快；冲突；不一致；“jar”的现在分词
words.ex: The loud music was jarring to her ears.
words.ex_cn: 那刺耳的音乐让她感到不适。
words.en: If you describe something as jarring, you mean that it has a harsh and unpleasant effect, especially because it seems out of place.

words.tr:
n. 黄疸病；偏见
v. 使产生黄疸；使怀偏见
words.ex: The baby had jaundice and needed light therapy.
words.ex_cn: 这个婴儿患有黄疸，需要光疗。
words.en: Jaundice is a medical condition in which the skin and the whites of the eyes become yellow, caused by an excess of bile pigment in the blood.

words.tr:
adj. 患黄疸病的；有偏见的
v. 使产生黄疸；使怀偏见；“jaundice”的过去式
words.ex: His judgment was jaundiced by his personal dislike for the candidate.
words.ex_cn: 他对候选人的个人反感使他的判断带有偏见。
words.en: If someone has a jaundiced view of something, they see it in a negative way because they are jealous or bitter.

words.tr:
n. 远足；短途旅游
v. 远足；短途旅游
words.ex: We decided to take a jaunt to the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 我们决定去乡间远足。
words.en: A short journey or excursion, especially one taken for pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 轻松活泼的；得意洋洋的；自信满满的
words.ex: He walked with a jaunty step, clearly pleased with himself.
words.ex_cn: 他步伐轻快，显然对自己感到很满意。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as jaunty, you mean that they are full of confidence and energy.

words.ex: He felt jealousy when his friend got a new bike.
words.ex_cn: 当他的朋友得到一辆新自行车时，他感到妒忌。
words.en: Jealousy is the feeling of anger or bitterness which someone has when they think that another person is trying to take a lover or friend, or a possession, away from them.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄
n. 嘲笑；讥笑的言语
words.ex: The crowd began to jeer at the losing team.
words.ex_cn: 观众开始对落败的队伍嘘声四起。
words.en: To jeer means to laugh at someone or shout rude remarks at them in order to show that you do not respect them.

words.tr: adj. 空洞的；枯燥乏味的；不成熟的；缺乏营养的
words.ex: His jejune remarks made no sense to the audience.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的言论让听众无法理解。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as jejune, you are criticizing them for being very simple and unsophisticated.

words.ex: He put his job in jeopardy by being late every day.
words.ex_cn: 他因为每天迟到而危及了自己的工作。
words.en: Jeopardy is a situation of exposure to danger or harm.

words.ex: He gave the rope a sudden jerk to pull it up.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地一拉绳子，把它拉了上来。
words.en: If you jerk something or someone in a particular direction, or they jerk in a particular direction, they move a short distance very suddenly and quickly.

words.tr:
adj. 爱开玩笑的；说着玩的
v. 开玩笑；“jest”的现在分词
words.ex: He was known for his jesting remarks.
words.ex_cn: 他以幽默的言辞而闻名。
words.en: Jesting is the act of making jokes or saying things in a humorous way.

words.tr:
v. 丢弃；放弃；扔掉
n. 投弃；抛弃；投弃货物
words.ex: The pilot had to jettison extra fuel to land safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员不得不抛掉多余的燃料以安全着陆。
words.en: To jettison something means to throw it away or get rid of it, usually because it is not wanted or needed.

words.tr:
v. 嘲讽；嘲弄；相匹配
n. 嘲弄；挖苦
words.ex: His story doesn't jibe with the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他的故事与事实不符。
words.en: If one thing jibes with another, they agree or are very similar.
