words.tr: n. 沙文主义；侵略主义
words.ex: He shouted with jingoism during the national parade.
words.ex_cn: 他在国庆游行中带着沙文主义大喊大叫。
words.en: Jingoism is an extreme form of patriotism that often involves a belligerent foreign policy, advocating the use of threats or actual force against other countries in order to safeguard what it perceives as its country's national interests.

words.ex: The jockey rode the horse to win the race.
words.ex_cn: 骑师骑马赢得了比赛。
words.en: A jockey is someone who rides horses in races, especially as a profession.

words.ex: His jocund laughter filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 他那快活的笑声充满了整个房间。
words.en: If you describe someone as jocund, you mean that they are cheerful and happy.

words.ex: He jogs every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上慢跑以保持健康。
words.en: To run at a slow, steady pace, especially as a form of exercise.

words.tr:
adj. 愉快的；快乐的
v. 开玩笑；作乐
adv. 非常；很
words.ex: He is jolly at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上很快乐。
words.en: If you describe someone as jolly, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.ex: The sudden jolt woke me up.
words.ex_cn: 突然的震动把我惊醒了。
words.en: If something jolts or if something jolts it, it moves suddenly and quite violently.

words.ex: His josh made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他的玩笑让大家都笑了。
words.en: To tease or joke in a playful way.

words.tr:
v. 挤；推；撞；争夺
n. 挤拥；推撞
words.ex: People jostle in the crowded market.
words.ex_cn: 人们在拥挤的市场里推挤。
words.en: To jostle someone means to push or knock against them, usually in a crowd.

words.ex: He quickly jot down the phone number.
words.ex_cn: 他匆忙记下了电话号码。
words.en: To write or mark down quickly or briefly.

words.tr:
v. 猛烈的震动；颠簸
n. 猛烈的震动；颠簸
words.ex: The old car jounced us up and down on the bumpy road.
words.ex_cn: 那辆旧车在崎岖的路上颠簸着我们上下晃动。
words.en: To jounce means to move up and down abruptly and roughly, often as a result of being on a bumpy surface.

words.tr: adj.  快活的；愉快的；高兴的
words.ex: His jovial nature made him popular among his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他天性快活，这使他在同事中很受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone as jovial, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.tr: n. 欢腾；欢欣鼓舞；欢庆
words.ex: There was a lot of jubilation when the team won the championship.
words.ex_cn: 当球队赢得冠军时，人们欢呼雀跃。
words.en: A feeling of great happiness and triumph.

words.tr: adj. 司法的；法庭的；审判的；
words.ex: The judicial system protects people's rights.
words.ex_cn: 司法系统保护人民的权利。
words.en: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law.

words.ex: His judiciousness in decision-making has earned him respect.
words.ex_cn: 他在决策中的明智为他赢得了尊重。
words.en: The quality of having or showing good judgment; prudence.

words.ex: He poured milk from a jug.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个水壶里倒牛奶。
words.en: A jug is a container used for holding and pouring liquids. It typically has a handle and a spout for easy pouring.

words.tr: adj. 心惊肉跳的；胆战心惊的；神经质的
words.ex: She was feeling jumpy after watching a horror movie.
words.ex_cn: 看完恐怖电影后，她感到焦虑不安。
words.en: If you are jumpy, you are nervous and easily frightened.

words.ex: The car stopped at the junction.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在交叉路口停了下来。
words.en: A junction is a place where two or more things, especially roads or railways, come together.

words.tr: n. 管辖权；司法权；裁判权；
words.ex: The court has jurisdiction over this case.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这个案件有管辖权。
words.en: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments.

words.ex: He gave a justification for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他为迟到提供了一个正当的理由。
words.en: A justification for something is an acceptable reason or explanation for it.

words.ex: He juxtaposes old photos with new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他把老照片和新照片放在一起。
words.en: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.

words.tr: adj. 万花筒似的；千变万化的；五花八门的
words.ex: The kaleidoscopic lights made the room look magical.
words.ex_cn: 五彩缤纷的灯光让房间看起来像魔法一样。
words.en: If you describe something as kaleidoscopic, you mean that it consists of a lot of very different parts, such as different colors, patterns, or shapes.

words.ex: The kangaroo jumps high in the Australian wild.
words.ex_cn: 袋鼠在澳大利亚的野外跳得很高。
words.en: A kangaroo is a large Australian animal which moves by jumping on its back legs. Female kangaroos carry their babies in a pouch on their stomach.

words.ex: His ken does not include quantum physics.
words.ex_cn: 他的知识范围不包括量子物理。
words.en: Ken is the range of one's knowledge or understanding.

words.tr:
n. 狗舍；养狗场
v. 把…置于狗舍
words.ex: The dog sleeps in a kennel at night.
words.ex_cn: 狗晚上睡在狗窝里。
words.en: A kennel is a small hut made for a dog to sleep in, or a place where dogs are bred or looked after.

words.ex: The kernel of the computer is the operating system.
words.ex_cn: 计算机的核心是操作系统。
words.en: The kernel of something such as a nut or a seed is the part inside the shell. The kernel of an idea or a theory is the central and most important part of it.

words.tr:
v. 绑架；劫持；诱拐
n. 绑架罪
words.ex: The man tried to kidnap the little girl.
words.ex_cn: 这个人试图绑架那个小女孩。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force, typically to obtain a ransom.

words.tr: n. 扫兴的人；煞风景的人
words.ex: She was a killjoy, always finding something to complain about.
words.ex_cn: 她是个令人扫兴的人，总是能找到抱怨的事情。
words.en: A killjoy is someone who spoils other people's fun or enjoyment.

words.ex: She invited all her kin to the family reunion.
words.ex_cn: 她邀请了所有亲属参加家庭聚会。
words.en: Your kin are your relatives.

words.tr: v. 点燃；生火；激起；发亮
words.ex: He used a match to kindle the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: To kindle something means to cause it to begin burning or to arouse or inspire it.

words.tr:
n. 船长；运动队队长
v. 担任船长、球队队长等
words.ex: The skipper guided the boat safely through the storm.
words.ex_cn: 船长带领船只安全地穿过了风暴。
words.en: The person who is in charge of a ship or boat.

words.ex: He has a knack for fixing bikes.
words.ex_cn: 他有修自行车的技巧。
words.en: A knack is a special skill or ability that someone has, especially one that is hard to explain or teach.

words.ex: He kneads dough every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上揉面团。
words.en: To knead is to press and stretch dough or another substance with your hands in order to make it smooth and ready to use.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.tr: adj. 多结节的；难以解决的；棘手的
words.ex: The old tree had a knotty trunk.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树有一个多结节的树干。
words.en: A knotty problem or issue is very complicated and difficult to solve.

words.ex: He received kudos for winning the science competition.
words.ex_cn: 他因赢得科学竞赛而获得荣誉。
words.en: Praise and honor received for an achievement.

words.tr: adj. 易变化的；不稳定的
words.ex: The labile emotions of the character made the story unpredictable.
words.ex_cn: 这个角色易变的情绪使得故事变得不可预测。
words.en: If you describe someone as labile, you mean that their emotions or behavior are unstable and can change quickly.

words.tr:
n. 地方；方位；
v. 安放；安置；
words.ex: This is a quiet place to read books.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个安静的地方读书。
words.en: A particular position or point in space.

words.ex: The accident lacerated his arm.
words.ex_cn: 事故使他的手臂受了伤。
words.en: To lacerate something means to make deep cuts in it, especially in someone's skin.

words.tr: adj. 流泪的；爱哭的；引人落泪的
words.ex: The lachrymose melody of the violin added to the somber atmosphere.
words.ex_cn: 小提琴哀伤的旋律增添了忧郁的气氛。
words.en: If you describe someone as lachrymose, you mean that they are sad or likely to cry easily.

words.tr: adj. 无光泽的；暗淡的；无生气的；乏善可陈的
words.ex: The paint on the car looked lackluster after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴过后，车漆显得暗淡无光。
words.en: If you describe something as lackluster, you mean that it is not exciting or not very good quality.

words.tr: adj. 乳的；乳汁的；得自乳汁的
words.ex: The lactic acid buildup caused muscle soreness.
words.ex_cn: 乳酸堆积导致了肌肉酸痛。
words.en: Relating to or derived from milk.

words.ex: The lion returned to its lair at night.
words.ex_cn: 狮子晚上回到了它的兽穴。
words.en: A lair is a place where a wild animal lives, often hidden or difficult to find.

words.ex: The angry father lambasted the bully with his belt.
words.ex_cn: 愤怒的父亲用皮带痛打了那个欺凌者。
words.en: If you lambaste someone, you criticize them severely, usually in public.

words.tr: adj. 可悲的；令人惋惜的；质量低劣的
words.ex: The situation was lamentable, with many people losing their homes.
words.ex_cn: 情况非常可悲，许多人失去了家园。
words.en: If you describe something as lamentable, you mean that it is very unfortunate or disappointing.

words.tr:
n. 讽刺作品
v. 讽刺
words.ex: The cartoon lampooned the president with funny drawings.
words.ex_cn: 这幅漫画用搞笑的图画讽刺了总统。
words.en: To lampoon someone or something means to criticize them very strongly in a humorous way, especially in a piece of writing.

words.ex: The doctor used a lancet to draw a drop of blood.
words.ex_cn: 医生用采血针抽取了一滴血。
words.en: A lancet is a small, broad, two-edged surgical knife or blade with a sharp point used to make small incisions.

words.tr: n. 山崩；塌方；压倒性的胜利
words.ex: The heavy rain caused a landslide.
words.ex_cn: 大雨引发了山体滑坡。
words.en: A landslide is a victory in an election in which a person or political party gets far more votes or seats than their opponents.

words.tr: adj. 无精打采的；疲倦无力的
words.ex: He gave a languid smile before lying down.
words.ex_cn: 他躺下前给了一个慵懒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as languid, you mean that they show little energy or interest and are very slow and casual in their movements.

words.tr: v. 衰弱；凋萎；憔悴；受折磨
words.ex: The prisoner languishes in a dark cell.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯在黑暗的牢房中饱受煎熬。
words.en: If someone languishes somewhere, they are forced to remain and suffer in an unpleasant situation.

words.ex: The hot weather filled the room with a sense of languor.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让房间里充满了倦怠的感觉。
words.en: A pleasant feeling of laziness or tiredness, especially when you are not doing anything.

words.tr: adj. 细长而弯曲的；瘦削的；平直的；稀疏的
words.ex: Her lank hair hung down to her waist.
words.ex_cn: 她那细长柔软的头发垂到了腰部。
words.en: If someone is lank, they are tall and thin in a way that is not attractive.

words.tr: n. 一圈；（人坐着时）大腿部；
words.ex: He ran three laps around the track.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑道上跑了三圈。
words.en: The upper part of the legs of a seated person; a single turn or round in a race or other competition.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr:
n. 猪油
v. 放入猪油于
words.ex: He put lard on the bread.
words.ex_cn: 他把猪油涂在面包上。
words.en: Lard is a white, solid fat obtained from pigs, used in cooking.

words.ex: The company showed its largess by donating to several charities.
words.ex_cn: 公司通过向几家慈善机构捐款展示了它的慷慨。
words.en: Largess refers to the generous giving of gifts or money, often by a person of high status, such as a king or noble, to their subjects or followers.

words.tr: n. 云雀；百灵鸟；玩乐；嬉戏
words.ex: The lark sings loudly at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 云雀在日出时大声歌唱。
words.en: A lark is a small brown bird that is known for its beautiful song. It is also used to describe a carefree adventure or a playful activity.

words.tr: n. 倦怠；疲乏；无精打采
words.ex: He felt lassitude after working all day.
words.ex_cn: 他工作了一整天后感到乏力。
words.en: A state of physical or mental weariness; lack of energy.

words.tr:
n. 套索
v. 用套索套捕
words.ex: The cowboy expertly lassoed the runaway horse.
words.ex_cn: 牛仔熟练地用套索套住了逃跑的马。
words.en: A lasso is a long rope with a loop at one end, used especially by cowboys for catching cattle. To lasso means to catch an animal by throwing a lasso around its neck.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；恒久的； v. 持续；“last”的现在分词；
words.ex: The friendship between them is lasting.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的友谊是持久的。
words.en: Something that is lasting continues to exist or have an effect for a very long time.

words.tr:
n. 门闩；碰锁；弹簧锁
v. 用闩闩上；用碰锁锁上
words.ex: The door has a simple latch to keep it closed.
words.ex_cn: 这扇门有一个简单的门闩来保持关闭。
words.en: A latch is a fastening for a door or gate, consisting of a bar that is lifted from its catch, groove, or hole by a lever, or that slides or is pushed into place.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.tr:
n. 车床
v. 用车床加工
words.ex: He uses a lathe to shape wood.
words.ex_cn: 他用车床加工木材。
words.en: A lathe is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece about an axis of rotation to perform various operations such as cutting, sanding, knurling, drilling, or deformation with tools that are applied to the workpiece to create an object with symmetry about that axis.

words.ex: The window was covered with a lattice of iron bars.
words.ex_cn: 窗户被铁条格子覆盖。
words.en: A lattice is a structure consisting of strips of wood or metal crossed and fastened together with square or diamond-shaped spaces left between.

words.tr:
n. 薰衣草；淡紫色
adj. 淡紫色的
words.ex: She smells the lavender in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里闻着薰衣草的香味。
words.en: Lavender is a small aromatic evergreen shrub of the mint family, with narrow leaves and bluish-purple flowers, used in perfumery and medicine.

words.tr:
adj. 通便的
n. 泻药；通便剂
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a laxative for his constipation.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了一种泻药来治疗便秘。
words.en: A laxative is a substance that you take to make you go to the toilet, especially when you are constipated.

words.tr:
v. 过滤；滤去；渗入
n. 过滤；滤去
words.ex: The soil is leached of nutrients.
words.ex_cn: 土壤中的养分被过滤掉了。
words.en: To leach means to remove or be removed from a substance by a percolating liquid, especially to remove soluble constituents from soil, ash, or similar material by the action of percolating water.

words.tr:
n. 漏洞；泄露；
v. 漏；泄露；
words.ex: The leak in the roof caused water to drip inside.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶的漏洞导致水滴进屋里。
words.en: If a container or pipe leaks, or if it leaks a substance such as liquid or gas, the substance comes out of it accidentally because there is a hole or crack in it.

words.ex: The pipe has a small leakage.
words.ex_cn: 这条管道有一个小泄漏。
words.en: The accidental escape or entry of a substance or radiation through a hole or crack.

words.tr:
adj. 精瘦的；精简的；不景气的；
v. 倾斜；倚靠；
words.ex: The dog is lean and fast.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗精瘦而敏捷。
words.en: If you lean in a particular direction, you bend your body in that direction. If you lean on or against someone or something, you rest against them so that they partly support your weight. If you describe someone as lean, you mean that they are thin but look strong and healthy. If you describe a period of time as lean, you mean that it is a time when people have very little of something, especially money.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.tr:
v. 斜睨；恶意地瞟；抛媚眼
n. 斜睨；恶意的瞟视；媚眼
words.ex: He gave her a leering look.
words.ex_cn: 他色迷迷地看了她一眼。
words.en: To look at someone in an unpleasant way that shows sexual interest.

words.tr: adj. 猜疑的；机警的；有戒心的
words.ex: He was leery of strangers and preferred to keep to himself.
words.ex_cn: 他对陌生人很猜疑，宁愿独来独往。
words.en: If you are leery of something or someone, you are cautious or suspicious about them.

words.tr:
adj. 背风的；下风的；顺风的
adv. 向下风
n. 下风；背风面
words.ex: The boat sailed on the leeward side of the island.
words.ex_cn: 船在岛的背风面航行。
words.en: On the side away from the wind.

words.ex: The legislature passed a new law last week.
words.ex_cn: 立法机构上周通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A legislature is the part of a country's government that is responsible for making laws.

words.ex: He enjoys the leisureliness of Sunday mornings.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢星期天早上的悠闲。
words.en: The quality or state of being leisurely; unhurriedness.

words.ex: The judge showed leniency toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: Leniency is the quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.tr: n. 损害；身体上的伤害
words.ex: The doctor found a lesion on his skin.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的皮肤上发现了一个病灶。
words.en: A lesion is an area of damage to the body, such as a wound, ulcer, or tumor.

words.ex: He felt lethargy after eating too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完太多垃圾食品后感到无精打采。
words.en: Lethargy is the condition or state of being lethargic; sluggishness, drowsiness, or apathy.

words.ex: The levee held back the floodwaters, preventing a disaster.
words.ex_cn: 堤坝挡住了洪水，防止了一场灾难。
words.en: A levee is an embankment built to prevent the overflow of a river.

words.tr: adj. 头脑冷静的；清醒的
words.ex: She is always levelheaded in a crisis.
words.ex_cn: 她在危机中总是保持冷静。
words.en: If you describe a person as levelheaded, you mean that they are calm and sensible even in difficult situations.

words.tr:
v. 征收；征税；征募
n. 征兵；征税
words.ex: The government will levy a new tax next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将征收一项新税。
words.en: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. It can also refer to the act of enlisting or drafting individuals into military service.

words.ex: He uses simple lexical items in his writing.
words.ex_cn: 他在写作中使用简单的词汇项。
words.en: Relating to the words or vocabulary of a language.

words.ex: He is a lexicographer who writes dictionaries.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位编写词典的词典编纂者。
words.en: A lexicographer is a person who writes, compiles, or edits dictionaries.

words.ex: He looked up the word in his lexicon.
words.ex_cn: 他在词典里查了这个词。
words.en: The vocabulary of a person, language, or branch of knowledge.

words.ex: He accepted liability for the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他承担了事故的责任。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a liability, you mean that they cause a lot of problems or embarrassment.

words.ex: He is the liaison between the two departments.
words.ex_cn: 他是两个部门之间的联络人。
words.en: A liaison is a person who acts as a link to assist communication between different groups or organizations.

words.tr:
n. （文字）诽谤
v. 发表文字诽谤（某人）
words.ex: He wrote a false story about her, and it was libel.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于她的虚假文章，这是诽谤。
words.en: A libel is a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation; a written defamation.

words.tr: adj. 诽谤的；损害名誉的
words.ex: The article was filled with libelous accusations.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章充满了诽谤性的指控。
words.en: If a statement in a book, newspaper, or magazine is libelous, it falsely harms the reputation of a person or organization.

words.tr: n. 慷慨大方；宽大；心胸开阔
words.ex: His liberality in sharing his wealth was well-known.
words.ex_cn: 他慷慨分享财富的行为是众所周知的。
words.en: The quality of being generous and open-minded.

words.ex: The address is 720 liberty street.
words.ex_cn: 地址是自由大街720号。
words.en: The state of being free within society from oppressive restrictions imposed by authority on one's way of life, behavior, or political views.

words.ex: He gave a licentious speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上发表了一篇放荡不羁的演讲。
words.en: If you describe a person as licentious, you mean that they are very immoral in their sexual behavior.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: The furniture was made from ligneous materials.
words.ex_cn: 这些家具是用木质材料制成的。
words.en: Relating to, consisting of, or resembling wood.

words.ex: He likens his job to a puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的工作比作一个拼图。
words.en: To liken something to something else is to say that they are similar in some way.

words.ex: The child hurt his limb while playing.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩耍时伤到了肢体。
words.en: A limb is one of the jointed appendages of an animal used for locomotion or grasping: arm; leg; wing; flipper.

words.tr: n. 林波舞；不稳定状态；中间过渡状态
words.ex: The project is currently in limbo while we wait for approval.
words.ex_cn: 该项目目前处于待批准的中间状态。
words.en: A situation of uncertainty or neglect, especially one regarded as being in a state of waiting or not progressing.

words.ex: The artist limned the scene with great detail.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家非常详细地描绘了那个场景。
words.en: To depict or describe in painting or words.

words.ex: The limnetic ecosystem is characterized by its freshwater habitats.
words.ex_cn: 淡水生态系统以其淡水栖息地为特征。
words.en: Relating to or inhabiting the open water of a lake or pond.

words.ex: He rode in a limousine to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他坐豪华轿车去参加婚礼。
words.en: A limousine is a large, luxurious car, especially one driven by a chauffeur and having a partition separating the passengers from the driver.

words.tr:
v. 跛行；蹒跚；瘸着走
adj. 无力的；无生气的
words.ex: He limps after hurting his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他受伤后走路一瘸一拐。
words.en: If someone limps, they walk with difficulty or in an uneven way because one of their legs or feet is hurt.

words.ex: He is a lineal descendant of the founding family.
words.ex_cn: 他是创始家族的直系后裔。
words.en: Lineal means relating to a direct line of descent or ancestry.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.ex: She has a lingual talent for learning new languages.
words.ex_cn: 她有语言学习的天赋。
words.en: Relating to the tongue or language.

words.ex: He is studying linguistics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习语言学。
words.en: Linguistics is the scientific study of language and its structure, including the study of morphology, syntax, phonetics, and semantics.

words.ex: They lionize the famous singer everywhere she goes.
words.ex_cn: 无论她去哪里，人们都把她当作名人追捧。
words.en: To treat someone as a celebrity or hero.

words.ex: Heat will liquefy the ice.
words.ex_cn: 加热会使冰融化。
words.en: To make or become liquid.

words.tr: v. 清算；变卖；消除；铲除
words.ex: The company will liquidate its assets to pay debts.
words.ex_cn: 公司将变卖资产来偿还债务。
words.en: To liquidate a company means to sell its assets in order to pay its debts, or to sell an asset for cash.

words.ex: Her lissome movements captivated the audience.
words.ex_cn: 她柔软敏捷的动作吸引了观众。
words.en: If you describe someone as lissome, you mean they are thin, supple, and graceful.

words.tr:
n. 表；名单；
v. 列出；
words.ex: He wrote his name on the list.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己的名字写在了表上。
words.en: A list is a set of items, especially names, written or printed one after the other.

words.tr: adj. 易弯的；柔软的；动作轻盈的
words.ex: The dancer is lithe and moves gracefully.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者身材柔韧，动作优雅。
words.en: A person or animal that is lithe is thin, supple, and graceful.

words.tr:
n. 一条（面包）
v. 游荡；虚度光阴
words.ex: He bought a loaf of bread from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他从面包店买了一条面包。
words.en: A loaf is a quantity of bread that is shaped and baked in one piece and usually sliced before being eaten. As a verb, to loaf means to spend time in a lazy way, doing nothing in particular.

words.ex: The locus of the accident is near the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 事故的位置在桥附近。
words.en: A particular position or place where something occurs or is situated.

words.ex: He used a common locution in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中使用了一个常见的表达方式。
words.en: A particular style or manner of speaking; a phrase or expression.

words.tr:
n. 原木；航海日志；
v. （正式地）记载；
words.ex: The fire burned brightly with a large log.
words.ex_cn: 大火用一根大原木烧得很旺。
words.en: A log is a piece of a thick branch or trunk of a tree that has been cut so that it can be used for fuel or for making things. A log is also a written record of events, often on a ship or aircraft.

words.ex: The company improved its logistics to deliver packages faster.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司改进了物流，以更快地配送包裹。
words.en: Logistics refers to the detailed organization and implementation of a complex operation.

words.ex: He is loitering near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他正在公园附近闲逛。
words.en: If someone loiters somewhere, they remain there or walk up and down without any real purpose.

words.tr: adj. 气长的；啰嗦的；冗长的
words.ex: His long-winded speech made everyone sleepy.
words.ex_cn: 他冗长的演讲让所有人都犯困。
words.en: If you describe something that someone says or writes as long-winded, you are critical of it because it is too long, often because the same thing is said more than once.

words.ex: He tried to loosen the tight screw.
words.ex_cn: 他试图拧松那颗紧的螺丝。
words.en: If you loosen something or if it loosens, it becomes less tight, less firmly fixed, or less strongly attached.

words.tr:
v. 大步走；大步跑
n. 大步慢跑；平稳、轻松的步伐
words.ex: The deer loped gracefully through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 鹿优雅地大步慢跑穿过森林。
words.en: To run or move with a long, easy stride.

words.tr: adj. 倾向一方的；不平衡的；悬殊的
words.ex: The game was lopsided, and one team won by 10 points.
words.ex_cn: 这场比赛比分悬殊，一支队伍以10分获胜。
words.en: Something that is lopsided is uneven because one side is lower or heavier than the other.

words.ex: He is well-versed in the lore of ancient civilizations.
words.ex_cn: 他对古代文明的知识了如指掌。
words.en: Knowledge and traditions relating to a particular subject or held by a particular group.

words.ex: There are a lot of books on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书架上有许多书。
words.en: A lot refers to a large number or amount of something. It can also mean a piece of land or someone's fate or destiny.

words.ex: He bought a lottery ticket last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周买了一张彩票。
words.en: A lottery is a type of gambling game in which people buy numbered tickets. Several numbers are then chosen, and the people who have those numbers on their tickets win a prize.

words.ex: He was regarded as a clumsy lout by his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他的同事们认为他是个笨拙的人。
words.en: A lout is a man who behaves in a rude and aggressive way.

words.ex: He made a loutish noise at the dinner table.
words.ex_cn: 他在餐桌上发出了粗鲁的噪音。
words.en: If you describe someone as loutish, you are critical of them because they behave in an impolite or aggressive way.

words.tr: adj. 未受过好教育的；粗野的
words.ex: He was rude and lowbred at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 他在晚宴上粗鲁且低俗。
words.en: If you describe someone as lowbred, you mean that they are rude, vulgar, or ill-mannered.

words.ex: The mechanic applied a lubricant to the moving parts.
words.ex_cn: 机械师给活动部件涂上了润滑油。
words.en: A substance, such as oil or grease, used to minimize friction, heat, and wear between mechanical parts in contact with each other.

words.ex: He was solely motivated by the prospect of lucre.
words.ex_cn: 他唯一被钱财的前景所驱动。
words.en: Money, especially when regarded as sordid or distasteful or gained in a dishonorable way.

words.tr: v. 刻苦钻研；专心著作
words.ex: He likes to lucubrate on small ideas for long hours.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢长时间深入思考小想法。
words.en: To study or work laboriously, especially late at night.

words.ex: He had to lug the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不用力拖动那个沉重的箱子穿过房间。
words.en: To carry or drag something heavy with great effort.

words.tr: adj. 微温的；不冷不热的；不热情的
words.ex: The water is lukewarm, so I didn't swim.
words.ex_cn: 水是温的，所以我没游泳。
words.en: If you describe something as lukewarm, you mean that it is only slightly warm, or that it is not very enthusiastic or interested.

words.ex: The factory buys lumber to make furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂购买木材来制造家具。
words.en: Lumber refers to wood that has been processed into beams and planks, a stage in the process of wood production. It is also used to describe the action of moving in a slow, heavy, awkward way.

words.ex: The light output is measured in lumens.
words.ex_cn: 光输出以流明为单位进行测量。
words.en: A unit of luminous flux in the International System of Units, equal to the amount of light emitted per second in a unit solid angle of one steradian by a uniform point source of one candela.

words.ex: The sun is a bright luminary in the sky.
words.ex_cn: 太阳是天空中一个明亮的发光体。
words.en: A luminary is a person who is very famous and highly respected, especially in a particular field.

words.ex: He ate a lump of sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块糖。
words.en: A lump is a solid piece of something, often with no particular shape. If you lump things together, you put them together in a group or treat them as the same.

words.ex: The lunatic was taken to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯人被送到了医院。
words.en: A lunatic is someone who behaves in a crazy or very foolish way.

words.tr:
n. 猛冲；冲刺；扑
v. 猛冲；冲刺；扑
words.ex: He made a sudden lunge at the ball.
words.ex_cn: 他突然向前扑向球。
words.en: If you lunge in a particular direction, you move in that direction suddenly and forcefully.

words.tr:
n. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
v. 突然倾斜；急动；踉跄
words.ex: The boat made a sudden lurch to the left.
words.ex_cn: 船突然向左倾斜。
words.en: If you lurch, you move suddenly and uncontrollably in one direction.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；甘美的；满足感官的；性感的
words.ex: The fruit was luscious and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这种水果甘甜可口。
words.en: If you describe something as luscious, you mean that it is very pleasant to taste, smell, look at, or listen to.

words.tr:
n. 强烈的性欲；强烈的欲望
v. 对…有极强的性欲（或欲望）
words.ex: His lust for power ruined his relationships.
words.ex_cn: 他对权力的强烈欲望毁掉了他的关系。
words.en: Lust is a strong feeling of wanting to have or to do something, especially sexual desire.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: The lustrous pearl shone under the light.
words.ex_cn: 这颗有光泽的珍珠在光下闪耀。
words.en: Something that is lustrous shines brightly and gently, often because it is very smooth or clean.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；生气勃勃的；健壮的
words.ex: The young man sang a lusty song at the party.
words.ex_cn: 那个年轻人在派对上唱了一首嘹亮的歌。
words.en: If you describe someone as lusty, you mean that they are strong and healthy and full of energy.

words.ex: She stayed in a luxurious hotel with gold faucets.
words.ex_cn: 她住进了一家有金色水龙头的奢侈酒店。
words.en: Something that is luxurious is very comfortable and expensive, and often involves great pleasure or indulgence.

words.tr: adj. 淋巴的；苍白无力的
words.ex: The lymphatic system plays a crucial role in the immune response.
words.ex_cn: 淋巴系统在免疫反应中起着至关重要的作用。
words.en: Relating to, affecting, or produced by lymph or the lymphatic system.

words.ex: She macerated the fruit in wine overnight.
words.ex_cn: 她把水果在酒中浸泡了一整夜。
words.en: To macerate something means to soften it, or to cause it to break down, by soaking it in a liquid.

words.ex: The machinations of the rival company were uncovered.
words.ex_cn: 竞争对手公司的阴谋被揭露了。
words.en: A machination is a plot or scheme, especially one that is complex or devious.

words.tr: n. 牧歌；无伴奏合唱歌曲
words.ex: The choir sang a beautiful madrigal at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 合唱团在音乐会上演唱了一首优美的牧歌。
words.en: A madrigal is a type of secular vocal music composition, usually a part song, of the Renaissance and early Baroque eras. Traditionally, madrigals were unaccompanied; the number of voices varied from two to eight, and most frequently from three to six.

words.tr:
n. 品红；紫红色
adj. 品红色的；洋红色的
words.ex: The flower is magenta.
words.ex_cn: 这朵花是洋红色的。
words.en: A color that is a purplish red, one of the primary colors in the printing process.

words.tr: adj. 夸大的；言过其实的
words.ex: He gave a magniloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behaviour as magniloquent, you mean that it is too elaborate and formal.

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.tr: adj. 宏伟的；壮丽的；威严的；
words.ex: The majestic mountain stood above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 那座宏伟的山峰耸立在云层之上。
words.en: If you describe something as majestic, you mean that it has a quality of greatness and impressiveness that often inspires admiration or awe.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

words.ex: He shouted a malediction at the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他对着小偷咒骂了一句。
words.en: A malediction is a curse or the act of uttering a curse.

words.ex: The police caught the malefactor who stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓到了偷钱的罪犯。
words.en: A malefactor is someone who has committed a crime or done something wrong.

words.ex: The maleficent storm destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场有害的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing harm or destruction, especially by supernatural means.

words.tr: n. 渎职；不法行为；不正当
words.ex: The mayor was fired for malfeasance.
words.ex_cn: 市长因渎职被解雇了。
words.en: Malfeasance is the act of committing an illegal or wrongful act, especially by a public official.

words.ex: The car had a malfunction in the engine.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的发动机出现了故障。
words.en: If a machine or device malfunctions, it fails to work properly.

words.ex: He acted out of malice, not mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于恶意，而不是错误。
words.en: Malice is behavior that is intended to harm people or their reputations, or cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.ex: She put the wet clothes into the mangle to remove the water.
words.ex_cn: 她把湿衣服放进衣物轧干机里去除水分。
words.en: To mangle something means to severely damage it, usually by twisting, tearing, or cutting it, so that it is no longer in its original condition.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.ex: He wrote a manifesto to explain his ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份宣言来解释他的观点。
words.en: A manifesto is a written statement of the beliefs, aims, and policies of an organization, especially a political party.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.ex: He lives in a big mansion near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一座大宅子里。
words.en: A mansion is a very large, impressive house, especially one that is the home of a wealthy or important person.

words.ex: Farmers spread manure on the fields to help crops grow.
words.ex_cn: 农民把肥料撒在田里以帮助庄稼生长。
words.en: Manure is organic matter used as fertilizer in agriculture.

words.ex: The maple leaves turn red in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 枫树的叶子在秋天变红。
words.en: A maple is a tree or shrub with lobed leaves, winged fruits, and colorful autumn foliage, which is often cultivated for its sap, wood, or ornamental value.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.tr:
v. 抢劫；掠夺
n. 袭击
words.ex: The soldiers marauded through the village, taking whatever they wanted.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在村庄里四处掠夺，拿走了他们想要的一切。
words.en: To maraud means to roam around in search of things to steal or people to attack.

words.ex: The marine birds fly over the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这些海鸟在海面上飞翔。
words.en: Marine is used to describe things relating to the sea or to the ships and boats which sail on it.

words.ex: The mariner sailed the ship across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 这位海员驾船横渡了海洋。
words.en: A mariner is a sailor.

words.tr: n. 骨髓；精华；活力；西葫芦
words.ex: The bone marrow makes blood cells.
words.ex_cn: 骨髓制造血细胞。
words.en: The soft fatty substance in the cavities of bones, in which blood cells are produced; the essence or most vital part of something.

words.tr:
n. 元帅；高级军官；典礼官；消防局长
v. 整理；集结
words.ex: The marshal led the army into battle.
words.ex_cn: 元帅率领军队上战场。
words.en: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, especially in the army or air force, or a person who arranges or directs a public event.

words.ex: Kangaroos are marsupials that carry babies in a pouch.
words.ex_cn: 袋鼠是有袋动物，它们把幼崽放在育儿袋里。
words.en: A marsupial is a type of mammal that carries its young in a pouch.

words.ex: He practices martial arts every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天练习武术。
words.en: Martial is used to describe things relating to soldiers or war.

words.tr:
n. 殉道者；殉教者；烈士
v. 处死；折磨
words.ex: He became a martyr for freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他为自由而成为烈士。
words.en: A martyr is someone who is killed or made to suffer greatly because of their religious or political beliefs, and is admired and respected by people who share those beliefs.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.ex: The brewery uses fresh mash to make beer.
words.ex_cn: 酿酒厂使用新鲜的麦芽浆来酿造啤酒。
words.en: To crush or smash something into a soft, pulpy mass.

words.tr:
n. 化妆舞会；伪装
v. 伪装；冒充
words.ex: We went to a masquerade last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚去参加了一个化妆舞会。
words.en: A masquerade is a party or dance where people wear masks and costumes, or it refers to the act of pretending to be someone or something else.

words.tr:
v. 屠杀 
n. 大屠杀
words.ex: The soldiers committed a massacre in the village.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在村庄里进行了大屠杀。
words.en: The indiscriminate killing of a large number of people.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大而重的；
words.ex: The company launched a massive advertising campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司发起了一场大规模的广告活动。
words.en: Something that is massive is extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

words.ex: The sailboat's mast is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 帆船的船桅很高。
words.en: A mast is a tall pole on a ship or boat that supports the sails.

words.ex: He carefully masticated his food before swallowing.
words.ex_cn: 他在吞咽前仔细咀嚼食物。
words.en: To chew food.

words.ex: He put a mat on the floor to keep it clean.
words.ex_cn: 他在地上放了一块垫子以保持清洁。
words.en: A mat is a piece of thick fabric or other material that is placed on a floor or other surface to protect it or to provide a soft surface to stand or sit on.

words.tr: v. 成为现实；成有形；实现；现身
words.ex: The dream did not materialize.
words.ex_cn: 这个梦想没有实现。
words.en: To materialize means to become actual fact; to happen or to appear in physical form.

words.tr: v. 准许入学；被录取入学
words.ex: He will matriculate next fall.
words.ex_cn: 他将在明年秋天入学。
words.en: To matriculate means to enroll at a college or university, or to be accepted as a student by a college or university.

words.tr:
adj. 无光粗糙的
n. 无光粗糙面；锍；冰铜
v. 变得无光粗糙
words.ex: The painting had a matte finish to reduce glare.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画采用了无光泽的表面处理，以减少反光。
words.en: A matte surface or color is dull and not shiny.

words.ex: He bought a new mattress for his bed.
words.ex_cn: 他为床买了一个新床垫。
words.en: A mattress is a large, flat pad that is placed on a bed to make it comfortable to sleep on.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.tr:
v. 严重伤害；粗暴对待；抨击
n. 大木槌
words.ex: The bear mauled the hiker, leaving deep wounds.
words.ex_cn: 熊袭击了徒步者，留下了深深的伤口。
words.en: To maul someone or something means to attack them and cause them serious injury, or to handle them roughly.

words.ex: She would sit for hours, maundering about her past.
words.ex_cn: 她会坐上几个小时，唠叨她的过去。
words.en: To talk or move aimlessly or idly.

words.tr: adj. 多愁善感的；令人作呕的；自作多情的
words.ex: The movie was too mawkish with its fake tears.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影用虚假的眼泪显得过于矫情。
words.en: If you describe something as mawkish, you mean that it is sentimental in a way that you find unpleasant or silly.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；错综复杂的曲径；
words.ex: The children got lost in the maze.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A maze is a complex system of paths or passages in which it is easy to get lost.

words.tr:
v. 意思；导致；打算；
n. 平均数；
adj. 低劣；平均；
words.ex: What does this word mean?
words.ex_cn: 这个词是什么意思？
words.en: If you want to know what a word, a sentence, or an expression means, you want to know what it refers to or what its significance is.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢而弯曲地流动；漫步；闲聊
n. 河流的曲折；漫步；迂回曲折的进程
words.ex: The river meanders through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河蜿蜒穿过森林。
words.en: To meander means to follow a winding and turning course, often used to describe the way a river flows or the way a person walks without a clear direction.

words.tr: adj. 很小（少）的；微不足道的；
words.ex: He gave me a measly $5 for my help.
words.ex_cn: 他只给了我五美元作为帮忙的报酬。
words.en: If you describe an amount, quantity, or size as measly, you are critical of it because it is very small or inadequate.

words.tr: v. 测量；“measure”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 慎重的；谨慎小心的；
words.ex: He measured the length of the table.
words.ex_cn: 他测量了桌子的长度。
words.en: If you describe someone's way of speaking as measured, you mean that it is slow and deliberate, often because they are trying to hide their feelings.

words.ex: The body has a mechanism to fight viruses.
words.ex_cn: 人体有一种对抗病毒的机制。
words.en: A mechanism is a part of a machine that does a particular task, or a system that is intended to achieve something or deal with a problem.

words.ex: He won a gold medal in the Olympics.
words.ex_cn: 他在奥运会上赢得了一枚金牌。
words.en: A medal is a small metal disc which is given as an award for bravery or as a prize in a sporting event.

words.ex: Don't meddle in my affairs.
words.ex_cn: 别插手我的事情。
words.en: To meddle means to interfere in something that is not one's concern.

words.ex: The doctor medicated the patient for the infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生用药物治疗了患者的感染。
words.en: To medicate means to treat someone with medicine or to add medicine to something.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: He does meditation every morning to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以放松。
words.en: Meditation is the act of remaining in a silent and calm state for a period of time, as part of a religious training, or so that you are more able to deal with the problems of everyday life.

words.ex: The meek boy quietly listened to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个温顺的男孩静静地听老师讲课。
words.en: If you describe a person as meek, you think that they are gentle and quiet, and likely to do what other people say.

words.tr:
v. （使）合并；（使）融合；（使）混合
n. 合并；混合
words.ex: He melds the two ideas into one.
words.ex_cn: 他把这两个想法融合成一个。
words.en: To combine or blend to form a single entity.

words.tr: adj. 声音甜美的；悦耳动听的
words.ex: Her mellifluous voice made everyone calm.
words.ex_cn: 她悦耳的声音让每个人都平静下来。
words.en: A mellifluous sound or voice is smooth and pleasant to listen to.

words.ex: He ate a sweet melon for dessert.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块甜瓜当甜点。
words.en: A melon is a large, juicy fruit with a hard rind, belonging to the gourd family, typically eaten fresh.

words.ex: The cell has a thin membrane.
words.ex_cn: 细胞有一层薄薄的膜。
words.en: A membrane is a thin layer of tissue or material that covers or lines a part of the body, or separates one area from another.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.ex: He will mend his broken shoe.
words.ex_cn: 他将修补他破掉的鞋子。
words.en: If you mend something that is broken or damaged, you repair it, so that it works properly or so that it looks like new again.

words.tr: adj. 撒谎的；不真实的；捏造的
words.ex: She was known for her mendacious stories.
words.ex_cn: 她以编造虚假故事而闻名。
words.en: If someone is mendacious, they are not telling the truth.

words.ex: Her constant mendacity made it difficult to trust her.
words.ex_cn: 她不断的谎言让人难以信任她。
words.en: The quality of being untruthful; lying.

words.tr:
adj. 行乞的
n. 乞丐
words.ex: The mendicant monks wandered the streets, seeking alms.
words.ex_cn: 托钵僧在街上徘徊，寻求施舍。
words.en: A mendicant is someone who lives by asking people for money or food, especially as a member of a religious group that does this as a way of life.

words.ex: Menthol is often used in cough drops to provide a cooling sensation.
words.ex_cn: 薄荷醇常用于止咳糖中，以提供清凉的感觉。
words.en: Menthol is a crystalline alcohol with a cooling mint flavor and odor, obtained from peppermint oil or other mint oils or made synthetically, used in cigarettes, cough drops, and ointments.

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.ex: The merit of this plan is its simplicity.
words.ex_cn: 这个计划的优点是简单。
words.en: If something has merit, it has good or worthwhile qualities.

words.tr:
adj. 该得的；应得的
v. 值得；应得；“merit”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His hard work merited the recognition he received.
words.ex_cn: 他的辛勤工作值得他得到的认可。
words.en: Deserved or earned, especially through hard work or good behavior.

words.ex: He used mesmerism to calm the anxious patient.
words.ex_cn: 他用催眠术使焦虑的病人平静下来。
words.en: Mesmerism refers to the practice of inducing a state of hypnosis or a trance-like state in a person, often for therapeutic purposes or entertainment. It is also used to describe a compelling charm or fascination that holds one's attention.

words.tr:
v. 分配；给予
n. 边界
words.ex: He mete out justice fairly.
words.ex_cn: 他公平地施以正义。
words.en: To distribute or allot something, especially justice or punishment.

words.tr: adj. 有节奏的；有韵律的
words.ex: The poem follows a strict metrical pattern.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗遵循严格的韵律模式。
words.en: Relating to or composed in poetic meter.

words.ex: He showed his mettle in the tough race.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰苦的比赛中展现了实力。
words.en: Mettle is the ability and determination to do something successfully in spite of difficult conditions.

words.ex: The microbe causes sickness.
words.ex_cn: 这种微生物会引起疾病。
words.en: A microbe is a very small living thing, which you can only see if you use a microscope. Some microbes can cause diseases.

words.tr:
pron. 我的（东西）；
n. 矿；
v. 采矿；
words.ex: This book is mine.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是我的。
words.en: Used to refer to a thing or things belonging to or associated with the speaker. A place where minerals are extracted from the earth. To extract minerals from the earth.

words.tr:
v. （使）生气
n. 发脾气；微怒
words.ex: She got a miff when I forgot her birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记了她的生日，她有点恼火。
words.en: To cause to be annoyed or offended.

words.tr:
adj. 巨大的；强大的；
adv. 非常；
words.ex: The mighty river flows through the valley.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的河流流经山谷。
words.en: Possessing great power, strength, or force; formidable.

words.ex: The militia protected the village during the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 民兵在冲突期间保护了村庄。
words.en: A militia is a group of people who are not professional soldiers but who have military training and can act as an army.

words.ex: He drinks a glass of milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝一杯牛奶。
words.en: Milk is a white liquid produced by cows, goats, and some other animals, which people drink and use in cooking.

words.tr:
v. 切碎；剁碎；装腔作势地小步走
n. 绞碎的肉
words.ex: He minces garlic for the sauce.
words.ex_cn: 他把大蒜剁碎用来做酱。
words.en: To mince means to cut food, especially meat, into very small pieces, or to walk or speak in an affected manner.

words.tr: v. 使相混；使联结；交际
words.ex: He mingled the two colors to make a new one.
words.ex_cn: 他把两种颜色混合在一起，创造出一种新颜色。
words.en: If things such as sounds, smells, or feelings mingle, they mix or combine with each other, or if people mingle, they talk to each other at a social event.

words.ex: The minnows darted around in the shallow water.
words.ex_cn: 鲦鱼在浅水中快速游动。
words.en: A minnow is a small freshwater fish, often used as bait in fishing.

words.ex: She added a mint leaf to her drink.
words.ex_cn: 她在饮料里加了一片薄荷叶。
words.en: Mint is a plant with fresh-tasting leaves. It is also the place where coins are made, or the act of making coins.

words.ex: The ballroom was filled with couples dancing the minuet.
words.ex_cn: 舞厅里充满了跳小步舞的情侣。
words.en: A minuet is a slow, stately ballroom dance for two in triple time, popular especially in the 18th century.

words.ex: I walked to the station in minutes.
words.ex_cn: 我十分钟内走到了车站。
words.en: Minutes are the official written record of what was said and decided at a meeting.

words.ex: He was obsessed with the minutiae of daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他对日常生活的琐事着迷。
words.en: The small, precise, or trivial details of something.

words.ex: He saw a mirage in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 他在沙漠中看到了海市蜃楼。
words.en: An optical illusion caused by atmospheric conditions, especially the appearance of a sheet of water in a desert or on a hot road caused by the refraction of light from the sky by heated air.

words.ex: The children laughed with mirth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们带着欢乐大笑。
words.en: Mirth is amusement which you express by laughing.

words.ex: The book is a delightful miscellany of poems, essays, and short stories.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是一部令人愉快的诗歌、散文和短篇小说的杂集。
words.en: A miscellany is a collection of various items, especially literary compositions, that are not related to each other.

words.ex: The miscreant was caught red-handed.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍被当场抓住。
words.en: A miscreant is someone who behaves badly or does not obey the law.

words.tr: adj. 吝啬的；小气的；少量的
words.ex: He was miserly with his money and never spent a penny on others.
words.ex_cn: 他对钱很吝啬，从不为别人花一分钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is miserly, you disapprove of them because they seem to hate spending money, and to spend as little as possible.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.ex: He misperceives her silence as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误以为她的沉默是生气。
words.en: To perceive incorrectly or misunderstand.

words.tr: n. 误述；歪曲；表达不当
words.ex: The politician was accused of misrepresentation of the facts.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客被指控歪曲事实。
words.en: A misrepresentation is a false statement of fact made by one party to another, which has the effect of inducing that party into a contract.

words.tr: adj. 畸形的；奇形怪状的；扭曲变形的；
words.ex: The misshapen toy looked strange to the children.
words.ex_cn: 那个畸形的玩具让孩子们觉得奇怪。
words.en: If something is misshapen, it has a shape that is not the normal or natural one, often because it has been damaged or has not developed correctly.

words.ex: He received a missive from the headquarters.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了来自总部的公函。
words.en: A missive is a letter or other written message.

words.tr: n. 密史脱拉风；干冷北风
words.ex: The mistral wind can be quite harsh, especially in the winter months.
words.ex_cn: 密史脱拉风在冬季尤其凛冽。
words.en: A strong, cold, north-westerly wind that blows through the Rhône valley to the Mediterranean coast of France.

words.ex: He uses mnemonics to remember the dates.
words.ex_cn: 他使用助记法来记住这些日期。
words.en: Mnemonics is a method or system for improving the memory by using formulas or techniques.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；呼啸；抱怨
n. 呻吟声；萧萧声；抱怨
words.ex: He moans when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候会呻吟。
words.en: If you moan, you make a low sound, usually because you are unhappy or in pain.

words.ex: The old castle has a deep moat around it.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的城堡周围有一条深深的护城河。
words.en: A moat is a deep, wide ditch that is dug around a place such as a castle and is usually filled with water, in order to protect the place from attack.

words.ex: The mobile table can be moved easily.
words.ex_cn: 这个可移动的桌子很容易搬动。
words.en: A mobile is something that can move or be moved easily.

words.ex: The new policy improves worker mobility.
words.ex_cn: 新政策提高了工人的流动性。
words.en: The ability to move or be moved freely and easily.

words.tr:
v. 嘲笑；嘲弄；
adj. 仿制的；
words.ex: They mock him for his accent.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他口音而嘲笑他。
words.en: To mock someone means to laugh at them, tease them, or make them look foolish, often by imitating their behavior or speech.

words.ex: The mode of transportation is a bike.
words.ex_cn: 出行的方式是骑自行车。
words.en: A mode is a particular way or style in which something is done or experienced.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.ex: She wears modish clothes every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天穿时髦的衣服。
words.en: If something is modish, it is fashionable and modern.

words.ex: The bread became moldy in the warm kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包在温暖的厨房里发霉了。
words.en: Something that is moldy is covered with mold.

words.ex: He was arrested for molesting a child.
words.ex_cn: 他因骚扰儿童而被逮捕。
words.en: To molest someone means to assault or harass them, especially sexually.

words.ex: He tried to mollify his angry friend with an apology.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用道歉来安抚他生气的朋友。
words.en: To mollify someone means to make them feel calmer and less angry, upset, or worried.

words.tr:
v. 娇惯；纵容
n. 娇惯的男人；女性化的男人
words.ex: Don't mollycoddle the child; let him learn from mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 不要过分溺爱这个孩子；让他从错误中学习。
words.en: To mollycoddle someone is to treat them in an overprotective or indulgent way.

words.ex: He waited for a moment before speaking.
words.ex_cn: 他等了一会儿才开口。
words.en: A moment is a very short period of time.

words.ex: The team gained momentum after scoring the first goal.
words.ex_cn: 球队在进第一个球后获得了势头。
words.en: Momentum is the ability of something to keep increasing, developing, or being more successful.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.ex: He wears a monocle to read books.
words.ex_cn: 他戴单片眼镜看书。
words.en: A monocle is a type of corrective lens used to correct or enhance the vision in only one eye.

words.ex: He wrote a monograph on ancient Chinese pottery.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一本关于中国古代陶器的专著。
words.en: A monograph is a detailed written study or report on a specific subject or aspect of a subject, especially by a single author.

words.tr: adj.  独块巨石的；整体的；庞大的；单一的；统一的
words.ex: The ancient temple was built from a monolithic stone.
words.ex_cn: 这座古代神庙是由一块巨石建成的。
words.en: A monolithic structure is extremely large and made of one piece or one type of material.

words.tr: n. 独白；独角戏；长篇大论
words.ex: He gave a monologue on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他在舞台上发表了一段独白。
words.en: A monologue is a long speech by one person, especially in a play or film, or a long speech by one person during a conversation.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.ex: The monsoon brings heavy rain to India each summer.
words.ex_cn: 季风每年夏天给印度带来大雨。
words.en: A monsoon is a seasonal wind in South and Southeast Asia, blowing from the southwest between May and September and bringing rain (the wet monsoon), or from the northeast between October and April (the dry monsoon).

words.ex: The monster made a monstrous sound.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物发出了巨大的声音。
words.en: If you describe something as monstrous, you mean that it is extremely large or that it is extremely unpleasant or wrong.

words.tr: adj. 喜怒无常的；情绪多变的；
words.ex: He is moody and changes his mind often.
words.ex_cn: 他喜怒无常，经常改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as moody, you mean that their feelings and behavior change frequently, and in particular that they often become depressed or angry without any warning.

words.tr:
v. 抑郁不乐；闲逛；无精打采
n. 闷闷不乐的人
words.ex: He mopes all day after losing the game.
words.ex_cn: 他输掉比赛后整天闷闷不乐。
words.en: If you mope, you spend time feeling sorry for yourself, often because you are unhappy or disappointed.

words.ex: The team's morale improved after they won the game.
words.ex_cn: 球队赢了比赛后，士气提升了。
words.en: Morale is the amount of confidence and cheerfulness that a group of people have.

words.tr: n. 荒野；[地理]沼泽；系泊（moor 的复数）; v. 使停泊；被系住（moor 的三单形式）
words.ex: The sheep walk on the moors near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊群在村庄附近的荒原上行走。
words.en: Moors are areas of open, uncultivated land, often covered with heather, that are found in parts of Britain and other countries.

words.tr: adj. 濒临死亡的；垂死的；
words.ex: The moribund patient stopped breathing.
words.ex_cn: 这位濒临死亡的病人停止了呼吸。
words.en: If you describe something as moribund, you mean that it is in a very bad condition and is not active or successful.

words.ex: She took a tiny morsel of cake and savored it slowly.
words.ex_cn: 她咬了一小口蛋糕，慢慢地品味着。
words.en: A morsel is a small piece or amount of something, especially food.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.tr: n. 屈辱感；窘迫感；坏疽
words.ex: The mortification of his public failure was almost unbearable.
words.ex_cn: 他因公开失败而感到的屈辱几乎难以忍受。
words.en: A feeling of shame, humiliation, or wounded pride.

words.ex: A mote of dust floated in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 一粒微尘在阳光中飘浮。
words.en: A very small piece of a substance, especially dust.

words.tr: adj. 能动的；有自动力的
words.ex: The sperm cells are highly motile and can swim towards the egg.
words.ex_cn: 精子细胞非常活跃，能够游向卵子。
words.en: A motile organism is capable of moving independently, using metabolic energy.

words.ex: The bacteria show high motility in warm water.
words.ex_cn: 这种细菌在温水中具有很高的运动能力。
words.en: The ability of an organism or fluid to move or be moved.

words.ex: Her motto is 'Never give up.'
words.ex_cn: 她的座右铭是‘永不放弃’。
words.en: A motto is a short sentence or phrase that expresses a rule for sensible behavior, especially a way of behaving in a particular situation.

words.ex: She mourns her dog every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天都在哀悼她的狗。
words.en: To feel or express deep sorrow or regret for someone or something.

words.ex: The pig rolled in the muck.
words.ex_cn: 猪在污物里打滚。
words.en: Muck is dirt or some other unpleasant substance. It can also refer to manure used for fertilizing the land. As a verb, to muck means to spread manure on the land or to make something dirty.

words.tr: adj. 泥泞的；模糊不清的；
words.ex: The road became muddy after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后，这条路变得泥泞。
words.en: If something is muddy, it is covered in mud or full of mud. If you muddy something, you make it muddy or you make it less clear or more complicated.

words.tr: v. 使声音降低；压抑（声音）；蒙住；裹
words.ex: He muffled his laugh with a pillow.
words.ex_cn: 他用枕头捂住笑声。
words.en: To muffle a sound is to make it quieter or less clear, often by covering it or wrapping it in something.

words.ex: It is muggy outside today.
words.ex_cn: 今天外面闷热。
words.en: If you describe the weather as muggy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and damp.

words.ex: He is mulish and refuses to change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，拒绝改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as mulish, you mean they are determined to do what they want to do and will not change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.tr:
v. 烫热；思虑
n. 细软薄布；混乱
words.ex: He mulls the wine before serving it.
words.ex_cn: 他在上菜前把葡萄酒烫热。
words.en: To mull means to think about something deeply and at length.

words.tr: adj. 多种的；各式各样的
words.ex: She has multifarious hobbies, like painting, singing, and gardening.
words.ex_cn: 她有很多不同的爱好，比如绘画、唱歌和园艺。
words.en: If you describe things as multifarious, you mean that they are many and of various types.

words.tr: n. 大数目；多种多样；繁多
words.ex: There is a multiplicity of stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有大量星星。
words.en: A multiplicity of things or people means a large number or great variety of them.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝；含糊地说
n. 含糊的话；咕哝
words.ex: He mumbles when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会嘟囔。
words.en: If you mumble, you speak very quietly and not at all clearly with the result that the words are difficult to understand.

words.ex: She sat munching on a bag of crisps.
words.ex_cn: 她坐着用力咀嚼着一袋薯片。
words.en: If you munch food, you eat it by chewing it slowly and steadily.

words.ex: The municipality cleaned the streets last week.
words.ex_cn: 这个自治市上周清理了街道。
words.en: A municipality is a city or town that has its own government to manage local affairs.

words.tr: n. 土地所有权证明文件；档案
words.ex: The lawyer carefully reviewed the muniments to ensure their authenticity.
words.ex_cn: 律师仔细审查了这些契据以确保其真实性。
words.en: Documents or records that serve as evidence of rights or privileges, especially those relating to property.

words.tr:
n. 军火；军需品
v. 供给军需品
words.ex: The soldiers stored munition in the bunker.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们把军火储存在掩体里。
words.en: Munition refers to military weapons, ammunition, equipment, and stores.

words.tr:
n. 低语声；嘟哝
v. 低语；咕哝；私下抱怨
words.ex: I heard a murmur from the next room.
words.ex_cn: 我听到隔壁房间传来低语声。
words.en: A murmur is a low, indistinct, continuous sound, as of a stream or of voices.

words.tr:
v. 沉思
n. （作家、画家等的）灵感；缪斯
words.ex: He often muses about the meaning of life.
words.ex_cn: 他常常沉思生命的意义。
words.en: In Greek mythology, the Muses are the goddesses of the inspiration of literature, science and the arts. As a verb, to muse means to think about something carefully and for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 软而稠的；糊状的；多愁善感的
words.ex: She made a mushy dessert with bananas and cream.
words.ex_cn: 她做了一道香蕉和奶油的糊状甜点。
words.en: If you describe something as mushy, you mean that it is very soft.

words.ex: The soldier fired a musket in the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵在战斗中开了一支火绳枪。
words.en: A musket is an old-fashioned type of gun which was used before rifles were invented.

words.tr:
v. 鼓起；集合；召集
n. 集合；集合的人群
words.ex: He must muster courage to speak in public.
words.ex_cn: 他必须鼓起勇气在公众面前发言。
words.en: To muster means to gather or assemble (troops, etc.), especially for inspection or in preparation for battle. It can also mean to summon up (a feeling, attitude, or response).

words.ex: The virus can mutate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以迅速变异。
words.en: If an animal or plant mutates, or something mutates it, it develops different characteristics as the result of a change in its genes.

words.tr:
adj. 哑的；无声的
n. 哑巴；沉默的人
v. 减弱…的声音
words.ex: He stayed mute during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议期间保持沉默。
words.en: If someone is mute, they are unable to speak.

words.tr: adj. 减弱的；变得轻柔的
words.ex: The muted sound came from the old TV.
words.ex_cn: 微弱的声音来自那台旧电视。
words.en: If something is muted, it is less intense or less noticeable than usual.

words.ex: The mutineer was court-martialed for his actions.
words.ex_cn: 这名叛变者因自己的行为而受到军事法庭的审判。
words.en: A mutineer is someone who takes part in a mutiny, which is a rebellion against authority, especially by soldiers or sailors against their officers.

words.ex: The mutinous crew refused to follow the captain's orders.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱的船员拒绝服从船长的命令。
words.en: If someone is mutinous, they are strongly dissatisfied with a person in authority and are likely to stop obeying them.

words.tr:
v. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
n. 咕哝地抱怨；嘀咕
words.ex: He mutters under his breath when he is angry.
words.ex_cn: 当他生气时，他会低声嘟囔。
words.en: To speak or say something in a low voice that is hard to hear, often because you are annoyed or complaining.

words.tr: adj. 模糊不清的；迷糊的；头脑发昏的
words.ex: The instructions were muzzy and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明模糊不清，难以理解。
words.en: If someone is muzzy, they are confused and unable to think clearly, often because they are tired or have drunk too much alcohol.

words.ex: He has myopia and needs glasses to see far objects.
words.ex_cn: 他有近视，需要戴眼镜才能看清远处的物体。
words.en: Myopia is a condition of the eye where light focuses in front of, instead of on, the retina. This results in distant objects appearing blurry while close objects can be seen clearly.

words.tr: adj. 近视眼的；缺乏远见的
words.ex: He is myopic and needs glasses to see far.
words.ex_cn: 他近视，需要戴眼镜才能看远。
words.en: If you describe someone as myopic, you are critical of them because they seem unable to realize that their actions might have negative consequences.

words.ex: The stock price hit its nadir last month.
words.ex_cn: 股票价格上个月跌至最低点。
words.en: The nadir of something is the worst or lowest point that it reaches.

words.tr:
v. 唠叨；喋喋不休；不断困扰
n. 老马；驽马；矮小马
words.ex: She nagged him to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 她不停地催他打扫房间。
words.en: If someone nags you, they keep asking you to do something you have not done yet or do not want to do.

words.ex: The child gave a naive smile when he believed the story.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子相信这个故事时，他露出了天真的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as naïve, you think they lack experience and so expect things to be easy or people to be honest or kind.

words.tr:
adj. 多愁善感的；柔弱的；无生气的
n. 柔弱伤感的人
words.ex: His namby-pamby approach to the problem didn't impress anyone.
words.ex_cn: 他对问题的软弱态度没有给任何人留下深刻印象。
words.en: If you describe something as namby-pamby, you mean that it is sentimental or weak.

words.ex: He shows narcissism by always talking about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他总是谈论自己，表现出自恋。
words.en: Narcissism is the habit of always thinking about yourself and your appearance and abilities, and believing that you are better than other people.

words.tr: n. 自我陶醉者；自恋者
words.ex: He is a narcissist who only talks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他是个只谈论自己的自恋者。
words.en: A narcissist is someone who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves.

words.ex: He has a nasal voice when he has a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他感冒时声音有鼻音。
words.en: Nasal is used to describe something relating to the nose or the production of sound through the nose.

words.ex: The nascent industry is growing quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个新生的产业正在迅速发展。
words.en: Nascent things or processes are just beginning, and are expected to become stronger or to grow bigger.

words.ex: He visited his natal village for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 他第一次回到了自己的出生村庄。
words.en: Relating to the place or time of one's birth

words.ex: The smell of the food made her feel nausea.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A feeling of sickness with an inclination to vomit.

words.ex: The smell of rotten food nauseates me.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味让我想吐。
words.en: If something nauseates you, it makes you feel as if you are going to vomit.

words.ex: He works on a nautical chart.
words.ex_cn: 他正在使用一张航海图。
words.en: Nautical means relating to ships, sailing, or navigation at sea.

words.tr:
v. 否认；拒绝
n. 否认；拒绝
words.ex: He always naysay when others suggest new ideas.
words.ex_cn: 当别人提出新想法时，他总是反对。
words.en: To say no to something; to deny, refuse, or oppose something.

words.tr: n. 反对者；否定者；爱唱反调的人
words.ex: Despite the naysayers, she managed to achieve her goals.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有那些摇头族，她还是设法实现了自己的目标。
words.en: A naysayer is someone who always says something will not work or is not possible.

words.tr: adj. 贫困的；贫乏的；紧急的
words.ex: The necessitous family received assistance from the local charity.
words.ex_cn: 这个贫困的家庭从当地慈善机构获得了帮助。
words.en: Being in need; impoverished or destitute.

words.ex: She picked up a needle to sew the button.
words.ex_cn: 她拿起一根针来缝纽扣。
words.en: A needle is a thin, pointed piece of metal that is used in sewing. It has a hole at one end for thread to pass through.

words.ex: The nefarious thief stole money from the poor.
words.ex_cn: 那个极坏的贼从穷人那里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe an activity as nefarious, you mean that it is wicked and immoral.

words.tr: n. 否定；反面；对立面；拒绝
words.ex: He gave a negation of the statement.
words.ex_cn: 他否定了那个陈述。
words.en: A negation is a statement that denies or contradicts another statement.

words.ex: His negligence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: Negligence is failure to take proper care over something that you are responsible for, which might cause damage or loss.

words.ex: His dishonesty became his nemesis.
words.ex_cn: 他的不诚实成了他的天谴。
words.en: Someone's nemesis is a person or thing that is very difficult for them to defeat.

words.ex: The internet created many new neologisms like 'selfie' and 'blog'.
words.ex_cn: 互联网创造了许多新词，比如'selfie'和'blog'。
words.en: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression that may be in the process of entering common use, but has not yet been accepted into mainstream language.

words.ex: The neonate cried loudly after birth.
words.ex_cn: 新生儿出生后大声哭喊。
words.en: A neonate is a newborn child, especially one less than four weeks old.

words.tr: n. 新信徒；新手；初学者
words.ex: The neophyte learned the prayers from the elder.
words.ex_cn: 新信徒向长者学习祷告。
words.en: A neophyte is someone who is new to a particular activity, subject, or religion and is therefore inexperienced.

words.ex: The nerve in his finger was damaged.
words.ex_cn: 他手指里的神经受到了损伤。
words.en: A nerve is a bundle of fibers that transmits impulses of sensation to the brain or spinal cord, and impulses from these to the muscles and organs. It also refers to the courage or control needed to do something difficult or dangerous.

words.ex: The nethermost part of the cave was filled with water.
words.ex_cn: 洞穴的最下面部分充满了水。
words.en: The nethermost part of something is the lowest or deepest part of it.

words.tr:
n. 荨麻
v. 激怒
words.ex: The child touched the nettle and got a rash.
words.ex_cn: 孩子碰了荨麻，皮肤起了疹子。
words.en: A nettle is a wild plant with leaves that sting when you touch them. If you are nettled by something, it makes you annoyed or angry.

words.ex: He works in neurology at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院从事神经学工作。
words.en: The branch of medicine or biology that deals with the anatomy, functions, and organic disorders of nerves and the nervous system.

words.tr: n. 神经症；神经衰弱症
words.ex: He has a neurosis about being late.
words.ex_cn: 他对迟到有一种神经症般的焦虑。
words.en: A neurosis is a mental illness that causes feelings of fear and worry, often leading to unreasonable behavior.

words.tr: v. 使中立；中和；使无效
words.ex: The government tried to neutralize the conflict by talking to both sides.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图通过与双方交谈来使冲突中立化。
words.en: To neutralize something means to stop it from having any effect or to make it ineffective.

words.ex: This nifty app helps me learn English every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个极好的应用程序每天帮助我学习英语。
words.en: Something that is nifty is particularly good, clever, or effective.

words.ex: He made a niggle about the coffee being too hot.
words.ex_cn: 他抱怨咖啡太烫了。
words.en: To niggle means to worry about or pay too much attention to small or unimportant details, or to cause someone to do this.

words.tr:
adj. 琐碎的；费神的；烦扰的
v. 为琐事费心；吹毛求疵；找茬儿；“niggle”的现在分词
words.ex: He has a niggling pain in his back.
words.ex_cn: 他背部有一种持续的小疼痛。
words.en: A niggling problem or worry is small but bothers you over a period of time.

words.ex: The score was nil at the end of the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束时分数为零。
words.en: Nothing or none; used to indicate the absence of something.

words.tr: adj. 灵活的；敏捷的；机敏的
words.ex: The cat is nimble and jumps over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫很敏捷，跳过了篱笆。
words.en: Someone who is nimble is able to move their fingers, hands, or legs quickly and easily.

words.ex: The dog gave a small nip to his leg.
words.ex_cn: 狗轻轻咬了他的腿一口。
words.en: To nip means to pinch, squeeze, or bite something quickly and sharply. It can also refer to taking a small amount of a drink.

words.tr: n. 游牧民；流浪者；游牧生活；流浪生活
words.ex: The nomad walks with his sheep across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 游牧民带着他的羊群穿越沙漠。
words.en: A nomad is someone who has no permanent home and moves according to the seasons from place to place in search of food, water, and grazing land.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: They will nominate her for the award.
words.ex_cn: 他们将提名她获得这个奖项。
words.en: If someone is nominated for a job or position, their name is formally suggested as a candidate for it.

words.tr:
v. 使迷惑；使不知所措
n. 迷惑；困惑；为难
words.ex: The tricky question nonplused the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个棘手的问题让老师不知所措。
words.en: To cause to be at a loss as to what to say, think, or do; perplex.

words.tr:
n. 绳套；套索；绞索；绞刑
v. 用套索捕捉；处绞刑；诱入圈套
words.ex: The hunter threw the noose over the deer's head.
words.ex_cn: 猎人把套索套在了鹿的头上。
words.en: A noose is a loop at the end of a rope that tightens when the rope is pulled, used especially for trapping animals or for hanging.

words.ex: He drank the old man's nostrum for his cough.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了老人的秘方来治咳嗽。
words.en: A nostrum is a medicine, especially one that is not considered effective, that is prepared by someone who is not a doctor.

words.ex: The smoke from the factory is noxious.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟雾是有害的。
words.en: Something that is noxious is harmful or poisonous.

words.tr:
v. （使）成核
adj. 有核的
words.ex: Bubbles begin to nucleate when the water boils.
words.ex_cn: 当水沸腾时，气泡开始形成。
words.en: To form or cause to form a nucleus.

words.tr: adj. 无价值的；无效的；无关紧要的
words.ex: The contract was declared nugatory due to a lack of signatures.
words.ex_cn: 由于缺少签名，该合同被宣布为无效。
words.en: If you describe something as nugatory, you mean that it is worthless or has no value.

words.tr: v. 使无效；抵消；废除；取消
words.ex: The judge will nullify the contract.
words.ex_cn: 法官将宣布该合同无效。
words.en: To nullify something means to make it have no effect or value.

words.ex: The old temple felt numinous at night.
words.ex_cn: 那座古庙在晚上显得神圣神秘。
words.en: Something that is numinous is spiritual or supernatural in a way that inspires awe or reverence.

words.tr: n. 钱币奖章收藏家；钱币学家
words.ex: He is a numismatist who collects old coins.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位收藏古币的钱币学家。
words.en: A numismatist is a person who studies or collects coins, tokens, and paper money.

words.ex: The travelers found an oasis with water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 旅行者们发现了一个有水和树木的绿洲。
words.en: An oasis is a small area in a desert where water and plants are found, making it a place of relief and beauty in an otherwise barren landscape.

words.ex: He took an oath to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他发誓要说出真相。
words.en: An oath is a formal promise, especially one made in a court of law or a religious ceremony, or a swear word.

words.ex: The obedient child cleaned his room without being told.
words.ex_cn: 这个听话的孩子没被要求就打扫了房间。
words.en: An obedient person or animal does what they are told to do.

words.ex: He showed obeisance to the king by bowing deeply.
words.ex_cn: 他通过深深鞠躬向国王表示敬意。
words.en: Obeisance is a gesture or movement of the body expressing respect or submission.

words.ex: He raised an objection to the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了反对。
words.en: An objection is an expression or feeling of disapproval or opposition; a reason for disagreeing.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.tr: adj. 间接的；不直截了当的；
words.ex: He gave an oblique answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个间接的回答。
words.en: If you describe a statement as oblique, you mean that is not expressed directly or openly, often because it is difficult or embarrassing.

words.ex: He faced obloquy for speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因说出真相而遭受非议。
words.en: Obloquy is strong public criticism or verbal abuse.

words.ex: The loud music was obnoxious and made everyone leave.
words.ex_cn: 那刺耳的音乐非常讨厌，让所有人都离开了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as obnoxious, you think that they are very unpleasant because of being aggressive, loud, or offensive.

words.ex: He showed observance of the school rules.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守了校规。
words.en: The practice of following a custom, rule, or law.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.tr: n. 痴迷；困扰；着魔；强迫观念；
words.ex: His obsession with video games made him ignore his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的痴迷让他忽略了学业。
words.en: An obsession is an idea or thought that continually preoccupies or intrudes on a person's mind.

words.ex: He has an obsessive need to clean everything.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种强迫性的需求，要把一切都打扫干净。
words.en: If someone's behaviour is obsessive, they cannot stop doing a particular thing or behaving in a particular way.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；固执的；顽固的；
words.ex: He is obstinate and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很执拗，不肯改变主意。
words.en: If you describe someone as obstinate, you are being critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to change their mind or be persuaded to do something else.

words.ex: The obstreperous crowd made it difficult to hear the speaker.
words.ex_cn: 吵闹的人群使得演讲者的话难以听清。
words.en: If you say that someone is obstreperous, you are annoyed because they are noisy and difficult to control.

words.ex: The fallen tree was an obstruction on the road.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstruction is something that blocks a road, passage, or entrance, or the act of blocking something.

words.tr: v. 强使接受；打扰；闯入
words.ex: He tried to obtrude his opinions on the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图强使组里接受他的观点。
words.en: To force something on someone in a way that is unwelcome or intrusive.

words.tr: adj. 钝的；愚钝的；钝角的
words.ex: The angle is obtuse, so it is larger than 90 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 这个角是钝的，所以它大于90度。
words.en: If you describe someone as obtuse, you mean that they are slow to understand things.

words.ex: The obverse of the coin features the head of the queen.
words.ex_cn: 硬币的正面印有女王的头像。
words.en: The obverse of something is the main or most obvious part of it, or the side of it that is most often seen or used.

words.ex: The leaf occluded the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 叶子堵住了管道。
words.en: To occlude means to block or stop up a passage, opening, or vessel.

words.tr:
adj. 超自然的；神秘的；隐藏的
v. 掩蔽
n. 神秘的事物；神秘学
words.ex: He is interested in the occult.
words.ex_cn: 他对神秘学感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to mystical, supernatural, or magical powers, practices, or phenomena.

words.tr:
adj. 眼睛的；视觉的
n. 目镜
words.ex: He wore ocular glasses to see better.
words.ex_cn: 他戴着眼镜以便看得更清楚。
words.en: Relating to the eye or vision.

words.ex: He wrote an ode to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的母亲写了一首颂歌。
words.en: A lyric poem, typically one in the form of an address to a particular subject, written in varied or irregular meter.

words.ex: He adds sodium to his food for taste.
words.ex_cn: 他为了味道在食物里加钠。
words.en: Sodium is a soft, silvery-white, highly reactive metal. Sodium is an alkali metal, being in group 1 of the periodic table, because it has a single electron in its outer shell that it readily donates, creating a positively charged ion—the Na⁺ cation.

words.ex: The car's odometer shows 50,000 miles.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的里程表显示50,000英里。
words.en: An odometer is an instrument in a vehicle that measures and displays the total distance that the vehicle has traveled.

words.tr: adj. 散发气味的；香的；臭的
words.ex: The odoriferous flowers filled the room with their sweet scent.
words.ex_cn: 芬芳的花朵用它们的甜香充满了房间。
words.en: Having or giving off a smell, especially a pleasant one.

words.tr: adj. 不寻常的；非传统的；不落俗套的
words.ex: He likes offbeat movies that no one else understands.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢那些别人都不理解的古怪电影。
