words.en: If you describe something or someone as offbeat, you mean that they are different from what is usual or expected in an unusual and appealing way.

words.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他偷窃触犯了法律。
words.en: If you offend someone, you upset or embarrass them by saying or doing something that they think is rude or insulting.

words.tr: adj. 冒犯的；令人不快的；进攻性的；
words.ex: His offensive words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他冒犯的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's language or behavior as offensive, you mean that it is rude or insulting.

words.ex: He was offish when I said hello.
words.ex_cn: 我跟他打招呼时，他很冷淡。
words.en: If you describe someone as offish, you mean that they are not very friendly towards other people.

words.ex: The rain offset the heat yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天的雨抵消了炎热。
words.en: If one thing is offset by another, the effect of the first thing is reduced by the second, so that any advantage or disadvantage is cancelled out.

words.tr:
n. 谷歌（网络搜索引擎）；
vt. 用搜索引擎搜索（尤指用谷歌搜索引擎）；
words.ex: I use Google to find information online.
words.ex_cn: 我使用谷歌在网上查找信息。
words.en: To use the Google search engine to find information on the internet.

words.ex: He put ointment on his cut.
words.ex_cn: 他把药膏涂在伤口上。
words.en: A smooth substance that is rubbed on the skin to heal wounds or soothe pain.

words.tr: adj. 油质的；油滑的；油嘴滑舌的
words.ex: The fish had a slightly oleaginous texture.
words.ex_cn: 这条鱼的质地有点油腻。
words.en: If you describe someone as oleaginous, you are criticizing them for being excessively flattering or ingratiating.

words.ex: The olfactory nerve helps us smell food.
words.ex_cn: 嗅神经帮助我们闻到食物的味道。
words.en: Relating to the sense of smell.

words.ex: He made an omelet for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐做了一个煎蛋卷。
words.en: An omelet is a dish made by beating eggs and cooking them in a frying pan, often with other ingredients such as cheese, vegetables, or meat folded inside.

words.tr: adj. 无所不在的；遍及各处的
words.ex: The smell of bread is omnipresent in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨面包的香味无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something as omnipresent, you mean that it seems to be everywhere at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 全知的；无所不知的
words.ex: The omniscient narrator knows everything about the characters.
words.ex_cn: 全知的叙述者了解角色的一切。
words.en: Knowing everything; having infinite awareness, understanding, and insight.

words.ex: Bears are omnivorous animals.
words.ex_cn: 熊是杂食动物。
words.en: An omnivorous animal or person eats both plants and meat.

words.ex: The onset of winter brought heavy snow.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的开始带来了大雪。
words.en: The onset of something is the beginning of it, especially something unpleasant.

words.ex: The onslaught of rain flooded the streets.
words.ex_cn: 大量倾泻的雨水淹没了街道。
words.en: An onslaught is a very powerful, often violent, attack against someone or something.

words.ex: The onus is on you to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 完成这个项目是你的职责。
words.en: The responsibility for something, especially a duty or task.

words.tr:
v. 渗出；流出；分泌出
n. 软泥；淤泥；泥浆
words.ex: Mud is oozing from the hole.
words.ex_cn: 泥巴正从洞里渗出来。
words.en: If a liquid oozes from something or if something oozes a liquid, the liquid flows from it slowly and in small quantities.

words.ex: The sea shows opalescence under the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 月光下，大海呈现出彩虹般的光泽。
words.en: Opalescence is the visual property of something that has a milky iridescence like that of an opal.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.ex: He opined that the new policy would benefit the company.
words.ex_cn: 他认为新政策将对公司有利。
words.en: To opine means to express an opinion.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.

words.ex: The king oppresses the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王压迫穷人。
words.en: If someone oppresses people, they treat them cruelly or unfairly and prevent them from having the same rights as other people.

words.ex: The palace showed opulence with golden walls and silk curtains.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿以金墙和丝绸窗帘展现了富裕。
words.en: Opulence is great wealth or luxuriousness.

words.ex: The priest was known as an oracle who spoke for the gods.
words.ex_cn: 这位祭司被称为传达神谕的传神谕者。
words.en: An oracle is a person or thing considered to provide wise and insightful guidance or prophetic predictions, often through divine inspiration.

words.ex: His oracular words confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他那神秘莫测的话语让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as oracular, you mean that it is like an oracle, especially because it is mysterious or difficult to understand.

words.ex: He works in a laboratory on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在星期五去实验室工作。
words.en: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific research, experiments, or teaching.

words.ex: He walks in the orchard every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在果园里散步。
words.en: An orchard is an area of land where fruit trees are grown.

words.tr: v. 授予圣职；命令；注定
words.ex: The priest will ordain the new pastor next Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 神父将在下个星期日任命这位新牧师。
words.en: To ordain someone as a priest or minister means to officially make them a priest or minister, usually in a religious ceremony. To ordain something means to order or command it officially.

words.ex: The city passed an ordinance to stop littering.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市通过了一项禁止乱扔垃圾的法令。
words.en: An ordinance is an authoritative rule, law, decree, or command.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.ex: The ornate ceiling had gold patterns and flowers.
words.ex_cn: 华丽的天花板上有金色的图案和花朵。
words.en: Something that is ornate is highly decorated with complex patterns.

words.tr: adj. 脾气坏的；难相处的
words.ex: He is known for his ornery disposition.
words.ex_cn: 他以坏脾气著称。
words.en: If you describe someone as ornery, you mean that they are bad-tempered, difficult, and often do things that are mean.

words.tr: adj. 朗朗的；宏亮的；做作的；夸张的
words.ex: His orotund speech was filled with grandiose phrases.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲充满了夸大的措辞，显得非常做作。
words.en: An orotund voice or style of speaking is clear, full, and impressive.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.ex: The pendulum oscillate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆缓慢地摆动。
words.en: If an object oscillates, it moves repeatedly from one position to another and back again, or if a figure or value oscillates, it keeps moving up and down.

words.tr: n. 渗透；渗透作用；潜移默化
words.ex: Water moves by osmosis through a thin membrane.
words.ex_cn: 水通过半透膜以渗透的方式移动。
words.en: Osmosis is the process by which a liquid passes through a membrane from a less concentrated solution into a more concentrated one.

words.ex: The osseous tissue supports the body.
words.ex_cn: 骨组织支撑身体。
words.en: Of, relating to, or consisting of bone.

words.ex: His ostensible reason for leaving was sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他离开的表面原因是生病。
words.en: An ostensible reason or purpose seems to be the real one, but it is not.

words.ex: He faced ostracism from his classmates for speaking up.
words.ex_cn: 他因为发声而遭到同学的排斥。
words.en: Ostracism is the act of excluding someone from a group or society by common consent.

words.tr: adj. 受人支配的；缺少自主性的
words.ex: He is other-directed and always listens to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他很在意他人意见，总是听朋友的话。
words.en: An other-directed person is someone whose attitudes and behaviors are determined more by the external environment and social norms than by internal values.

words.tr: adj. 没有用的；不必要的；多余的
words.ex: The meeting was deemed otiose as it did not address any new issues.
words.ex_cn: 这次会议被认为是多余的，因为它没有解决任何新问题。
words.en: If you describe something as otiose, you mean that it serves no practical purpose or has no effect.

words.ex: The detective managed to outfox the criminal.
words.ex_cn: 侦探设法智胜了罪犯。
words.en: To outfox someone means to defeat them by being more clever or cunning than they are.

words.ex: He wore an outlandish hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as outlandish, you mean that it is very unusual, strange, or exaggerated.

words.tr: n. 出口；发泄途径；经销店；折扣店
words.ex: The river flows out through an outlet.
words.ex_cn: 河水通过一个出口流出。
words.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow out, or a point in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment to the electricity supply.

words.ex: The general managed to outmaneuver the enemy forces.
words.ex_cn: 这位将军设法用计谋胜过了敌军。
words.en: To outmaneuver someone means to use clever tactics to gain an advantage over them, especially in a military context or in any kind of strategic competition.

words.ex: At the outset, he was unsure about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 在开始时，他对这个计划并不确定。
words.en: The outset of something is the beginning of it.

words.ex: He can outshine others with his bright ideas.
words.ex_cn: 他能用他出色的想法胜过别人。
words.en: If you outshine someone, you are much better at doing something than they are.

words.ex: He outwit the opponent with a clever trick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个聪明的计策胜过了对手。
words.en: To outwit someone means to use your intelligence or a clever trick to defeat them or gain an advantage over them.

words.ex: She put the cake in the oven.
words.ex_cn: 她把蛋糕放进烤箱里。
words.en: An oven is a device for cooking food, using dry heat.

words.ex: His overbearing boss always tells him what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他专横的老板总是告诉他该做什么。
words.en: If you describe someone as overbearing, you mean that they behave in a very unpleasant way because they are too confident of their own importance.

words.tr:
n. 溢出；
v. 泛滥；
words.ex: The rain caused an overflow of the river.
words.ex_cn: 雨水导致河水溢出。
words.en: If a liquid or a river overflows, it flows over the edges of the container or place it is in.

words.tr:
n. 彻底检修；大修；彻底革新；全面修订
v. 彻底检修；超过（赛跑对手）
words.ex: The plane needs an overhaul before the next flight.
words.ex_cn: 这架飞机在下次飞行前需要彻底检修。
words.en: If you overhaul a system or method, you examine it carefully and make many changes in it in order to improve it.

words.tr: v. 伸得过长；做得过火；走过头
words.ex: He overreachs his authority and makes bad decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他越权行事，做出了错误的决定。
words.en: If you say that someone overreaches themselves, you mean that they fail at something because they are trying to do more than they are able to.

words.tr: adj. 最重要的； v. “override”的现在分词；
words.ex: The overriding goal is to keep everyone safe.
words.ex_cn: 最重要的目标是确保每个人的安全。
words.en: An overriding issue or feeling is more important than any other.

words.ex: The manager oversees the team's daily work.
words.ex_cn: 经理监督团队的日常工作。
words.en: To oversee means to watch and direct a piece of work, the people doing it, or the way it is done in order to ensure that it is done correctly.

words.ex: His oversight caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致项目失败。
words.en: An oversight is a mistake that is made by not noticing something or by forgetting to do something.

words.ex: The people tried to overthrow the corrupt government.
words.ex_cn: 人民试图推翻腐败的政府。
words.en: To overthrow a government or a leader means to remove them from power, often by force.

words.tr: n. 前奏曲；主动表示；提议；提案
words.ex: The orchestra played a soft overture before the show.
words.ex_cn: 演出开始前，管弦乐队演奏了一段轻柔的序曲。
words.en: An overture is a piece of music played by an orchestra at the beginning of an opera or ballet, or a suggestion or approach made to someone with the aim of opening negotiations or establishing a relationship.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；自负的；自以为是的
words.ex: His overweening pride led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 他过于自信的骄傲导致了他的失败。
words.en: If you describe someone as overweening, you are criticizing them because they are too confident and think they are better than other people.

words.ex: The iron will oxidize in wet air.
words.ex_cn: 铁在潮湿的空气中会氧化。
words.en: To combine or become combined chemically with oxygen.

words.ex: He tried to pacify the crying baby with a toy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个玩具让哭闹的婴儿安静下来。
words.en: If you pacify someone who is angry, upset, or not pleased, you make them calm or content.

words.ex: The two countries made a pact to stop fighting.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家达成了一项停止战斗的协议。
words.en: A pact is a formal agreement between two or more people, organizations, or governments to do a particular thing or to help each other.

words.tr:
n. 异教徒；无宗教信仰者
adj. 异教的；异教徒的；无宗教信仰的
words.ex: He lived in a pagan village long ago.
words.ex_cn: 他很久以前住在一个异教村庄里。
words.en: A pagan is someone who worships many gods or no god, especially one who belongs to a religion that existed before Christianity.

words.ex: He made a painstaking effort to fix the small details.
words.ex_cn: 他细心地努力修正每一个小细节。
words.en: If you describe someone's work as painstaking, you mean that they do it very carefully and thoroughly, often taking a long time.

words.tr: n. 上腭；味觉；审美眼光；嗜好；爱好
words.ex: The roof of the mouth is called the palate.
words.ex_cn: 口腔的顶部被称为上腭。
words.en: The palate refers to the roof of the mouth in humans and other mammals, separating the oral cavity from the nasal cavity. It also refers to a person's ability to distinguish between and appreciate different flavors.

words.tr: adj. 宫殿般的；宏伟的；富丽堂皇的
words.ex: He lives in a palatial house near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边一座宏伟的房子里。
words.en: If you describe a building or a place as palatial, you mean that it is very large, impressive, or luxurious, like a palace.

words.tr:
v. 空谈；废话；阿谀奉承
n. 谈判；空谈；奉承
words.ex: The negotiators engaged in a lengthy palaver to reach a compromise.
words.ex_cn: 谈判代表们进行了长时间的谈判以达成妥协。
words.en: Palaver is prolonged and idle discussion, often intended to avoid addressing a problem directly.

words.ex: The painter arranged his colors on the palette.
words.ex_cn: 画家把颜色放在调色板上。
words.en: A palette is a flat piece of wood, plastic, etc., on which an artist mixes paints.

words.tr:
n. 柩衣；棺罩；帷幕；遮盖物
v. 使人厌倦；变得枯躁无味
words.ex: The pall of smoke from the factory hung over the town.
words.ex_cn: 工厂的烟幕笼罩着整个城镇。
words.en: A pall is a dark cloud of smoke, dust, or similar, or a feeling of fear, sadness, or depression.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medication to palliate the patient's pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了药来减轻病人的疼痛。
words.en: To palliate means to make something less severe or intense without actually solving the cause of it. It can refer to the easing of physical pain or the attempt to make a fault or crime seem less serious.

words.tr:
n. 治标药物；缓解剂
adj. 减轻的；缓和的；治标的
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a palliative to reduce his pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一种治标药物来减轻他的疼痛。
words.en: A palliative is a drug or medical treatment that relieves suffering without dealing with the cause of the suffering.

words.tr: adj. 苍白的；暗淡的；无生气的
words.ex: Her face was pallid after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 久病之后，她的脸色变得苍白。
words.en: If you describe something such as a performance or a piece of writing as pallid, you mean that it is weak and not at all exciting or interesting.

words.ex: Her heart palpitated with excitement.
words.ex_cn: 她的心脏因兴奋而悸动。
words.en: If your heart palpitates, it beats very fast and in an irregular way, usually because you are anxious or frightened.

words.ex: She pampered her baby with warm baths and soft blankets.
words.ex_cn: 她用温水浴和柔软的毯子细心照顾她的婴儿。
words.en: To treat someone very kindly, often too kindly, by letting them have or do whatever they want.

words.ex: He put the bread in the pan.
words.ex_cn: 他把面包放进平底锅里。
words.en: A pan is a round metal container with a long handle, which is used for cooking things in, usually on top of a stove.

words.tr: n. 喧嚣；大混乱；大吵大闹
words.ex: The crowd created pandemonium when the winner was announced.
words.ex_cn: 当获胜者被宣布时，人群陷入了混乱。
words.en: Pandemonium is a situation in which there is a lot of noise and confusion because people are excited, angry, or frightened.

words.ex: The show pandered to children's tastes.
words.ex_cn: 这个节目迎合了孩子们的口味。
words.en: If you pander to someone or to their wishes, you do everything that they want, often to get some advantage for yourself.

words.ex: The window has a broken pane.
words.ex_cn: 这扇窗户有一块碎了的玻璃。
words.en: A pane is a piece of glass that is fitted into a window or door.

words.tr: n. 一阵剧痛；突然而强烈的情感
words.ex: He felt a pang of guilt after lying.
words.ex_cn: 他说谎后感到一阵内疚。
words.en: A pang is a sudden strong feeling of physical or emotional pain.

words.tr:
n. 恐慌；
v. 感到恐慌；
words.ex: A panic spread through the crowd when the fire alarm rang.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了恐慌。
words.en: Panic is a very strong feeling of anxiety or fear, which makes you act without thinking carefully.

words.ex: He saw a beautiful panorama from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 他从山顶看到了美丽的全景。
words.en: A panorama is a view of a wide area, or a description or study that presents all the different parts or aspects of a particular subject.

words.ex: The view from the hill is panoramic.
words.ex_cn: 从山上望去，景色一览无余。
words.en: A panoramic view or picture is one that shows a wide area of land or sea.

words.ex: The parallelism between the two events is striking.
words.ex_cn: 这两件事之间的相似之处非常明显。
words.en: Parallelism is the state of being parallel or of corresponding in some way.

words.tr: v. 使麻痹；使瘫痪；使无效；使停止活动
words.ex: The accident paralyzed his leg.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他的腿瘫痪了。
words.en: If someone is paralyzed by an accident or an illness, they have no feeling in their body, or in part of their body, and are unable to move.

words.ex: The sun parched the land.
words.ex_cn: 太阳晒干了土地。
words.en: To make something very dry, especially by exposure to heat.

words.ex: He will pare the apple with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他将用刀削苹果。
words.en: To pare something means to cut off its outer layer or to reduce its size or amount by cutting or trimming.

words.ex: The parity of the numbers is important in this game.
words.ex_cn: 这些数字的奇偶性在这个游戏中很重要。
words.en: If there is parity between two things, they are equal to each other.

words.tr:
v. 会谈；谈判
n. 会谈；谈判
words.ex: The two sides agreed to parley in order to resolve their differences.
words.ex_cn: 双方同意进行会谈以解决分歧。
words.en: A parley is a discussion between two opposing sides in a conflict, especially a discussion of terms for a truce.

words.tr:
adj. 危险的；难对付的
adv. 非常地；极度地
words.ex: The situation was parlous, and we had to tread carefully.
words.ex_cn: 情况非常危险，我们必须小心行事。
words.en: A parlous situation is full of danger or uncertainty.

words.tr: adj. 教区的；地方范围的；思想狭隘的
words.ex: The priest served in a small parochial church.
words.ex_cn: 牧师在一座小型教区教堂服务。
words.en: If you describe someone as parochial, you are criticizing them because you think they are too concerned with their own affairs and should be thinking about more important things.

words.tr:
v. 挡开；避开；回避
n. 挡开；闪避
words.ex: He parries the punch with his arm.
words.ex_cn: 他用胳膊格挡了这一拳。
words.en: If you parry a question or argument, you cleverly avoid answering it or dealing with it. In fencing, if you parry a blow, you defend yourself against it by pushing it away with your weapon.

words.ex: Can you particularize your request?
words.ex_cn: 你能详细说明你的要求吗？
words.en: To particularize means to describe or consider something in detail, often by listing its individual parts or aspects.

words.tr:
n. 划分；隔离物；分割
v. 分开；隔开
words.ex: The partition of the room made it more private.
words.ex_cn: 房间的隔断让它更私密了。
words.en: A partition is a wall, screen, or divider that separates one part of a room, vehicle, or other space from another.

words.ex: The mother experienced parturition at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 这位母亲在黎明时分分娩。
words.en: The process of giving birth to offspring.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；已过盛年的
words.ex: The fashion styles of the 1980s are now considered passé.
words.ex_cn: 20世纪80年代的时尚风格现在被认为已经过时了。
words.en: No longer fashionable or in vogue; out of date.

words.ex: He remained passive during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持被动。
words.en: Accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

words.tr: n. 模仿作品；风格拼凑的艺术作品
words.ex: The movie is a pastiche of various genres.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是各种类型的混成曲。
words.en: A pastiche is a work of art, literature, or music that imitates the style of someone else's work or is a mixture of different styles.

words.ex: The pastoral man tends his sheep on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这位牧人在山上照看他的羊。
words.en: Relating to the countryside or to the work of a shepherd; idyllically rural.

words.ex: He bought a warm pastry from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他从面包店买了一个热乎乎的点心。
words.en: Pastry is a food made from flour, fat, and water that is mixed together, rolled flat, and baked in an oven. It is used as a base or covering for pies, tarts, and other dishes.

words.ex: He planted carrots in a small patch.
words.ex_cn: 他在一小块地上种了胡萝卜。
words.en: A patch is a piece of material used to mend a hole or a weak spot in something, or a small area that is different from the area around it.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.ex: He is studying pathology to understand diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习病理学以了解疾病。
words.en: Pathology is the study of the causes and effects of diseases, especially the branch of medicine that deals with the laboratory examination of samples of body tissue for diagnostic or forensic purposes.

words.ex: He is a true patriot who loves his country.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位真正热爱祖国的爱国者。
words.en: A patriot is someone who loves their country and is willing to defend it against enemies or detractors.

words.tr: n. 爱国主义；爱国精神；
words.ex: He showed patriotism by serving his country in the army.
words.ex_cn: 他通过在军队中为国家服务表现出爱国主义。
words.en: Patriotism is the love and devotion to one's country.

words.ex: The pauper lived in a small hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个穷人住在一间小屋里。
words.en: A pauper is someone who is extremely poor and has very little money or possessions.

words.ex: The child was pavid of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子害怕黑暗。
words.en: If someone is pavid, they are showing fear or timidity.

words.ex: He left his watch as a pawn at the shop.
words.ex_cn: 他把手表当成了典当品放在店里。
words.en: To pawn something means to leave it with a pawnbroker, who lends you money in exchange. The pawnbroker keeps the item until you pay back the money plus interest.

words.ex: Everything is peachy in her life.
words.ex_cn: 她生活中的一切都很美好。
words.en: If you describe something as peachy, you mean that it is very pleasant, attractive, or enjoyable.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.ex: He wears a peaky cap in winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天戴一顶尖顶帽子。
words.en: If someone looks peaky, they look pale and ill.

words.ex: He eats a pecan every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一颗山核桃。
words.en: A pecan is a type of nut that grows on a tree native to North America. It is used in cooking, especially in desserts like pecan pie.

words.tr:
v. 啄；连续敲击；轻吻
n. 啄痕；啄食；轻吻
words.ex: The bird pecked at the bread on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿啄地上的面包。
words.en: To peck means to strike or bite something with the beak, or to kiss someone lightly and quickly.

words.ex: After a long hike, I was feeling peckish.
words.ex_cn: 长途徒步后，我感到有点饿。
words.en: If you say that you are peckish, you mean that you are slightly hungry.

words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: The teacher learned new pedagogy from the workshop.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师从研讨会中学到了新的教学法。
words.en: The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept.

words.ex: He pressed the pedal to speed up the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他踩下踏板让自行车加速。
words.en: A pedal is a lever that you press with your foot in order to control a vehicle or machine.

words.tr: v. 兜售；沿街叫卖； 散播
words.ex: He tries to peddle fake watches on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在街上兜售假手表。
words.en: To peddle goods or ideas means to try to sell them or make them accepted by going from place to place.

words.ex: The statue was placed on a marble pedestal.
words.ex_cn: 雕像被放置在大理石底座上。
words.en: A pedestal is the base or support on which a statue, obelisk, or column is mounted.

words.tr:
v. 偷看；窥视
n. 偷看；窥见
words.ex: He peeked through the keyhole.
words.ex_cn: 他从钥匙孔里偷看。
words.en: To peek means to look at something quickly and secretly, especially through a small opening or from behind something.

words.tr:
n. 果皮；
v. 去皮；剥落；
words.ex: The apple peel is rich in fiber.
words.ex_cn: 苹果皮富含纤维。
words.en: To remove the outer covering from something, especially a fruit or vegetable.

words.tr:
v. 偷看；微露出；唧唧叫
n. 窥视；隐现；唧唧声
words.ex: He peeped through the keyhole to see what was inside.
words.ex_cn: 他从钥匙孔里偷看里面是什么。
words.en: To look quickly and often secretively at something or someone.

words.tr:
n. 同辈；同等的人；
v. 凝视；
words.ex: He feels comfortable talking to his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他觉得和同辈交谈很自在。
words.en: A peer is someone who is equal to another in abilities, qualifications, age, background, or social status. As a verb, to peer means to look keenly or with difficulty at someone or something.

words.ex: The peery glances from the crowd made her feel uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 人群中怀疑的目光让她感到不舒服。
words.en: Showing curiosity or inquisitiveness, especially in a way that is unwelcome or intrusive.

words.tr:
n. 气恼；讨厌的对象
v. （使）气恼
words.ex: It always peeves me when people are late.
words.ex_cn: 当人们迟到时，我总是很恼火。
words.en: If something peeves you, it annoys you.

words.tr:
adj.  胡乱的；匆忙的
adv. 乱糟糟地；匆忙地
words.ex: The students rushed pell-mell into the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 学生们慌乱地冲进教室。
words.en: If people move or act pell-mell, they move or act in a hurried, disorganized way, often because they are excited or frightened.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；易懂的
words.ex: The water in the mountain stream was so pellucid that we could see the fish swimming.
words.ex_cn: 山间溪流中的水如此清澈，我们可以看到鱼儿在游动。
words.en: If something is pellucid, it is very clear and easy to understand.

words.tr:
v. 剥...的皮；投掷；急降；急跑
n. 毛皮；投掷；猛落；疾行
words.ex: The hunter pelted the fox after catching it.
words.ex_cn: 猎人抓到狐狸后剥了它的皮。
words.en: The skin of an animal with the fur or hair still on it, or to attack someone by throwing a lot of things at them.

words.ex: He got a penalty for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规则而受到惩罚。
words.en: A penalty is a punishment that is imposed on someone for doing something that is against the rules or the law.

words.tr:
n. （赎罪的）苦行；苦修；忏悔
v. 使...以苦行赎罪
words.ex: He performed penance for his sins.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的罪行忏悔。
words.en: Penance is the act of doing something to show that you are sorry for something wrong that you have done, especially in some religions.

words.tr: adj. 吊着的；悬垂的；悬而未决的
words.ex: The light is pendent from the ceiling.
words.ex_cn: 灯悬挂在天花板上。
words.en: A pendent object is one that hangs down from something else, or a situation that is not yet decided or settled.

words.tr: adj. 松垂的；悬垂摆动的
words.ex: The pendulous branches swayed in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 垂下的枝条在风中摇曳。
words.en: Something that is pendulous hangs or swings freely.

words.ex: The pendulum swings back and forth in the clock.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆在钟里来回摆动。
words.en: A pendulum is a weight that is hung from a fixed point so that it can swing freely, especially a rod with a weight at the end that regulates the mechanism of a clock.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: The doctor gave him penicillin for his infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了青霉素治疗感染。
words.en: An antibiotic drug obtained from molds or produced synthetically, used to treat infections caused by bacteria.

words.ex: He lives in penury after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Penury is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: He perambulates through the park every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上在公园里散步。
words.en: To walk or travel through a place, especially for pleasure and in a leisurely way.

words.tr:
n. 栖枝；鲈鱼；
v. 栖息；处于（高处）；
words.ex: The bird sat on a perch near the tree.
words.ex_cn: 鸟停在树旁的一根栖枝上。
words.en: A perch is a branch or rod where a bird rests or a high position where someone or something is located. As a verb, it means to rest or be located in a high position.

words.tr: v. 滤；渗透；用渗滤壶煮咖啡
words.ex: Water percolates through the soil.
words.ex_cn: 水透过土壤渗出。
words.en: If a liquid percolates, it moves slowly through a substance that has very small holes in it.

words.tr: adj. 断然的；不容置辩的；专横的
words.ex: He gave a peremptory order to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他下达了一个不容置疑的离开命令。
words.en: If someone's manner or behavior is peremptory, they are so confident and sure of their authority that they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.ex: His perfidy shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的背信弃义让所有人震惊。
words.en: Perfidy is the act of deliberately betraying someone's trust; treachery.

words.ex: The machine can perforate the paper quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器可以快速地在纸上打孔。
words.en: To make a hole or holes through something, especially by piercing or drilling.

words.ex: The hikers faced great peril in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者在风暴中面临巨大危险。
words.en: Peril refers to serious and immediate danger.

words.tr: adj. 迂回曲折的；转弯抹角的
words.ex: The politician used a periphrastic response to avoid directly answering the question.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家用一种迂回的回答来避免直接回答问题。
words.en: If someone uses periphrastic language, they express something in an indirect way, using more words than necessary.

words.ex: The flowers will perish if you don't water them.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不给花浇水，它们会死。
words.en: If people or animals perish, they die as a result of very harsh conditions or as the result of an accident.

words.tr:
adj. 令人极难受的；可恶的；酷寒的
adv. …得要命；非常
v. 死；暴卒；毁灭；“perish”的现在分词
words.ex: The perishing cold made it hard to breathe.
words.ex_cn: 令人极难受的寒冷让人难以呼吸。
words.en: extremely cold; causing discomfort or suffering

words.ex: He will perjure himself in court.
words.ex_cn: 他将在法庭上作伪证。
words.en: If someone perjures themselves in a court of law, they lie, even though they have promised to tell the truth.

words.ex: He was charged with perjury after lying in court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后被控伪证罪。
words.en: The crime of telling a lie in a court of law after having sworn to tell the truth.

words.ex: Free lunch is a perk of this job.
words.ex_cn: 免费午餐是这份工作的一个额外补贴。
words.en: If someone perks up or if something perks them up, they become more cheerful or lively.

words.tr: adj. 活泼的；神气的；意气洋洋的；有生气的
words.ex: She is perky after drinking coffee.
words.ex_cn: 她喝完咖啡后精神抖擞。
words.en: Someone who is perky is cheerful and lively.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.ex: They persecute people for their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们因人们的信仰而迫害他们。
words.en: If someone is persecuted, they are treated cruelly and unfairly, often because of their race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: His persiflage made the meeting feel light and funny.
words.ex_cn: 他的戏谑让会议显得轻松有趣。
words.en: Persiflage is light, slightly mocking talk or writing.

words.ex: His persistence helped him pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚持让他通过了考试。
words.en: Persistence is the determination to do something even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.tr: adj. 爱挑剔的；难应付的
words.ex: She is very persnickety about her food, always looking for the best ingredients.
words.ex_cn: 她对食物非常挑剔，总是寻找最好的食材。
words.en: If you describe someone as persnickety, you think that they pay too much attention to small, unimportant details and are difficult to please.

words.ex: This rule pertains to all students.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: If one thing pertains to another, it relates, belongs, or applies to it.

words.ex: He is pertinacious about finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要完成作业。
words.en: Someone who is pertinacious continues trying to do something in a very determined way, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: He peruses the newspaper every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上浏览报纸。
words.en: To read or examine something carefully or thoroughly.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；任性的；乖张的；故意作对的；悖理的
words.ex: He gave a perverse answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个反常的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as perverse, you mean that they deliberately behave in an unreasonable way, especially by doing the opposite of what is expected or wanted.

words.tr:
v. 使堕落；误用；歪曲；使走邪路
n. 堕落者；性变态者；色狼
words.ex: He tried to pervert the truth with lies.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用谎言歪曲真相。
words.en: If you pervert something, you change it from what it should be or what it was originally intended to be into something that is wrong or harmful.

words.ex: He read the previous chapter last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了前一章。
words.en: Existing or occurring before in time or order.

words.tr: v. 不断打扰；纠缠；烦扰
words.ex: The child keeps pestering his mom for candy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子不停地缠着妈妈要糖果。
words.en: If you say that someone is pestering you, you mean that they keep asking you to do something, or keep talking to you, and you find this annoying.

words.tr: adj. 致死的；瘟疫的；有害的
words.ex: The pestilent disease killed many people in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这种致死的疾病夺去了村里许多人的生命。
words.en: Something that is pestilent is likely to cause or spread a deadly disease, or is extremely harmful or unpleasant.

words.tr:
n. 杵；碾槌
v. 用槌磨；用杵捣
words.ex: She used a pestle to grind the herbs into a fine powder.
words.ex_cn: 她用杵把草药捣成细粉。
words.en: A pestle is a heavy tool with a rounded end, used for crushing and grinding substances such as spices or drugs, usually in a mortar.

words.ex: The rose has five pink petals.
words.ex_cn: 这朵玫瑰有五片粉红色的花瓣。
words.en: A petal is one of the colored parts of a flower that are often shaped like a leaf and grow in a circle around the center.

words.tr: n. 请愿人；上诉人；离婚上诉方
words.ex: The petitioner asked the court for help.
words.ex_cn: 申请人请求法院给予帮助。
words.en: A petitioner is a person who presents a petition to a court or other authority in order to request a legal action or a favor.

words.tr: v. 使石化；使僵化；吓呆
words.ex: The lightning petrified the tree into stone.
words.ex_cn: 闪电把树变成了石头。
words.en: To petrify means to make someone so frightened that they are unable to move or think.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；爱发脾气的
words.ex: She was feeling pettish after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 工作了一整天后，她感到很易怒。
words.en: Easily irritated or annoyed; peevish.

words.tr: adj. 琐碎的；微不足道的；心胸狭窄的
words.ex: He got angry over a petty mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他因为一个微不足道的错误生气了。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as petty, you mean that they care too much about small, unimportant things and perhaps that they are unnecessarily unkind.

words.tr: n. 坏脾气；性急；急躁言行
words.ex: His petulance was evident in every word he spoke.
words.ex_cn: 他的易怒在他说的每一个字中都显而易见。
words.en: Petulance is the quality of being childishly sulky or bad-tempered.

words.ex: The phantom appeared in the mist near the old house.
words.ex_cn: 幻影出现在老房子附近的薄雾中。
words.en: A phantom is a ghost or a figment of the imagination.

words.tr: adj. 伪善的；伪装虔诚的
words.ex: His pharisaic attitude towards religion was deeply hypocritical.
words.ex_cn: 他对宗教的伪善态度非常虚伪。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as pharisaic, you are criticizing them for being hypocritical and self-righteous.

words.ex: He studies pharmacology to understand how drugs work.
words.ex_cn: 他学习药理学以了解药物如何发挥作用。
words.en: Pharmacology is the branch of medicine concerned with the uses, effects, and modes of action of drugs.

words.ex: He developed a passion for philately at a young age.
words.ex_cn: 他从小就对集邮产生了浓厚的兴趣。
words.en: The collection and study of postage stamps, postmarks, and related materials.

words.tr: n. 语文学；语言学；文献学
words.ex: He loves philology because it helps him understand old texts.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱语言学，因为它帮助他理解古文。
words.en: Philology is the study of language in written historical sources; it is a combination of literary studies, history and linguistics.

words.ex: The phoenix rises from its ashes.
words.ex_cn: 凤凰从灰烬中重生。
words.en: A phoenix is a mythical bird that is said to be cyclically regenerated or reborn. Associated with the sun, a phoenix obtains new life by arising from the ashes of its predecessor.

words.tr:
adj. 假的；冒充的；欺骗的
n. 骗子；伪君子；假货
words.ex: He gave a phony excuse for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他编了一个虚假的借口来解释迟到。
words.en: If you describe something as phony, you disapprove of it because it is false rather than genuine.

words.tr: adj. （非正式）不值钱的；眼光狭小的；微不足道的; n. 价值低微的小硬币；西班牙小币；（非正式...
words.ex: He dismissed her concerns as picayune.
words.ex_cn: 他不屑一顾地认为她的担忧微不足道。
words.en: If you describe something as picayune, you mean that it is very small, unimportant, or trivial.

words.tr:
adj. 有图画的；图示的
n. 画报
words.ex: The book has a pictorial guide to plants.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一本植物的图解指南。
words.en: A pictorial representation or image is one that is made using pictures or shows things in a way that pictures do.

words.ex: Don't piddle your time away on small things.
words.ex_cn: 不要把时间浪费在琐事上。
words.en: To piddle means to spend time in a wasteful or trifling manner, or to urinate.

words.tr:
adj. 无用的；琐碎的；微不足道的
v. 撒尿；鬼混；游荡；“piddle”的现在分词
words.ex: He is piddling away his time on useless games.
words.ex_cn: 他正在浪费时间玩无用的游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as piddling, you are emphasizing that it is very small or unimportant.

words.ex: The piebald horse trotted gracefully across the meadow.
words.ex_cn: 那匹花斑马优雅地小跑穿过草地。
words.en: A piebald animal has patches of black and white on it.

words.tr:
adj. 零碎的；
adv. 零碎地；
words.ex: He fixed the car piecemeal, one part at a time.
words.ex_cn: 他一点一点地修理汽车，一次修一个零件。
words.en: If you describe a change or process as piecemeal, you disapprove of it because it happens gradually, usually at irregular intervals, and is probably not satisfactory.

words.ex: The pied butterfly fluttered among the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 那只杂色蝴蝶在花丛中翩翩起舞。
words.en: Having patches of two or more colors, typically black and white.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.ex: The pigment in leaves changes color in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 叶子中的色素在秋天会变色。
words.en: A pigment is a substance that gives something a particular color.

words.tr: v. 小偷小摸；偷窃（小东西）
words.ex: He was caught pilfering from the store.
words.ex_cn: 他因在商店里小偷小摸被抓。
words.en: To pilfer means to steal things of little value or in small quantities, often in a stealthy way.

words.tr:
n. 掠夺；抢劫；掠夺物
v. 抢劫；掠夺
words.ex: The soldiers committed pillage after winning the battle.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在赢得战斗后进行了掠夺。
words.en: If a group of people pillage a place, they steal a lot of things from it and often cause a lot of damage, especially in a war.

words.ex: The pilot landed the plane safely.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员安全地降落了飞机。
words.en: A pilot is a person who operates the flying controls of an aircraft. Also, to pilot something means to test or introduce a new idea, product, etc., to see if it will be successful.

words.ex: He gave her a light pinch on the arm.
words.ex_cn: 他轻轻捏了她的胳膊一下。
words.en: To pinch someone or something means to squeeze them tightly between your thumb and finger, or between two surfaces, especially in a way that causes pain.

words.tr: adj. 开胃的；辛辣的；刺激的；迷人的；兴奋的
words.ex: The sauce has a piquant flavor.
words.ex_cn: 这种酱汁味道辛辣可口。
words.en: Something that is piquant is pleasantly strong and sharp in taste or smell.

words.tr:
v. 激怒；使生气；激起
n. 怨恨；愤恨
words.ex: His rude comment piqued her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论激怒了她。
words.en: If something piques your interest or curiosity, it makes you interested or curious.

words.ex: The pirate sailed the sea with a black flag.
words.ex_cn: 海盗带着黑旗在海上航行。
words.en: A pirate is someone who attacks and robs ships at sea. The term can also refer to someone who illegally copies and distributes software, music, or films.

words.tr:
n. 单脚尖旋转
v. 用脚尖旋转；表演旋转舞
words.ex: She executed a perfect pirouette.
words.ex_cn: 她完成了一个完美的单脚尖旋转。
words.en: In ballet, a pirouette is a turn or spin on one foot, typically with the raised foot touching the knee of the supporting leg.

words.ex: The town is famous for its piscatorial activities.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇以其渔业活动而闻名。
words.en: Relating to fish or fishing.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；哀怨的；令人怜悯的
words.ex: The piteous cries of the injured animal echoed through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 受伤动物的哀怨叫声在森林中回荡。
words.en: If something is piteous, it makes you feel pity for someone, especially because they are in a very bad situation.

words.tr:
n. （木）髓；（柑橘等）外皮下的海绵层；精髓；核心
v. 除去木髓
words.ex: The pith of the essay is its call for social change.
words.ex_cn: 这篇文章的核心是其呼吁社会变革。
words.en: The essential or most vital part of some idea or experience.

words.ex: The pithiness of his speech impressed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他讲话的有力之处让所有人都印象深刻。
words.en: The quality of being concise and meaningful in expression.

words.tr: adj. 冷酷的；无情的；无怜悯心的
words.ex: The pitiless wind blew all night.
words.ex_cn: 无情的风刮了一整夜。
words.en: If you describe someone as pitiless, you mean that they are very cruel and have no pity for anyone.

words.tr: n. 微薄的工资；极少的报酬
words.ex: He lived on a pittance during his early career.
words.ex_cn: 他在职业生涯初期靠微薄的收入生活。
words.en: A very small or inadequate amount of money paid to someone as an allowance or wage.

words.tr:
n. 枢；中心；旋转
v. 在枢轴上转动；以…为中心
words.ex: The door pivots on a hinge.
words.ex_cn: 门围绕一个铰链旋转。
words.en: A pivot is the central point, pin, or shaft on which a mechanism turns or oscillates. It can also refer to the central or most important person or thing in a situation.

words.tr:
n. 招贴；海报；标语牌；广告牌
v. 张贴布告于；在…贴广告
words.ex: The walls were covered with political placards.
words.ex_cn: 墙上贴满了政治海报。
words.en: A placard is a large notice or sign, often carried in public places to announce something or to protest against something.

words.ex: He plagiarized the essay from the internet.
words.ex_cn: 他从网上抄袭了这篇论文。
words.en: To plagiarize means to use someone else's ideas or work and pretend that it is your own.

words.tr:
n. 瘟疫；疫病；
v. 困扰；折磨；
words.ex: The plague killed many people in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 瘟疫在中世纪的欧洲杀死了许多人。
words.en: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills a lot of people. It can also refer to a large number of insects or animals that cause damage or are a nuisance.

words.tr:
n. 平原；
adj. 简单明了的；朴素的；
words.ex: The cows graze on the plain.
words.ex_cn: 牛在平原上吃草。
words.en: If something is plain, it is easy to see, hear, or understand.

words.tr:
n. 辫子；辫状物；发辫
v. 将…编成辫
words.ex: She wore her hair in a neat plait.
words.ex_cn: 她把头发编成了整齐的辫子。
words.en: A plait is a length of hair that has been twisted over and under other pieces of hair to form one thick length. To plait hair means to twist three or more lengths of hair over and under each other to form one thick length.

words.ex: The plangent sound of the church bells echoed through the valley.
words.ex_cn: 教堂钟声的轰鸣声在山谷中回荡。
words.en: A plangent sound is loud, deep, and often sad.

words.ex: He nailed the wooden plank to the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把木板钉在了地板上。
words.en: A plank is a long, flat piece of wood, often used in building or as part of a structure.

words.tr:
n. 灰泥；
v. 涂以灰泥；敷以膏药；
words.ex: The wall was covered with white plaster.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁上覆盖着白色灰泥。
words.en: A substance applied to walls or ceilings to smooth or decorate them, or a medical dressing used to cover wounds.

words.ex: The sheep graze on a high plateau.
words.ex_cn: 羊群在高高原上吃草。
words.en: A plateau is a large area of high and fairly flat land. It can also refer to a period during which there are no large changes.

words.tr: adj. 柏拉图式的（指不含性爱）
words.ex: They had a platonic relationship, with no romantic involvement.
words.ex_cn: 他们的关系是纯精神的，没有任何浪漫的牵扯。
words.en: Platonic describes a relationship or love that is intimate and affectionate but not sexual.

words.ex: The actor received a plaudit for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而获得赞誉。
words.en: Plaudit refers to an expression of praise or approval, often given in the form of applause or enthusiastic commendation.

words.ex: Children play in the plaza after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在广场上玩耍。
words.en: A plaza is an open public space that is found in the heart of a city or town. It is often surrounded by buildings and may include shops, restaurants, and other amenities.

words.tr: v. 恳求；辩护；答辩；以…为理由
words.ex: He pleaded for help when he was lost.
words.ex_cn: 当他迷路时，他恳求帮助。
words.en: If you plead with someone to do something, you ask them in an intense, emotional way to do it.

words.tr:
n. 褶；褶状物
v. 使打褶
words.ex: She ironed the pleat in her skirt.
words.ex_cn: 她把裙子上的褶皱熨平了。
words.en: A pleat is a fold in a piece of cloth, made by doubling the material over on itself and then pressing or stitching it into place.

words.tr:
adj. 平民的；粗俗的
n. 平民；下层人；老百姓
words.ex: The speech was criticized for its plebeian language.
words.ex_cn: 这篇演讲因其粗俗的语言而受到批评。
words.en: A plebeian is a member of the general populace, especially one of the common people of ancient Rome. As an adjective, it describes something that is common, ordinary, or vulgar.

words.ex: He made a pledge to help the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了帮助穷人的保证。
words.en: A pledge is a serious promise or agreement, especially one made publicly or officially. It can also refer to something given as security for the fulfillment of a contract or the payment of a debt.

words.tr:
adj. 全体参加的；无限的；完全的
n. 全会；全体会议
words.ex: The plenary session started at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 全体会议在上午九点开始。
words.en: A plenary session or meeting is one that is attended by everyone who has the right to attend.

words.ex: The garden was in a state of plenitude, with flowers blooming everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 花园里繁花似锦，处处充满生机。
words.en: The state of being full or complete; abundance.

words.ex: There is a plentitude of food at the party.
words.ex_cn: 聚会上食物非常多。
words.en: Plentitude refers to a large or sufficient quantity or supply of something.

words.ex: The phrase 'free gift' is pleonastic because 'gift' implies something given without charge.
words.ex_cn: 短语'免费礼物'是冗言的，因为'礼物'本身就意味着不收费。
words.en: Using more words than are necessary to convey meaning, often to the point of redundancy.

words.tr:
v. 艰难地行走；吃力地行进
n. 劳苦；沉重的脚步（声）
words.ex: He plodded through the snow with heavy boots.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着沉重的靴子艰难地在雪地中行走。
words.en: To plod means to walk slowly with heavy steps, especially because you are tired or working hard. It can also mean to work slowly and steadily at something, especially something that is boring or difficult.

words.tr:
n. 犁；犁形器具
v. 犁；耕；艰苦前进
words.ex: The farmer uses a plow to turn the soil.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用犁翻土。
words.en: A plow is a farm tool with one or more heavy blades that breaks the soil and cuts a furrow for sowing seeds.

words.ex: He wants to apply for a job at the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他想申请银行的工作。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.ex: The plumber fixed the leaky pipe.
words.ex_cn: 水管工修好了漏水的管道。
words.en: A plumber is a person whose job is to connect and repair things such as water and drainage pipes, baths, and toilets.

words.ex: The apple plummeted from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上垂直落下。
words.en: If an amount, rate, or price plummets, it decreases quickly by a large amount.

words.tr:
v. 掠夺；抢劫
n. 掠夺物；掠夺；赃物
words.ex: The pirates plundered the ship.
words.ex_cn: 海盗劫掠了那艘船。
words.en: If someone plunders a place or plunders things from a place, they steal things from it.

words.tr:
n. 多元论者
adj. 多元化的；多元性的
words.ex: The city is known for its pluralist society, embracing diversity in all aspects.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市以其多元社会而闻名，在各个方面都拥抱多样性。
words.en: A pluralist is someone who believes that different groups, systems, or beliefs can coexist in a society.

words.ex: The hotel has a plush lobby with velvet chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店有一个豪华的大堂，配有丝绒椅子。
words.en: Plush refers to something that is luxurious and expensive, or a type of fabric that is very soft and thick.

words.ex: He was accused of poaching ideas from his colleague.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控盗用同事的想法。
words.en: To poach means to illegally hunt or catch animals or fish, or to cook something such as an egg without its shell in or over boiling water.

words.ex: The pea grows inside a green pod.
words.ex_cn: 豌豆长在绿色的荚里。
words.en: A pod is a case that holds the seeds of certain plants, such as peas and beans.

words.ex: He visited a podiatrist for his sore feet.
words.ex_cn: 他因为脚疼去看足病医生。
words.en: A podiatrist is a medical professional devoted to the study and medical treatment of disorders of the foot, ankle, and lower extremity.

words.ex: He stood on the podium to receive the gold medal.
words.ex_cn: 他站在领奖台上领取金牌。
words.en: A podium is a small platform on which someone stands to give a speech or conduct an orchestra, or on which a medal winner stands during a prize-giving ceremony.

words.ex: The poignancy of the moment was not lost on anyone.
words.ex_cn: 那一刻的辛酸没有被任何人忽略。
words.en: The quality of evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret.

words.ex: The frog is poisonous.
words.ex_cn: 这只青蛙是有毒的。
words.en: Something that is poisonous will kill you or make you ill if you eat it, drink it, or absorb it.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；捅
n. 戳；刺；捅
words.ex: He poked the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke means to prod or jab someone or something with a finger or a pointed object, or to move something in a particular direction with a sharp movement. It can also refer to the act of making a hole or opening in something by pushing a pointed object into it.

words.ex: His article was a polemic against government corruption.
words.ex_cn: 他的文章是对政府腐败的抨击。
words.en: A polemic is a very strong written or spoken attack on, or defence of, a particular belief or opinion.

words.tr: adj. 辩论的；引起争论的；争议的
words.ex: His polemical article sparked strong debates.
words.ex_cn: 他那篇有争议的文章引发了激烈争论。
words.en: A polemical piece of writing or speech is one that strongly argues against or in favor of a particular opinion, person, or idea, often in a way that is intended to provoke controversy.

words.ex: The poll showed that most people support the new law.
words.ex_cn: 这项民意调查表明，大多数人支持这项新法律。
words.en: A poll is a survey in which people are asked their opinions about something, usually in order to find out how popular something is or what people intend to do in the future.

words.ex: The pollster conducted a survey to gauge public opinion on the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 民意调查员进行了一项调查，以了解公众对新政策的看法。
words.en: A pollster is a person or organization that conducts polls, especially to find out people's opinions about political issues.

words.tr: n. 博学者；学识渊博的人；
words.ex: Leonardo da Vinci was a polymath who excelled in art, science, and engineering.
words.ex_cn: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇是一位博学者，在艺术、科学和工程方面都很出色。
words.en: A polymath is a person who knows a lot about many different subjects.

words.ex: He wears a poncho when it rains.
words.ex_cn: 下雨时他穿一件篷风衣。
words.en: A poncho is a piece of clothing that consists of a large piece of material, usually waterproof, with a hole in the middle for the head.

words.ex: He sat by the window to ponder his future.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边深思自己的未来。
words.en: If you ponder something, you think about it carefully.

words.tr: adj. 可衡量的；可估计的；值得考虑的
words.ex: The question of ethics is a ponderable issue in this debate.
words.ex_cn: 道德问题是这场辩论中值得考虑的问题。
words.en: Capable of being weighed or assessed.

words.tr: adj. 教皇的；武断的；傲慢的
words.ex: He wore a pontifical robe during the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上穿了一件教皇式的长袍。
words.en: Relating to the Pope or to the office or authority of the Pope; having the pomp or dignity associated with high ecclesiastical office.

words.ex: She poohed the idea of going to the party.
words.ex_cn: v. 她对去参加聚会的想法嗤之以鼻。
words.en: To express contempt or disdain for something.

words.tr: n. 水塘；水池；备用物资；美式撞球；
words.ex: The children play near the small pool.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在小水塘边玩耍。
words.en: A pool is a small area of still water, especially one that is artificially created.

words.tr: adj. 预示的；凶兆的；装腔作势的
words.ex: The dark clouds are a portentous sign of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的预示。
words.en: If someone's way of speaking, writing, or behaving is portentous, they speak, write, or behave more seriously than necessary because they want to impress other people.

words.ex: He posits that the earth is round.
words.ex_cn: 他提出地球是圆的。
words.en: To posit something is to suggest it as a basic fact or principle from which a further idea is formed or developed.

words.ex: Her positiveness about the future was contagious.
words.ex_cn: 她对未来的信心具有传染性。
words.en: The quality or state of being positive; assurance, confidence, or certainty.

words.ex: He put up a poster on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把一张海报贴在墙上。
words.en: A poster is a large notice or picture that you stick on a wall or board, often in order to advertise something.

words.tr:
n. 仿造品
adj. 画蛇添足的
words.ex: Her postiche was so well-made that it was impossible to distinguish it from real hair.
words.ex_cn: 她的假发做得非常好，几乎无法与真发区分开来。
words.en: A postiche is a piece of false hair worn to cover baldness or as part of a disguise.

words.ex: After a long hike, a cool potation was most welcome.
words.ex_cn: 长途跋涉后，一杯清凉的饮料最受欢迎。
words.en: The act of drinking, especially alcoholic beverages.

words.tr: n. （为赚钱而）粗制的文艺作品
words.ex: He wrote a potboiler to earn money quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一部快餐作品来快速赚钱。
words.en: A potboiler is a book, film, or other creative work that is produced quickly and purely to make money, often of poor quality.

words.ex: The potentate ruled with an iron fist.
words.ex_cn: 这位统治者以铁腕统治。
words.en: A potentate is a ruler who has great power, especially one who rules over a large area or empire.

words.ex: This drug can potentiate the effect of painkillers.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物可以增强止痛药的效果。
words.en: To increase the power, effectiveness, or potency of something, especially a drug or a biochemical agent.

words.tr: n. 喧闹；骚动；心神不宁
words.ex: The pother of the city streets was overwhelming.
words.ex_cn: 城市街道的喧闹让人难以忍受。
words.en: A state of nervous activity or confusion; a commotion.

words.tr: n. 百花香；混杂物；集锦
words.ex: The book is a potpourri of various literary styles.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是各种文学风格的混合体。
words.en: A potpourri is a mixture of dried petals and leaves from various flowers and plants that is used to make a room smell pleasant. It can also refer to a mixture of things, especially musical or literary pieces, that are varied and not connected with each other.

words.tr: n. 小袋；囊状袋；育儿袋；
words.ex: The kangaroo carries its baby in a pouch.
words.ex_cn: 袋鼠把幼崽放在小袋里。
words.en: A pouch is a small, flexible bag, typically made of leather or fabric, used for carrying small items.

words.ex: The book costs five pounds.
words.ex_cn: 这本书五英镑。
words.en: The pound is the unit of money used in Britain. It is also a unit of weight equal to 16 ounces or 0.4536 kilograms. As a verb, to pound means to hit something hard many times or to crush something into a powder or paste.

words.tr: v. 腾跃；阔步行走；神气地快速走动
words.ex: The horse prances across the field.
words.ex_cn: 那匹马在田野上欢快地跳跃。
words.en: If a horse prances, it moves with high, springy steps.

words.tr: n. 恶作剧；开玩笑；戏谑
words.ex: He played a prank on his friend with a fake spider.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个假蜘蛛捉弄了他的朋友。
words.en: A prank is a trick or practical joke that is played on someone, often to make them look foolish or to amuse others.

words.tr:
v. 胡扯；唠叨；喋喋不休
n. 唠叨；喋喋不休
words.ex: He likes to prate about his trips.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢喋喋不休地谈论他的旅行。
words.en: To talk excessively and pointlessly; chatter.

words.ex: He preaches kindness every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都宣扬仁爱。
words.en: If you preach, you give a talk on a religious or moral subject during a religious service.

words.ex: The preamble explains the purpose of the law.
words.ex_cn: 序言解释了法律的目的。
words.en: A preamble is an introduction to a speech or piece of writing, especially one that explains what follows.

words.tr: n. (尤指道德方面的)戒律；准则
words.ex: He follows the precept to be kind every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天遵循要善良的教诲。
words.en: A precept is a general rule intended to regulate behavior or thought.

words.ex: The precocious child could read before age five.
words.ex_cn: 这个早熟的孩子在五岁前就会阅读了。
words.en: A precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, especially in a way that is unusual for their age.

words.ex: He has a predilection for sweet food.
words.ex_cn: 他偏爱甜食。
words.en: If you have a predilection for something, you have a strong liking for it.

words.tr: v. 用喙整理羽毛；精心打扮；感觉良好
words.ex: The bird preens its feathers every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟每天早上梳理它的羽毛。
words.en: If a bird preens or preens itself, it cleans and arranges its feathers using its beak.

words.ex: The dark clouds prefigure a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If one thing prefigures another, it is a sign that the other thing will happen or exist in the future.

words.tr: adj. 可盘卷的；能抓住的；有理解能力的；贪婪的
words.ex: The monkey has a prehensile tail to grab trees.
words.ex_cn: 这只猴子有一条能抓握的尾巴来抓住树木。
words.en: A prehensile tail or limb is adapted for grasping or holding.

words.ex: The quiet music was a prelude to the loud concert.
words.ex_cn: 轻柔的音乐是盛大音乐会的前奏。
words.en: A prelude is an introductory piece of music, event, or action that comes before a more important one.

words.ex: The movie's premiere was held last night.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的首映昨晚举行。
words.en: The first public performance of a play, film, or other form of entertainment.

words.tr: n. 额外费用；保险费；溢价；
words.ex: You need to pay a premium for faster delivery.
words.ex_cn: 你需要支付额外费用才能享受更快的配送。
words.en: A premium is an amount of money that you pay regularly to an insurance company for an insurance policy, or an amount of money that is more than usual for a product or service because it is of higher quality.

words.tr: adj. 占优势的；主要的；压倒性的
words.ex: The preponderant influence of the older generation is still evident.
words.ex_cn: 老一代的占优势的影响仍然明显。
words.en: If something is preponderant, it is more important, powerful, or numerous than other things in a particular situation.

words.ex: The advantages of the new system preponderate over its disadvantages.
words.ex_cn: 新系统的优势超过了它的劣势。
words.en: To be greater in number, influence, or importance than something else.

words.tr:
adj. 给人良好印象的；令人喜爱的；吸引人的
v. 使预先具有（某种思想）；使…先怀偏见；使产生偏爱；“prepossess”的现在分词
words.ex: She had a prepossessing smile that could light up a room.
words.ex_cn: 她有一个迷人的微笑，能照亮整个房间。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as prepossessing, you mean that they have a quality that makes you like or approve of them immediately.

words.ex: It's preposterous to think cats can drive cars.
words.ex_cn: 认为猫会开车是极其荒谬的。
words.en: If you describe something as preposterous, you mean that it is extremely unreasonable and foolish.

words.tr:
n. 预示；前兆；预感
v. 预示；预兆
words.ex: The dark clouds presage a storm.
words.ex_cn: 乌云预示着一场风暴。
words.en: If something presages a situation or event, it is considered to be a warning or sign of what is about to happen.

words.ex: He showed prescience by predicting the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他通过预测风暴展现了先见之明。
words.en: The ability to know or predict what will happen in the future.

words.ex: He gave a presentation about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个关于气候变化的报告。
words.en: The act of showing or explaining something to an audience.

words.ex: She had a presentiment that something bad was going to happen.
words.ex_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得会有坏事发生。
words.en: A presentiment is a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.tr: adj. 紧迫的； v. 按；“press”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pressing issue is finding clean water.
words.ex_cn: 紧迫的问题是找到干净的水。
words.en: If something is pressing, it needs to be dealt with immediately because it is important or urgent.

words.ex: The university has great prestige for its research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学因其研究而享有很高的声望。
words.en: The widespread respect and admiration felt for someone or something on the basis of a perception of their achievements or quality.

words.tr: n. 假定；推定；冒昧；放肆
words.ex: His presumption that he would win surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以为自己会赢的这种假设让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A presumption is something that is thought to be true because it is likely, although there is no proof.

words.ex: His plan is based on a presupposition that everyone will agree.
words.ex_cn: 他的计划基于一个所有人都会同意的假设。
words.en: A presupposition is something that you assume to be true, especially something which you must assume is true in order to continue with a line of argument or a course of action.

words.tr: n. 伪装；假象；虚伪的表现
words.ex: He was accused of using pretense to gain sympathy.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控利用伪装来博取同情。
words.en: A pretense is an action or way of behaving that is intended to make people believe something that is not true.

words.tr: n. 自命不凡；自称；标榜；虚荣
words.ex: His pretension made others think he was better than them.
words.ex_cn: 他的自命不凡让别人觉得他比他们强。
words.en: If you say that someone has pretensions, you mean that they claim or pretend that they are more important, intelligent, or skilled than they really are.

words.ex: He used a pretext to leave the meeting early.
words.ex_cn: 他找了个借口提前离开了会议。
words.en: A pretext is a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason.

words.ex: He prevaricates when asked about the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到错误时，他回避回答。
words.en: If you prevaricate, you avoid giving a direct answer or making a firm decision.

words.ex: He gave a quick preview of the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他简要预看了这部电影。
words.en: A preview is an opportunity to see something such as a film or a collection of works of art before it is open to the public.

words.ex: He made a prevision of the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他预见到这场风暴。
words.en: The ability to foresee or predict future events or developments.

words.tr:
n. 猎物；受害者；受骗者；
v. 捕食；坑害；折磨；
words.ex: The lion chased its prey across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在平原上追逐它的猎物。
words.en: An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；主要的；基本的；最好的；
words.ex: This is the prime reason for the delay.
words.ex_cn: 这是延误的首要原因。
words.en: Prime is used to describe something that is of the best possible quality, or the most important or basic part of something.

words.ex: The family endured years of privation during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个家庭在战争期间经历了多年的贫困。
words.en: Privation is a situation in which you do not have the things that are essential for a comfortable life, such as enough food, clothing, or shelter.

words.ex: Going first is a privilege, not a right.
words.ex_cn: 优先权是一种特权，而不是权利。
words.en: A privilege is a special right or advantage that only one person or group has.

words.tr:
n. 探测器；
v. 探查；
words.ex: The probe sent back photos from Mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器从火星传回了照片。
words.en: If you probe into something, you ask questions or try to discover facts about it. A probe is also a long thin instrument that doctors and dentists use to examine parts of the body.

words.ex: The proceeds from the sale went to charity.
words.ex_cn: 销售所得收益捐给了慈善机构。
words.en: Proceeds are the money that is received from a particular event or activity, especially when it is used for a specific purpose.

words.ex: The procession moved slowly down the street.
words.ex_cn: 行列缓缓沿着街道行进。
words.en: A procession is a group of people who are walking, riding, or driving in a line as part of a public event.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: He always procrastinates doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他总是拖延做作业。
words.en: If you procrastinate, you keep leaving things you should do until later, often because you do not want to do them.

words.ex: The procrustean approach to education enforces a standardized curriculum.
words.ex_cn: 这种强求一致的教育方式强制推行标准化课程。
words.en: If you describe something as procrustean, you mean that it is based on the idea that everyone or everything must be made to fit a particular standard, even if this means ignoring individual differences or needs.

words.tr:
adj. 亵渎的；不敬神的；世俗的
v. 亵渎神灵；亵圣
words.ex: He used profane words during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵中说了脏话。
words.en: If someone uses profane language, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, especially because it refers to sex or other bodily functions in a way that is considered inappropriate.

words.tr:
v. 献出；拿出；提供
n. 献出；拿出；提供
words.ex: He proffered a cup of tea to his guest.
words.ex_cn: 他递给客人一杯茶。
words.en: If you proffer something to someone, you offer it to them for acceptance.

words.tr:
v. 牟取暴利
n. 获暴利的人；投机商
words.ex: The company was accused of profiteering during the pandemic.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司被指控在疫情期间牟取暴利。
words.en: A profiteer is someone who makes large profits in a way that people consider unfair or dishonest, especially by selling goods that are difficult to get at a very high price.

words.tr:
adj. 挥霍无度的；行为不检点的；放荡的
n. 放荡的人；恣意挥霍的人
words.ex: His profligate lifestyle led to his financial ruin.
words.ex_cn: 他放荡的生活方式导致了他经济上的破产。
words.en: Someone who is profligate spends too much money or uses too much of something.

words.ex: The ancient hunter is the progenitor of our family.
words.ex_cn: 这位古代猎人是我们家族的祖先。
words.en: A progenitor is a direct ancestor of someone or the originator of a particular idea or movement.

words.ex: The old tree produced many progeny.
words.ex_cn: 这棵老树生了许多后代。
words.en: The offspring or descendants considered as a group.

words.tr: n. 预断病情；预后；预测
words.ex: The prognosis for patients with this disease is generally poor.
words.ex_cn: 这种疾病的患者预后通常不佳。
words.en: A prognosis is an estimate of the future course and outcome of a disease, especially of the chances of recovery.

words.ex: He tries to prognosticate the weather tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他试图预测明天的天气。
words.en: To prognosticate means to foretell or predict something based on present signs or symptoms.

words.tr:
n. 抛射物；射弹；发射物；自动推进武器
adj. 发射的；射弹的；推进的
words.ex: The boy threw a projectile into the air.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把一个抛射物扔向空中。
words.en: A projectile is an object that is thrown or shot forwards, such as a bullet fired from a gun.

words.ex: The projection of the movie started at 8 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 电影的放映晚上8点开始。
words.en: A projection is an estimate or forecast of a future situation or trend based on a study of present ones.

words.ex: The teacher turned on the projector to show the video.
words.ex_cn: 老师打开投影仪来播放视频。
words.en: A projector is a machine that projects films or slides onto a screen or wall.

words.ex: His prolix speech made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他冗长的演讲让所有人都感到无聊。
words.en: Using or containing too many words; tediously lengthy.

words.ex: The book begins with a short prologue.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一个简短的序言开始。
words.en: A prologue is an introduction to a book, play, or other written work that sets the scene or provides background information.

words.ex: We walked along the promenade by the sea.
words.ex_cn: 我们在海边的步行区散步。
words.en: A promenade is a leisurely walk, especially one taken in a public place for pleasure or display.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: adj. 表示允诺的；约定支付的
words.ex: He signed a promissory note to pay back the loan.
words.ex_cn: 他签署了一张本票来偿还贷款。
words.en: Relating to or containing a promise.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.tr: n. 叉状物；尖齿；分支；方面
words.ex: The deer was caught by the prongs of the hunter's spear.
words.ex_cn: 那只鹿被猎人的矛尖刺中。
words.en: A prong is one of two or more long pointed parts at the end of a fork.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支柱；道具
v. 支撑；靠
words.ex: He uses a prop to support the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个道具来支撑架子。
words.en: A prop is an object or piece of furniture that is used in a play or film to make a scene look more realistic, or something that is used to support or hold up another object.

words.ex: The old woman made a prophecy about the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言了会有雨。
words.en: A prophecy is a statement that something will happen in the future, especially one made by someone with religious or magical powers.

words.ex: The prophet told the people about the coming storm.
words.ex_cn: 预言者告诉人们即将到来的风暴。
words.en: A prophet is a person who is believed to be chosen by God to lead the people and to tell them what God wants them to do.

words.ex: The rocket uses chemical propulsion to fly into space.
words.ex_cn: 火箭使用化学推进力飞入太空。
words.en: Propulsion is the force that moves something forward, especially in vehicles like cars, planes, or spacecraft.

words.ex: The parliament was prorogued until further notice.
words.ex_cn: 议会被休会，直到另行通知。
words.en: To prorogue a legislative body is to discontinue the meetings of the body without dissolving it.

words.ex: The prosecution brought evidence against the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 起诉方提供了针对嫌疑人的证据。
words.en: The act or process of holding a trial against a person who is accused of a crime to see if they are guilty.

words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.ex: The city became prosperous after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市变得繁荣了。
words.en: A prosperous person, place, or economy is rich and successful.

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.tr: adj. 变化多端的；千变万化的
words.ex: He is protean in his interests, changing often.
words.ex_cn: 他对兴趣变化多端，经常改变。
words.en: Able to change frequently or easily; versatile.

words.ex: The two countries signed a protocol to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项停止战争的协议。
words.en: A protocol is a set of rules or a system of rules about the correct way to act in formal situations.

words.tr: n. 凸起物；突出部分；结节；瘤
words.ex: The rock has a small protuberance on top.
words.ex_cn: 这块石头顶部有一个小突起。
words.en: A protuberance is a part that sticks out from the surface of something.

words.tr: adj. 突起的；凸出的；隆起的
words.ex: The dog has a protuberant belly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗的肚子凸出来。
words.en: Something that is protuberant sticks out from a surface in a noticeable way.

words.ex: The provenance of this ancient vase is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个古花瓶的起源未知。
words.en: The place of origin or earliest known history of something.

words.tr: adv. 如谚语所说；众所周知地
words.ex: He is proverbially late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他开会总是习惯性地迟到。
words.en: In a manner that is well known or typical, as if it were a proverb or a well-known saying.

words.tr: adj. 机缘巧合的；及时的；凑巧的
words.ex: It was providential that he found the lost key.
words.ex_cn: 他找到丢失的钥匙真是幸运。
words.en: If you describe something as providential, you mean that it happens at exactly the right time, often by chance, and often in a way that is very fortunate.

words.tr: n. 高超的技艺；造诣；英勇；
words.ex: His prowess in basketball amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在篮球方面的高超技艺让所有人都惊叹。
words.en: Exceptional skill or ability in a particular field or activity.

words.tr:
v. 潜行以觅食；窥伺；逡巡于
n. 悄然潜行；四处觅食；徘徊
words.ex: The cat will prowl around the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 猫会在晚上在房子周围徘徊。
words.en: To move around quietly in a place trying not to be seen or heard, especially when you are looking for something or someone.

words.tr: n. 故作守礼的人；假正经的人
words.ex: She is a prude who won't wear short skirts.
words.ex_cn: 她是个拘谨的人，不愿意穿短裙。
words.en: A prude is a person who is easily shocked by matters relating to sex or nudity.

words.ex: She ate a prune for a healthy snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一颗梅干作为健康零食。
words.en: To prune means to cut off some of the branches of a tree or bush to make it grow better. It can also mean to reduce the extent of something by removing superfluous or unwanted parts.

words.tr:
n. 窥探；杠杆；爱打探的人
v. 打听；窥探；用杠杆撬开
words.ex: His pry into my private messages made me angry.
words.ex_cn: 他窥探我的私信让我很生气。
words.en: To try to find out private information about someone or something in a way that is annoying or rude.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: His puerile jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他幼稚的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puerile, you mean that they are silly and childish.

words.tr: n. 夸大宣传；吹捧的广告
words.ex: The company's marketing campaign is full of puffery, making exaggerated claims about the product.
words.ex_cn: 该公司的营销活动充满了夸大广告，对产品做出了夸张的声明。
words.en: Exaggerated or false praise or publicity, especially in advertising.

words.tr: adj. 强有力的；强盛的；有势力的
words.ex: The puissant ruler commanded respect from all his subjects.
words.ex_cn: 这位强大的统治者赢得了所有臣民的尊敬。
words.en: Having great power or influence; potent.

words.ex: Her pulchritude was the talk of the town.
words.ex_cn: 她的美貌是全镇的话题。
words.en: Physical beauty, especially of a woman.

words.ex: The farm is home to many pullets and roosters.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场养了许多小母鸡和公鸡。
words.en: A young hen, especially one less than one year old.

words.tr: v. 发芽；繁殖；大量发展
words.ex: Seeds pullulate after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 种子在雨后发芽。
words.en: To breed or spread rapidly; to sprout or bud.

words.ex: The orange was squeezed into a sweet pulp.
words.ex_cn: 橙子被榨成了甜美的浆状物。
words.en: The soft, wet, shapeless mass of material that is left after the juice has been removed from fruit or vegetables, or the soft inner part of a tooth.

words.ex: The priest stood at the pulpit and spoke loudly.
words.ex_cn: 牧师站在讲坛上大声讲话。
words.en: A pulpit is a raised platform in a church from which the preacher delivers a sermon.

words.tr: v. 粉碎；磨成粉；彻底击败；摧毁
words.ex: The machine will pulverize the rocks into dust.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会把岩石碾成粉末。
words.en: To pulverize something means to crush it into a fine powder or to defeat someone or something completely.

words.ex: He punched the wall in anger.
words.ex_cn: 他生气地打了墙一拳。
words.en: To punch means to hit someone or something hard with your fist, or to make a hole in something using a tool.

words.tr: adj. 谨小慎微的；一丝不苟的
words.ex: He is punctilious about following every rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对遵守每一条规则都谨小慎微。
words.en: If someone is punctilious, they are very careful to behave correctly and to follow the details of rules or customs.

words.tr: n. 权威人士；专家；评论员
words.ex: The pundit said the team will win tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这位专家说球队明天会赢。
words.en: A pundit is a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is often asked to give their opinions to the public.

words.ex: He is puny and can't lift the box.
words.ex_cn: 他很瘦弱，举不起那个箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puny, you mean that they are small and weak.

words.tr: n. 炼狱；受难的处所（或状态）；折磨
words.ex: He felt like he was in purgatory while waiting for the results.
words.ex_cn: 他在等待结果时感觉自己身处炼狱。
words.en: Purgatory is a place or state of suffering inhabited by the souls of sinners who are expiating their sins before going to heaven.

words.tr:
v. 净化；清除；清洗；整肃
n. 净化；清除；泻药
words.ex: The company purged its outdated systems.
words.ex_cn: 公司净化了其过时的系统。
words.en: To purge an organization or place of something or someone means to remove them from it because they are considered undesirable or harmful.

words.ex: The machine purifies water by removing dirt.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器通过去除杂质来净化水。
words.en: To purify something means to make it clean and pure by removing dirty or harmful substances from it.

words.ex: He was accused of purloining company funds.
words.ex_cn: 他被指控偷窃公司资金。
words.en: To purloin means to steal something, especially in a sneaky or stealthy manner.

words.tr:
adj. 据称的；传言的
v. 声称；意指；意味着；“purport”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The purported owner of the car was not the real one.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的所谓主人并不是真正的主人。
words.en: If you say that something purports to be true or to have a particular quality, you mean that it claims to be true or to have that quality, although it may not be.

words.tr: n. 女用小包；钱包；资金；
words.ex: She put her keys in her purse.
words.ex_cn: 她把钥匙放进她的女用小包里。
words.en: A purse is a small bag used especially by women to carry everyday personal items.

words.ex: He purveys fresh bread to the local shop.
words.ex_cn: 他向当地商店供应新鲜面包。
words.en: To purvey means to supply or provide something, especially food, as a business.

words.tr: adj. 执意强求的；要强的
words.ex: He is too pushy when he asks for help.
words.ex_cn: 他请求帮助时太咄咄逼人了。
words.en: If you describe someone as pushy, you mean that they try in a forceful way to get things done as they would like or to increase their status or influence.

words.ex: His pusillanimous behavior in the face of danger was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 他在危险面前的懦弱行为令人失望。
words.en: If you say that someone is pusillanimous, you mean that they are timid or afraid, especially in a way that you find irritating or disappointing.

words.tr: adj. 推定的；假定的；一般认为的
words.ex: The putative father was asked to take a DNA test.
words.ex_cn: 被推定的父亲被要求做DNA测试。
words.en: Generally believed to be or to exist, but not proved to be so.

words.ex: The meat will putrefy if left in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 如果把肉放在阳光下，它会腐烂。
words.en: To decay or cause to decay and have a foul smell.

words.ex: The putrid meat smelled awful.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂的肉闻起来很臭。
words.en: Something that is putrid has decayed and smells very unpleasant.

words.tr:
n. 嘎嘎叫声；庸医；冒充内行的人
v. 嘎嘎地叫；大声闲谈；冒充内行
words.ex: The duck made a loud quack.
words.ex_cn: 鸭子发出了响亮的嘎嘎叫声。
words.en: A quack is someone who pretends to have medical skills that they do not really possess. It can also refer to the sound a duck makes.

words.tr: v. 豪饮；痛饮；开怀畅饮
words.ex: He quaffed the cold drink quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速地喝下了那杯冷饮。
words.en: To drink (a beverage) heartily and with gusto.

words.tr:
n. 鹌鹑；鹌鹑肉 
v. 畏缩；胆怯
words.ex: The farmer raised quail for their eggs.
words.ex_cn: 农夫饲养鹌鹑来获取它们的蛋。
words.en: If someone quails, they feel or show fear or hesitation.

words.tr: n. 恶心；晕眩；疑虑；不安
words.ex: The smell of the food gave her a qualm.
words.ex_cn: 食物的气味让她感到恶心。
words.en: A qualm is a feeling of uneasiness about whether what you are doing is right.

words.tr: n. 困境；窘境；困惑之境；进退两难
words.ex: He is in a quandary about what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他对于该做什么感到困惑。
words.en: A situation in which you are unsure or confused about what to do.

words.tr: adj. 古怪的；难以解释的
words.ex: He is queer and proud of who he is.
words.ex_cn: 他是同性恋，并为自己是谁而自豪。
